ID (PMID): 42989998
Título: Comparing Gleason pattern 4 measurement approaches on prostate biopsy using machine learning: a proof-of-principle study.
Resumen: There is increasing evidence that length of Gleason Pattern (GP) 4 on biopsy is a stronger predictor of oncological outcomes than Grade Group (GG) or %GP4. However, there is no consensus regarding the optimal method for quantifying GP4 length. We propose that machine learning (ML) can be used to quantify GP4 on digitized biopsy slides using multiple measurement approaches, allowing direct comparison of their prognostic performance. In this study, we attempt to demonstrate proof-of-principle for this approach. We assembled a convenience sample of 726 patients with GG2-4 prostate cancer on systematic biopsy who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2014 and 2023. ML algorithm (PAIGE-AI) quantified GP4 using different approaches, varying by how gaps between cancer foci were handled. GP4 extent was assessed using linear and pixel-based metrics. Discrimination of each quantification approach, along with GG, was assessed for adverse radical prostatectomy pathology and biochemical recurrence. We identified 15 different quantification approaches and observed differences between their discrimination. The highest discrimination was in the pixel-counting method (AUC 0.648). GP4 quantification outperformed GG for predicting adverse pathology (AUC 0.627 versus 0.608). The amount of GP3 was non-predictive once GP4 was known. These findings were consistent for BCR. We were able to measure slides using 15 distinct measurement approaches and replicated prior findings using ML to quantify GP4. Our findings support the use of ML as a research tool to compare different GP4 quantification approaches. We intend to use our method on larger cohorts to determine which measurement approach best predicts oncological outcome.

--- ARTÍCULO 3 ---
ID (PMID): 42989703
Título: Establishment and Validation of a Model of Indwelling Nasogastric Tube in Patients After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Resumen: Dysphagia is common after stroke, and accurately predicting its duration is essential for guiding therapeutic decisions. Timely indwelling nasogastric tube (NGT) placement is critical for patient prognosis. The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a predictive model for indwelling NGT requirements in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). From 2020 to 2022, we retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 553 patients with AIS. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate logistic regression were employed to identify predictors. Multiple machine learning (ML) classifiers were integrated to identify the optimal model, followed by validation. Finally, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretation and personalized risk assessment. A total of five variables-patient's National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, age, free thyroxine (fT4), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and stroke location, were derived from Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and logistic regression as independent predictors associated with indwelling NGT requirement in AIS patients. Among nine machine learning classifiers, random forest demonstrated optimal performance. The model achieved an AUC of 0.850 in fivefold cross-validation within the training cohort and 0.853 in the independent testing cohort. The proposed model serves as a user-friendly prognostic tool for reliably predicting swallowing dysfunction while offering interpretable results. It may assist clinicians in making NGT placement decisions for AIS patients, facilitating personalized care.


--- ARTÍCULO 4 ---
ID (PMID): 42989659
Título: A novel feature-agnostic approach for glaucoma detection in fundus images.
Resumen: To design and validate a fully automated, feature-agnostic deep learning approach for the early detection of glaucoma from fundus images. The retrospective study was conducted at Al-Shifa Trust Eye Hospital, Rawalpindi, Pakistan, using publicly available retinal fundus image datasets from October 2024 to January 2025, and comprised 1,707 fundus images from five publicly available retrospective datasets. A computer-aided detection system was employed based on state-of-the-art deep convolutional neural networks, including EfficientNetV2b0, Xception, InceptionV3, Visual Geometry Group and ResNet50. The images were labelled either as glaucomatous or healthy after they were pre-processed through cropping, normalisation and data augmentation. The models were fine-tuned using transfer learning, and evaluated using standard metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and area under the curve, which were calculated using Python-based statistical libraries. Among the tested models, EfficientNetV2b0 achieved the best performance with an area under the curve of 0.98 and an accuracy of 93%. The best-performing model achieved a sensitivity/recall of 97%, precision of 89% and F1-score of 93%, indicating reliable performance for glaucoma classification. The robustness of the proposed method was validated across multiple datasets, ensuring its generalisability in diverse clinical scenarios. The proposed deep learning-based approach provided a reliable and efficient method for early glaucoma detection. Its automation and high accuracy made it suitable for use in mass screening programmes and under-resourced clinical environments, potentially reducing the burden on ophthalmologists and enabling timely intervention.


--- ARTÍCULO 5 ---
ID (PMID): 42989632
Título: Artificial intelligence in dialysis.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in dialysis have matured beyond the initial phase of algorithm development. Recent work has shifted toward clinical implementation, evaluation, and governance. During the past year, the first randomized trial of AI-guided dosing in maintenance hemodialysis has been published, a meta-analysis of technology-guided dry-weight adjustment has appeared, and the first professional society framework for the responsible use of AI in kidney care has been released. The Anemia Control Model is now supported by hospitalization outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses. A randomized trial demonstrated that AI-guided erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing achieved outcomes comparable to physician-directed dosing. Technology-guided dry-weight adjustment is supported by a meta-analysis of 21 randomized trials. Machine learning for vascular access is evolving toward preoperative clinical decision support, while peritoneal dialysis is beginning to receive greater attention from the machine learning community. Large language models are entering nephrology along two complementary paths: open generative systems for education and clinical support, and deterministic, protocol-driven frameworks designed for safety-critical bedside applications. At the same time, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released comprehensive lifecycle guidance for AI-enabled medical devices. The major challenge for AI in dialysis is no longer developing accurate prediction models. Instead, success will depend on effective workflow integration, validation across diverse patient populations, ongoing postdeployment monitoring, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.


--- ARTÍCULO 6 ---
ID (PMID): 42989602
Título: Predicting adolescent gaming addiction: insights from individual, family, and school-level factors via machine learning.
Resumen: Game addiction is increasingly acknowledged as a major adolescent mental health concern worldwide. To better understand its development, it is essential to identify both risk and protective factors. However, most existing studies have focused on only a limited number of variables. To address this gap, this study adopted machine learning to identify the most important predictors across individual, family, and school domains. The analysis was conducted with a sample of 21,239 Chinese parent-adolescent pairs (for parents: 68.92% mothers; <i>M</i><sub>age</sub> = 40.42 years, <i>SD</i> = 5.78 years; for adolescents: 45.00% males; <i>M</i><sub>age</sub> = 13.41 years, <i>SD</i> = 2.14 years). Using the machine learning classification models, this study examined the accuracy of the selected variables in predicting game addiction and explored the relative importance of the studied variables in the prediction process. Both the Random Forest and XGBoost models achieved accuracies exceeding 0.80 and consistently identified several key predictors of game addiction. Risk factors include high levels of externalizing problems and attention problems, being male, bullying victimization, alienation from parents, parental depression, and a performance-oriented school environment. The protective factors include high levels of perseverance, good academic performance, and academic self-efficacy. In conclusion, the findings point out the value of using machine learning approaches to uncover the crucial predictors of game addiction, offering important insights for targeted prevention and intervention efforts across individual, familial, and school contexts.


--- ARTÍCULO 7 ---
ID (PMID): 42989526
Título: SERPINE1 Identifies a Shared Injury-associated Molecular Signature in Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Epilepsy.
Resumen: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and epilepsy are clinically linked neurological disorders, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular candidates across ICH and epilepsy by integrating transcriptomic data with a curated set of genes with established circadian relevance. Transcriptomic datasets for ICH and epilepsy were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus, and candidate genes were curated from the Molecular Signatures Database and GeneCards. Differentially expressed candidate genes were intersected, and an integrative machine-learning framework-including Boruta, LASSO, XGBoost, and CatBoost-was applied to prioritize shared genes. Integrated machine-learning and network analyses nominated SERPINE1 for further investigation. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis identified higher scores for porphyrin, folate and pterine, and arachidonic acid metabolism in both disease comparisons. SERPINE1 expression correlated positively with arachidonic acid metabolism scores in both datasets, while Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis linked its expression to inflammatory transcriptional signatures, including TNFA signaling via NFKB and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling. Gene interaction, drug-mRNA, transcription factor-mRNA, and competing endogenous RNA networks further characterized its regulatory and pharmacological context. Independent bulk transcriptomic datasets and experimental models supported SERPINE1 upregulation, with single-nucleus RNA-sequencing providing complementary cellular context, while single-nucleus analyses and immunostaining further supported its preferential microglial localization. Collectively, these findings identify SERPINE1 as a shared injury-associated molecular feature of ICH and epilepsy, with preferential microglial localization and associations with inflammatory transcriptional signatures and metabolic pathway scores. Although SERPINE1 is known to be clock-regulated, whether its temporal expression pattern is altered in ICH or epilepsy remains to be determined.


--- ARTÍCULO 8 ---
ID (PMID): 42989508
Título: AWARE_AI, a Machine-Learning-Based Reproducible Workflow Modelling the Fundamentals of Care Framework and Patient-Reported Wellbeing: A Cross-Sectional Feasibility Study.
Resumen: To examine whether theory-ordered Fundamentals of Care domain associations are present in patient-reported data and to assess the feasibility of a reproducible machine-learning-based workflow for modelling these associations and wellbeing in an Australian pilot sample. Secondary cross-sectional feasibility analysis. We analysed de-identified survey data from 36 adults who had received healthcare in the previous 12 months using a frozen Python workflow. The workflow estimated theory-ordered bivariate associations among Context of Care, Relationship, Integration of Care, and a 12-item study-specific wellbeing index, assessed out-of-sample prediction and explored item-level patterns using penalised regression. Feasibility was assessed across process, analytical, predictive, and reproducibility dimensions. Theory-ordered bivariate associations were positive and consistent with the proposed Fundamentals of Care ordering. Context of Care was associated with Relationship, Relationship with Integration of Care and Integration of Care with wellbeing. Their descriptive serial product was positive but does not support mediation or causal interpretation. Process, analytical and reproducibility feasibility criteria were met, whereas predictive feasibility was not. Out-of-sample prediction was negligible and unstable. Associations were strongest for evaluative wellbeing indicators and weaker for affective and health-status indicators. Care context, relational quality, integrative care and patient-reported wellbeing co-varied in a pattern consistent with the FoC framework. The cross-sectional design does not establish a conditional pathway, causation or individual-level prediction. AWARE_AI provides a transparent foundation for larger longitudinal validation. Clinicians and leaders should treat item-level patterns as hypotheses for future testing, not actionable determinants. Researchers can reuse the workflow in larger longitudinal studies with wellbeing measured before and after defined care episodes. We followed STROBE and TRIPOD+AI. This secondary analysis did not include patient or public involvement in study design, conduct, analysis, interpretation or manuscript preparation. Patients contributed data as survey respondents.


--- ARTÍCULO 9 ---
ID (PMID): 42989492
Título: Analysis and Identification of Candidate Genes Associated with M1 Macrophage Infiltration and Glycolysis in Breast Cancer.
Resumen: Macrophage polarization and glycolytic reprogramming contribute to the breast cancer microenvironment. However, the genes associated with these features and their clinical relevance remain poorly defined. Breast cancer transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using immune deconvolution, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis. We identified 101 genes shared by the M1 macrophage-associated, glycolysis-related, and differentially expressed gene sets. Eight genes showed suggestive genetically predicted associations with BC risk. Machine learning selected seven consensus genes. In TCGA-BRCA, six genes differed significantly between tumor and normal tissue, but only five changed in the same direction as in GSE65194. In the 56 paired clinical tissues, ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were upregulated in tumors, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M were downregulated. ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were preferentially expressed in M1-like TAMs, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M showed higher expression in M2-like TAMs. In BMDMs, overexpression of ADAM15, XPO5, or PPP1R14B, as well as knockdown of PPM1M or FAM172A, increased the proportion of CD80-positive cells and ATP, glucose uptake, and lactate production. Five genes showed significant associations with overall survival. Functional enrichment analyses implicated immune regulation, extracellular matrix organization, and metabolic pathways.


--- ARTÍCULO 10 ---
ID (PMID): 42989450
Título: Random forest segmentation and spatial analysis of injected cardiac spheroids in optically cleared myocardium.
Resumen: Accurate quantification of transplanted cardiac spheroids requires three-dimensional (3D) localisation within intact myocardium, yet this remains technically challenging. Optical clearing and light-sheet microscopy enable volumetric imaging of injection sites, but automated segmentation is difficult when transplanted spheroids and host tissue are labelled with the same fluorescent markers and cannot be separated by simple intensity thresholding. We developed an application-focused workflow for 3D segmentation and spatial analysis of injected hiPSC-derived cardiomyocyte and H9c2 spheroids in optically cleared rabbit myocardium. Random forest pixel classification using intensity, edge, and texture features was used to segment spheroids, with connected-component analysis subsequently used to reconstruct individual objects. Compared with simple intensity thresholding, random forest classification provided substantially improved segmentation, although a U-Net achieved higher segmentation performance. The resulting 3D segmentations enabled automated extraction of spheroid size, nearest-neighbour distance, and epicardial depth. This workflow provides an end-to-end pipeline from volumetric light-sheet microscopy of injected cardiac spheroids to automated 3D spatial quantification, using sparse annotations to support segmentation of large cleared-tissue datasets.

--- ARTÍCULO 12 ---
ID (PMID): 42989416
Título: Longitudinal MRI-based Delta-Habitat model for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
Resumen: To develop and validate a machine learning model integrating habitat imaging features before and after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) to predict pathological complete response (pCR) to NACI in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). A multicenter retrospective study was conducted involving 520 HNSCC patients who received NACI across three hospitals. Unlike conventional Delta-Radiomics, we developed Delta-Habitat model that integrates Pre-NACI and Post-NACI MRI spatial habitat radiomics features, and dynamically learns task-specific contributions from each timepoint. Predictive performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to quantify the contribution of individual features to model predictions. We assessed and compared the diagnostic performance of senior and junior radiologists, both with and without the aid of the Delta-Habitat model. Delta-Habitat model outperformed Pre-NACI feature-based models and traditional radiomics-based Delta-Rad model, with AUC of 0.828, 0.825 and 0.813 in validation and two external test cohorts respectively. Post-treatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (Post-NLR) was identified as an independent predictor of pCR. Integrating Delta-Radiomics and clinical features into Delta-Habitat model did not yield a significant improvement in predictive performance, the combined model showed slightly improved AUC over Delta-Habitat alone, reaching 0.877 (train), 0.834 (val), 0.837 (test1), and 0.834 (test2). SHAP analysis revealed that Post-NACI features contributed more substantially to model predictions than Pre-NACI features. The Delta-Habitat model consistently exhibited better performance than radiologists in comparative evaluations. Moreover, senior and junior radiologists both showed increases in AUC values with the assistance of the Delta-Habitat model, by 0.073 and 0.177 respectively on the internal validation cohort and by 0.087 and 0.142 on the external test cohort. The longitudinal MRI-based habitat model can provide valuable information for predicting the response to NACI in HNSCC and enhance radiologists' diagnostic performance.


--- ARTÍCULO 13 ---
ID (PMID): 42989400
Título: Software-based concordance analysis of a predictive surgical planning model for target gap achievement in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
Resumen: In robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA), achieving soft-tissue balance requires repeated intraoperative plan adjustment and remains experience-dependent. Predictive models may support planning, but their clinical value depends on whether model-generated plans approximate predefined target gaps within the robotic workflow. This study assessed the software-based concordance between model-generated plans and predefined target gaps in robotic-assisted TKA. The predefined target gaps were planning set points established within the robotic software rather than measured intraoperative gaps. This retrospective software-based concordance study included 209 complete-case knees undergoing robotic-assisted TKA. A machine-learning-based predictive model generated a bone-resection plan, which was imported into the robotic planning software to calculate software-derived medial and lateral gaps in extension and flexion. These software-derived gaps were compared with predefined target gaps, which were planning set points rather than measured values and were 18 mm in 819 of 836 gap-level observations (98.0%). The primary analysis focused on target gap deviation, defined as the software-derived gap minus the predefined target gap. As a benchmark, the deviation of the preadjustment gaps from the same targets was used as a preadjustment reference. A total of 836 gap-level observations were analyzed. The overall mean target gap deviation was -0.142 mm (SD, 1.411 mm), with a mean absolute error of 1.016 mm. Overall, 77.6% of software-derived gaps were within ±1 mm of target, and 93.4% were within ±2 mm. Bland-Altman analysis showed a small overall bias of -0.142 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -2.91 to +2.62 mm. At the knee level, only 43.1% of knees had all software-derived gaps within ±1 mm of target. Gap-level deviations ranged from -7 mm to +5 mm, and 16.3% of knees (34/209) had at least one gap with an absolute deviation > 2 mm. Compared with the preadjustment reference (MAE 2.002 mm, 49.4% within ±1 mm), the model substantially reduced deviation (MAE 1.016 mm, 77.6% within ±1 mm, p < 0.001). In this software-based concordance analysis, the predictive planning model generated surgical plans whose robotic software-derived gaps approximated predefined target gaps with a mean absolute deviation of approximately 1 mm. The model-generated plan reduced target-gap deviation relative to the initial preadjustment plan within this target-conditioned workflow. However, because the targets were near-uniform (98.0% at 18 mm) and all measurements were software-derived, compartment-specific bias, moderate whole-knee consistency (43.1%), and occasional outlier deviations indicate that the model should be used as a surgeon-supervised decision support tool rather than as an autonomous planner. Prospective validation against measured intraoperative and postoperative gaps is required before clinical effectiveness can be claimed.


--- ARTÍCULO 14 ---
ID (PMID): 42989381
Título: AI decision-support in the initial management of orthopedic trauma: a systematic review.
Resumen: Early orthopedic trauma care requires rapid, high-stakes decision-making under conditions of physiologic instability and diagnostic uncertainty. Conventional clinical scores and guideline-based tools aim to standardize early management but often demonstrate limited patient-level accuracy and variable performance across care settings. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based decision-support tools have been proposed as adjuncts to support early trauma decisions, yet their scope and performance in orthopedic trauma remain uncharacterized. A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted of prediction-model and implementation studies published between January 2010 and October 2025 using MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies evaluated AI/ML-based tools designed to predict or support early orthopedic trauma decisions in the emergency department, trauma bay, or prehospital setting. Target decision domains included hemorrhage control, operative versus nonoperative management, limb salvage versus amputation, and level-of-care or interfacility triage. Data extraction focused on study design, clinical decision targets, model inputs, validation strategy and reported performance metrics. From 361 identified records, 9 studies met inclusion criteria. Study populations, modeling approaches, and clinical targets were heterogeneous. Reported discriminatory performance was generally moderate to favorable, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values ranging from 0.67 to 0.97 across decision domains. External validation was limited, and reporting of calibration and decision-analytic metrics was inconsistent. Imaging-adjacent AI tools enabled automated computed tomography (CT) based hematoma quantification for pelvic trauma and real-time CT auto-segmentation workflows for maxillofacial trauma (Dice ≈0.92-0.93) with substantial time reduction. However, the included studies did not directly evaluate downstream effects on clinician decisions or workflow throughput beyond segmentation tasks, or patient-centered outcomes. AI/ML-based decision-support tools for early orthopedic trauma management show strong technical feasibility and encouraging performance in existing validation studies, supporting their potential role as adjuncts to clinician judgment in early, high-stakes decisions. The current literature is dominated by retrospective evaluation and offers limited evidence on real-world impact. Next steps should prioritize prospective, workflow-integrated studies with standardized reporting of calibration and decision utility to determine how these tools can most effectively improve care delivery and patient outcomes in early orthopedic trauma.


--- ARTÍCULO 15 ---
ID (PMID): 42989373
Título: Spectral-habitat analysis and perfusion fingerprinting on contrast-enhanced ultrasound for characterizing tumor perfusion in breast lesions.
Resumen: To develop a short-time Fourier transform (STFT)-based perfusion fingerprinting method combined with spectral-habitat analysis for characterizing pixel-wise perfusion heterogeneity on contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) and to evaluate its ability to differentiate benign and malignant breast lesions. Pixel-wise CEUS time-series data were transformed into the time-frequency domain using STFT. Principal component analysis (PCA) was then applied to reduce the dimensionality of STFT-derived features and generate perfusion fingerprinting maps that preserved spatial and temporal perfusion information. Spectral-habitat maps were generated using K-means clustering to identify perfusion-related tumor subregions. A triple-branch multi-layer fusion model was constructed to integrate full-region and habitat-derived features for lesion classification. To provide an exploratory conventional CEUS quantitative baseline, TIC-derived perfusion features were additionally extracted and evaluated using machine learning classifiers. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), and confusion matrix. The proposed STFT-based perfusion fingerprinting method enabled a more comprehensive characterization of tumor perfusion heterogeneity by preserving pixel-wise spatiotemporal dynamics of CEUS signals. CEUS-derived spectral-habitat maps provided visual representations of intratumoral perfusion heterogeneity and improved the interpretability of the model outputs. In this cohort, the triple-branch multi-layer fusion model achieved an AUC of 0.953, with accuracy of 0.909, precision of 0.907, recall of 0.925, and F1 score of 0.912. Exploratory TIC-based conventional CEUS models achieved AUCs ranging from 0.7677 to 0.8186. DCA suggested potential clinical utility of the proposed model across a range of threshold probabilities, and confusion matrix analysis showed favorable classification performance. The STFT-based perfusion fingerprinting method combined with spectral-habitat analysis provides a promising CEUS-based framework for characterizing perfusion heterogeneity in breast lesions. By preserving pixel-wise spatiotemporal information, this approach may provide complementary quantitative information for more interpretable differentiation between benign and malignant lesions.


--- ARTÍCULO 16 ---
ID (PMID): 42989372
Título: Recent advances in volumetric super-resolution imaging through computational adaptive optics.
Resumen: Optical microscopy's power to resolve nanoscale structures deep within living tissues is limited by light diffraction and sample-induced aberrations. While super-resolution microscopy (SRM) has broken through the diffraction limit, its performance rapidly deteriorates in thick, heterogeneous specimens. Adaptive optics (AO) has emerged as a suitable solution to this challenge. By measuring and correcting wavefront distortions, AO restores imaging conditions, enabling SRM to achieve its full potential deep within complex biological samples like living brain tissue and developing organoids. The integration of AO with SRM (AO-SRM) is unlocking volumetric imaging capabilities, enhancing imaging depth and restoring nanoscale resolution. A recent advance has been the fusion of these hardware corrections with deep learning (DL). This convergence encompasses a dual paradigm of high-fidelity algorithmic restoration to bridge signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gaps and systemic autonomy through self-driving frameworks for real-time hardware loop optimization. By employing intelligent agents that autonomously navigate aberration landscapes and trigger acquisition during biological events, this synergy maximizes experimental throughput while optimizing the photon budget to prevent sample degradation. DL algorithms enhance imaging capabilities by providing high-speed aberration prediction and robust computational reconstruction. This synergy not only boosts image contrast and resolution but also improves data processing efficiency and mitigates phototoxicity, enabling volumetric imaging with nanoscale precision. This review synthesizes recent developments in AO-integrated super-resolution imaging - encompassing image restoration approaches such as denoising and deblurring as well as wavefront correction techniques - and addresses how this convergence empowers the study of neuronal morphology and subcellular-scale dynamics deep within biological tissues.


--- ARTÍCULO 17 ---
ID (PMID): 42989370
Título: Unlocking biological insight from single-cell data with an interpretable dual-stream foundation model.
Resumen: Deep learning foundation models are revolutionizing single-cell biology, yet learning holistic and discriminative representations from complex, high-dimensional data remains a central challenge. Although transformer-based single-cell language models have shown significant progress, they typically rely on a single input-encoding scheme, a practice that results in the loss of critical gene expression information and hinders the effective learning of global cellular representations. To address these challenges, we propose scDMC, an innovative single-cell pre-training framework. At the input encoding level, scDMC employs a 'dual-stream' architecture by processing a rank-based sequence and an absolute expression-aware sequence in parallel to overcome the information loss inherent in single-encoding schemes. Building upon this, our framework synergistically optimizes local gene context and global cellular representation by combining masked language modeling at the gene level with momentum contrastive learning at the cell level. Pre-trained on only 2 million cells far fewer than the datasets used by mainstream models, scDMC sets a new state-of-the-art in multiple benchmark tasks, including cell annotation, clustering, and data integration. More importantly, we demonstrate that scDMC can uncover functional gene modules, infer cell-type-specific regulatory networks in a data-driven manner, and provides attention-guided biological insights. scDMC provides a powerful and extensible foundation model framework for single-cell biology. By reconciling relative gene importance with absolute expression magnitude, it enhances representation fidelity. Its robust performance and biologically meaningful interpretations offer a new paradigm for data-driven discovery, facilitating deeper insights into cellular heterogeneity and gene regulatory mechanisms across diverse biological contexts.


--- ARTÍCULO 18 ---
ID (PMID): 42989368
Título: Multi-omics analysis reveals microbial and metabolic signatures associated with neutral detergent fiber digestibility in dairy cattle.
Resumen: The rumen microbiome is central to fiber degradation in dairy cows, yet the precise functional and metabolic networks driving variations in neutral detergent fiber (NDF) digestibility remain poorly understood. Elucidating these microbiome-host interactions is critical for improving forage utilization and advancing sustainable dairy production. Employing an integrative metagenomics-metabolomics approach, we characterized the rumen microecology of lactating dairy cows exhibiting high and low NDF digestibility phenotypes (n = 10/group). Metagenomic profiling revealed a significant enrichment of fibrolytic taxa (Prevotella sp., Lachnospiraceae bacterium) and carbohydrate-active enzymes in the high-NDF group (HI). In addition, species-level differential abundance testing showed that Methanobrevibacter spp. was more abundant in the low-NDF group (LO) than in the HI group, whereas no archaeal differences were detected at the phylum or genus levels. Functional and metabolomic analyses indicated broader enrichment of amino acid degradation functions and higher concentrations of major volatile fatty acids (VFAs) in HI cows, consistent with stronger overall ruminal fermentation activity. Furthermore, VFAs and microbial composition explained 54.3% and 43.0% of the variation in NDF digestibility, respectively. An exploratory machine learning model based on selected annotated metabolite features showed moderate discriminatory performance, with an out-of-bag accuracy of 77.19%. Our findings suggest that coordinated shifts in rumen microbial composition, amino acid metabolism, and VFA production are associated with variation in NDF digestibility in dairy cattle. These results provide a basis for future studies aimed at improving fiber utilization through microbiome-informed nutritional or breeding strategies.


--- ARTÍCULO 19 ---
ID (PMID): 42989357
Título: Distinguishing artificial intelligence from robotic execution in total knee arthroplasty: a narrative review and evidence map.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning methods are increasingly discussed in relation to robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, robotic assistance, computer navigation, and AI-based prediction represent distinct functions that are often conflated under the single label "AI-assisted robotic TKA," obscuring the state of evidence for each. This review clarifies these distinctions and maps the current evidence for AI-related functions across the TKA pathway, keeping AI prediction evidence analytically separate from robotic execution evidence at the level of each clinical function. We performed a critical narrative review and evidence map of peer-reviewed literature relevant to robotic-assisted TKA, navigation-assisted TKA, AI/ML prediction models, digital planning, implant sizing, intraoperative decision support, postoperative monitoring, implementation, and economic evaluation. Evidence was interpreted according to clinical function, comparator structure, validation status, and translational maturity. Because the available literature is methodologically and conceptually heterogeneous, quantitative pooling and formal comparative-effectiveness claims were not attempted. Robotic-assisted and navigation-assisted TKA have the most mature evidence base for improving technical precision, particularly implant positioning and radiographic alignment. In contrast, AI/ML evidence is concentrated mainly in adjacent pathway functions, including radiographic interpretation, implant-sizing prediction, patient-selection support, dissatisfaction prediction, outcome modelling, perioperative risk stratification, and postoperative monitoring. Direct clinical evidence demonstrating that AI-enabled robotic TKA provides incremental patient-level benefit beyond conventional robotic assistance remains limited. Current studies are constrained by inconsistent terminology, short follow-up, limited external validation, incomplete reporting of AI components, heterogeneous outcomes, cost uncertainty, and uncertain generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings. AI should not currently be treated as a single validated surgical intervention in TKA. Rather, it represents a family of emerging pathway-level functions that may support preoperative planning, intraoperative decision support, patient selection, risk communication, and longitudinal recovery monitoring. Future studies should explicitly define the AI component being evaluated, distinguish AI functionality from robotic or navigation assistance, use standardized comparators, and assess long-term patient-reported outcomes, implant survivorship, safety, cost-effectiveness, and equity across multicenter prospective cohorts or randomized trials.


--- ARTÍCULO 20 ---
ID (PMID): 42989343
Título: Deep learning-based automated segmentation of target volumes for pediatric craniospinal irradiation in proton therapy.
Resumen: Accurate target delineation is essential for achieving optimal plan quality in craniospinal irradiation (CSI), particularly in pediatric proton therapy. However, manual target delineation is highly time-consuming due to the large anatomical extent of craniospinal axis. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning-based automated segmentation model to streamline the target delineation for pediatric proton CSI. Fifty pediatric patient datasets treated with proton CSI at the National Cancer Center Korea were utilized. The nnU-Net v2 framework was employed for model training using 40 datasets, with the remaining 10 used for independent evaluation. Segmentation performance was assessed using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Intersection over Union (IoU), 95th percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95), and Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD). Workflow efficiency was evaluated by comparing manual and automated contouring times, and clinical acceptability was assessed using a Likert scale. The model achieved high geometric accuracy, with mean DSC, IoU, HD95, and ASSD values of 0.9587, 0.9222, 2.4948 mm, and 0.7900 mm, respectively. The target delineation time was reduced from approximately 8 h to 30 min. Clinical acceptability was favorable, with the majority of Likert scale ratings falling within the positive-to-neutral range. This study demonstrates that the developed deep learning-based automated segmentation model can achieve accurate and robust target delineation for proton CSI. By integrating this framework into the planning workflow, CSI can be performed with greater efficiency, reproducibility, and standardization. Our findings highlight the potential of automation to advance precision and productivity in pediatric proton CSI practice.

Título: Integrating machine learning and traditional statistics to evaluate the Uric acid-to-HDL cholesterol ratio for identification of prevalent COPD in older adults.
Resumen: The uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) is a novel inflammatory and metabolic biomarker, but its association with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in older adults remains unclear. Weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated the UHR-COPD association. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis characterized the dose-response relationship, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated model performance. Elevated UHR is associated with a higher prevalence of COPD in older adults. UHR may serve as a low-cost, routinely measurable marker to aid in the identification of prevalent, physician-diagnosed COPD in geriatric care. Because COPD status was ascertained at a single survey time point in a cross-sectional analysis, no prospective-screening inference is intended.

Trial, extension, cohort, post-marketing, registry, and case-based evidence consistently supported IL-1 pathway inhibition. Dose escalation, interval modification, and individualized treat-to-target adjustment were frequent across the published reports. This case supports early MVK testing when recurrent infantile inflammation persists after treatment for suspected incomplete Kawasaki disease. The patient had marked hyperinflammation with several HLH-associated abnormalities, but not enough evidence for a formal HLH/MAS diagnosis. Her response is consistent with the established therapeutic rationale for IL-1 blockade in systemic MKD; however, the c.827 A > G variant requires fuller laboratory documentation, and the firsekibart observation remains a single-patient, short-term, agent-specific experience.

Resumen: Early and accurate diagnosis of critical diseases is essential for timely intervention and improved patient outcomes. Boruta algorithm and LASSO regression jointly identified HDL, HGB, BASO, NLR, and SIRI as candidate features; NLR was subsequently removed during backward stepwise regression, yielding a final Logistic Regression model comprising HDL, HGB, BASO, and SIRI. Among the eight machine learning models, Random Forest achieved the highest validation set AUC (0.897). DeLong test showed no statistically significant differences in AUC among models on the validation set (P > 0.05). Considering model robustness, Logistic Regression was ultimately selected as the final model. This model achieved an AUC of 0.896 in the training set and 0.882 in the validation set, with Brier scores of 0.101 and 0.102 in the training and validation sets, respectively. DCA analysis demonstrated that using the machine learning model yielded positive net benefit within the threshold probability range of 2%-98%. The clinical auxiliary diagnostic model constructed based on peripheral blood HDL, HGB, BASO, and SIRI demonstrates good discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability, providing an objective and reliable decision support tool for auxiliary diagnosis of AD.

Título: Diagnostic accuracy of machine-learning models for detecting pulmonary embolism in patients with pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Resumen: Pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients with pneumonia presents a major diagnostic challenge because of overlapping clinical features and the limited specificity of conventional tools. Título: Improving rare event prediction in imbalanced clinical data using cost-sensitive logistic regression.
Resumen: Rare outcomes are common in clinical research and often result in severe class imbalance. Under such conditions, traditional logistic regression tends to favor the majority class and shows limited sensitivity to clinically important rare events. Although complex machine learning methods may improve prediction, their limited interpretability can restrict clinical use. Therefore, an effective and interpretable modeling strategy for highly imbalanced clinical data remains needed. We developed a cost-sensitive logistic regression (CS-LR) model by incorporating different misclassification costs for different classification outcomes into the logistic loss function. The proposed framework was designed to prioritize rare but clinically important outcomes while retaining odds ratio interpretation. Simulation studies were conducted across four covariate scenarios, imbalance ratios from 1% to 30%, and sample sizes of 500 and 2000. CS-LR was compared with traditional logistic regression, cost-sensitive support vector machines, and AdaBoost. External validation was performed using a liver fibrosis dataset and a post-ESD bleeding dataset. Across simulated scenarios, CS-LR showed stable convergence and improved minority-class detection, particularly under small sample (N = 500) and highly imbalanced (positive class ratio < 5%) settings. The advantages were most evident in recall, F1-score, and G-mean, while AUC remained broadly comparable. In the liver fibrosis validation, CS-LR consistently achieved higher recall and G-mean than traditional logistic regression across different sample sizes and positive class ratios. In the post-ESD bleeding dataset, CS-LR showed the most favorable overall performance among the compared models while retaining interpretable coefficients and odds ratio estimates. CS-LR provides an interpretable and clinically practical framework for rare event prediction in highly imbalanced medical data. It may be particularly useful in clinical prediction tasks where missed positive cases have important consequences, such as cancer screening, postoperative complication prediction, and detection of uncommon adverse clinical events.

Título: MutFormer: a multimodal deep learning framework for predicting somatic mutation hotspots from sequence and chromatin features.

Título: Emergence of polarization in networks of large language model agents.
Resumen: Rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) have empowered autonomous agents to generate social networks, communicate, and form shared and diverging opinions on political issues. Título: Artificial Intelligence as a Bridge to Gaps in Delirium Prediction, Detection, and Management.
Resumen: Delirium affects up to one-third of hospitalized older adults and is associated with adverse outcomes. We review how artificial intelligence (AI) could bridge these gaps and distinguish model development and validation, real-world clinical implementation, and emerging concepts in delirium care. Responsible AI adoption requires a clearly defined intended use, external validation, action pathways, equitable performance, privacy and security, consent and transparency, clinician oversight, patient preferences, and post-deployment monitoring. AI is most defensible as an adjunct that connects evidence-based delirium care to reliable execution rather than as a replacement for clinical assessment. Prospective comparative studies should evaluate patient outcomes, resource use, and balancing measures.

While these approaches have been used separately to assess motor performance in animal models, this is the first time they have been combined within a reproducible analysis pipeline specifically designed for assessing coordinated grasping movements following traumatic brain injury. By linking behavioral performance to quantitative descriptors of movement execution and inter-segmental coordination, the proposed framework provides a more comprehensive characterization of motor impairments than outcome criteria measure alone.

Derived indices and machine-learning algorithms did not consistently improve clinically meaningful prediction; an isolated positive continuous NRI for hypothyroidism was not supported by improved AUC or IDI. Early hypothyroidism should be interpreted as a 3-month biochemical state rather than definitive ablation.

Título: A review on ultrasonic guided wave-based non-destructive testing and structural health monitoring for adhesive joints.
Resumen: Adhesively bonded joints pose a distinctive ultrasonic guided wave (UGW) inspection challenge because thin adhesive layers, dissimilar adherends, geometric transitions, and interfacial degradation produce attenuation, multimodal propagation, mode conversion, and signatures that can be difficult to distinguish from structural and environmental variability. Título: When Missing Data Speak: An Adherence-Driven Sparsity Framework for Patient-Generated Telemedicine Data.
Resumen: Telemedicine and mobile health technologies increasingly rely on patient-generated health data collected outside traditional clinical settings. These data promise continuous monitoring, personalization, and early intervention, but in practice, they are often sparse, irregular, and incomplete because data availability depends on sustained patient participation. In this viewpoint, we argue that missingness in patient-generated telemedicine data should not be treated solely as a technical data quality problem. In many contexts, it may reflect patient adherence behavior and, therefore, carry behavioral or clinical meaning. We introduce the adherence-driven sparsity framework, an interpretive and reporting framework for reasoning about missingness in these data. The framework is grounded in 4 principles: patient adherence behavior is a central determinant of data availability, missingness patterns may carry clinically meaningful information, adherence heterogeneity creates differential representation in observed data, and analytical methods should be aligned with actual data characteristics rather than assumed data ideals. The adherence-driven sparsity framework does not propose a new algorithm or validated decision rule. Instead, it provides a structured workflow for preanalysis reasoning: identifying the data generation context; distinguishing adherence-driven from system-driven gaps; characterizing missingness across 6 reporting dimensions; assessing the plausibility of missing completely at random, missing at random, and missing not at random mechanisms; and aligning analytical choices with sparsity, irregularity, heterogeneity, and available evidence. The framework is intended for telemedicine researchers, clinical data scientists, and biostatisticians working with mobile health data. This viewpoint also cautions against the uncritical transfer of machine learning methods from dense, regularly sampled domains to patient-generated telemedicine data. In this setting, methodological sophistication alone is insufficient; researchers must first understand how the data were generated, why observations are missing, and whether missingness itself may be informative. Recognizing adherence-driven sparsity can support more transparent reporting, more defensible analytical decisions, and more clinically meaningful interpretation of patient-generated data.

Título: Initial failure morphology of shallow loess containing millimeter-scale cracks: Insights from CT 3d imaging.
Resumen: Frequent shallow loess slope failures in loess regions pose significant threats to both linear infrastructure and local communities. Millimeter-scale initial cracks induced by water, temperature, and weathering are key factors controlling such loess failures. Early diagnosis and prevention remain challenging, largely because the disaster chain triggered by millimeter-scale initial cracks is not fully understood, and the early failure behavior of these cracks is poorly characterized. In this study, laboratory experiments were conducted on loess specimens containing artificial millimeter-scale initial cracks to simulate natural cracks. Uniaxial compression tests combined with CT scanning were performed on specimens with initial cracks of varying characteristics. Three-dimensional structural models of the specimens at initial failure were reconstructed using machine learning methods, and the morphology and structural characteristics of the cracks were analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively. The test results show that the cracks generated in the initial failure state mainly involve wing cracks and extension cracks from the initial crack edges as well as wing cracks extending from both sides, initial cracks of varying characteristics produce different types of secondary cracks. Compared to intact specimens, samples with shallow, 45°-inclined, or shallow-surface compound cracks reached initial failure at substantially lower axial stresses-reduced by 78%, 65%, and 81%, respectively. This reduction is attributed to the development of larger-volume failure cracks in specimens with initial cracks. The distribution, inclination, and combination of millimeter-scale initial cracks exacerbate initial failure. Specifically, deeper initial cracks promote more large-volume failure cracks; 45° inclined initial cracks generate more large-volume failure cracks than horizontal or vertical ones; and two initial cracks produce more large-volume, large-diameter failure cracks than a single crack.

ID (PMID): 42986719
Título: Interaction embedding via factorized linear models for multi-element machine learning interatomic potentials.
Resumen: Linear machine-learning interatomic potentials, such as the Ultra-Fast Force Field (UF3), deliver near-density functional theory accuracy at low computational cost. Their number of parameters, however, grows combinatorially with the number of chemical species, limiting their use on multi-element systems. We address this scaling problem with pseudo-interaction UF3 (PI-UF3), a factorized linear model in which the Z(k) real k-body potentials are expressed as linear combinations of a small number P(k) ≪ Z(k) of shared pseudo-interactions. Learned element embeddings are standard in nonlinear potentials; inside a linear model, the embedding becomes a rank constraint on the coefficient matrix of each body order, and the resulting bilinear problem is trained with alternating least squares, where each block update is one closed-form linear solve. We benchmark PI-UF3 on a five-element refractory high-entropy alloy (HEA) and a subset of MD22, training on forces, with restarts and cross-validation. On the chemically homogeneous HEA, compression acts as implicit regularization: with three-body terms included, PI-UF3's test force root-mean-squared error drops below the unfactorized UF3 baseline with 3% of the baseline's parameters on the predefined split and 7% on every cross-validation fold, and the maximally compressed model recovers a chemically meaningful ordering of homonuclear interaction strengths consistent with experimental bulk melting temperatures. On the chemically heterogeneous MD22 subset, where UF3 is not expressive enough to overfit, PI-UF3 approaches the baseline from above and reaches parity with it at about two thirds of the parameter count. Compression thus regularizes only where the unfactorized model overfits, while a parameter reduction is available in both regimes.

Título: Identifying multi-omics spatial domains via masked autoencoder and diffusion-based latent regularization with SpaMEDM.
Resumen: Spatial multi-omics data provide complementary molecular views of tissue organization. Here, we present Spatial Masked autoEncoder and Diffusion-based Model (SpaMEDM), an end-to-end graph representation learning framework that augments a dual-attention graph-integration backbone with masked reconstruction and diffusion-based latent noise-prediction regularization. Título: Patient-reported outcomes, predictive modeling, and artificial intelligence in spine surgery: current limitations and future directions.

Despite advances in surgical technique and instrumentation, outcomes remain highly variable, with up to half of patients experiencing little or no meaningful improvement. This variability has prompted growing interest in predictive models that forecast which patients are most likely to benefit from surgery. This review examines the current landscape of predictive modeling for patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in spine surgery. Transparency and external validation remain essential for clinical implementation. While PROs remain essential for understanding patient experiences and benchmarking surgical success, they often fall short as standalone predictive tools. Título: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.
Resumen: Characterizing cerebellar morphology is fundamental for accurately mapping its structure and function across individuals, yet remains challenging due to its densely foliated architecture. Although multiple automated segmentation pipelines exist, the measurement reproducibility of these tools has not been comprehensively benchmarked. We conducted a systematic assessment of reliability for cerebellar morphology estimates using four commonly used pipelines: one classic parcellation method (CERES), two deep-learning methods (ACAPULCO, DeepCERES), and one voxel-based morphometry toolbox (SUIT). Leveraging the HNU dataset, which provides MRI scans for ten timepoints per individual over a month, we evaluated the test-retest reliability for each of the four pipelines using ReX, an integrative tool for quantifying and optimizing measurement reliability and individual differences. We quantified intra- and inter-individual variability, as well as the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), for each pipeline at both global and region-of-interest levels. We used two pools of data: a common dataset of 12 subjects x 5 sessions to benchmark all the pipelines, and method-specific datasets including pools of subjects with 5 valid sessions for each pipeline to assess the generalizability of our findings. Overall, all pipelines yielded highly reliable segmentation volumes (ICC > 0.87). DeepCERES demonstrated the most consistent performance across all metrics and subject pools, while SUIT achieved the highest ICC on the common dataset but showed decreased reliability when evaluated on a larger subject pool. Importantly, our analysis highlighted substantial heterogeneity in reliability across lobules for each method. Lobule X consistently showed reduced reliability whereas lobules I-V, VI, Crus I, IX, and VIIIB were reliably estimated across all pipelines. While all pipelines demonstrated strong reliability, DeepCERES showed the most robust and consistent performance overall. Substantial lobule-specific variability and method-dependent failure rates underscore the need for reliability-aware pipeline selection to optimize cerebellar morphology estimation in research.

Título: Structured variation in daily life experience within and across individuals.
Resumen: Human experience varies across contexts and individuals. Yet, psychological studies typically seek to constrain rather than discover structured variation. Here we leverage a powerful alternative approach to examine variability in emotional experience by sampling multimodally from individuals across a variety of contexts throughout their daily life and employing unsupervised machine learning to discover reliable, person-specific, multimodal patterns of experience. Healthy adults (<i>N</i> = 97) completed 14 days of biologically triggered experience sampling. Participants wore mobile cardiac monitors for 8 hr/day and reported their current valence, arousal, primary activity (e.g., relaxing), social context (e.g., alone), and emotional experience (via free report) when prompted. Prompts were initiated whenever a sustained change in cardiac interbeat interval was detected in the absence of gross bodily movements (and twice randomly each day). From each event (10,755 total, <i>M</i> = 110.9 events/person), we extracted cardiovascular, postural, affective, and contextual features, which were submitted to integrative clustering to derive reliable patterns for each individual. Clustering identified 313 multimodal patterns (<i>M</i> = 3.2 patterns/person). Multimodal patterns varied across people in number and, to varying extents, in nature. The features that best distinguished patterns from one another also varied by person. Critically, all participants mapped many emotion labels to a single multimodal pattern and a single emotion label to many patterns (i.e., a many-to-many mapping). Simulated data sets validated our novel analytic strategy. This comprehensive approach has broad utility for discovering structured variation in emotional experience "in the wild" and provides further evidence that emotions are diverse populations of instances constructed by a perceiver in context. Título: A Roaming-like Mechanism for Hydrogen Bond Network Rearrangements in Water Clusters.
Resumen: Unraveling hydrogen bond network rearrangements governing water reactivity is central to the physical and life sciences. Water mediates roaming in other systems, but whether water itself can roam remains unresolved. By mapping the potential energy surfaces of the water dimer and trimer, which together exhaust the elementary rearrangements, we identify five candidate roaming pathways that share reactants and products with the known rearrangements but traverse a flat region near the O-H dissociation asymptote. Each roaming-like saddle point sustains a spin-polarized, broken-symmetry state with near-unity spin population on the migrating hydrogen, consistent with neutral radical character. Interpretable machine learning reaches 93.1% accuracy in buffered within-scan tests and quantifies descriptor contributions, complementing the electronic-structure characterization, although transfer to withheld scans is limited and a distance-and-cluster-size baseline performs comparably. These findings point to roaming-like H atom migration as a candidate elementary channel of hydrogen bond network rearrangement in water clusters, with implications for radical chemistry in extended networks.

Título: Applications, Technical Characteristics, and Evaluation Approaches of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Nursing: Scoping Review.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) show great potential for widespread application in the field of nursing; however, their limitations include hallucinations, insufficient domain knowledge, and delays in updating evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), by combining external knowledge retrieval with text generation, holds promise for optimizing model outputs. However, current evidence on the use of RAG in nursing remains fragmented and has not been systematically synthesized. This scoping review aims to map the applications of RAG in the nursing field, identify current research characteristics and gaps, and provide a foundational evidence base to inform future research and development of intelligent tools for nursing practice. This study adopted the Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and followed PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting standards. We systematically searched 9 databases-PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, VIP Database, Wanfang Database, and Sinomed-from inception to September 2026. Backward and forward citation searches were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Eligible publications were restricted to those in English or Chinese during study selection. Two independent reviewers completed study screening and data extraction, and descriptive synthesis was performed for all eligible records. A total of 28 studies published between 2024 and 2026 were included. The application of RAG in nursing primarily focused on 4 scenarios: patient education (n=9), nursing informatics (n=8), clinical decision support (n=7), and nursing education (n=4). The base LLMs included the GPT series, LLaMA, ChatGLM, and Doubao, among others, while the knowledge bases primarily integrated literature, clinical guidelines, institutional resources, and clinical data. Most studies relied on dense retrieval, while some incorporated hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, and reranking to achieve optimization. Generation and task-output evaluations were reported in 27 studies, whereas retrieval evaluation, safety and reliability evaluations, and implementation or outcome evaluations were less frequently reported. Only 4 studies were conducted in real-world clinical settings. Overall, RAG demonstrated potential to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-generated outputs in specific nursing tasks; however, most studies validated only in simulated environments. This review systematically maps and synthesizes the application scenarios, technical characteristics, reporting completeness, evaluation methods, and research outcomes of RAG from the perspective of nursing tasks, further refining the evidence landscape for RAG research in nursing contexts. By summarizing the selection of base LLMs, knowledge bases and retrieval processes, the key elements of technical reports, and the areas for tiered evaluation, this review provides evidence-informed considerations for the design, validation, and reporting of future RAG-based nursing AI systems. The findings may assist clinical nurses, nursing educators, and hospital IT teams in identifying application scenarios, key safety requirements, and evaluation priorities, while also highlighting the necessity of conducting prospective validation within real-world nursing workflows.

Título: Toward Machine Learning Enhancement of Accelerated Surface Hopping with Scaled Spin-Orbit Couplings.
Resumen: Surface hopping (SH) methods are typically employed to simulate ultrafast nonadiabatic processes, but long time scales often remain beyond their reach. To address this, the accelerated SH scheme mitigates this limitation by scaling the driving forces of such processes, either nonadiabatic couplings (NACs) in the case of internal conversion or spin-orbit couplings (SOCs) for intersystem crossing. However, obtaining the actual time constant requires extrapolation from several ensembles of trajectories with different scaling factors. This introduces a significant computational demand, often restricting the number of trajectories per ensemble and, therefore, reducing the statistical confidence in the resulting time constant. Finally, we showcase and discuss how ML models can enhance the reliability of an accelerated SH scheme.

Título: Effective Point Spread Function Estimation for ADF-STEM Resolution Enhancement Using an Atomically Thin 2D Reference.

Título: Learning lattice parameters from powder X-ray diffraction data using invariants.
Resumen: We present a machine learning (ML) method to determine unit-cell parameters from powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data using a novel invariant lattice representation. However, these parameters depend strongly on the unit-cell reduction or convention used. In this work, we construct an invariant representation of the reciprocal lattice that is independent of primitive-cell convention, based on the bispectrum - a descriptor built from spherical harmonic projections of lattice points. The calculation of the lattice bispectrum is differentiable, and we demonstrate how to invert it using gradient-based optimization initialized from a nearest-neighbor lookup. We additionally benchmark our approach against pre-existing XRD data to crystal structure models such as Crystalyze and assess its performance on experimental data. Beyond unit-cell representation, we anticipate this invariant lattice representation could serve more broadly as a geometry-aware target for other crystallographic ML tasks such as structure generation.

Título: SRNR: Deep learning-based MRI super-resolution using noisy high-resolution reference data.

Título: From genome to phenotype: advances, challenges and One Health perspectives in the genomic prediction of antimicrobial resistance.
Resumen: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has substantially improved the detection and surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) by enabling the rapid identification of acquired resistance genes, resistance-associated point mutations, and mobile genetic elements. However, the presence of a resistance determinant does not necessarily establish its functional contribution to the antimicrobial phenotype. This mini-review argues that a central limitation of current genotype-to-phenotype prediction is representational: multidimensional resistance architectures are frequently reduced to binary presence-absence profiles. Such representations disregard gene integrity, expression state, promoter architecture, copy number, genomic localization, regulatory topology, strain background, and within-isolate population heterogeneity. Using functionally silent determinants, pseudogenized resistance genes, inducible and dosage-dependent resistance, altered permeability and efflux, heteroresistance, and genomic-context dependence as examples, we examine how this loss of biological information can generate both false-resistant and false-susceptible predictions. We further discuss why metagenomic ARG detection cannot be directly equated with phenotypic resistance and why prediction models trained on restricted clinical populations may not generalize across species, lineages, and One Health compartments. Moving from determinant detection toward context-aware and quantitative phenotype prediction will require the selective integration of long-read sequencing, transcriptomics, copy-number analysis, population-aware sequencing, standardized phenotypic metadata, and externally validated computational models. The relevant unit of AMR prediction is therefore not the resistance gene alone, but its functional state within a specific genomic, cellular, population, and environmental context.

Título: CT-based prediction of <i>EGFR</i> mutation subtypes and <i>TP53</i> co-mutation status in lung adenocarcinoma.

The branch solely fed with CT images reached an accuracy of 55.61% and a macro-average AUC of 0.6347. This comparison proved that CT deep representations outperform traditional handcrafted imaging and semantic features, and multi-modal fusion further improves subtype stratification performance. Título: IFI-ML: a novel framework combining Fuzzy Inference and Machine Learning for Parkinson's disease classification.

Título: Computational Link Between Motivational Factors and Cognitive Deficits in Depression.
Resumen: Cognitive deficits are a common symptom of depression and contribute significantly to the disabling effects of the disorder. Experimentally, they are observed as increased reaction times, increased error rates, and deficient performance adaptation after making errors or receiving adverse feedback, in multiple cognitive paradigms. In the current study we aimed to address the cause of these cognitive deficits from a theoretical perspective. We constructed computational models of optimal resource allocation in two cognitive tasks - Delayed Match to Sample (DMS), and Eriksen Flanker (EF). The models explicitly link performance feedback values and beliefs about task controllability with measures of cognitive performance including accuracy, reaction times, and post-error improvement in accuracy (PIA). In the DMS task, altered control belief and lower valuation of correct performance accounted for decreased accuracy and decreased PIA. Increased valuation of adverse feedback, on the other hand, was linked to increased EF accuracy and increased ERN signal magnitude. Furthermore, in the EF task, different combinations of depression-related motivational factors led to different patterns of cognitive performance, which could offer a basis for stratification. Our study offers a novel perspective on how cognitive deficits in depression can be viewed as consequences of altered motivational factors. The developed models provide an explicit computational and algorithmic bridge between the commonly observed cognitive deficits (increased reaction times, decreased performance accuracy, worse post-error adaptation) and factors such as learned helplessness and anhedonic valuation. Título: A systematic review of DoS and DDoS attack detection in cloud environments: evolutionary trends and the emerging role of meta-learning for cross-domain adaptability.
Resumen: Denial of Service (DoS) and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks continue to be one of the most persistent and rapidly evolving threats to current network infrastructures as they are becoming more sophisticated and increasingly disrupting the availability, reliability and security of cloud-based systems, Software-Defined Networks (SDNs), Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems and next generation communication environments. Malnutrition was assessed using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria at 6 months post-surgery. Core predictors for 6-month malnutrition were screened by taking the intersection of Lasso regression and the Boruta algorithm. Ten machine learning models were constructed and systematically compared, with the optimal model interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). LCGM identified three distinct weight change trajectories: persistent weight loss (28.3%), gradual recovery (38.5%), and rapid recovery (33.2%). Multinomial logistic regression (reference category: persistent weight loss group) showed that age > 65 years and ASA III-IV were associated with lower odds of gradual recovery, whereas colon cancer (right or left) was associated with higher odds. For rapid recovery, female, age > 65 years, ASA III-IV, and adjuvant chemotherapy were associated with lower odds, whereas colon cancer (right or left) was associated with higher odds. The overall incidence of GLIM-defined malnutrition at 6 months was 33.2%. Among the ten machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the best comprehensive performance, with an AUC of 0.836 (95% CI: 0.779-0.894). Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across a 9-91% threshold range. SHAP analysis revealed that lower preoperative BMI, receipt of adjuvant chemotherapy, older age, and rectal tumor location were associated with increased malnutrition risk. This study revealed three distinct postoperative weight loss trajectories in CRC patients. The developed XGBoost model, incorporating four readily available clinical variables, demonstrated favorable predictive performance and clinical utility for early identification of patients at high risk of long-term malnutrition, pending further external validation.

ID (PMID): 42984488
Título: Characterization of local linearity in deep learning CT denoising networks.
Resumen: Deep learning algorithms for image processing have been proposed for a wide range of applications. In particular, deep learning CT denoising has demonstrated superior ability to reduce noise compared to conventional methods. However, the nonlinear nature of these algorithms makes it difficult to inspect and visualize how the model accomplishes the denoising task. We propose a local linearization approach to characterize and analyze the behavior of deep learning algorithms. Example analysis was performed for a classic denoising architecture with convolutional neural network and ReLU activation functions, and was extended to GELU activation and a transformer-based architecture. We defined strictly local linear regions as the input space over which the activation patterns of all ReLU activation functions are the same. The extent of these regions was investigated by perturbing clinically relevant features of a lung lesion. We further defined approximately local linear regions as the input space where Jacobians are similar and linear approximation results in small error. We developed an algorithm to partition input space over a range of lesion and background features into approximately local linear regions, and separately quantified the contribution of the noise realization and anatomical background to this approximation error. The behavior of networks trained with different levels of denoising, as well as alternative architectures, was compared. The extent of strictly local linear regions was found to be very small. Perturbations on the scale of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow><msup><mn>10</mn> <mrow><mo>-</mo> <mn>8</mn></mrow> </msup> <msup><mtext>mm</mtext> <mrow><mo>-</mo> <mn>1</mn></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> were enough to push the network to a neighboring strictly local linear region. However, the Jacobians over a large number of strictly local linear regions were found to be highly similar, which suggests that the network behaves approximately as a piecewise linear system. The partitioning algorithm identified a small number of approximately local linear regions within input spaces characterized by clinically relevant features; this number was similar for the GELU variant but increased for networks trained with more aggressive noise reduction and for a transformer-based architecture, while Jacobians transferred across anatomical backgrounds also increased approximation error. The local linearity analysis framework can be a useful tool for elucidating the behavior of neural networks that are traditionally considered as "black-boxes." Preliminary results suggest that the framework can be applied to other differentiable architectures, subject to empirical validation, to characterize these highly nonlinear, data-dependent algorithms over input spaces of interest.

Título: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn-Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes.
Resumen: The Jahn-Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn-N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn-N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

Título: A New Paradigm for Computational Chemistry.
Resumen: Computational chemistry has become an indispensable tool for generating data and insights, pervading all branches of experimental chemistry. Its most central concept is the potential energy hypersurface, which is key to all chemistry and materials science, as it assigns an energy to a molecular structure, the necessary ingredient for reaction mechanism elucidation and reaction rate calculation. Density functional theory (DFT) has been the most important method in practice for obtaining such energies, which is reflected in the use of high-performance computing hardware. Very recently, this roadblock has been overcome by so-called foundation machine learning interatomic potentials, which are poised to completely change the way we do computational chemistry, likely prompting us to abandon DFT as the prime method of choice for this purpose in less than a decade.
