Título: Artificial intelligence-enabled interventions for smoking cessation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in digital smoking-cessation tools, but whether AI-enabled personalisation improves abstinence, and whether any benefit reflects the AI component rather than digital support more broadly, remain uncertain. To systematically review and meta-analyse randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of AI-enabled smoking-cessation interventions using an explicit operational framework that distinguished learning, inference and substantive language-understanding components from conventional fixed-rule automation. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 7 August 2026 without language, date, publication-status or study-design filters; Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform were searched, and backward and forward citation searching was undertaken, on 21 October 2026. Eligible studies were RCTs in adults who smoked combustible cigarettes in which an AI-enabled component materially generated, selected, personalised, adapted, predicted, recommended or timed cessation support. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2; disagreements were resolved by a third reviewer. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, separately for abstinence at the longest follow-up of at least six months (primary) and at approximately three months (secondary). Exploratory sensitivity analyses were restricted to biochemically verified abstinence, and further analyses examined missing-data assumptions, completeness of AI reporting and results available only in trial registries. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Fourteen RCTs involving 101,331 randomised participants were included, eight of which contributed to meta-analysis. AI functions comprised message recommender systems (five trials), conversational agents (three trials), wearable-sensor smoking-detection models (three trials), lapse-risk prediction models applied to ecological momentary assessments (two trials) and one app described as AI-enabled without technical detail. Pooled abstinence at six months or longer was RR 1.33 (95 % CI 0.82-2.15; I-squared = 67.6 %; four trials, 2,694 participants), and at approximately three months RR 1.36 (95 % CI 0.63-2.93; I-squared = 58.4 %; four trials, 715 participants). Exploratory analyses restricted to biochemically verified abstinence yielded RR 1.53 (95 % CI 1.07-2.19; three trials, 1,207 participants) at six months or longer and RR 2.03 (95 % CI 1.03-4.03; three trials, 366 participants) at approximately three months; these analyses changed the composition of the evidence set by excluding the largest null trials and should not be interpreted as confirmatory. Adding two completed trials whose results were available only in a trial registry moved the six-month estimate towards the null (RR 1.20, 95 % CI 0.91-1.59). In an exploratory comparison by comparator architecture, point estimates more consistently favoured AI-enabled packages versus usual or minimal care than versus active non-AI digital comparators, where results were inconsistent; however, comparator type was confounded with other trial characteristics. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. No included trial randomised a generative large language model intervention. Randomised evidence for AI-enabled smoking cessation remains sparse, heterogeneous and imprecise. AI-containing packages may improve abstinence when added to usual or minimal care, but current trials do not establish a consistent incremental benefit of AI over well-designed non-AI digital support. Larger trials with biochemically verified long-term endpoints, matched comparators that isolate the algorithmic contribution, and transparent AI-specific reporting are needed before superiority of AI-enabled cessation support can be inferred.

Título: A temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation for lightweight network intrusion detection.

Título: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn-Triazolate MOFs.
Resumen: Flexible metal-organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Título: Artificial Intelligence in Dietary Management and Nutritional Interventions: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence, Applications, and Translational Challenges.
Resumen: This narrative review examines the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in nutrition and dietetics, focusing on AI-assisted dietary assessment, precision nutrition, generative AI for dietary counselling, and the ethical, regulatory, and implementation challenges affecting clinical translation. A critical narrative synthesis of evidence on AI applications in nutrition and dietetics was undertaken, covering convolutional neural network (CNN)-based food image recognition and portion estimation, machine learning (ML) models for predicting postprandial glycaemic response (PPGR), and large language model (LLM)-based chatbots for dietary counselling, meal planning, and behaviour change. Furthermore, we developed a ML-informed PBPK module and a high-throughput ADMET-PBPK screening module. In the ML-informed module, ML-predicted compound-specific parameters were integrated into a GastroPlus® rat PBPK model. For 9 intravenously administered compounds, the predicted systemic exposures fell within a two-fold error range of observed data, with a 66.7% accuracy for elimination half-life. Título: Heteroscedastic nearest shrunken centroid classification: methods and applications to high-dimensional data.
Resumen: Despite of recent advances in machine learning methods with huge training data, classification of high-dimensional, low-sample-size (HDLSS) data remains challenging because limited sample sizes increase the risk of overfitting and hinder reliable parameter estimation. The nearest shrunken centroid classifier, also known as Prediction Analysis of Microarrays (PAM), combines centroid-based discrimination with feature selection through thresholding. However, its homoscedasticity assumption may limit classification performance when feature variances differ across classes, as commonly observed in gene expression data. The results show that accounting for heteroscedasticity substantially improves classification accuracy, particularly with hard and order thresholding, while maintaining competitive feature sparsity. These findings highlight the importance of modeling variance heterogeneity in high-dimensional classification and provide practical tools for improved cancer subtype prediction.

Título: Crystallographic fragment screening in cancer and antiviral drug discovery: from electron density to translational outcomes.
Resumen: Crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) provides an experimental starting point for small-molecule discovery by defining a fragment's binding site, pose and routes for chemical elaboration. By establishing a structural hypothesis before major medicinal-chemistry investment, CFS reduces early uncertainty and the risk of pursuing a binding mode inferred from activity or modeling but not supported by experimental structural evidence. This review examines how CFS advances fragments into lead series, preclinical candidates and clinical molecules. CFS is most powerful when it provides an experimentally grounded binding hypothesis early in discovery. It converts weak binding into actionable geometry, reveals ligandable pockets and supplies credible design starting points. Computational and machine-learning methods can extend this information by exploring chemical space, ranking fragment elaborations and supporting multiparameter prioritization, but they do not replace experimental determination of binding modes or functional validation. Título: Train-test splits matter more for evaluation than for performance.
Resumen: In machine learning for QSAR/QSPR, the choice of train-test splitting algorithm alters both a model's realized performance and the accuracy with which that performance is estimated from the held-out test set. For every measure the differences in estimation bias between splitters greatly exceed the differences in benchmark performance (for Spearman <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math> , a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>≈</mo></math> 0.20 bias gap versus a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>≈</mo></math> 0.02 benchmark gap), and the two criteria are inversely ranked (rank correlation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>≈</mo></math> -0.70 to -0.83). Cluster-shuffle splitting provides near-zero estimation bias while maintaining competitive external performance, making it the recommended default for offline model evaluation, where calibration is the primary concern. Because no splitter separates on model-selection quality, it is a sound default for model selection as well. Practitioners who wish to explicitly optimize model selection may use KS-type splitting to identify the best model configuration, then re-split with cluster-shuffle to obtain a calibrated performance estimate.Scientific contribution We provide the first head-to-head comparison of fifteen train-test splitting algorithms from four method families on a common drug-discovery regression benchmark, showing that their effect on the credibility of internal performance estimates is roughly an order of magnitude larger than their effect on realized model performance. We further show that this optimism is general across all eleven evaluation measures, give it a geometric explanation in terms of train-test distributional distance, and separate the splitting problem into two tasks, performance estimation and model selection, that have different optimal choices. On this basis we recommend cluster-shuffle splitting as a calibrated default; whereas prior work described the overoptimism of a single method family (Kennard-Stone), our comparison spans four families and all eleven measures and turns this into a concrete recommendation.

Título: Peripheral molecular signatures of major depressive disorder: a systematic review of blood-derived biomarkers for diagnosis, stratification, and treatment response.

Título: Mind the Gap: Continuous magnification sampling for pathology foundation models.
Resumen: In histopathology, pathologists examine both tissue architecture at low magnification and fine-grained morphology at high magnification. Yet, the performance of pathology foundation models across magnifications and the effect of magnification sampling during training remain poorly understood. We model magnification sampling as a multi-source domain adaptation problem and develop a simple theoretical framework that reveals systematic trade-offs between sampling strategies. We show that the widely used discrete uniform sampling of magnifications (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 mpp) leads to degradation at intermediate magnifications. Finally, we evaluate current histopathology foundation models, finding that magnification is a primary driver of performance variation across models. Our work paves the way towards future pathology foundation models that perform reliably across magnifications.

Resumen: Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium-ion batteries. Título: Breathing life into activation functions: the SWIn framework for sustained nonlinearity.
Resumen: Activation functions serve as the primary mechanism for introducing nonlinearity into deep learning models, playing an indispensable role in both model training and inference. By incorporating nonlinear transformations, they significantly enhance the representational capacity of neural networks, thereby improving overall model performance, particularly for complex tasks - such as Computer Vision (CV) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, most mainstream activation functions suffer from a common limitation: they tend to degenerate into linear-like behaviors when inputs assume extremely large or small values, consequently impairing their ability to model complex, nonlinear relationships across all non-saturated input domains. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel Sinusoidal Wave Integration (SWIn) framework. The core innovation lies in superimposing adjusted sinusoidal wave onto the activation function, which ensures that the composite function preserves the original monotonicity and global trend of the base activation function while guaranteeing persistent nonlinear characteristics within all non-plateau regions of the continuous base activation functions. We conducted extensive evaluations comparing standard activation functions with their SWIn-enhanced counterparts on image classification (CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K), machine translation (WMT14 DE-EN, CS-EN, RU-EN) tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the SWIn framework yields significant performance improvements for continuous activation functions such as SiLU, Mish, and GELU. This is attributed to the enriched function representation and improved gradient propagation introduced by the controlled oscillations. In contrast, for inherently non-smooth functions like PReLU and SELU, the SWIn transformation tends to amplify existing gradient discontinuities, resulting in marginal or no performance gains.

Título: Hybrid Ab Initio and Empirical Machine Learning Models for the Potential Energy Surface.
Resumen: We propose a methodology to generate hybrid machine learning models for the potential energy surface trained simultaneously on data from ab initio electronic structure calculations and on thermodynamic and/or structural observables from experiment. The approach is based on the use of a loss function that includes the mean square error of observables with respect to their experimental values, in addition to the usual terms involving the mean square error of the energies and forces with respect to ab initio data. We employ a reweighting procedure that allows for the calculation of ensemble averages of observables during training for arbitrary values of the model parameters and on the fly. The method is general and can be applied to any set of static observables. We illustrate the usefulness of this approach by applying it to the generation of hybrid models for water that reproduce accurately the experimental density maximum and the radial distribution function of liquid water in molecular dynamics simulations.

Título: TIP-INN: A thermodynamics-informed machine learning framework for the mechanical behavior of rocks.
Resumen: Modeling the mechanical deformation of geological materials across relevant thermodynamic conditions and dynamic processes remains a fundamental challenge in Earth sciences. Conventional rheological models rely on isolated disciplinary approaches and hard-coded iterative solvers that struggle with strongly coupled, nonlinear constitutive laws. Inverting macroscopic laboratory data to infer subgrid microphysics is also ill-posed, producing structural nonuniqueness and models that may violate thermodynamic laws during transient loading. To address these limitations, we present TIP-INN (Thermodynamics of Irreversible Processes Informed Neural Network), a thermodynamically consistent machine learning framework grounded in the generalized standard materials (GSM) formalism. TIP-INN discovers constitutive laws directly from time-series stress-strain data by learning two strictly convex thermodynamic potentials-the Helmholtz free energy and the dual dissipation potential-architecturally guaranteeing non-negative mechanical dissipation. A continuous, differentiable neural integrator solves internal state variable evolution as an initial-value problem, enabling stable, rapid training across complex rheologies. Benchmarked against existing thermodynamics-informed networks, TIP-INN trains 10 to 30 times faster than variational baselines and reduces extrapolation error by up to two orders of magnitude. We resolve the nonuniqueness of this inverse problem through two strategies: (i) diverse loading protocols (e.g. cyclic and stress-relaxation paths) that map the full geometry of the potential state space and (ii) a multimodal loss assimilating auxiliary seismo-acoustic data. TIP-INN thus rigorously bridges continuum damage mechanics and laboratory seismology. Finally, to ensure physical interpretability, the learned potentials are distilled via sparse identification of nonlinear potentials into closed-form expressions for efficient implementation in geodynamic codes.

Picosecond recovery times indicate rapid reversible desorption but limited residence time. We address misconceptions in the field, provide recommendations for future work, and discuss gaps in the literature in relation to diagnostic implementations as well as control for prostheses or brain-computer interfaces. Overall it can be concluded that promising UQ methods are available, but that research is needed on how people and systems may interact with an uncertainty-model in a (clinical) environment.

Título: Do machine learning models really encode cross-cultural lifestyle-health differences? A leakage-free reanalysis of two university cohorts in India and Japan.
Resumen: Machine-learning (ML) studies increasingly compare feature-importance rankings between small, unevenly sized cohorts and interpret the differences as evidence of culturally specific "risk architectures." We show that such comparisons can be highly misleading without leakage-free evaluation, using a worked example from our own cross-sectional lifestyle and health data collected during June-August 2024 from two universities in India and Japan. Three problems were identified in our preliminary analysis: (1) an outcome (obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 25) that was tautologically predicted by including BMI itself as a model input; (2) model evaluation without a held-out test set; and (3) feature-importance comparisons that ignored sampling variability from an eightfold difference in cohort size. We addressed each problem using penalized logistic regression, Random Forest, and gradient-boosted trees with proper train/test splitting, held-out permutation importance, and bootstrap confidence intervals. We also ran a sensitivity analysis that repeatedly subsampled the Indian cohort down to the size of the Japanese cohort. Removing body mass index (BMI) as a predictor collapsed obesity-model discrimination from perfect (AUC = 1.00) to chance level (AUC = 0.50-0.57), confirming that the BMI-obesity association was definitional rather than empirical. Held-out predictive performance for the remaining viable outcome, elevated self-rated stress, was modest at best (AUC 0.49-0.71). Critically, in the subsampling analysis, every feature-importance value observed in the actual Japanese data fell within the range produced by sample-size noise alone. We present this analysis as a transparent, reproducible case study of specific, checkable pitfalls: label leakage, missing train/test evaluation, unadjusted small-sample comparison, and mislabeled psychometric instruments. These should be routinely screened for before ML feature importance is interpreted as evidence of population-level or cultural differences in digital health research.

Título: A machine learning framework for stage-structured predator-prey systems with fear effect: Sparse Identification, Gaussian Process Regression, and bifurcation analysis.
Resumen: This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning framework for the analysis of a stage-structured predator-prey system incorporating the fear effect, intra-specific competition among juvenile predators, and maturation delay. The three-species model, comprising prey (<i>N</i>), juvenile predators (<i>P</i> <sub>1</sub>), and mature predators (<i>P</i> <sub>2</sub>), is governed by a non-linear ordinary differential equation system in which the prey growth rate is modulated by a fear factor 1/(1+<i>kP</i> <sub>2</sub>). Additionally, the effect of maturation delay τ on system stability is examined through delay differential equation analysis with a fourth-order Runge-Kutta integrator, revealing delay-induced destabilization and transitions to limit cycle dynamics at τ ≥ 10. All numerical results are independently verified and all performance metrics are computed from actual analyses. The framework provides a rigorous, reproducible methodology for applying modern data-driven methods to stage-structured ecological models.

Solubility was transformed as log₁₀(S), and XGBoost, CatBoost, and multilayer perceptron regression were each tuned using tree-structured Parzen estimation, differential evolution, and particle swarm optimization. Evaluation used five-fold nested group cross-validation, with complete drugs held out from training and tuning. For each test drug, predictions were assessed before calibration and after 1, 3, or 5 randomly selected measurements, repeated ten times. Within the present evaluation framework, the lowest-log-MAE zero-shot configuration was XGBoost optimized by tree-structured Parzen estimation (log-MAE = 0.584; R² = -0.087; RMSE = 1.713 g/L), showing that the four descriptors were insufficient for reliable extrapolation to unseen compounds. Sparse calibration substantially improved transfer: the lowest-log-MAE one-shot result was obtained by CatBoost-particle swarm optimization (log-MAE = 0.418; R² = 0.166), whereas XGBoost-tree-structured Parzen estimation had the lowest log-MAE at three shots (log-MAE = 0.298; R² = 0.317) and at five shots (log-MAE = 0.251; R² = 0.452; RMSE = 1.223 g/L). Median absolute relative deviation decreased from 82.4% to 42.9% between zero and five shots. These results establish sparse, leakage-controlled calibration as a more defensible use case than unconditional prediction for unseen drugs, while identifying the need for richer molecular descriptors and external prospective validation. In practical terms, this few-shot strategy can reduce the experimental burden for a newly introduced drug by using a small screening set to calibrate a global model before mapping the remaining pressure-temperature domain.

A total of 28 patients achieved a testicular volume greater than 4 mL after treatment, indicating favorable reproductive outcomes. The multimodal model that integrated all information demonstrated the highest predictive performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.891-0.997), outperforming the clinical model (AUC = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.747-1.000). The combined imaging model (ultrasound + MRI) yielded an AUC of 0.759 (95% CI: 0.510-0.969). Among the top 10 SHAP-ranked features in the multimodal model, two originated from ultrasound, one from MRI, and seven from clinical variables. The multimodal model, which integrated clinical factors with radiomic features from both ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging, demonstrated favorable performance in predicting reproductive outcomes in patients with CHH after treatment.

Título: Codon optimization as a design variable in biotherapeutics.
Resumen: Codon optimization (CO) is a key design variable in biotherapeutics that is used to enhance expression of recombinant proteins, gene therapies, and vaccines. Although synonymous codon substitutions were historically considered neutral, codon choice can influence messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, translation kinetics, cotranslational folding, and immunogenicity. The results suggest that a DeepSeek-augmented lightweight BERT classifier can extract meaningful influenza-related signals from noisy Chinese social media data and produce a surveillance index that shows an approximate 1-week lead relative to official ILI reporting, with improved performance over keyword-based and TF-IDF approaches. This framework provides a proof-of-concept for cost-effective real-time influenza nowcasting using social media data.

Título: Advances and challenges in the prediction of atom transition maps.
Resumen: Understanding how complex phenotypes emerge from large-scale biochemical networks necessitates accurate representation of biochemical reactions that extend beyond mass and charge balances. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups. Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes. Título: Bridging wildfire risk science and forest management: a modular integrated framework for loss estimation and economic-environmental trade-off analysis.

The framework is deliberately flexible with respect to specific asset categories and management contexts, making it potentially transferable to other fire-prone regions with the necessary data. We discuss alignment with international and European policy instruments and outline priority directions for further application and validation. Current limitations include reliance on historical fire data, simplified treatment of burn probability, and the absence of formal uncertainty propagation into the final monetary estimates.

Título: Transductive learning via validation risk minimization for semi-supervised learning.

The model is trained and validated using naturalistic driving data collected in Norway-comprising a dataset of 311,908 observations that link vehicle measurements with weather, road surface, and lighting conditions, along with a five-month road record dataset from Narvik. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) in acceleration prediction under snowy conditions that is approximately 28.1% lower than that of the standalone ICES-IDM model, 9.2% lower than that of the TL-Net model, and 4.2% lower than that of the conventional Stacking-IDM-LSTM framework. The model exhibits excellent generalization capability across varying snow intensity levels, providing theoretical support for vehicle car-following safety warning systems in snowy environments.

ID (PMID): 42961910
Título: Where intention goes, responsibility flows: Grounding AI accountability in the machine learning paradigm.
Resumen: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and postdeployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: Trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor's responsibility by their intent's specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology's pace. Targeted reforms drawing on environmental, vaccine, and financial regulatory precedents can close these gaps without requiring new legal categories, AI speech rights, AI legal personhood, or defining AI consciousness.

Título: Automatic Time-Series Labeling via Grammatical Inference With Error-Bounded Variable-Length Motifs.
Resumen: Data labeling is a crucial step in machine learning, providing semantic annotations that give raw data context, meaning, and structure. In time series, point-level automatic labeling is particularly challenging because it must transform continuous, high-dimensional signals into discrete and interpretable representations. Most existing approaches, mainly based on discretization and motif discovery, often rely on sensitive design choices (e.g., window length, alphabet size, or exact pattern matching), which can limit robustness on noisy or heterogeneous datasets. This article proposes GI4EVM (grammatical inference (GI) with error-bounded variable-length motif discovery), a two-stage framework for automatic time-series labeling. Phase 1 performs an adaptive, error-bounded discretization controlled by a single user-facing relative error budget $\epsilon $ , producing a compact symbolic sequence while preserving local variability. Phase 2 applies noise-tolerant GI to discover recurring variable-length patterns and to group structurally similar motifs using a tolerance $\tau $ derived deterministically from $\epsilon $ . Experiments on 50datasets show that GI4EVM yields favorable fidelity/compression tradeoffs and competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art discretization and grammar-based baselines, while producing structured and interpretable symbolic representations.

Título: Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Recomposition for Robust Audio-Visual Segmentation.
Resumen: Audio-visual segmentation (AVS) plays a critical role in multimodal machine learning by effectively integrating audio and visual cues to precisely segment objects or regions within visual scenes. Ignoring these differences can result in suboptimal performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our FAVS framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on three benchmark datasets, and abundant qualitative visualizations further verify the effectiveness of the proposed FDED and SCMC modules. The project repository is available at https://github.com/happylife-pk/FAVS.

Título: Rechargeable aqueous Zn-air batteries: coupled interfacial chemistry from oxygen electrocatalysis to Zn-anode regulation.
Resumen: Rechargeable aqueous Zn-air batteries (ZABs) combine a high theoretical energy density with low material cost and intrinsic safety, yet their practical performance remains constrained by mutually coupled reactions at the air cathode, electrolyte, and Zn anode. Particular emphasis is placed on regulating not only interfacial reaction kinetics but also the form, location, and conversion pathway of Zn-containing species. We further highlight a transition from isolated component optimization toward mechanism-informed, multi-objective full-cell design under application-relevant conditions.

Título: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.

Título: Field-Driven Proton Transport in Water Revealed by Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics.
Resumen: Excess-proton transport in water arises from the coupling of proton transfer (PT), hydrogen-bond rearrangement, and solvent polarization. While equilibrium Grotthuss diffusion has been widely studied, its response under strong electric fields remains difficult to resolve because simulations must capture both chemical reactivity and induced polarization over long time scales. Here, we have developed a reactive and polarizable machine-learning interatomic potential for molecular dynamics simulations of the hydrated excess proton in water. A fine-tuned PiNet2 model provides an accurate zero-field reference for structure and diffusion, while an AD(OS)-based finite-field coupling enables non-equilibrium simulations under an applied electric field. Our simulations revealed a distinct field-response of protonated water, whose hydrogen-bond network largely preserves its structural fluctuations and mobility without a comparable dielectric-saturation signature. Furthermore, free-energy analysis shows that strong fields stabilize the hydronium species with four-fold H-bond coordination.

Class imbalance was addressed with the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Six machine learning models were developed and compared. Feature-level associations between dietary micronutrients, daily dietary intake, and food consumption and the risk of hypertension-CHD comorbidity were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Higher intakes of vitamin E, polyunsaturated fatty acids, folate, calcium, protein, and total energy were associated with lower odds of comorbidity, whereas zinc and iron intake showed positive associations. Dietary patterns rich in protein foods, poultry, seafood, and vegetables were inversely related to comorbidity, while starchy vegetables and cured meats were associated with increased risk. At the food level, bananas, coffee, cream substitutes, and tomato-based products were linked to lower risk, whereas yeast breads, margarine, cakes, and pies were linked to higher risk. Machine-learning models reinforced these findings and highlighted the cumulative influence of food choices rather than single nutrients. In adults with anxiety disorders, we identified clear and consistent dietary patterns associated with the coexistence of hypertension and coronary heart disease. By combining micronutrient intake, dietary patterns, and food-level data with interpretable machine-learning approaches, this study demonstrates that diet may contribute to cardiometabolic vulnerability in this understudied population. These findings highlight diet as a modifiable factor that could be incorporated into broader prevention efforts and support the value of routine dietary assessment in both psychiatric and general healthcare settings.

Título: Transformer-based molecular fragment prediction using SMILES and DeepSMILES representations in a fragment-based drug discovery pipeline.
Resumen: Fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) uses small molecular fragments as starting points for drug development, and machine-learning models that operate on molecular string representations are increasingly applied to fragment-related tasks. SMILES is the dominant such representation, but its paired ring closures and balanced parentheses introduce syntactic complexity that can affect model behavior. We present a controlled study of how molecular string representation influences transformer-based fragment recovery, using an FBDD-motivated label pipeline: reference fragments are derived from known drugs via RECAP fragmentation and docking-based ranking, and the model is scored on recovering them. A per-sample selection between the two representations raises mean Tanimoto to 0.43, and a deployable variant that selects on model confidence rather than the reference recovers most of this gain. Among molecules where one representation strictly wins, DeepSMILES wins more often than SMILES (27.8% vs. 16.3% of test molecules). These results show that string representation meaningfully influences transformer fragment recovery and that representation-aware selection outperforms either representation alone.

Título: χ-SOM: emergent self-organizing maps for large chemical space visualization.
Resumen: The exploration and visualization of chemical space using dimensionality reduction (DR) methods are fundamental to cheminformatics, as they enable the exploitation of the similar property principle. However, most methods, including t-SNE and UMAP, struggle to preserve valuable distance and density properties from ambient space in the latent space representation. The emergent self-organizing map (ESOM), an often-ignored extension of the self-organizing map (SOM) algorithm, demonstrates projection behavior that circumvents the disadvantages of these methods. As a suitable implementation of this algorithm for large cheminformatic datasets is not available, we present χ-SOM, the ChemInformatics (ChI)-SOM library, a high-performance framework for training emergent self-organizing maps on large molecular datasets and for interactively exploring the resulting projections. χ-SOM integrates an optimized implementation of the SOM algorithm with CPU and CUDA backends, an on-disk HDF5-based datastore with PyTorch DataLoader support for efficient parallel access to millions of fingerprints, and a graphical user interface tailored to chemical structure visualization and property overlays. We compared our implementation with t-SNE and UMAP on synthetic and chemical data benchmarks that probe density and inter‑cluster distance preservation. On the synthetic benchmarks, ESOM retained both properties where t‑SNE and UMAP did not. On the fingerprint-based equivalents, all three methods performed comparably. χ-SOM was also benchmarked against established SOM libraries across varying dataset sizes and fingerprint lengths, demonstrating competitive or superior performance. As a final proof-of-concept, we successfully trained an ESOM of the ChEMBL33 database (1.7 million compounds; 5.1 million neurons), to our knowledge the largest SOM reported to date, and show that local neighborhood relationships on the map align well with medicinal chemists' intuition of chemical similarity. χ-SOM thus provides a practical, extensible tool for large scale exploratory analysis of chemical space.

Hybrid feature-selection approaches also showed competitive performance with Ensemble learning. Hybrid LASSO + GA with Ensemble and Hybrid mRMR + PSO with Ensemble both achieved a balanced accuracy of 89.81%. SHAP analysis consistently identified physical activity as the most influential predictor, followed by dietary, socioeconomic, and contextual variables, including fruit consumption frequency, yearly income, occupation, and place of residence. Título: Comparison of parametric versus machine-learning multiple imputation in clinical trials with missing continuous outcomes.
Resumen: Flexible machine-learning (ML) models to generate imputations within the Multiple Imputation (MI) framework has recently gained traction, particularly in non-randomised observational settings. For randomised controlled trials (RCTs), it is unclear whether ML approaches to MI, in combination with Rubin's Rules, provide valid inference in terms bias, confidence interval coverage, mean squared error (MSE), Type I error and power of the treatment effect estimator. We conducted two simulation studies in RCT settings that have an incomplete continuous outcome but fully observed covariates and treatment assignment. We compared Complete Cases, standard MI (MI-norm), MI with predictive mean matching (MI-PMM) and ML-based approaches to MI, including classification and regression trees (MI-CART), Random Forests (MI-RF) and SuperLearner when outcomes are missing completely at random or missing at random conditional on treatment/covariate. The first simulation explored a cross-sectional outcome with non-linear covariate-outcome relationships in the presence/absence of covariate-treatment interactions. The second simulation explored skewed repeated measures, motivated by a trial with digital outcomes. For the cross-sectional simulation without interaction, we found that Complete Cases yielded valid inference; MI-norm performed similarly, except when there is a non-linear covariate-outcome relationship and missingness depends on the covariate. ML approaches led to smaller MSE in specific non-linear settings, but provided unreliable inference for others. MI-PMM, which is the default setting in the R package mice, led to unreliable inference under some settings. In the presence of complex treatment-covariate interactions, performing MI separately by arm, either with MI-norm, MI-RF or MI-CART, provided inference that had comparable or better properties compared to Complete Cases when the analysis model omits the interaction term. In the repeated measures setting, ML approaches to MI and MI-PMM led to bias and under- or over-coverage, particularly when missingness depended on treatment. Based on the simulation findings, Complete Cases and MI-norm are more appropriate than ML approaches to MI for making inference, especially for late phase RCTs where Type I error control is crucial. While ML approaches may provide gains in MSE for complex covariate-outcome relationships, results should be interpreted with the caveat that Rubin's Rules are not guaranteed to be valid when used with ML imputation methods, and can lead to bias in the estimated effect and/or its standard error.

Título: P4MC: A Monte Carlo Classification Method Based on Partial Variables for Postoperative Complication Prediction.
Resumen: Predicting postoperative complications is a critical task for improving patient care and optimizing resource management. We formulate the task as a binary classification problem based on two-stage clinical data: preoperative and intraoperative variables. Título: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning.

Título: Liver Viscosity Dominates Liver Stiffness in MASLD: A Multiparametric Ultrasound Study With IPTW Adjustment and Explainable Machine Learning.

Nonlinear associations were observed for aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, while triglycerides and glucose showed no significant nonlinear relationships. These findings suggest that liver stiffness reflects viscosity-related viscoelastic alterations rather than fibrosis alone. Multiparametric ultrasound, particularly the integration of viscosity and stiffness, may provide incremental value for identifying high-risk individuals, including those with lower BMI.

Título: Development and cross-tissue validation of a machine learning-based methylation profile score for the cortisol response to stress.
Resumen: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA axis) dysregulation is a risk factor for poor mental and physical health. Animal studies indicate that DNA methylation may regulate the HPA axis, although studies in humans have produced mixed results. A data-driven, machine learning approach may provide new insight. Using a novel machine learning pipeline, we developed a methylation profile score (MPS) to predict the salivary cortisol response (AUCi) to the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) from whole blood Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation 450K BeadChip data (N = 84, mean age = 34, 49% female). The MPS was associated with the cortisol response in an independent, cross-tissue cohort (N = 53, mean age = 20, 51% female), both before (β = 0.33, 95% CI [0.09, 0.54]) and after a social stressor (β = 0.3, 95% CI [0.09, 0.47]). The effect remained statistically significant after adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, and smoking, but it became non-significant at the pre-stress (but not post-stress) time point after additional adjustment for cell proportion estimates (pre: β = 0.16, 95% CI [-0.1, 0.47]; post: β = 0.26, 95% CI [0.004, 0.49]). We developed a DNA methylation-based score that was associated with the cortisol response to stress in a separate, cross-tissue cohort. The predictive signal may depend, at least in part, on differences in cell composition associated with the phenotype. The methods used in this paper can be adapted and expanded upon in future research developing and testing novel epigenetic scores for complex, stress-related phenotypes.

Título: Development and validation of a model using thoracic vertebrae data from low-dose CT scans for detecting AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis.
Resumen: Despite evidence supporting opportunistic lumbar osteoporosis screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT), a clinically deployable screening strategy is lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate a model using thoracic bone mineral density (BMD) from LDCT for opportunistic screening. This multi-center, cross-sectional study included 18,298 adults who underwent LDCT with coverage from T1 to L2 at 134 Chinese health check-up centers. Outcome was defined as "artificial intelligence quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) defined lumbar osteoporosis" based on a mean L1-L2 BMD < 80 mg/cm<sup>3</sup> by phantom-less AI-QCT system. Five machine learning models were trained on T1-T12 BMD (n = 11,065) and evaluated internally (n = 4743) and externally (n = 2490). Performance metrics included accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, Brier score, F1 score and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis was present in 1730 (9.5%) participants. Higher thoracic BMD was inversely associated with the AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis. T12 exhibited the strongest association: each 1 mg/cm<sup>3</sup> increment reduced odds by 21.9% (OR: 0.781, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.769, 0.793, P < 0.001). Logistic regression was selected as the final model. In external validation, it achieved an AUC of 0.993 (95% CI: 0.991, 0.996), AUPRC of 0.922 (95% CI: 0.887, 0.951), F1 score (0.813), sensitivity (0.975), and specificity (0.963). AI-QCT-derived thoracic BMD showed potential for identifying AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis. Integrating phantomless AI-QCT into lung cancer screening may enable large-scale opportunistic screening, but prospective validation against independent standards is required.

Título: Machine learning based on behavioral, fecal and oocyst analyses for chicken coccidiosis diagnosis: A systematic review with exploratory extension.
Resumen: In the context of large-scale and intensive poultry farming, avian coccidiosis causes substantial economic losses. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective control and prevention. However, conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopic examination and molecular assays, are constrained by limited efficiency and a heavy reliance on specialized expertise, rendering them inadequate for real-time, high-throughput diagnosis in modern farming systems. Recent advances in machine learning have demonstrated significant potential in image recognition and early disease detection, particularly for diagnosing coccidiosis based on fecal and oocyst images, positioning this technology as a promising tool for future diagnosis of avian coccidiosis. Despite considerable progress in this area, approaches that rely solely on fecal and oocyst recognition face challenges in early screening. Moreover, limitations in current datasets and models often lead to insufficient generalization under practical farming conditions. Furthermore, although monitoring behavioral and physiological abnormalities could facilitate early detection, research on this aspect remains largely unexplored for avian coccidiosis. To address these gaps, this systematic review with exploratory extension adopts a three-dimensional framework, "behavioral physiology, fecal characteristics, and oocyst morphology" to systematically summarize the current applications and challenges of machine learning in identifying avian coccidiosis, with the aim of clarifying existing research gaps and technical bottlenecks. Finally, to systematically meet the demand for early and efficient diagnosis, this review proposes a conceptual framework for an AI-based surveillance system for chicken coccidiosis that integrates multimodal data across behavioral screening, fecal validation, and oocyst-based analysis encompassing species identification, oocyst counting, sporulation-state classification and viability assessment. This framework will serve as a theoretical foundation for moving the field from laboratory research toward field applications, thereby enabling early, precise, efficient, and intelligent prevention and control of avian coccidiosis.

Título: Integrated experimental and machine learning-driven multi-objective optimization for phenol removal via silica aerogel/ZSM-5 nanocomposite: Isotherm and kinetic analysis, thermodynamic insights and pareto-based process design.
Resumen: Phenol is a highly toxic pollutant frequently detected in industrial wastewater. This study presents the first investigation of a hydrophilic silica aerogel/ZSM-5 nanocomposite for phenol adsorption, integrated with advanced machine-learning modeling and multi-objective optimization. Silica aerogel was synthesized via an ambient-pressure sol-gel route and combined with hydrothermally prepared ZSM-5. The 75:25 aerogel/ZSM-5 composite showed the highest surface area and adsorption performance after hydrophilic conversion. Batch experiments evaluated adsorbent dosage (0.1-0.5 g), initial concentration (5-50 mg L⁻¹), contact time (5-180 min), and temperature (25-55 °C). Under optimized conditions (0.3 g, 10 mg L⁻¹, 90 min, 55 °C), 96.1% removal was achieved. Equilibrium data followed the Freundlich isotherm, indicating multilayer adsorption on a heterogeneous surface, while kinetics obeyed the pseudo-second-order model. Thermodynamic parameters confirmed a spontaneous, endothermic process; the low ΔH° (30.27 kJ mol⁻¹) and activation energy (18.54 kJ mol⁻¹) indicate weak interactions between the adsorbate and adsorbent surface. Ethanol regeneration retained the highest capacity over three cycles. Four machine-learning models trained on 150 data points showed that the NSGA-II-optimized ANN and XGBoost delivered superior accuracy (test R² > 0.995). Multi-objective particle swarm optimization identified a validated Pareto-optimal solution (0.139 g, 11.44 mg L⁻¹, 180 min, 54.2 °C) yielding 90.95% removal and 4.86 mg g⁻¹ capacity. SHAP and partial-dependence analyses ranked contact time and initial concentration as the dominant variables. The integrated experimental-ML framework offers a robust pathway for designing high-performance adsorbents and optimizing phenol-removal processes under conflicting objectives.

Título: Stratifying heterogeneity in mild cognitive impairment: A multimodal subtype and stage inference approach.
Resumen: This study aims to identify distinct clinical and biological subtypes of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and their progression stages using a data-driven multimodal approach, aimed at improving the stratification and prediction of conversion to Alzheimer's disease (AD). We applied the Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) algorithm to a multimodal dataset from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) to identify distinct MCI subtypes and their progression stages on 558 patients classified as MCI amyloid-positive. Our model incorporated T1-weighted structural MRI (measuring cortical, subcortical, and hippocampal volumes), CSF biomarkers (Aβ<sub>1-42</sub> and p-TAU), APOE-ε4 status, and a comprehensive set of neuropsychological scores. We delimited four subtypes, which two exhibited higher risk for conversion to AD. The remaining two were characterized by prominent ventricular enlargement and a significant association with geriatric depression, respectively. Predictive performance was driven mainly by the class of input features: a multimodal model using individual biomarkers alone achieved the best discrimination (AUC 0.865; accuracy 0.810), and adding SuStaIn subtype and stage did not improve it. However, subtype and stage in isolation (two variables rather than sixteen) reached an AUC of 0.811 with the highest recall observed (0.867), statistically indistinguishable from the full model. Thus, applying SuStaIn to multidomain data successfully disentangles the phenotypic heterogeneity of MCI. By separating temporal disease progression (staging) from inherent trait differences (subtyping), this framework provides a more refined diagnostic tool for patient stratification and early intervention in the AD continuum.

Título: Quantifying environment-dependent global antibiotic resistance gene risk patterns and mitigation scenarios using integrated machine learning and counterfactual scenario evaluation.
Resumen: Environmental antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) pose major ecological and public health risks, yet environmentally conditioned risk patterns and mitigation potential remain poorly quantified. This study aimed to characterize global ARG risk patterns, identify associated environmental and agricultural factors, and evaluate potential mitigation scenarios using an integrated machine learning framework. Using 274,382 sample-ARG-environment records and 150 environmental and agricultural variables, quantile models characterized conditional risk index (RI) distributions and upper-tail risks, multi-model analysis assessed predictive variable importance, and DML estimated covariate-adjusted conditional associations. These model-based findings support global ARG risk characterization and management prioritization within the One Health framework, subject to empirical validation.

Título: The dynamics of large biomolecular assemblies.
Resumen: With recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy/cryo-electron tomography (cryoEM/cryoET), computational capabilities and machine learning, there has been an incredible increase in the speed of structure determination for large biomolecular assemblies. In order to connect these static descriptions with biological function, one needs reliable and accurate approaches to quantify the factors that regulate dynamics. For this, models that employ simplified energetics and/or coarse-grained representations have become indispensable tools for integrating structural insights, biochemical analyses and physical principles. Here we discuss examples where molecular simulations have provided a framework for understanding dynamics in assemblies of increasing size and complexity. We focus on three classes for which there have been notable advances in recent years: ribosomes, viral capsids and nuclear pore complexes. Each possesses unique physical attributes that have required distinct theoretical and computational strategies. Together, these studies provide a rich conceptual and technical foundation that can help shape our perspective on the machinery of the cell.

Título: Spatial multi-omics and AI for decoding tumor heterogeneity: implications for target discovery and therapy resistance.
Resumen: Tumor heterogeneity remains a major bottleneck for effective cancer therapy because many determinants of target expression, biomarker performance, and treatment resistance are spatially organized within the tumor ecosystem. Bulk molecular profiling averages these signals across cell populations, whereas dissociation-based single-cell approaches disrupt the tissue architecture that shapes cell state, signaling, and drug access. Spatial multi-omics addresses these limitations by mapping transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and epigenomic features in situ, while AI enables integration of these modalities with histology, spatial coordinates, and clinical outcomes. Current evidence suggests that graph-based and neighborhood-aware models are most useful for spatial domain detection and niche mapping, whereas multimodal and histology-based models require stronger external validation before clinical deployment. In this review, we examine how spatial multi-omics and AI are redefining tumor heterogeneity as a translational variable in oncology. We focus on target discovery, patient stratification, and resistance biology. We also discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including platform bias, FFPE compatibility, assay cost, molecular coverage, segmentation and registration errors, limited benchmarking, domain shift, and the need for independent multicenter validation.

Título: Rapid and low-cost water quality monitoring via smartphone colorimetry and rule-based inference in Ohio inland lakes.
Resumen: Water quality monitoring is essential for protecting freshwater ecosystems and drinking water supplies, yet cost and logistical constraints limit comprehensive coverage. In Ohio's inland lakes, this challenge is particularly acute, with over 78% of assessment units impaired or insufficiently characterized and only a small subset routinely monitored. Here, we develop an integrated, low-barrier framework that couples smartphone-based colorimetry, machine learning (ML), and association rule mining of historical data to deliver a screening-level assessment of Ohio's inland water quality. We compiled previously unpublished Ohio EPA records (1999-2024) from ten Ohio lakes to mine high-confidence association rules and independently collected eight rounds of field samples from 20 Ohio lakes (2024-2025) to develop smartphone-ML models for six inorganic ions (Cl⁻, NH₄⁺, PO₄³⁻, NO₃⁻, NO₂⁻, SiO₃²⁻; R² = 0.86-0.98, RMSE = 0.03-1.68 ppm). Coupling 13 directly measured indicators with the mined rules enabled rule-based inference of the likely high/low state of 40 additional parameters (rule confidence 60-98%). The assessment shows that nutrient enrichment (nitrate, phosphate, ammonium) is the dominant present-day concern across nearly all ten lakes, while trace metals (e.g., chromium, copper, lead, nickel, zinc) are inferred to be at low levels under typical conditions; site-specific concerns persist, including elevated atrazine at Caesars and Alum Creek and elevated zinc at Alum Creek and Hoover Lakes. Overall, this framework supports low-cost, high-frequency monitoring and provides a pathway that is in principle transferable to other data-limited water systems.

Título: Cost-effectiveness analysis of Mpox control policies: A hybrid rough set-machine learning approach.
Resumen: Mpox remains a major global public health challenge, with ongoing human-to-human transmission and increased severity from emerging viral clades, despite vaccine availability. We introduce a non-autonomous deterministic mathematical model to examine effective and economical Mpox policy across all 31 possible intervention combinations. The Mpox model incorporates five time-dependent interventions: vaccination, awareness, isolation, hospitalization, and booster dose vaccination, linked to transmission reduction and policy evaluation. We estimate the model parameters from Mpox outbreak data and determine the basic reproduction number. Sensitivity analysis identifies human transmission rate, vaccination rate, and vaccine failure rate as the most influential parameters affecting transmission. We establish the existence of optimal controls and derive the corresponding optimality conditions. We numerically evaluate 31 intervention policies using the forward-backwards sweep method over 90 days. Implementing all five controls yields the highest effectiveness, with an efficiency index of 99.37%, while awareness alone achieves 94.30%. The average cost-effectiveness ratio (ACER) analysis demonstrates that awareness alone is the most cost-effective policy. However, ACER only ranks policies and does not show policymakers under which budget and impact conditions a policy remains cost-effective. To address this gap, we combine rough set theory (RST) with machine learning methods. The RST identifies intervention cost as the core attribute and generates IF-THEN decision rules linking budget level and expected infections averted to cost-effectiveness class, helping policymakers select interventions under economic constraints. The hybrid RST-neural network model achieves the highest classification accuracy (approximately 93%), confirming the consistency of the extracted rules. These results provide a transparent, data-driven framework to help public health authorities develop effective Mpox prevention and control policies.

Título: Analysis of risk factors for glaucoma associated with environmental persistent pollutant exposure based on the NHANES database: Construction of a machine learning prediction model and exploratory pathway decomposition.
Resumen: Glaucoma, an irreversible blinding eye disease, may be influenced by environmental pollutant exposure. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the associations between exposure to environmental persistent pollutants and glaucoma risk, and to explore the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. A cross-sectional analysis was performed using data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), including 2272 participants. Baseline characteristics were summarized, and serum concentrations of 12 PFAS compounds and 4 heavy metals were measured. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and subgroup interaction tests were used to examine associations between exposure levels and glaucoma risk. Exploratory pathway decomposition was conducted for key exposure factors nominally associated with glaucoma. Additionally, multiple machine learning models were constructed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretability. Glaucoma was defined by self-report, which may underestimate true prevalence and cannot distinguish glaucoma subtypes. Participants with glaucoma had a higher prevalence of diabetes and hypertension, as well as higher blood lead and MPAH levels. In the primary analysis, inorganic mercury showed a nominal inverse association with glaucoma, whereas higher quartiles of MPAH and blood lead showed nominal positive associations. However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (minimum *q* = 0.128). Restricted cubic spline models indicated nonlinear dose-response relationships between some exposures and glaucoma risk. Multiple machine learning models achieved satisfactory performance in predicting glaucoma. Exploratory pathway decomposition suggested that the nominal association between MPAH and glaucoma risk might be partly mediated by pathways involving age, race/ethnicity, and blood pressure; however, these results should be interpreted with caution given the cross-sectional design and the lack of FDR-corrected significance. Nominal associations were observed between certain PFAS compounds and heavy metals and glaucoma prevalence, but none survived FDR correction. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger studies. Interpretable machine learning achieved modest discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.74) for glaucoma risk, which may be adequate for population-level signal detection but not for individual diagnostic use. These findings provide epidemiological evidence and methodological support for identifying environmental risk factors, screening susceptible populations, and guiding early prevention of glaucoma.

Título: Natural deep eutectic solvent ultrasound extraction and imprinting recognition for sustainable harvesting of flavonoid aglycones from safflower: Experimental and multi-scale simulations.
Resumen: Flavonoid aglycones derived from safflower are valuable antioxidants, however, conventional extraction and separation methods rely on large volumes of organic solvents and suffer from poor selectivity. A choline chloride-based NADES was screened as the optimal extractant under ultrasonic assistance (40 kHz, 100 W), with the extraction yield of flavonoid aglycones from safflower reaching as high as 5.37 mg/g. Machine learning (ML) was employed to optimize adsorption conditions, reducing experimental effort and cost. The NADES extract was processed through a SMIP-packed syringe-based SPE cartridge, which effectively eliminated interference from complex matrices and efficiently enriched flavonoid aglycones, followed by HPLC detection. The method achieved excellent precision (RSD = 0.318%) and maintained > 90% recovery after seven adsorption-desorption cycles. This NADES-SMIP-SPE platform offers a green, selective, and reusable route for safflower valorization and isolation of bioactive compounds from complex plant matrices. In addition, the green NADES and recyclable, highly selective SMIP can help reduce energy consumption and costs in the industrial separation of plant active ingredients, showing promising potential for scalable and industrial application.

Título: A review of aeroacoustic shape optimization of micro-UAV rotors.
Resumen: With the development of micro-unmanned aerial vehicles (micro-UAVs) in more applications, especially the urban areas, the rotor aeroacoustic noise becomes increasingly concerning. Operating mostly within low-Reynolds-number regimes (Re ≈ 104~105), micro rotors encounter complex unsteady flow phenomena like laminar separation and boundary layer transition that heavily influence both aerodynamic efficiency and noise emission. This review systematically examines the generation mechanisms and predictive methodologies of micro-UAV rotor noise, highlighting the reason behind traditional macroscopic geometric optimizations (e.g., chord, twist, and tip modifications) that frequently descend into a zero-sum game between acoustic attenuation and aerodynamic performance. Then the recent advancements in bio-inspired aeroacoustic shape optimization trying to transcend these inherent bottlenecks were summarized. The physical mechanisms underlying owl-inspired serrations, dragonfly-inspired corrugations, and flexible porous materials that otherwise effectively modulate near-wall turbulence and disrupt spanwise coherent structures were paid closely attention. Furthermore, the paradigm shift driven by Multidisciplinary Design Optimization and data-driven machine learning frameworks due to prohibitive costs of high-fidelity simulations can be circumvented during achieving true aeroacoustic-aerodynamic synergistic design were explored prior to outlining a future roadmap emphasizing the critical transition from isolated-rotor tailoring to array-level system aerodynamic interference control with an aim to provide a theoretical foundation for the development of future low-noise micro-UAV platforms.

Título: Genetic architecture of cichlid brain morphology.
Resumen: How evolutionary and developmental processes interact to determine axes of neural variation that produce behavioural diversity has been debated for many decades, with alternative hypotheses giving differential emphasis to functional coupling, which favours co-evolution, and developmental constraint, which enforces it. A critical omission is data on the genetic architecture of brain size and structure, which more closely illuminates the shared developmental dependencies between components of an integrated system. Here, we exploit ecological divergence between Astatotilapia calliptera and Aulonocara stuartgranti, two closely related cichlid species from Lake Malawi, to explore the genetic architecture of brain evolution. Using computer vision and machine learning techniques to extract volumetric data from micro-tomographic images, we first demonstrate significant divergence in brain composition between these species. Genomic and micro-tomographic imaging data from a population of hybrids generated between the two species were used to investigate genetic factors shaping this differentiation. We show that the majority of brain components are integrated phenotypically in hybrids, but genetic correlations between them are generally weaker. We further show that variation in multiple brain components is associated with variation in largely structure-specific quantitative trait loci, rather than determined by genetic factors with broad effects across the entire brain. These results suggest a genetic architecture that can facilitate modular changes in brain structure, and imply that individual components are independently evolvable.

Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used for text-based emotional support. We developed and evaluated YuanChat, a family of specialized LLMs for context-sensitive emotional support; assessed whether E-URIAL improved response quality; and compared YuanChat with base LLMs. We constructed 2 datasets from anonymized real-world counseling sessions: ECD-3 (104,897 counselor response turns) for fine-tuning and <i>D<sub>gold</sub></i> (9413 manually annotated counselor responses). The findings indicate that fine-tuning on real-world counseling data and annotating models with structured emotional support labels improved context-sensitive empathic responding in LLMs. Without updating model parameters, E-URIAL further improved empathy identification and empathic expression across multiple models. Together, these methods provide a scalable, theory-informed approach to enhancing the emotional support capabilities of LLMs.

Título: Pistachio powder authenticity assessment using supervised machine learning algorithms.
Resumen: Adulteration of premium pistachio products with cheaper legume powders poses a significant food safety and economic concern. This study developed a non-destructive detection framework using visible-shortwave near infra-red (Vis-SWNIR) hyperspectral spectroscopy (400-1000 nm) combined with three machine learning algorithms-Discriminant Analysis (DA), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)-to discriminate pure pistachio powder from powder adulterated with 25% and 50% fava bean powder. Spectral absorption analysis revealed a monotonic decrease in absorption across all wavelengths (425-990 nm) with increasing fava bean concentration, with no wavelength showing higher absorption in adulterated samples. To reduce dimensionality and collinearity, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed on the pre-processed spectra, and the first five principal components were retained as inputs for classification, explaining at least 99% of the cumulative spectral variance. Among the classifiers, DA achieved the highest accuracy (97.3%), followed by SVM (94.6%) and KNN (91.9%). All three classifiers perfectly or near-perfectly distinguished pure pistachio from adulterated samples, with errors occurring primarily between the two adulteration levels. The results demonstrate that Vis-SWNIR hyperspectral spectroscopy combined with DA or SVM provides a rapid, accurate, and non-destructive solution for detecting fava bean adulteration in pistachio powder, with potential for development into low-cost portable screening devices.

Título: Taking a bottom-up, data-driven approach to characterizing variability across early-life environments.
Resumen: Children's long-term outcomes correlate with the physical and social features of the homes, schools, and neighborhoods in which they grow up. Yet, current techniques for establishing these correlations are limited. This article (a) presents five main issues linked to the currently used approaches. For example, most research relies on questionnaires or coding brief videoed interactions, which focus on a limited set of dimensions selected by researchers ("top-down" approach). As a result, these methods are limited because they provide only a static snapshot, which often conflates conceptually diverse levels, including the physical (e.g., noise, light) and social environments (e.g., caregiver mood, responsiveness). New technologies offer alternative approaches to these issues. This article (b) highlights how continuous multifeature observations, processed using machine learning tools, can improve our description of early development and inform theorizing of the mechanisms through which environments shape outcomes. Devices worn by children and those around them provide long-form recordings, allowing researchers to track how naturalistic environments vary over time and how children respond to them in real time. This shift supports a more dynamic, bottom-up, data-driven, and potentially culturally neutral approach to characterizing environmental variability. Finally, the article (c) discusses key limitations, notably the need to ensure that machine learning methods used to analyze early environments are trained using culturally diverse data, evaluating remaining risks of bias, and practical and ethical considerations. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

Título: Online COVID-19 Misinformation and Infodemic Governance During the Peak Pandemic Period: Scoping Review of Social Media Research From 2020 to 2022.
Resumen: During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media platforms became major channels for public health communication and public sensemaking, but they also enabled the rapid circulation of rumors, false claims, conspiracy narratives, and misleading health information. Research on online COVID-19 misinformation expanded rapidly during the peak pandemic period, yet the evidence base was fragmented across public health, computing, communication, and information science. This scoping review synthesizes empirical research on online COVID-19 misinformation on social media during the peak pandemic period from February 2020 to October 2022. It examines how misinformation was conceptualized, which platforms and public health contexts were emphasized, and how computational methods shaped the evidence base for infodemic management. Its distinct contribution is an integrated comparison of conceptual definitions, thematic and platform concentration, the computational research pipeline, and the gap between detection and actionable infodemic governance. We conducted a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-informed scoping review of empirical studies indexed in PubMed and IEEE Xplore in November 2022 using COVID-19, social media platforms, and misinformation-related terms. Eligible reports were English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies published between February 2020 and October 2022 that analyzed social media data using computational, quantitative, or social media analytic methods; the language restriction applied to the publication, not to the underlying dataset. The final synthesis included 100 studies selected from 1688 records. Within the included corpus, the literature was concentrated around vaccine-related discourse, public health and social measures-related misinformation, and text-based data from X (X Corp), formerly known as Twitter. Studies commonly used misinformation detection, classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network analysis. Fewer studies examined diffusion pathways, source tracing, cross-platform movement, intervention effectiveness, or platform governance. The evidence base remains more developed for detecting and describing misinformation than for evaluating actionable responses to it. Peak-pandemic COVID-19 misinformation research produced important computational and empirical knowledge, but it remains detection-centered and unevenly connected to public health action. Future infodemiology research should link computational outputs to intervention design, risk communication, fact-checking workflows, platform moderation, multilingual and multimodal analysis, and the evaluation of infodemic governance strategies.

GRU was ranked second and outperformed LSTM on most of the metrics used in this evaluation. GARCH models remain a viable option for estimating risk measures and calibrating VaR, especially during period of stability in the financial markets.

Título: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes.

Resumen: With the deep integration of digitalization and artificial intelligence technologies into enterprise knowledge management, AI-assisted learning is reshaping the channels through which knowledge is acquired within organizations. Fourth, the spatiotemporal simulations demonstrate that, under optimal regulation, knowledge dissemination can form a stable diffusion pattern with high coverage. Título: The Current Roles of AI in Public Health Practice: Scoping Review.
Resumen: AI is a broad field encompassing various techniques, which include algorithms that learn from data to perform automated tasks without explicit human programming. Public health aims to protect and improve the health of communities and populations at the local, regional, national, and global levels, but it typically has limited resources. While AI may lead to improved efficiency or effectiveness of public health interventions, the adoption of AI interventions should be informed by evidence of effective use in practice. This review aims to summarize how AI-assisted interventions are currently used by public health professionals. We conducted a scoping review to identify the current uses of AI in public health. We searched MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), Web of Science (Core Collection), and Scopus for relevant reports published between January 1, 2020, and July 24, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened reports. Eligible reports were primary studies (experimental or observational), commentaries, and editorials that discussed how AI tools have been used in practice in public health contexts relevant to high-income countries, excluding outbreaks. Data were extracted by one reviewer and checked by a second. We screened 5400 records and 155 full texts, including 8 reports. These reports discussed a variety of uses of AI tools across public health domains: 3 reports used chatbots in different settings, 1 report used machine learning to forecast health service demand, 2 reports used AI for symptom checking, and 2 reports used AI for evidence synthesis. While assessing the effectiveness of AI tools for public health was beyond the scope of this review, and most reports did not robustly evaluate effectiveness, the evidence for the effectiveness of AI tools was nonetheless mixed. One report described a chatbot that users found helpful, while another found a specific chatbot to be ineffective, highlighting its potential to undermine trust in the organization that developed it. Another report highlighted both benefits and drawbacks of a large language model used to communicate with socially isolated individuals. The main finding of this review was that even with a comprehensive search across multiple databases, there were few reports of how AI tools are being used in practice in public health contexts. The lack of evidence from public health practice, excluding outbreaks, makes it difficult to know which uses of AI, if any, would be useful to incorporate into practice in high-income countries. In the absence of evidence, new interventions, including those using AI, should be evaluated to ensure they are effective (and cost-effective). These evaluations should be widely and accessibly disseminated to create an evidence base that other public health teams could use to inform their own decisions around AI tools.

The proposed BCFL-DAI-PUB achieves a final AUC of 0.91, improving upon the HE-based BCFL-PS-HER baseline (0.86) by 1.06×.
