Título: Robust Prediction-Reliability Assessment in Biomedical Sensing and Classification Under Data Scarcity Using Conformal Prediction and Statistical Randomization.
Resumen: Reliable assessment of prediction reliability is important in biomedical sensing and measurement applications, where machine learning models increasingly transform imaging, physiological, chemical, and molecular measurements into clinically relevant predictions. Such applications often operate under limited labeled data because sensor acquisition, experimental measurement, and expert annotation can be costly, while biological and measurement variability can further challenge model development. Under these conditions, reliability scores derived from standard inductive conformal prediction (ICP) can be sensitive to the particular division of available data into proper-training and calibration subsets. To address this issue, we propose three randomized ICP variants: bootstrapping ICP (BICP), randomized ICP (RICP), and out-of-bag ICP (OOB-ICP), to improve the informativeness and repeated-sampling stability of conformal-derived prediction-reliability scores under data scarcity. Results show that the proposed methods produce aggregate credibility scores that are informative of prediction correctness and less sensitive to randomness in training-data sampling. Empirical prediction-set coverage analyses further characterize the behavior of the aggregated conformity scores relative to nominal error levels without assuming that they retain the exact finite-sample validity of conventional conformal <i>p</i>-values. Among the evaluated methods, OOB-ICP achieved strong overall classification performance and informative, stable prediction-reliability scores, supporting statistical randomization as a practical strategy for stabilizing conformal-derived reliability assessment under limited training data in biomedical sensing and measurement applications.

Título: Frequency-Time Harmonization of Multi-Station Spectrograms for Machine Learning Applications in Solar Radio Burst Analysis.
Resumen: The collection of solar radio burst spectrograms through the spatial distribution of survey sites reveals heterogeneity and differences in frequency sampling, temporal resolution, signal intensity, and local observing conditions. Because of this heterogeneity, it is difficult to incorporate observations of diverse stations directly into a single dataset, which restricts the generalizability of machine learning models that were trained using records from isolated stations. Thus, it is well established that for reliable automated analysis of solar radio bursts, a standard representation of spectrograms is necessary. This paper proposes a framework for harmonizing heterogeneous multi-site spectrograms of solar radio bursts, which transforms them into a unified representation capable of accommodating station-specific observational configurations suitable for machine learning applications. The proposed methodology combines adaptive frequency interval selection, frequency sampling consistency checking, logarithmic intensity transformation with baseline correction, time-frequency harmonization, and explicit handling of missing frequency channels using binary validity masks. To overcome the heterogeneous nature of the observations taken from different instruments and stations, nearest-neighbor interpolation in both time and frequency domains is applied. The unified frequency grid is constructed considering the statistics of the frequency channels used in spectrometers that form the e-CALLISTO network, a space weather instrument array. Two one-dimensional convolutional autoencoders with two latent space dimensions (32 and 64) are proposed and trained on more than 17,000 spectrograms to evaluate the quality of latent representations of the harmonized data. The best performance was achieved by the autoencoder with simpler architecture and with 64-dimensional latent space, reaching root-mean-square error of 0.88dB and a mean absolute error of 0.61dB. The experimental results show that models with 64-dimensional latent space outperform their 32-dimensional counterparts, while increased architectural complexity provided no substantial improvement. The proposed methodology provides a standardized basis for constructing harmonized datasets suitable for a wide range of subsequent machine learning applications in solar radio astronomy, including automated burst detection, classification, representation learning, anomaly detection, and predictive modeling.

Unlike water-driven aggregation dominated by the hydrophobic effect, self-assembly in ILs is governed by the cooperative interplay of solvophobic interactions, electrostatic screening, hydrogen-bond networks, specific ion effects, and solvent nanostructuring. Although substantial progress has been achieved during the past decade, a unified mechanistic understanding that links IL structure to aggregate morphology and functional performance remains lacking, and the literature is fragmented across system classes that are rarely compared under matched experimental conditions. This review presents a mechanism-oriented synthesis of surfactant self-assembly in IL media. The review is organized around an explicitly defined classification of IL-amphiphile systems, distinguishing neat IL media, IL-water mixtures, surface-active ionic liquids (SAILs), ILs used as cosurfactants, and conventional surfactants dissolved in ILs, and it states the literature-search strategy and eligibility criteria used to assemble the evidence base. The fundamental driving forces responsible for aggregation are then analyzed critically, with emphasis on how solvophobic interactions, electrostatic screening, hydrogen bonding, and packing-parameter modulation jointly determine aggregate formation and structural evolution, and on the quantitative thermodynamic and structural parameters, namely the Gibbs energy, enthalpy, and entropy of micellization, the critical micelle concentration (CMC), and the aggregation number, that make these contributions comparable between systems. Representative self-assembled architectures, including micelles, reverse micelles, lyotropic liquid crystals, microemulsions, and worm-like micelles, are discussed together with the resolution limits, artifacts, and applicable concentration ranges of the characterization techniques and simulation approaches used to resolve them. Applications in nanomaterial synthesis, electrochemical energy storage, drug delivery, enhanced oil recovery, and green separation technologies are reorganized around explicit structure-property-performance relationships, and claims that currently rest on schematic or correlative evidence are identified as such. Finally, a critical roadmap is presented that addresses reproducibility, standardized reporting, viscosity and transport limitations, impurity and water sensitivity, scale-up, cost, toxicity, recyclability, and quantitative predictive design, including realistic opportunities for machine-learning-assisted modeling. By integrating recent advances from molecular mechanisms to practical applications, this review provides a unified framework for understanding surfactant self-assembly in ionic liquids and offers guidance for the rational design of next-generation soft functional materials.

Complete three-criterion timing concordance was lower after complicated recovery (28.6% vs. 94.3%; <i>p</i> < 0.001). Patient-perceived concordance correlated with the timing concordance score (Spearman ρ = 0.395; <i>p</i> < 0.001). Mean multidisciplinary appropriateness across 72 ratings was 8.50 ± 0.50. <i>Conclusions</i>: The fixed AI-generated THA information set was rated favorably by patients and clinicians, and its three prespecified timing statements corresponded closely to routine documented recovery. Both experiential and timing concordance were lower after complicated courses. These findings support clinician-reviewed AI information as an adjunct while underscoring that generalized timelines are conditional ranges, not individualized predictions.

Título: Repeated Internal Validation and Interpretation of Models Predicting Surgery Documented at a Study Institution Within 90 Days After Acute Knee Trauma: A Secondary Analysis.

Logistic regression most often ranked first for AUROC, whereas random forest most often ranked first for AUPRC and Brier score; however, paired comparisons did not identify significant differences between these two models. Título: Pathway-Masked Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Yield an Interpretable Transcriptomic Score Associated with Colorectal Cancer Progression Independently of Clinical Stage.
Resumen: Prognostic gene expression signatures in colorectal cancer are usually reported by standalone discrimination, a standard that random gene sets can meet, and are rarely tested for what they add to routine clinical variables. TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ were pooled into a single colorectal cohort (596 patients, 153 progression-free events). PathKAN places learnable univariate spline functions on a sparse gene-to-pathway topology drawn from MSigDB and BioGRID, reducing 20,681,472 dense weights to 127,985 edges, and is fitted under a Cox partial-likelihood objective. Of the 50 highest-ranked genes, 42 were differentially expressed between tumour and adjacent normal tissue. Título: Entropy Estimation: From Statistical Physics to Classification.
Resumen: Driven by the common entropy formalism in statistical physics and information theory, here we show that methods developed for the analysis of molecular configurational ensembles may be successfully used for classification. Entropy is estimated using the k-th nearest neighbor method combined with the Maximum Information Spanning Tree method to account for the mutual information between variables. This formalism is used to classify new samples using their estimated cross-entropy with the training set. The method is tested using the hand-written digits MNIST and the functional genomics CuMiDa datasets. The results obtained on these diverse datasets are comparable to those obtained by machine learning methods, or better when the number of samples is small. The methods described here have the advantage, compared to other classification methods, of directly linking variables and pairs of variables to the assigned class, a valuable feature when aiming at identifying causal relationships between features and classes (e.g., the relationship between genes and diseases).

Título: Atopic Dermatitis in the Era of Exposome and Artificial Intelligence.
Resumen: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a heterogeneous, relapsing inflammatory skin disease in which epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, microbial imbalance, genetics, and the environment interact continuously over time. Although a substantial body of literature has linked AD with air pollution, weather, allergens, stress, infections, sleep disturbance, skin care practices and microbial perturbation, most studies have assessed single exposures in isolation. This reductionist approach only partially reflects the real-world biology of AD, where patients experience dynamic combinations of external and internal exposures whose effects are non-linear, cumulative and modified by age, phenotype, treatment and susceptibility. The exposome paradigm offers a broader conceptual lens by considering the totality of exposures over the life course. However, exposomic research in AD is methodologically challenging because the data are multimodal, high-dimensional, time-dependent, and often incomplete. Artificial intelligence (AI) can help address this complexity by integrating heterogeneous data layers, modelling temporal dependencies, discovering latent patterns, and generating individualized predictions. This narrative review examines current evidence and proposes a theoretical framework that integrates AI and the exposome in AD. We define the principal domains of the AD exposome, describe a multilevel analytical architecture spanning environmental, clinical, behavioural, microbiome, and multi-omics data. We distinguish applications evaluated in AD studies from exploratory analyses and proposed objectives: prediction of annual flare burden remains exploratory, whereas exposome-informed short-term flare alerts are proposed applications. Although selected AI applications have been evaluated in AD, the added predictive value of exposure data and the clinical utility of a fully integrated exposome-AI system remain to be established. We also outline key methodological and translational priorities, including exposure assessment, temporality, treatment-confounding, interpretability, fairness, data governance, and external validation. The proposed framework offers a structured basis for future research, with clinical translation dependent on prospective validation and evidence of benefit to patient care.

We integrated multi-omics and computational analyses to identify candidate targets that overlap between predicted TCS-related molecular targets and PCa-related transcriptomic alterations. Cross-database target mapping, differential expression, and network analyses were combined with machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell transcriptomic profiling. Single-cell analysis further showed cell-type-specific expression of candidate genes in tumor-enriched epithelial populations. These findings provide an integrative framework for generating mechanistic hypotheses on how TCS-related molecular targets may be associated with PCa biology.

Título: Evaluation of Two Combined Analytical Approaches to Assess the Impact of Rare Variants on Severe COVID-19.
Resumen: Severe COVID-19 displays substantial inter-individual variability that cannot be fully explained by common genetic variants, suggesting a contribution of rare functional variation. We performed whole-genome sequencing in 191 Italian patients (96 moderate, 95 severe) to investigate rare coding variants (minor allele frequency <1% and <5%) via complementary network-based and machine learning approaches. Classical single-variant and burden tests did not identify significant associations after multiple testing correction. However, Network-based Heterogeneity Clustering (NHC) revealed that multiple gene clusters were enriched in severe cases, particularly those involving RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription, RNA metabolism, and vesicle-mediated transport pathways. Gene-level rare variant analysis via the variable threshold method identified five genes significantly associated with severe disease (FDR < 0.05), namely, <i>EIF4G3</i>, <i>GTF2F2</i>, <i>LY96</i>, <i>COX6A1</i>, and <i>STK11</i>, which are involved in transcriptional and translational regulation, innate immune signaling, and mitochondrial function. Unsupervised biclustering significantly stratified patients by severity, and a decision tree model highlighted the burden of <i>DOCK10</i> variants as a key discriminator between phenotypes. Convergence between the network-based and machine learning results further supported the robustness of the identified signals. Overall, our integrative framework underscores the contribution of rare variants to COVID-19 severity and highlights the coordinated perturbation of interconnected molecular pathways as a determinant of clinical outcome.

Título: DeepAVPred: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating RECM-DWT and BiGRU for Accurate Antiviral Peptide Prediction.
Resumen: Viral infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge. Antiviral peptides (AVPs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their high specificity, favorable safety profiles, and broad-spectrum antiviral activity. However, experimental AVP identification is time-consuming and costly, while existing computational predictors often have limitations in predictive accuracy and feature representation. Here, we propose DeepAVPred, a deep learning-based framework for AVP identification. DeepAVPred integrates complementary sequence descriptors to capture physicochemical properties and pairwise residue interactions. We present a novel feature representation, the Residue Energy Content Matrix augmented with a Discrete Wavelet Transform (RECM-DWT). RECM-DWT characterizes multi-scale patterns in residue-energy information and complements conventional sequence descriptors by providing wavelet-derived features across multiple resolution levels. The integrated features are then modeled using an attention-based Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) network to learn contextual dependencies and informative sequence patterns. On the AVP<sub>train</sub> dataset, DeepAVPred achieved strong performance in 10-fold cross-validation, with an accuracy of 0.990, a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.980, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993. On the independent test dataset, AVP<sub>test</sub>, DeepAVPred achieved an accuracy of 0.942, an MCC of 0.886, and an AUC of 0.949. These results demonstrate the predictive performance of DeepAVPred and support its potential as a computational framework for prioritizing candidate antiviral peptides for further experimental validation.

Título: The Role of <i>SOD1</i> and Oxidative Stress in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: An Overview.
Resumen: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressing neurodegenerative disorder that selectively affects motor neurons. The median survival time after diagnosis is 2 to 5 years. Oxidative stress (OS), driven mainly by reactive oxygen species (ROS), plays a central role in motor neuron (MN) degeneration. In this narrative review, we analyse the pathogenic role of SOD1 variants and their contribution to OS in ALS. SOD1 mutations alter the Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase enzyme, thereby promoting oxidative damage and triggering neuroinflammatory cascades via the MAPK, NF-κB and Nrf2/ARE signalling pathways. We also discuss emerging proteomic and machine-learning biomarkers, as well as the current therapeutic landscape. Riluzole and edaravone are approved treatments, while AMX0035 was approved in 2022 but withdrawn in 2024. Masitinib and EPI-589 remain investigational. In the realm of genetic therapies, the antisense oligonucleotide tofersen received accelerated FDA approval in 2023 for SOD1-ALS, primarily due to its ability to reduce plasma neurofilament light chain levels. However, the clinical benefit remains modest. RNA interference has reached human trials, while CRISPR/Cas9 remains in the preclinical stage. Both approaches have shown promising results in experimental models. Further research into ALS pathogenesis is needed to develop treatments that integrate antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gene-editing strategies.

Título: Prediction of Lindane-Induced Breast Cancer Toxicity Through Multi-Target Network Analysis and Mechanistic Investigation.
Resumen: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets associated with Lindane-induced molecular alterations in breast cancer and elucidate its toxicological mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. GO and KEGG analyses were performed to explore biological functions, while machine learning models and SHAP analysis were applied to screen potential biomarkers. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to evaluate the interaction between Lindane and key proteins. Twenty-eight overlapping targets were identified and mainly enriched in lipid metabolism, sphingolipid signaling, and p53-related pathways. NR3C2 may serve as a potential regulatory molecule involved in cellular responses to Lindane exposure in breast cancer, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying environmental Lindane exposure and breast cancer-related toxicity.

Título: Urinary Metabolomics in Bladder Cancer: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Translation Implications.
Resumen: Bladder cancer (BC) diagnosis and surveillance currently rely largely on invasive cystoscopy, making urine an attractive non-invasive biofluid for discovering metabolic biomarkers, given its direct contact with the bladder urothelium. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of the literature on urinary metabolomic profiling in BC, summarising metabolites and metabolite panels associated with the disease, their relevant metabolic pathways, and diagnostic performance. A search was conducted in PubMed, complemented by records from reference lists of relevant reviews. After screening, 30 original studies comparing urinary metabolomic profiles between BC patients and cancer-free controls were included, encompassing diverse analytical platforms and statistical approaches. A wide range of urinary metabolites were reported to be altered between BC patients and controls, of which 52 were recurrently identified in at least two independent studies. Increased levels of taurine, valine, lactate, adenosine monophosphate and adipate were among the most consistent metabolic alterations, whereas the levels of citrate, glycerol, creatinine, and several dicarboxylic acids and acylcarnitines were consistently decreased. Other metabolites, such as hippurate, tyrosine, and histidine, showed variable trends in their levels. These alterations may reflect metabolic processes associated with tumour growth, energy reprogramming, lipid metabolism, and oxidative stress adaptation. Most studies also proposed multi-metabolite panels combining metabolites to discriminate BC patients from controls, achieving sensitivity and specificity up to 100% and AUC up to 0.983, while fewer studies explored panels for tumour stage and grade discrimination, with more modest performance. Overall, urinary metabolomics reveals a broad, biologically coherent set of metabolic alterations associated with BC, but methodological heterogeneity and limited independent validation still hinder clinical translation. Larger, harmonised, prospectively validated studies integrating multi-omics and machine learning are needed to establish robust urinary biomarkers for BC.

Título: Clinical Scores and Machine Learning at Matched Variable Domains in Acute Appendicitis: Performance of Recommended Rule-Out Thresholds in a CT-Verified Cohort.

Thresholds should be re-derived and verified in the population in which imaging is to be deferred. The model analysis was exploratory and was not externally validated.

Título: Prognosis Prediction in Adult Intensive Care-A Critical Analysis.
Resumen: <b>Background:</b> Prognosis prediction in adult intensive care units (ICUs) guides clinical decision-making, realistic goal-setting with families, and resource allocation, but is challenged by the marked heterogeneity of critically ill patients in multi-speciality wards. <b>Methods:</b> This narrative review critically analyses commonly used prognostic scoring systems by clinical application timeline. <b>Results:</b> Admission prognostic models, including the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE II/III/IV), Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS II/SAPS 3) and Mortality Probability Model (MPM), estimate in-hospital mortality from acute physiological derangement and comorbidity; the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) adds prognostic value. Prognostic estimates should inform multidisciplinary evaluation and shared decision-making, rather than independently determine treatment intensity or withdrawal.

Título: Virtual Surgery and CFD in Rhinology: A Scoping Review.
Resumen: <b>Background:</b> Nasal obstruction is one of the most common reasons for which patients present to an otolaryngologist, yet the outcomes of operations aimed at improving nasal patency remain inconsistent, and the correlation between conventional objective measures and perceived patency is uncertain. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) allows nasal airflow to be simulated from craniofacial computed tomography; combined with software that reconstructs and modifies sinonasal anatomy, it permits a planned procedure to be reproduced digitally and its functional impact predicted before any tissue is removed. This scoping review maps how CFD-based virtual surgery has been used in rhinology, how the simulations were validated, and which clinical outcomes were reported. <b>Methods:</b> Following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, PubMed and Scopus were searched in October 2025 for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Inclusion criteria restricted papers to English-language studies of virtual surgery tools involving CFD in humans or human-derived models. Pediatric (<18 years), sleep apnea, and orthognathic studies were excluded, as were studies of other parts of the respiratory tract and environmental or toxicological work. Duplicates were removed in Mendeley, and two authors independently screened titles and abstracts. Data were charted by two authors. The review was not registered. <b>Results:</b> Forty-one studies were included, covering the nasal septum, the inferior and middle turbinates, the ostiomeatal complex, the maxillary and sphenoid sinuses, septal perforations, and postoperative synechiae. Virtual results were compared with actual postoperative anatomy, airflow, or symptoms in only 7 of the 41 studies and agreed with them in most respects. In several small studies, a greater extent of resection did not improve airflow further and reduced mucosal heat and moisture exchange, wall shear stress, and regional cooling, but the extent that appeared best depended on the anatomy and the outcome considered. These parameters have been proposed as better correlates of the subjective sense of patency than resistance alone; this has rarely been tested in patients. The most recent work applies machine learning and adjoint optimization as research tools for planning support. <b>Conclusions:</b> CFD-based virtual surgery is a promising tool for planning the extent of rhinological procedures. Its routine use will require standardized methods, prospective validation, and correlation with patient-reported outcomes (NOSE, SNOT-22); larger studies with such endpoints are still lacking.

Resumen: <b>Background/Objectives:</b> Automated phonocardiogram (PCG) analysis is a candidate tool for scaling up cardiac auscultation, but the internal accuracy reported in many studies may not reflect performance when a model is applied to recordings from a different source. The approaches spanned classical machine learning (spport vector machine, random forest), standard deep models (1D-CNN, 2D-CNN, ResNet1D, CNN-BiLSTM, and two hybrid networks), image-based backbones (EfficientNet-B0, MaxViT), and a proposed four-branch fusion model (PCG-MambaConformer) combining raw-signal, mel-spectrogram, and continuous wavelet transform (CWT) representations. Threshold-transfer and precision-recall analyses, adversarial domain adaptation, an uncertainty-quantification benchmark, a disease-specific transfer analysis, multi-architecture ensembling, a branch ablation, a label-grouping sensitivity analysis, a reciprocal (reverse-direction) transfer experiment and explainability analyses (feature-space t-SNE with class-separability metrics and Grad-CAM saliency) were also performed. Performance was summarized using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with sensitivity and specificity. <b>Results:</b> Internal AUROC was similar across deep models (approximately 0.82-0.90) and largely independent of parameter count, whereas classical models were lower (0.67-0.69). On the heterogeneous external dataset, the highest AUROC was 0.738 and none of the nine deep models reached a sensitivity and a specificity both of at least 0.80 at any of the three thresholds examined. On the homogeneous external dataset, PCG-MambaConformer reached an AUROC of 0.985 (sensitivity 0.718, specificity 0.995 at the 0.5 threshold), whereas other models tended to collapse toward either always-normal or always-abnormal predictions. Adversarial adaptation improved performance on the homogeneous target but reduced it on the heterogeneous target. On the heterogeneous target, even an oracle threshold raised balanced accuracy by only 0.022 on average, whereas on the homogeneous target a source-derived threshold produced a balanced operating point only for PCG-MambaConformer (sensitivity 0.863, specificity 0.980). Models trained in the reverse direction (PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2016 to CirCor) also transferred poorly (AUROC 0.612-0.677). Branch ablation showed that three of the four single-branch configurations collapsed to a one-class operating point and that the full fusion model achieved the highest AUROC, and a feature-space analysis showed that successful transfer was associated with the class-separability of the target domain (silhouette score highest for the homogeneous dataset) rather than with the proximity of dataset centroids. <b>Conclusions:</b> In the two external datasets evaluated, successful cross-dataset PCG transfer was associated with the homogeneity of the target domain; because these datasets also differed in population, recording protocol, disease spectrum, class distribution and signal quality, homogeneity cannot be isolated as the sole determinant of transferability. Internal accuracy was a weak indicator of external behavior, model complexity alone did not close the heterogeneous transfer gap, and balanced cross-dataset performance on a homogeneous target was associated with multi-representation fusion. The near-perfect result on the homogeneous target should be read as technical cross-dataset transfer under favorable, highly curated conditions rather than as clinical external validation, whereas the heterogeneous result is the more realistic indication of current limitations. These findings support multi-metric external evaluation on independent data, followed by prospective clinical validation, before any clinical use is considered.

As a potential mathematical model, the scope for further improvement includes that the performance of the current framework depends significantly on the preprocessing of the data (i.e., the right size of signal that has substantial information on damage modes of both short and long type with least noise, elimination of the amplitude parameter by choosing manual amplitude bin). Here, sustainability refers mainly to climate impact, expressed as global warming potential per year of service life. We propose a design loop with two decision gates. Unlike existing service-life or life cycle frameworks, it checks reliability and climate impact together, and it gives credit only to methods with measured inputs in mortar or concrete. It connects binder choice, added protection, probabilistic service-life prediction, and life cycle metrics, and it updates itself with monitoring data. The review closes with a ranked list of research gaps and practical steps for researchers, designers, and asset owners.

Título: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning.
Resumen: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to Gács and Körner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

ID (PMID): 42940827
Título: Quantifying Dependence Between Random Vectors: A New Index with Applications.
Resumen: This article proposes a new index for quantifying the degree of dependence between random vectors with the same dimension. The index takes values in [0, 1] and equals zero if and only if the random vectors are sub-independent. Unlike mere uncorrelatedness, sub-independence implies a stronger form of dependence while remaining strictly weaker than full independence. The proposed index is constructed via characteristic functions and admits a simplified representation in terms of moments. We establish its theoretical properties and derive a computationally efficient formula for the corresponding empirical measure. Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic behavior and finite-sample performance of the estimator and demonstrate its practical utility through applications in machine learning, actuarial science, and renewal theory. A numerical comparison with Pearson correlation and squared distance correlation is also given under several dependence structures. We also give a real-data application to international stock and foreign exchange returns.

Resumen: Compression-based dissimilarities such as the normalized compression distance are widely used, but direct exponentiation need not produce a positive semidefinite kernel. In the resulting RKHS geometry, the MMD compares compressibility profiles, the HSIC is product-kernel MMD from the joint law to the product of its marginals, and KSDTP,k(Q)=MMDk(QTP,Q) for a target-stationary Markov kernel TP. Expected algorithmic mutual information is connected to the HSIC only through explicit source-description, mutual-information, support, and kernel conditions. Ideal AIT objects, computable feature surrogates, and finite-sample errors are separated explicitly. Reproducible synthetic experiments examine the identities, landmark approximation, and selected testing alternatives at the computable and empirical layers. They provide no evidence about ideal AIT quantities or general superiority over baselines. An algebraic example also shows that a characteristic finite-support kernel can give a constant permutation statistic: identification alone does not guarantee test power.

Repeated conversions of one network gave equations scoring -0.76 to 0.96, whereas an elementary edge basis makes the printed equation identical to the network up to rounding. With every lot serving as the blank, detection limits for samples resembling the calibration population were 8.9-21.6% adulterant, and blends at 4-12% were not quantified. The KAN provides an exact, inspectable screening calibration rather than higher accuracy.

Título: Predictors of Favourable Response to Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in Patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Narrative Review.
Resumen: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is an effective treatment for selected patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, but 30-40% of recipients do not respond. This narrative review summarizes predictors of a favourable response to CRT. Typical left bundle branch block (LBBB) and a QRS duration ≥ 150 ms remain the best-established baseline predictors. Sex, etiology, age and comorbidities affect how much benefit is gained rather than acting as yes/no predictors (the benefit is greater in women, partly because of their smaller heart size) and should not by themselves exclude an otherwise eligible patient. Combining mechanical dyssynchrony with septal viability on cardiac magnetic resonance appears to improve selection further. Procedure-related factors, including left ventricular lead position and a high percentage of biventricular pacing, are critical for success. A multimodal approach that combines clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic and imaging data, supported in the future by machine learning, appears most promising.

Título: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on <i>Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins</i>.
Resumen: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. However, compared with excitatory tools, optogenetic silencing tools have developed more slowly and remain limited by insufficient photosensitivity, poor membrane localization, ion-homeostasis perturbation, and phototoxicity. Because these properties are largely constrained by the structural and functional features of the parent microbial proteins, the discovery and in-depth characterization of natural rhodopsins remain essential for tool innovation. This narrative review focuses on ion-pumping archaeorhodopsins, with emphasis on the genus <i>Halorubrum</i> and on <i>He</i>AR, and describes how the literature was selected. We first summarize the functional classification, structural basis, photocycle, and ion-pumping mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins. We then discuss the diversity of <i>Halorubrum</i> archaeorhodopsins and the structural-functional features of <i>He</i>AR, a recently characterized archaeorhodopsin from a halophilic archaeon isolated from Ejinoor Salt Lake in Inner Mongolia, China. <i>He</i>AR absorbs at 550 nm (dark-adapted) and 560 nm (light-adapted), essentially the same maximum as AR3 (559 nm). Its Schiff-base counterion Asp-95 has a pKa of 3.5 ± 0.1, about one unit higher than BR Asp-85 (≈2.6) and AR3 Asp-95 (2.5 ± 0.2), but matched by AR4 Asp-85 (3.6); thus, this is a property that <i>He</i>AR shares with its closest relative rather than one that sets it apart. Its photocycle (≈100 ms) is prolonged-roughly ten times longer than the overall cycle of BR (11 ms), of AR4 (≈10 ms) and of the O-decay of AR3 (τ ≈ 14 ms)-while its M intermediate forms and decays faster than in BR; relative to AR3 and AR4, however, the M decay is slower (3.3 ms against ≈390 µs and 0.55/3 ms) and the overall cycle is longer. These are established in vitro properties of the heterologously expressed protein, and because a pump moves a fixed, small number of charges per photocycle, low-light performance remains a hypothesis to be tested rather than a demonstrated advantage. In this review "red-shifted" is used in one sense only: <i>He</i>AR's 550-560 nm window lies ≈80-90 nm to the red of excitatory channelrhodopsins (≈470 nm); relative to BR it is blue-shifted by ≈18 nm, and relative to AR3 the two absorption maxima coincide. We further review the evolution of optogenetic silencing tools, from inward chloride pumps and outward proton pumps to light-gated anion channels and potassium channels, and discuss structure-guided rational design strategies, including structure prediction, molecular dynamics simulation, directed evolution, and machine learning-assisted engineering. Finally, we outline current challenges and future opportunities in phototoxicity, deep-tissue light delivery, clinical translation and the exploitation of halophilic archaeal resources, and we specify which experiments are required before <i>He</i>AR can be judged as a silencing tool. Clinically validated optogenetics is kept separate throughout from speculative applications of newly characterized archaeorhodopsins. This review aims to provide a comparative framework linking the structural-functional properties of natural rhodopsins to the rational design of next-generation optogenetic silencing tools.

Título: BRAIN-TIME: Testing Whether Prospective Recovery Position Modifies the Benefit of the Same Intervention in Addiction.
Resumen: Addiction neuroscience has advanced the identification of vulnerability and mechanisms involving reward learning, salience, cognitive control, interoception, cue reactivity, and stress regulation. Yet a key translational question remains unresolved: when does an evolving post-perturbation brain-behavior trajectory become relevant to treatment benefit? Prediction models can estimate future craving, lapse, or deterioration, and adaptive-intervention systems can deliver support using prespecified tailoring variables, but neither dynamic treatment regimes, just-in-time adaptive interventions, nor causal machine learning specifies what evidence a temporal quantity must satisfy before it may serve as the tailoring variable itself. This Perspective asks whether prospective recovery position modifies the benefit of the same intervention, and introduces BRAIN-TIME as a falsifiable episode-level architecture for answering that question. It begins with a defined cue, stress, affective, or sleep-related perturbation, follows one prespecified recovery domain relative to an individualized reference, and separates retrospectively adjudicated sustained re-entry from a prospective estimate of incomplete recovery computed only from information available at the decision point, with no use of later observations. Its decisive Stage 1 test is treatment-effect moderation: at a common locked landmark, the benefit of the same intervention and dose must vary across prospectively estimated recovery positions by a prespecified, practically meaningful amount. A minimal proof of concept combines a standardized low-intensity challenge, repeated craving or autonomic sampling, an independent outward-function criterion, negative controls, and randomized fixed-content intervention. No original data are reported, and every quantity specified here is a proposed construct, estimand, or falsification criterion rather than an observed result. BRAIN-TIME is therefore neither a relapse classifier nor an autonomous treatment rule. Its central claim is deliberately narrow: temporal recovery information becomes relevant to treatment timing only when prospective episode position is shown to modify the benefit of the same intervention.

Randomised evidence came from 12 small trials, 10 of them craniomaxillofacial, which evaluated the delivered implant rather than the planning method; virtual surgical planning was used in 11 of them. When restricting to the four studies that measure deviation from the virtual plan, with smaller meaning better, patient-specific implants deviated less from the plan (standardised mean difference -1.21, 95% CI -1.69 to -0.74). Revision or removal was less frequent (3 of 135 against 25 of 149; risk ratio 0.28, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.72); operative time, complications and infection gave intervals compatible with a difference either way. No randomised trial was at low risk of bias, and 69 of 75 comparative studies were at serious risk, mostly of unadjusted confounding, so all estimates are of very low certainty. Among technical studies read in full, independent validation material was used in fewer than half, and files were shared in about one in fourteen. Of 36 artificial intelligence studies, 4 were evaluated on independent data, 2 were used for a real patient, none were clinically comparative, and 8 of 17 cranial studies relied on AutoImplant family benchmarks. The design pipeline is unequally validated: planning has clinical evidence concentrated in one region, computational methods are widely applied but rarely validated independently or shared, and artificial intelligence has benchmark evidence for cranial defect completion and little else. Outcome studies of patient-specific implants should be read as evidence about whole pipelines, and future studies should evaluate the components.

Current evidence demonstrates that AI can generate technically promising predictions, but it does not yet establish consistent clinical or economic benefit. Discrimination alone is insufficient to demonstrate clinical usefulness. Título: Hidden Signals in Serum Protein Electrophoresis: Artificial Intelligence from Laboratory Pattern Recognition to Clinical Validation.
Resumen: Serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) remains a central laboratory method for the detection and characterization of monoclonal gammopathies and other dysproteinemic patterns. Despite substantial analytical automation, interpretation still relies largely on graphical representation and expert visual assessment, making low-amplitude or borderline abnormalities particularly challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) approaches, has increasingly been applied to SPE, with high performance reported for automated recognition of established abnormalities, particularly M-proteins, i.e., monoclonal immunoglobulins or immunoglobulin fragments produced by clonal plasma cells. However, most models have been developed against predefined diagnostic targets and evaluated using expert interpretation, immunofixation, or immunotyping as reference standards. Improved recognition of known abnormalities should therefore not be equated with discovery of additional clinically meaningful information. Modern electrophoretic platforms generate machine-readable numerical signals that may preserve features not explicitly considered during routine graphical interpretation. This creates the possibility of extending AI-assisted SPE from conventional pattern recognition toward detection of low-amplitude, distributed, or sub-visual signal characteristics. Evidence is strongest for automated M-protein recognition, including low-amplitude abnormalities, whereas non-canonical systemic patterns, longitudinal signal analysis, and AI-assisted decomposition of therapeutic monoclonal antibody interference remain exploratory. This critical review addresses this translational gap by evaluating AI applications according to the nature of detected information, strength of supporting evidence, and proximity to clinical implementation. We propose a translational framework addressing four complementary domains: analytical validity, biological validity, clinical validity, and clinical utility. The evidence required in each domain depends on the intended claim and clinical use.

Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Título: Distilling First-Principles Accuracy into Compact Machine Learning Potentials for Condensed-Phase Chemistry.

Título: RACE: A Modular and Interpretable Radial-Angular Correlation Descriptor for Atomistic Machine Learning.

Chemical identity is incorporated through interchangeable scalar or multichannel weighting functions rather than through a mandatory set of element-pair channels. RACE is consequently presented as a simple and manipulable structural representation that complements, rather than universally replaces, systematic density-correlation descriptors.

Two-dimensional (2D) material-supported single-atom catalysts (SACs) address this challenge through atomically defined coordination environments that enable precise tuning of the critical *COOH and *CO adsorption energies, which strongly influence CO<sub>2</sub> activation and product selectivity, while the competing adsorption of *H governs HER suppression. This review examines the convergence of 2D-SAC design and machine learning (ML) for CO<sub>2</sub>RR catalyst discovery. We first outline the mechanistic foundations of the CO<sub>2</sub>RR together with comparative insights from the HER and OER and then discuss the structural and electronic principles governing single-atom stabilisation on nitrogen-rich carbon, transition metal dichalcogenide, and MXene supports. Recent catalytic advances are assessed with the CO<sub>2</sub>RR as the primary focus, including proximity-engineered systems that promote C-C coupling and multicarbon product formation. Finally, emerging ML frameworks are critically reviewed, covering electronic, geometric, and spectroscopic descriptor design, data source strategies, and high-throughput screening and inverse-design workflows. <i>Operando</i> ML integration has revealed the dynamic evolution of active sites under reaction conditions, highlighting the need to incorporate electrochemical-environment and reaction-condition-dependent structural information into future training datasets. Key priorities identified for the field are large-scale CO<sub>2</sub>RR-specific SAC database construction, product- and condition-specific descriptor development, and closure of the prediction-synthesis-validation feedback loop.

Título: An element-resolved coupled cluster atomization energy data set ranging across the periodic table.
Resumen: We introduce the total atomization energy periodic table compass (TAE-PTComp), a collection of 67 atomization energy data sets, each specifically designed to probe various chemical environments of one particular element of the periodic table. In total, this set comprises 2097 carefully curated closed-shell, single-reference molecules containing up to 50 atoms, with an average of 31 structures per element-specific subset. The chemical space covered ranges from conventional covalent and coordination compounds to noncovalently bound clusters, extracted fragments of periodic crystalline structures, and artificial "mindless" molecules. Additionally, we include a balanced amount of charged species with charges of ±1. For each molecule, as well as its constituent atoms (and ions), we provide high-level coupled cluster reference energies. We therefore envision this benchmark as a resource for parameter fitting, validation, and testing of approximate density functional theory methods, semi-empirical models, and machine-learning interatomic potentials. An initial assessment of TAE-PTComp for a representative set of density functional approximations, together with the semi-empirical g-xTB method and the machine-learned Universal Model for Atoms (UMA), shows that this benchmark can efficiently differentiate between broadly robust methods, such as the range-separated hybrid ωB97M-V, and approaches that exhibit localized, element-specific failures, such as the hybrid M06-2X functional.

ID (PMID): 42936578
Título: Hybrid quantum-classical machine learning potential with variational quantum circuits.
Resumen: Machine learning potentials (MLPs) based on equivariant message-passing neural networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracy for atomistic simulation, yet integration of variational quantum circuit (VQC) readouts into such frameworks remains unexplored for condensed-matter systems. Here we employ and characterize a hybrid quantum-classical MLP (HQC-MLP) by coupling an <i>E</i>(3)-equivariant message-passing network with VQC readout layers for predicting DFT energies and forces of liquid silicon (64 atoms, periodic cell, 2000-3000 K). We benchmark five VQC Ansatz architectures differing in entangling gate type (controlled-Z (CZ) <i>vs.</i> controlled-X (CX)) and circuit structure against a classical baseline. All HQC-MLP variants reproduce PBE-DFT energies with test-set RMSEs of ∼3.5 meV per atom when evaluated using exact expectation values, while entangled circuits exhibit faster training convergence in epoch count, although not in wall-clock time. CZ-based entangling gates achieve lower validation losses than their CX-based counterparts. This trend is consistent with two factors: the phase-preserving nature of CZ gates for amplitude-encoded features and their reduced effective entangling depth, since the final CZ layer commutes with the Pauli-Z measurement operators. Both molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations accurately reproduce the DFT radial distribution function at 2000 K, despite the models being trained exclusively on 3000 K configurations; molecular dynamics also reproduces the Si-Si-Si bond-angle distribution. Finite-shot analysis further shows that achieving an RMSE of approximately 2 meV per atom relative to shot-noise-free expectation values requires about 5 × 10<sup>4</sup> shots per circuit execution. This corresponds to approximately 2.56 × 10<sup>8</sup> shots for a single configuration force evaluation, making direct force calculations prohibitively expensive on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware and thereby motivating the proposed Monte Carlo protocol. Finally, the cutoff-radius sensitivity analysis reveals that HQC-MLP exhibits truncation behavior comparable to that of the classical MLP.

SHAP analysis identified BSA, standardized blood flow, and gender as the most influential predictors. Machine learning models, particularly SVM, the ensemble model, and NGBoost, can provide accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware predictions of Kt/V using non-invasive, readily available parameters. The development of a local standalone executable application further facilitates clinical translation, enabling pre-dialysis prediction and real-time prescription adjustment. Prospective validation in diverse populations is warranted to confirm generalizability.

Título: Prediction Models Versus Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) for Advanced Fibrosis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Verification-Audited Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Resumen: Researchers increasingly propose data-driven prediction models for non-invasive fibrosis assessment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, strong predictive performance alone does not show whether a model performs better than Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4), a simple and widely used fibrosis score based on routinely available clinical data. This review evaluated whether prediction models provide greater diagnostic discrimination than FIB-4 when both are assessed in the same patients for advanced fibrosis (≥F3). PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar were searched for studies evaluating prediction models and conventional non-invasive fibrosis tests in adults with MASLD, MASH, NAFLD, or NASH. Eligible head-to-head comparisons required the model and FIB-4 to be evaluated in the same cohort for the same ≥F3 endpoint with verifiable test-specific areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs). We used automation-based screening and quantitative validation, followed by full-text verification, targeted evidence recovery, and final cohort-level adjudication. Separate-cohort biopsy-validation evidence formed the primary analysis, while internal holdout evidence was included secondarily. The effect measure was the within-study difference in AUROC (ΔAUROC), pooled using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Of 23,420 deduplicated records, 2,892 reports were assessed for eligibility, and 44 potential same-cohort comparisons were identified. Final verification produced three eligible head-to-head studies. The primary separate-cohort evidence comprised two studies, with study-level ΔAUROCs of 0.053 and 0.140, respectively. The pooled primary ΔAUROC was 0.086 (95% Hartung-Knapp CI -0.448 to 0.621). Adding the internal holdout study, which reported a ΔAUROC of 0.165, increased the pooled estimate to 0.126 (95% CI -0.023 to 0.276). All three point estimates were positive, but both pooled CIs included no difference. A 500-record reference assessment of automated exclusions identified no false negatives, corresponding to a negative predictive value of 100.0% (95% CI 99.2%-100.0%). The available head-to-head evidence is too sparse and imprecise to establish that prediction models outperform FIB-4. Moreover, all included evaluations were conducted by the original model-development teams rather than by independent third-party investigators. The findings should therefore be considered preliminary and do not support replacing FIB-4. Future studies should prioritise third-party multicentre validation, calibration, clinically actionable thresholds, and direct assessment of net clinical benefit.

Título: Digital biomarkers derived from wearable and portable devices in prodromal Parkinson's disease and at-risk populations: a scoping review.
Resumen: Prodromal Parkinson's disease (pPD) represents a pre-diagnostic stage during which subtle and heterogeneous changes may be difficult to detect through conventional clinical assessments. Digital biomarkers derived from wearable or portable devices offer opportunities for objective and longitudinal assessment. This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on digital biomarkers in individuals with formally defined pPD or populations at increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), focusing on measurement approaches, analytical methods, types of evidence, and methodological gaps. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ACM Digital Library was conducted from database inception to August 31, 2026. Studies investigating digital biomarkers derived from wearable or portable devices in individuals with formally defined pPD or populations at increased risk of PD were included. Study characteristics, digital biomarker domains, measurement and analytical approaches, and types of evidence were synthesized descriptively. Forty-three studies were included, primarily involving individuals with iRBD or other high-risk states associated with <i>α</i>-synucleinopathies, population-based or broader prodromal-risk cohorts, genetic high-risk populations, and individuals with idiopathic hyposmia/anosmia. Digital biomarkers encompassed motor, speech, sleep/activity, and multidomain features, with motor-related measures, particularly gait and mobility, being the most extensively investigated. Machine-learning approaches were applied across several domains, whereas genuinely multidomain studies remained limited. Most studies provided cross-sectional evidence of group differences or discriminative performance, whereas prospective evidence regarding future PD diagnosis or phenoconversion was less extensive. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in measurement protocols, analytical approaches, and validation strategies. Wearable- and portable-device-derived digital biomarkers represent promising candidate tools for characterizing and monitoring individuals across the prodromal PD risk spectrum. However, evidence supporting clinical prediction of phenoconversion remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and a lack of sufficient longitudinal and external validation. Future research should prioritize standardized assessment, large, multicenter longitudinal cohorts, independent external validation, and integration with established clinical and biological markers.

The results showed that： ① On an interannual scale， the WUE of the entire region and all subregions had been showing an increasing trend. Except for in subregions A and D， biological factors and human activity intensity were the dominant driving factors of the interannual variations of WUE. The impact of climatic factors on the interannual variations of WUE exhibited significant regional differences. Precipitation （<i>P</i>） showed a negative effect in subregions A and D， while it mainly exerted a positive effect in other subregions. For temperature， it demonstrated a positive effect in most subregions except in subregion A1. ② Spatially， WUE exhibited a pattern of "low in the northwest and high in the southeast，" primarily driven by the combined effects of biological and climatic factors. Leaf area index （LAI） and kernel normalized difference vegetation index （kNDVI） had the most significant impacts in subregions A， C， and D， while solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence （SIF） and LAI were dominant in subregion B2. Threshold analysis revealed that WUE was inhibited when LAI &gt; 1 or <i>P</i> &lt; 300 mm and promoted when kNDVI was between 0.15 and 0.25 or elevation &gt; 2 000 m. Interaction effects indicated that WUE was promoted when kNDVI was between 0.10 and 0.30 combined with solar radiation （SR） &lt; 2 900 MJ·m<sup>-2</sup> but inhibited when SR &gt; 2 900 MJ·m<sup>-2</sup> combined with LAI &lt; 0.60. The research findings provide a scientific basis for understanding the carbon-water cycling coupling mechanism and optimizing regional ecological restoration strategies in the Loess Plateau.

Título: [Omics and integrative methods for assessing biological age.].
Resumen: Biological age, reflecting the extent of age-related changes in the organism at the molecular and systemic levels, serves as a more informative predictor of the risk of age-associated pathology and mortality compared to chronological age. This review systematizes current omics and integrative approaches to biological age assessment, analyzing their prognostic potential and limitations. Three generations of epigenetic clocks (Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE), transcriptomic markers of cellular senescence (p16INK4a, mTOR, S100A9), as well as proteomic and metabolomic biomarkers, including indicators of inflammation (IL-6, TNF-α, С-RP), glycan clocks (GlycanAge), clinical-biochemical panels, and oxidative stress markers, are examined. Key limitations hindering the clinical implementation of these methods are discussed. Further progress in this field requires large-scale longitudinal studies, unification of methodological approaches, and validation of multi-omics models in independent cohorts to facilitate their integration into personalized preventive medicine algorithms.

Título: [Screening and in vivo validation of key targets for triclosan-associated intervertebral disc degeneration].

Título: [Diagnostic agreement of large language models with clinical reference diagnoses of mental disorders and associated factors].

Diagnostic information completeness showed a positive trend toward association with Top-1 agreement, but the association did not reach statistical significance (<i>P</i>=0.075). Seven cases with frequent Top-1 disagreement were identified. Exploratory retrospective review suggested that the diagnostic disagreements may involve the temporal relationship between mood and psychotic symptoms, integration of cross-sectional presentation with longitudinal course, and missing or ambiguous key information required for differential diagnosis. At the level of the 3 diagnostic categories of schizophrenia spectrum disorders, bipolar disorders, and depressive disorders, general-purpose LLMs showed high agreement with clinical reference diagnoses and relatively stable outputs across repeated runs. Greater diagnostic complexity was associated with lower Top-1 agreement. Cases with frequent Top-1 disagreement may serve as exploratory signals for manual review but should not be directly interpreted as indicating model diagnostic errors or clinical misdiagnosis. The practical value of such signals requires further validation through independent expert assessment and external samples.

Título: Genetic architecture of low-temperature germinability in rice revealed by integrated maps of SNPs and structural variation.
Resumen: Low-temperature germinability (LTG) limits rice direct seeding, yet its genetic architecture and regulatory roles of structural variations (SVs) remain largely unclear. We evaluated LTG in 403 rice accessions at four temperatures (13°C, 15°C, 18°C, 21°C). Integrating SNP/SV-GWAS, RNA-seq, gene editing, population genetics, and machine learning, we dissected the genetic basis of LTG and built a genomic selection (GS) prediction model. The panel showed extensive LTG variation, which was negatively correlated with origin latitude. SV- and SNP-based GWAS for LTG detected 119 and 127 QTLs, respectively, with 25 loci overlapping between the two datasets. Population genetic analysis identified 29 inter-subspecies (Xian-Geng) and 37 intra-Xian divergent regions for LTG, implying shared selected regions across and within subspecies under low temperature. Using SNP and SV data, we built corresponding genomic selection (GS) models with the machine learning-based MFGP method, achieving high prediction accuracy across all temperatures. All cross-temperature prediction correlations exceeded 0.55, with optimal performance at 18°C. Our results clarify rice LTG genetic architecture and suggest potential regulatory roles for SVs that merit further investigation, providing candidate genes, favorable haplotypes, and a GS model for LTG genetic improvement in direct seeding rice.

Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the conceptual, methodological, and ethical foundations of educational evaluation and assessment. The classical assessment paradigm, grounded in the assumption that learner performance reflects individual and independently produced cognition, is increasingly inadequate in educational environments in which AI authors tasks, scores responses, generates feedback, converses with learners, and accompanies students as a partner in the learning processes. We argue that AI's integration into the learning-assessment ecosystem requires a fundamental reconceptualisation of assessment theory, validity, and learner agency under conditions of hybrid intelligence. We conclude by outlining a future research agenda for evaluation and assessment in AI-mediated educational environments.

Título: Artificial intelligence early-warning systems for sepsis: From risk scores to bedside action.
Resumen: BackgroundSepsis remains a leading cause of preventable mortality in critical care. This method is scalable and accessible, requires no coding expertise or commercial software, and offers a blueprint for generating truly quantitative histopathology data to veterinary pathologists and others engaged in MASH research.

Among these, statistically significant improvements were observed for ARIMA, CNN, and Decision Tree (P < 0.05). This study provides evidence that ARIMA model demonstrates excellent predictive performance for forecasting hepatitis B incidence trends in China. Additionally, BSI could serve as an effective supplement to traditional surveillance systems by providing real-time contemporaneous information that enhances situational awareness. Título: Revisiting the interaction between word frequency and predictability in natural reading: Large-scale evidence based on large language models.
Resumen: Word predictability-that is, the predictability of a word in a sentence based on the preceding context-reliably influences processing of that word. We leveraged an ensemble of large language models (LLMs) to derive predictability estimates across six natural reading eye-tracking datasets in English and Chinese. Título: [Interpretable dynamic adjacency graph attention network for epileptic seizure detection].
Resumen: To address the insufficient robustness of existing deep learning methods in modeling cross-channel dependencies in epileptic electroencephalogram (EEG) signals and the limited traceability of their decision-making rationale, this paper proposes an interpretable dynamic adjacency graph attention network (DA-GAT). The proposed model first extracts EEG features through a convolutional module, and subsequently introduces a dynamic graph learning module and a multi-head graph attention module with prior-gated fusion to achieve automatic epileptic EEG detection. Experimental results on three public datasets, namely the Children's Hospital Boston-Massachusetts Institute of Technology (CHB-MIT), Helsinki, and Siena datasets, demonstrate that DA-GAT outperforms the selected comparison methods in terms of accuracy, F1-score, and other evaluation metrics. Furthermore, by combining gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) with dynamic adjacency matrix visualization, DA-GAT provides interpretable evidence to support clinical review. In summary, this study provides a new methodological approach to cross-channel dependency modeling and interpretability analysis of epileptic EEG signals, and provides a reference for improving the reliability and clinical applicability of deep learning models for automatic epilepsy detection.

Título: [Construction of predictive models for type 2 diabetic retinopathy based on the principle of differentiation of syndrome elements].
Resumen: To construct a prediction model for occurrence of type 2 diabetic retinopathy (T2DR) by combining the principle of differentiation of syndrome elements with machine learning (ML). Cross-sectional data were collected from 273 patients with T2DR and 376 T2DM patients for comparison of routine test results and parameters of syndrome elements in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) identify the candidate TCM indicators for predicting T2DR occurrence. LASSO regression analysis was used to select the syndrome features with the highest predictive value. Six ML algorithms (LR, ANN, XGBoost, RF, SVM and KNN) were used to construct the prediction models, followed by internal validation of the model and evaluation of the importance of each predictive feature. LASSO analysis identified the liver, lung, and yang excess syndrome elements, among others, as the most predictive features for T2DR occurrence. Among the 6 ML models, LR and KNN models showed good discrimination power. The LR model yielded highly reliable and robust probability output in global calibration, and the KNN model had good performance for probability predictions. Both the LR and KNN models provided positive net clinical benefits over a wide range of threshold probabilities, but the net benefit curve of the LR model was above that of the KNN model in the whole range, especially in the validation set. The ML-based prediction models (especially the ML model) combining the features of syndrome elements effectively use the advantage of TCM for predicting disease and allow comprehensive prediction of T2DR in T2DM patients to assist clinical decision-making for early interventions.

ID (PMID): 42934094
Título: [Association between depressive symptoms and renal hyperfiltration in middle-aged and older adults].
Resumen: To investigate the associations of depressive symptoms and depressive episodes with renal hyperfiltration (RHF) in middle-aged and older adults. This cross-sectional study was conducted among 9469 middle-aged and older participants from Lanzhou site of the REACTION study. After excluding individuals with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL·min<sup>-1</sup>·1.73 m<sup>-2</sup>, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g, malignant tumors, incomplete depression questionnaire data, or antidepressant use, the participants were assessed for depressive symptoms using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and categorized in <5, 5-9, and ≥10 groups. Depressive episode status was also evaluated. RHF was defined as residuals above the 95th percentile from a regression model of log-transformed eGFR adjusted for age, sex, height, weight, hypertension, and diabetes. The associations of depressive status with RHF and the dose-response relationship between PHQ-9 total score and RHF risk were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analysis, respectively. Random forest, SHAP, and Boruta were used for exploratory analyses. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant nonlinear association between PHQ-9 total score and RHF risk. After multivariable adjustment, a significantly increased RHF risk was found in the PHQ-9 ≥10 group (OR=1.854, 95% <i>CI</i>: 1.074-3.201; <i>P</i>=0.027) but not in the PHQ-9 5-9 and PHQ-9 0-4 groups. When PHQ-9 was dichotomized as <10 and ≥10, a PHQ-9 score ≥10 was associated with a higher risk of RHF (OR=1.864, 95% <i>CI</i>: 1.080-3.210; <i>P</i>=0.025). Mild depressive episodes were not associated with RHF, whereas major depressive episodes were independently associated with increased RHF risks (OR=1.547, 95% <i>CI</i>: 1.082-2.212; <i>P</i>=0.017). Exploratory machine learning analyses showed that depressive episodes and clinically relevant depressive symptoms were stable features for RHF risk identification but with weaker contributions than age, fasting blood glucose, and systolic blood pressure. In middle-aged and older adults, depressive symptoms are nonlinearly associated with RHF risks, which increased significantly when PHQ-9 score reached a clinically meaningful threshold. Major depressive episodes are also associated with increased RHF risks, and their temporal relationship and underlying mechanisms require further investigation in prospective studies.

The stacking ensemble strategy enhances multimodal fusion and provides a highly accurate, interpretable tool for DLBCL risk stratification.

Título: Identification of metabolic risk phenotypes among U.S. adolescents: A machine learning analysis of NHANES 2017-2023.
Resumen: Adolescent metabolic risk is multidimensional and may not be fully characterized by individual anthropometric or biochemical indicators considered separately; however, evidence regarding data-derived metabolic-risk phenotypes among adolescents remains limited. To identify metabolic risk phenotypes among U.S. adolescents using unsupervised machine learning and examine demographic and socioeconomic factors associated with phenotype membership. Data from adolescents aged 12-17 years participating in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020 and 2021-2023 cycles were analyzed. K-means clustering was performed among 848 adolescents with complete data for seven anthropometric and cardiometabolic variables. Logistic regression examined sociodemographic factors associated with elevated metabolic-risk phenotype membership. A two-cluster solution yielded the highest silhouette coefficient (0.289), identifying a lower metabolic-risk phenotype (n = 580, 68.4%) and an elevated metabolic-risk phenotype (n = 268, 31.6%). The elevated-risk phenotype was characterized by substantially higher BMI and waist circumference, together with higher triglycerides and LDL-C cholesterol, lower HDLC, and modestly higher glycated hemoglobin. In the adjusted logistic regression analysis (n = 763), older age was associated with greater odds of elevated-risk phenotype membership (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.07-1.29), whereas income-to-poverty ratio was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.87). Unsupervised machine learning identified two exploratory metabolic-risk phenotypes characterized by concurrent differences in adiposity, lipid, and glycemic measures. The findings provide an exploratory basis for investigating multidimensional cardiometabolic assessment approaches relevant to pediatric nursing. Independent replication and longitudinal validation are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical utility.
