Título: Artificial intelligence to support infant feeding and nutritional care: a scoping review.
Resumen: Infant feeding and nutrition are critical for growth, development, and long-term health outcomes. As paediatric nurses play a central role in infant monitoring and feeding practices, there is growing interest in innovative approaches to support early assessment and personalised nutritional care. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly explored to support clinical decision-making; however, its applications in infant feeding and nutrition have not been comprehensively synthesised. To map AI applications in infant feeding and nutrition and examine their potential implications for clinical care and paediatric nursing practice. This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of research databases was conducted across seven electronic databases, grey literature, and trial registers, including studies published from inception to 26 May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and extracted and synthesised data. Twenty-nine studies were included. Seven broad AI application areas were identified: 1) prediction and classification of nutritional status, 2) estimation and monitoring of growth, 3) providing nutritional recommendations, 4) analysing nutritional practices and variations, 5) suckling and feeding behaviour analysis, 6) feeding method and behaviour monitoring, and 7) prediction and classification of feeding status. AI demonstrates potential to support paediatric nurses and healthcare professionals by enabling more timely, personalised interventions to improve nutritional care and long-term infant health outcomes. However, current evidence remains largely developmental, highlighting the need for real-world clinical studies to determine the safety, effectiveness, and integration of AI technologies into paediatric care. Open Science Framework (Registration Number: b45tv).


--- ARTÍCULO 1802 ---
ID (PMID): 42933903
Título: One-shot learning of paired association navigation with biologically plausible schemas.
Resumen: After learning a multiple paired-association (MPA) navigation task, rodents can rapidly learn new cue-location associations after a single exposure, a phenomenon proposed to be facilitated by cognitive schemas. However, it remains unclear what schemas support this behavior and how they could be implemented in biological neural circuits. Here, we identify a set of schemas sufficient for gradual then one-shot paired-association navigation, and implement them in a fully neural agent using biologically plausible plasticity rules. The agent gradually acquires a low-dimensional spatial metric representation using a path-integration based temporal-difference error, enabling self-localization across different environments. It also contains a memory network that forms one-shot associations between sensory cues and goal locations, implemented using reward-modulated exploratory Hebbian (EH) plasticity. A third network performs vector subtraction between the agent's current and goal location to compute goal-directed actions. Supplementing these schemas with an actor-critic enables one-shot navigation past obstacles. Lastly, learning a working-memory gating mechanism using the temporal-difference error enables one-shot learning even with brief cue and distractor presentation. The model reproduces key behavioral features of rodent learning in the MPA task and generates testable predictions about the neural mechanisms underlying schema-based one-shot learning.<b>Significance Statement</b> Schema-dependent learning is exemplified by better recall of a lecture when one already has a schema for understanding. A rodent navigation task showing a shift from slow to rapid learning has been proposed to reflect such schema use, yet how schemas are neurally implemented and enable faster learning is poorly understood. We clarify this gap in this computational study by describing several schemas and implement them as neural networks with biologically plausible learning rules. Composing them into an agent reproduces schema-dependent rodent learning behavior. Because schemas also shape self beliefs, clarifying their neural basis has implications for psychopathology. At the same time, understanding how biological schemas support rapid learning may inform advances in machine learning.

Título: Defining three coagulation-based phenotypes for OHCA patients undergoing ECPR: an unsupervised cluster analysis.
Resumen: Coagulopathy is frequent in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR), yet its prognostic significance and heterogeneity remain poorly characterised. To characterize coagulopathy at ECPR initiation, identify coagulation phenotypes, evaluate their association with outcomes, and describe their temporal evolution. All consecutive refractory OHCAs treated with ECPR (2013-2024) were included. Phenotypes were identified by unsupervised K-means clustering on PT-INR, aPTT, platelets, antithrombin, fibrinogen, and D-dimer measured at ECPR initiation. Associations with survival, neurological outcomes, and complications were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Of 406 ECPR patients, 360 had coagulation data for analysis (initial shockable rhythm 67%, low-flow 70 min [IQR 58-81]). Three phenotypes were identified: severe consumptive coagulopathy (phenotype 1, n=49, 13.6%), mild consumptive coagulopathy (phenotype 2, n=175, 48.6%), and preserved coagulation (phenotype 3, n=136, 37.8%). Phenotype severity correlated with ischaemic burden (lactate, arterial pH, end-tidal CO2, and low-flow duration). On multivariable analysis, phenotype 2 was associated with lower survival (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.55) and favourable neurological outcome (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.12-0.81) versus phenotype 3. Bleeding incidence rates were 38, 12, and 2.5 events per 100 patient-days in phenotype 1, 2, and 3, respectively (all p < 0.001). Three distinct coagulation phenotypes at ECPR initiation were independently associated with survival and neurological outcome and appear to reflect ischaemic injury severity. These findings require validation in independent cohorts before clinical application.

Título: The yEvo Mutation Browser: Enhancing student understanding of experimental evolution and genomics through interactive data visualization.
Resumen: Experimental evolution is a powerful method for studying the relationship between genotype and phenotype by observing how populations genetically adapt to controlled selective pressures. In educational settings, this approach also offers a dynamic way for students to engage with molecular genetics. One such educational effort, known as "yEvo" (yeast evolution), introduces experimental evolution into high school classrooms, allowing students to evolve the baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae under various stressors and investigate the resulting genetic changes. While the hands-on experiments have been successful in fostering student interest and understanding of evolution, the downstream data analysis (interpreting whole-genome sequencing results of evolved yeast compared to the ancestor) remains a challenge. Students often struggle to grasp the significance of their mutated genes and lack the broader context to determine which mutations are most phenotypically relevant. To address these issues, we developed the yEvo Mutation Browser, an intuitive web tool designed to assist students and researchers alike in visualizing and contextualizing genome sequencing data. Developed using R Shiny, this tool features an interactive chromosome map displaying mutated genes, graphs categorizing mutation types, a gene viewer illustrating specific mutation sites within genes, and a protein view that maps specific mutations onto protein structures. The app also features an option for non-yEvo-affiliated users to upload their own experimental evolution or genetic screen datasets and compare them with all yEvo data collected since 2018. The yEvo Mutation Browser streamlines data interpretation, helping students understand how organisms employ diverse genetic strategies to adapt to environmental stress. In the future, this framework could be adapted for use with other model organisms, offering a valuable resource for both genetics research and education.

Título: Data-Driven Approach to Estimate Ambient Ammonia Concentrations.
Resumen: The Netherlands experiences significant environmental impacts from reactive nitrogen, particularly ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>), whose long-term deposition harms soil, water, and biodiversity. NH<sub>3</sub> is emitted mainly from agriculture and its levels can be very high and variable in intensive livestock areas. Although monitoring stations are set up across multiple locations, data gaps may still arise due to issues with measurement instruments. Therefore, there is a need for models that can reliably fill in these missing observations. In this study, we first applied Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models to predict one day ahead NH<sub>3</sub> concentrations at six sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Wieringerwerf, Zegveld) in the Netherlands. All models captured daily NH<sub>3</sub> trends, with Random Forest initially performing best (R<sup>2</sup> up to 0.59 at Valthermond). Predictions were strongly driven by lagged NH<sub>3</sub> values with wind speed and precipitation contributing moderately. After correcting for prediction lag caused by autocorrelation, the linear regression performed best at most sites (with best performance observed at Zegveld with R<sup>2</sup> of 0.84) and was used for gap filling. It maintained reasonable accuracy despite sparse observations (every 2-7 days), with most sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Zegveld) exhibiting a significant correlation of almost or more than 0.5 even at 7 days measurement gaps. Additionally, we noted that historical data from existing sites could be effectively used to fill gaps at newly established locations that exhibited similar distributions of NH<sub>3</sub>.

Título: Systematic evaluation and machine learning-based driver analysis of cadmium-induced osteotoxicity in mammals.
Resumen: Cadmium (Cd) is a persistent environmental pollutant with a biological half-life of several decades in animals. However, the osteotoxic effects in the mammalian skeletal system and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using 374 control-observation comparisons from 47 studies, we systematically evaluated Cd-associated skeletal toxicity through meta-analysis and machine learning. The results indicate that Cd exposure significantly impairs overall bone health (13.68%, P < 0.001). TRACP5b (61.52%, P < 0.001) and CTX-I (35.29%, P < 0.01) showed the strongest responses, whereas BMD (10.28%, P < 0.001) and body weight (6.06%, P < 0.001) changed more moderately. TRACP5b responded approximately sixfold more strongly than BMD, supporting bone resorption markers as more sensitive early-warning indicators of Cd-induced skeletal toxicity. The XGBoost model demonstrated the best performance on the test set (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.752, RMSE = 0.325), highlighting its strong potential for predicting Cd-induced bone toxicity risk. SHAP analysis identified response indicators (9.5%-23.3%) and Cd concentration plus duration (18%) as major contributors to osteotoxic response variation. Biologically, these findings indicate that Cd-associated osteotoxicity is characterized by heterogeneous sensitivity across bone-remodeling endpoints, while exposure concentration and duration modulate the magnitude of this multi-target skeletal response. These findings provide a basis for refining cadmium risk assessment and screening early-warning biomarkers.

Título: Combining single-cell data with machine learning characterizes the molecular landscape of keratoconus.
Resumen: Keratoconus (KC) is a progressive disorder characterized by corneal ectasia, corneal thinning, and conical protrusion, which can lead to diminished vision and corneal scarring. However, the molecular mechanism underlying KC has not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, we combined bioinformatics tools and experimental assays to uncover cell-type-specific pathogenic regulators and candidate diagnostic biomarkers of KC. We analyzed the KC-associated bulk mRNA expression dataset GSE151631 (19 KC, 7 controls) and the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE285060 (5 KC, 3 controls) from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. After quality control, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and annotation of single cells, we assessed each subpopulation's role in the disease and conducted differential expression analysis on the most relevant subpopulation. Feature selection was then performed on the bulk RNA-seq dataset using LASSO regression and SVM-RFE algorithms to identify candidate diagnostic genes. As a preliminary in vivo validation, an acute rabbit model of KC was induced by intrastromal injection of collagenase type II, and corneal tissues were harvested at day 7 to assess key gene expression at the mRNA level by RT-qPCR and to qualitatively assess protein expression trends by representative immunofluorescence images. We also performed immune infiltration analysis, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA), transcriptional regulatory networks construction, pseudotime trajectory analysis, and connectivity map (cMap)-based drug prediction. Corneal stromal cells exhibited the highest contribution to the disease state. Three key genes (KIAA0930, CCDC85B, and KLHL21) were identified as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Notably, KIAA0930 was upregulated in the rabbit KC model, while CCDC85B and KLHL21 were downregulated, consistent with bioinformatic analysis. Immune infiltration analysis indicated increased cytolytic activity and CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells in KC samples, with key genes showing significant correlations with various immune cell types and factors. GSEA and GSVA analyses revealed that these three genes are linked to ECM-receptor interaction, MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and WNT/β-catenin signaling pathways. Pseudotime analysis revealed distinct transcriptional states between KC and control cells. Several small-molecule compounds, including menadione and PAC-1, were computationally predicted to show negative connectivity with the KC-associated gene expression signature. Our study identifies KIAA0930, CCDC85B, and KLHL21 as promising candidate biomarkers for KC diagnosis and highlights corneal stromal cells as a central contributor to KC pathological progression. By combining single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning with preliminary validation in an acute rabbit model, this work provides a molecular framework for early KC diagnosis and therapy, pending validation in chronic models and human cohorts.

Título: 3D-printed hierarchical microstructures from allyl cellulose-based ionic conductors for intelligent flexible pressure sensing.
Resumen: Flexible pressure sensors require simultaneous optimization of mechanical robustness, ionic conductivity, and structural programmability, properties that are rarely achieved in a single bio-based material system. Comprehensive validation spanning physiological monitoring, robotic tactile perception, and human-machine interfaces confirms the technology's versatility. These results establish allyl cellulose-based dual-network ionic conductors as a versatile bio-derived platform in which material composition, microstructural geometry, and data-driven signal processing can be co-designed to meet the divergent requirements of next-generation flexible pressure sensing.

Título: Machine learning-based stability optimization design and virtual screening of the anti-pulmonary fibrosis peptide DR3penA.

Título: Convex-relaxed counterfactual optimization for non-differentiable classifiers via neural surrogates.
Resumen: Counterfactual explanations (CE) facilitate actionable recourse by identifying minimal perturbations that transition an instance across a model's decision boundary. However, generating CEs for non-differentiable and non-smooth classifiers, including common nonparametric models such as kNN, random forests, and kernel SVMs, remains challenging because gradient information is unavailable or unreliable near irregular decision boundaries. Current model-agnostic approaches often neglect inherent structural priors, while surrogate-based methods frequently suffer from "metric distortion," where latent feature-space optimizations map to topologically invalid instances in the original input space. To resolve these theoretical impasses, we propose ECOer (Efficient Counterfactual Optimization with metric-preserving reconstruction regularization), a mathematically principled, end-to-end framework for post-hoc counterfactual generation for non-differentiable classifiers. ECOer constructs a ReLU-ReLU Single-hidden-layer Neural Network (R2SNN) as a differentiable surrogate, which we prove to possess tight universal approximation bounds for measurable decision regions. To preserve metric fidelity during latent-space search, we derive a novel metric-preserving reconstruction regularization mechanism grounded in Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) theory, ensuring that optimized features remain tied to the valid data manifold. Furthermore, we introduce a convex relaxation technique that yields a region-wise convex objective with zero relaxation gap within fixed decision regions. Extensive theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations on real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ECOer achieves a favorable trade-off between validity, proximity, plausibility, and online generation latency among the evaluated baselines. This work provides a rigorous algorithmic foundation for robust and reliable XAI in decision-critical tabular domains.

These findings support targeted, data-driven improvement plans that are practical for RTT-led implementation and compatible with evolving national safety expectations. Radiotherapy must follow strict safety measures because it uses high doses of radiation to treat cancer. This study reviewed safety practices at ten private radiotherapy centres in Morocco using a standard set of quality and safety measures. This study found that routine safety checks and staff radiation monitoring were generally strong, but some centres had fewer systems for quality management, incident learning, and quality assurance. This matters because improving these areas can help make cancer treatment safer for patients and staff.

Título: Management of transfusion in traumatic hemorrhagic shock.
Resumen: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock remains the leading preventable cause of early trauma death, with most deaths occurring within the first 24 h. This review summarizes recent advances in prediction tools, transfusion protocols, blood products and monitoring strategies for transfusion management. Transfusion management relies on early activation of major hemorrhage protocols and rapid delivery of balanced blood components to limit coagulopathy and restore oxygen delivery. Prehospital transfusion appears most beneficial in the most severely injured patients, particularly with prolonged transport times, though its mortality benefit varies across trauma systems and patient phenotypes. Low-titer group O whole blood simplifies logistics and may improve early hemostasis, but randomized trials have not shown a clear survival advantage over component therapy. Viscoelastic testing complements empirical algorithms by enabling faster, targeted correction of fibrinogen and factor deficiency. Emerging data also highlight the prognostic impact of ionized calcium disturbances and the potential of machine-learning models for early risk stratification. Current evidence supports a time-critical, system-based approach in which standardized transfusion bundles are triggered early and refined using viscoelastic guidance. Future work should prioritize prospective validation of decision-support tools, phenotype-specific strategies, clarification of whole blood's role, and rigorous evaluation of emerging blood products.

Título: Acute kidney injury phenotypes: clinical reality or statistical artifact?
Resumen: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common syndrome associated with poor outcomes; however, definitions based only on serum creatinine and urine output obscure patient-level differences relevant to prognosis and treatment. Sub-phenotyping strategies seek to resolve this heterogeneity. Título: Selective Electronic Pre-Activation of OH Bonds in Extremely Confined Water.
Resumen: Water under molecular-scale confinement is not simply a geometrically restricted form of bulk water, but can acquire distinct electronic, structural, and collective properties. However, how such an extremely confined state reshapes water's intrinsic chemistry remains poorly understood. Here, using ab initio calculations and enhanced-sampling machine-learning potential molecular dynamics, we show that extreme two-dimensional confinement activates water for proton generation. Monolayer-confined water exhibits a substantially lower free-energy barrier for forming separated H3O+ and OH- ions than bulk water, and this tendency is further enhanced by lateral compression and nuclear quantum fluctuations. This enhanced reactivity does not arise from a uniform weakening of all water molecules. Instead, confinement makes OH bonds breaking selectively. The water molecule contains electronically distinct OH bonds, with weak in-plane bonds preferentially activated for proton release, while stronger dangling bonds remain relatively inactive. The surrounding hydrogen-bond network then provides disordered pathways for proton relocation, and the enhanced in-plane polarization stabilizes the charged products. Our results suggest that two-dimensional confined water can act as an active and superdielectric medium as indicated by recent experiments. Our findings reveal extreme confinement as a route to tune water-mediated chemistry, with implications for nanofluidics, geochemical pores, biological environments, and catalytic interfaces.

A curated database was constructed from published studies, and five regression algorithms were evaluated. Extremely randomized trees, random forest, and gradient boosting achieved the best performance for tensile strength, Young's modulus, and elongation at break, with random five-fold cross-validation R<sup>2</sup> values of 0.895, 0.835, and 0.673, respectively. Shapely additive explanations (SHAP) analysis identified SPI and plasticizer concentrations as dominant compositional factors, while processing effects were property-dependent. Model-guided experiments then investigated the underexplored coupling between pH and heating temperature at fixed composition. Experiments reproduced broad processing-property trends but revealed reduced predictive accuracy under acidic and high-temperature conditions. Multiscale characterization linked these deviations to pH-dependent protein association, secondary-structure evolution, and network morphology. This literature-to-experiment workflow transforms heterogeneous published data into experimentally testable, mechanistically interpretable design principles for data-guided development of protein-based materials.

--- ARTÍCULO 1849 ---
ID (PMID): 42932717
Título: A Classification of Safety Risks in Medical AI.
Resumen: AbstractIn clinical practice, patient safety is paramount, guided by the principle "first, do no harm." For medical AI to become a core component of clinical care, safety cannot be determined by its performance or accuracy alone, but by whether or not it protects patients from harm. However, consequences of medical AI models - used either independently or in combination with clinicians - may result in harms that can emerge years after the initial AI-enabled diagnosis or intervention, are difficult to attribute to the original AI model, and are irreversible (e.g., serious morbidity or mortality). We propose a four-level clinical safety classification for medical AI. S1 refers to narrow, testable uses; S2 to decision support that clinicians can review before acting; S3 to uses in which important harms may appear only after follow-up and therefore require surveillance and outcome monitoring before wider rollout; and S4 to high-risk autonomous actions that should be prohibited or allowed only under exceptional safeguards. Using a real-world prospective study of DeepDR-LLM, an integrated image-language system that combines a large language model with image-based deep learning for primary diabetes care and diabetic retinopathy screening, we illustrate how the same AI function may remain classified as S2 when used as clinician-reviewed decision support, become S3 when safety depends on referral completion and follow-up outcomes, or approach S4 if used to bypass clinical judgment. We propose multiwindow postdeployment surveillance that captures near-term signals, scheduled follow-up checkpoints, and long-horizon monitoring beyond 12 months through registry or claims linkage and postimplementation surveillance studies, strengthening medicine's core commitment to "first, do no harm - both now and in the future."

Título: Language Models for Value-Informed Proxy Decision Support.

Título: Medicine as an Information Industry in the Age of Language Models.
Resumen: AbstractMedicine is fundamentally an information enterprise in which clinicians integrate patient data with prior knowledge and external sources to guide decisions. Over time, the delivery of medical knowledge has evolved from apprenticeship and print to digital search, improving access but not necessarily efficiency. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) marks a qualitative shift - from retrieval to synthesis - enabling rapid, contextually tailored responses to clinical questions. Yet only 5 of the 1430 AI- and/or machine learning-enabled medical devices cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration are modern pathology AI tools based on whole-slide images, whereas 1094 are classified in the radiology category. Furthermore, only approximately 4% of U.S. slide volume is currently read digitally. We argue that this disconnect reflects a hierarchy of barriers to clinical impact: foundational infrastructure and economic hurdles, postdigitization challenges related to sample variability and clinician trust, an underdeveloped implementation and governance pathway, and persistent equity gaps in low- and middle-income settings. Against this backdrop, two near- and medium-term translational pathways stand out: AI as a digital copilot for clinical evaluation and AI-enabled clinical trial design. Together, these approaches offer measurable workflow and trial-enabling benefits, with the potential to improve patient outcomes.

Título: Verifying Facts in Patient Care Documents Generated by Large Language Models Using Electronic Health Records.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) can generate clinical documents, but inaccuracies due to hallucinations create a barrier for use in medical practice. Reliance on clinician vigilance to remedy errors is infeasible, since mistakes may be subtle and interleaved among accurate statements within the document. An increasing trend in artificial intelligence (AI) has been to deploy LLMs as evaluators of LLM output (LLM-as-a-Judge), which has been shown to have high concordance with human judgment. We hypothesize that an LLM-as-a-Judge with relevant facts from a patient's electronic health record (EHR) can be used to automatically verify facts in any clinical document written about a patient and provide an overall estimate of the document's accuracy. To evaluate this hypothesis, we created a benchmark dataset called VeriFact - Brief Hospital Course (VeriFact-BHC), consisting of statements derived from the brief hospital course sections of discharge summaries, and established a ground truth from clinician chart review. We then devised an AI system, VeriFact, that combines retrieval-augmented generation of facts from a patient's EHR along with an LLM-as-a-Judge to perform automated evaluation of all statements in the dataset. VeriFact-BHC contains 100 patients with 13,070 statements derived from brief hospital courses, each annotated by three or more clinicians. VeriFact achieved 93.2% agreement with clinicians. The highest interrater agreement among clinicians was 88.5%, indicating that VeriFact can produce more consistent fact verification than humans. Scaling the size of the LLM-as-a-Judge model and adding reasoning capability improve different facets of AI judgment and are synergistic when combined. VeriFact can help clinicians verify facts in documents drafted by LLMs prior to committing them to the patient's EHR and can automate tasks requiring chart review. VeriFact-BHC can be used to develop and benchmark new methodologies for verifying facts in patient care documents. (Funded by Stanford University and others.).

Título: Comprehensive or Wasteful? Clinical AI and the Up-front Workup.
Resumen: AbstractClinical AI is being adopted faster than it is being evaluated, on the promise that it will improve health and reduce waste. Aran and colleagues show that large language models recommend more up-front testing, referrals, and treatment than the physicians who actually saw the patients and at more than three times cost, at least in the short-term. But practicing differently is not the same as practicing worse: whether this reflects wasteful excess or appropriate thoroughness is unknown, as are the consequences for long-run health and spending. On one hand, more up-front care could reduce diagnostic errors, catch disease earlier, deliver guideline-concordant treatment that clinicians overlook, and avert costly late-stage care. On the other hand, it could surface incidental findings that spark anxiety and follow-up cascades, add treatments of marginal benefit, and raise spending through added visits and more intensive billing and diagnosis coding. Neither vignettes nor single-visit studies can settle this. Clinical AI deserves the standard we would demand of any new therapy: trials that randomize practices to these tools and measure long-run effects on patients' health and spending.

Título: Comparative Cost of Care Recommended by Large Language Models versus Treating Physicians.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for clinical decision support, yet the cost of services or treatment they recommend has not been systematically evaluated. We evaluated 24 AI systems on 200 deidentified outpatient and emergency department notes from MTSamples, a public collection of deidentified U.S.-format clinical notes contributed by practicing clinicians. Each system received the presentation recorded before the physician's assessment and wrote its own plan; the physician's documented plan was the comparator. Orders from both were extracted by three independent LLMs and priced at 2026 Medicare rates. The primary outcome was the per-visit total cost of recommended care: diagnostic tests plus specialist referrals. New medications were counted rather than priced. We also tested two prompts: one cost-aware prompt and one parsimonious-but-safe prompt. Across the 20 general-purpose systems, AI-suggested care cost a mean of US$314 per visit, compared with US$97 for care recommended by treating physicians - a difference of US$216 per visit (95% confidence interval, US$177 to US$257; P<0.001) or 3.2 times the physicians' cost. AI system mean costs ranged from US$209 to US$599. The difference reflected US$105 in diagnostic tests and US$111 in specialist referrals; systems also recommended more new medications (1.14 vs. 0.59 per visit). The four specialized medical systems were no less costly (2.7× to 3.5×). Physicians recorded no diagnostic testing in 66% of visits; on those visits, every AI system suggested testing, usually a stereotyped panel. Prompting the systems to be cost-aware (2.5× the physician) or parsimonious (1.4×) reduced but did not remove the excess. The care these systems recommended cost substantially more than physicians' documented care, chiefly because they suggested testing at visits where the physician had ordered none. LLM outputs are suggestions, not plans of care; final decisions should remain with clinicians.

Título: From Molecular Topography to Ozone Pollution: Species Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals.

Título: Baseline microbial ecology encodes probiotic responsiveness through distinct metabolic and network configurations.
Resumen: Probiotic efficacy in inflammatory bowel disease varies widely between individuals, and the sources of that variability remain poorly understood. Título: From Binding Sites to Target Genes: Reframing Human microRNA Target Prediction.
Resumen: MicroRNA (miRNA) target prediction is often treated as a single problem, yet it encompasses two distinct computational tasks: identifying whether a miRNA can bind a particular target RNA binding site, and predicting the change in gene expression that follows from miRNA perturbation. Resumen: Liver transplantation remains a technically demanding procedure despite continued surgical advances. Successful outcomes depend on balancing donor selection with perioperative complexity, where each decision shapes graft and patient survival. Conventional scoring systems such as Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD)-based prioritisation only partially explain differences in patient outcomes across transplant centres worldwide. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-including longitudinal modelling of electronic health records, deep learning for imaging, and multimodal data integration-offer new opportunities to individualise risk stratification for graft selection, predict allograft dysfunction and rejection, and improve long-term survival. Clinically developed AI models may strengthen organ matching decisions and acceptance, while identifying candidates who require intensified immunosuppressant monitoring or targeted diagnostic testing in the postoperative period, without increasing rejection risk. However, introducing AI/ML systems requires thorough validation, careful calibration, and ongoing clinical audit to reduce bias, detect technical errors, and ensure reproducible performance. This review summarises current and emerging clinical applications of AI in liver transplantation and explores near-future directions. These include AI-driven graft evaluation during organ retrieval and normothermic machine perfusion, along with emerging evidence for the safety, reliability, and clinical utility of AI in transplantation practice.

Título: Neurophysiological and Psychophysical Biomarkers for Predicting Spinal Cord Stimulation Treatment Response in Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review.
Resumen: <b>Background:</b> Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established therapy for chronic neuropathic pain, yet a substantial minority of implanted patients do not obtain durable relief, and patient selection still relies largely on a subjective percutaneous stimulation trial. Objective neurophysiological and psychophysical biomarkers could enable precision selection, but their predictive value has not been consolidated across modalities. <b>Objectives:</b> To evaluate whether pre-treatment or intraoperative neurophysiological (electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP), evoked compound action potentials (ECAP)) and psychophysical (conditioned pain modulation (CPM), quantitative sensory testing [QST]) biomarkers predict SCS treatment response in adults with chronic neuropathic pain. <b>Methods:</b> Following a pre-registered protocol (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD420261410302)) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guideline, we searched six databases and two registries; the final search was run on 4 June 2026. Records underwent dual, independent screening in Rayyan; data were extracted in duplicate and risk of bias was assessed with the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST), or the Quality Assessment of Prognostic Accuracy Studies (QUAPAS) tool. Because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline. <b>Results:</b> Twelve peer-reviewed studies met eligibility. Most were prognostic-factor or responder-discrimination studies rather than prospectively validated predictors; two were multivariable machine learning prediction models and one used ECAP-derived neural dose as a therapy-embedded surrogate. Resting EEG/MEG spectral features (alpha, gamma) discriminated responders in several small cohorts. The two prediction models reported apparent internal accuracy of 76-88% (area under the curve up to 0.88) but neither underwent external validation. QST and CPM findings were promising but directionally inconsistent. All 12 studies were at high overall risk of bias. <b>Conclusions:</b> Objective biomarkers-most notably the preoperative SSEP and resting-state EEG/MEG spectral features-show promise for predicting SCS response, but the evidence is preliminary, heterogeneous, small, and lacks external validation. Adequately powered, prospective, externally validated studies are needed before clinical adoption.

Título: Early Differentiation of Barley Diseases (Net Blotch, Spot Blotch, and Stem Rust) Using Hyperspectral Imaging and Machine Learning.
Resumen: Early and accurate detection of fungal diseases is critical for sustainable barley production, yet multiclass differentiation at early stages remains a major challenge. Título: Three-Class Correspondence Reliability for Deformation-Preserving ICP: Controlled Synthetic Evaluation and a Cross-Domain Stress Test.
Resumen: Multi-epoch point-cloud analysis requires rigid alignment without allowing genuine geometric change to bias the estimated pose. This study presents a reliability-guided iterative closest point (ICP) formulation in which a compact classifier assigns each candidate correspondence to stable, deformation-candidate, or unreliable classes. Stable-class scores softly weight a Cauchy-robust point-to-plane objective on the special Euclidean group SE3, while deformation candidates are retained for signed-residual mapping. Controlled evaluation comprised 28 factor-level blocks, with 20 independently generated random trials per block and 560 paired trials per method. The three-class method achieved median rotational and translational errors of 0.227 degrees and 4.103 mm and 96.61% registration recall. Its principal benefit was changed-region discrimination: the F1 score (harmonic mean of precision and recall) reached 0.524 for the 5 and 10 mm cases, compared with 0.413 for binary classifier-guided ICP. However, the binary method produced slightly better rigid-registration accuracy, and the three-class stable-region false-positive rate was 6.71%. An external stress test on a Stanford Bunny scan pair used 60 controlled initialisations. Point-to-point ICP achieved 100% success, whereas the unretrained three-class method achieved 0% and assigned 39.3% of rigid-object correspondences to the deformation class. The results support three-way correspondence modelling as a controlled proof of concept but demonstrate that balanced synthetic training does not yield calibration-free transfer. Real-domain calibration, stronger geometric baselines, and validation with independent displacement ground truth are required before deployment.

Título: Deep-Learning-Based Assessment of Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography: Technical Validation, Cardiovascular Prognostic Value, and Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
Resumen: Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is a manifestation of medial arterial calcification frequently detected incidentally on screening mammography. Increasing evidence suggests that BAC may also serve as a marker of cardiovascular risk. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-based detection, segmentation, and quantification of BAC. It also evaluates the cardiovascular prognostic significance of automatically quantified BAC and examines the requirements for clinical translation. A targeted literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted for English-language publications available from database inception through 3 September 2026, with additional studies identified from reference lists. Deep-learning approaches included convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived segmentation architectures, transfer-learning models, and semi-supervised methods. Reported technical performance varied according to task and validation strategy. Representative segmentation models achieved Dice/F1 scores ranging from 0.666 to 0.756 and Jaccard indices from 0.581 to 0.614. Prognostic studies demonstrated graded associations between automated BAC burden and cardiovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, incremental predictive improvement may be small-in one study, the addition of BAC changed the 5-year AUC from 0.645 to 0.646. Overall, available evidence supports the feasibility of scalable AI-based BAC assessment and demonstrates consistent associations between AI-quantified BAC and cardiovascular outcomes. However, technical performance and independent prognostic associations alone do not establish clinical utility. Standardized BAC definitions, genuinely independent external validation, and prospective implementation studies are required before BAC-guided cardiovascular management can be recommended.

Título: Vulnerable Coronary Plaques on CT Angiography: Imaging Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Emerging Technologies for Risk Stratification.
Resumen: Coronary artery disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that many acute coronary events originate not from severely obstructive lesions but from structurally unstable atherosclerotic plaques. Consequently, the identification of vulnerable plaques has become a major objective in contemporary cardiovascular imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has evolved from a modality primarily focused on luminal stenosis assessment into a comprehensive non-invasive technique capable of evaluating plaque morphology, composition, and overall coronary atherosclerotic burden. Despite these advances, limitations remain, including restricted spatial resolution for microstructural plaque assessment and the limited ability of conventional CT to directly evaluate biological processes such as inflammation. Future developments integrating advanced CT technologies, artificial intelligence, and multimodality imaging are expected to further improve the non-invasive identification of vulnerable plaques and personalized cardiovascular risk stratification.

These findings indicate that integrating symbolic dynamics with bio-inspired pruning delivers a computationally efficient, highly accurate, and transparent solution suitable for edge-oriented energy management systems. The theoretical contribution is that the magnitude of a hidden unit's learned output weights provides a usable ranking signal at no additional computational cost beyond the closed-form solution already obtained. The practical contribution is that this signal allows the classifier head to be compressed by 87.3% without a measurable loss in accuracy.

Resumen: The coexistence of multiple chronic diseases is common among older adults and presents substantial challenges for disease prevention, management, and healthcare planning. However, most previous studies have focused on predicting individual diseases, although multiple chronic conditions commonly coexist. ID (PMID): 42930238
Título: First-Principles Modelling of Ion-Substituted Hydroxyapatite: Defect Chemistry, Site Preferences, and Structure-Property Relationships-A Critical Review.
Resumen: Hydroxyapatite (HAp) possesses exceptional compositional flexibility, allowing for extensive cationic, anionic, and coupled substitutions that can modify its structural, mechanical, electronic, magnetic, catalytic, and biological properties. However, experimental identification of dopant locations and charge-compensation mechanisms remains challenging, particularly in nanocrystalline, calcium-deficient, and multiphase materials. This review evaluates first-principles studies of ion-substituted HAp, with particular emphasis on substitution-site preferences, defect association, charge compensation, thermodynamic stability, configurational effects, surfaces, hydration, and comparison with experimental observables. Unlike earlier reviews that primarily catalogued individual dopants and their calculated effects, the present work critically examines the methodological and defect-chemical assumptions underlying reported substitution mechanisms, including charge compensation, configurational sampling, chemical-potential definitions, hydration, finite-temperature effects, and experimental validation. The literature demonstrates that dopant site preference is not an intrinsic and concentration-independent property of an element. Instead, it depends on supercell size, dopant concentration, hydroxyl ordering, oxidation and spin states, compensating defects, chemical potentials, hydration, temperature, and the presence of other impurities. Many apparent discrepancies between studies arise from small simulation cells, incomplete configurational sampling, inconsistent formation-energy definitions, or calculations performed for assumed compositions without explicit charge compensation. The strongest structural assignments combine defect energetics with directly calculated spectroscopic parameters. Future predictive models should treat substituted HAp as a condition-dependent ensemble of interacting defects and integrate large-scale configurational sampling, finite-temperature methods, hydrated surfaces, machine learning, and advanced spectroscopic validation.

Resumen: Liquid-phase quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) biosensors are commonly quantified using scalar readouts such as frequency shift, dissipation, or bandwidth. Here, we present a machine-learning-assisted impedance line-shape workflow for temporally robust quantitative 10 MHz QCM biosensing. A passive microfluidic mixer generated controlled glycerol-water concentration gradients under constant total flow while complex impedance spectra were acquired in real time, and each sweep was parameterized using constrained Gaussian/Lorentzian models to obtain 52 physically interpretable descriptors spanning resistance, reactance, impedance magnitude, admittance components, and phase. Feature-set ablation indicated that phase and conductance line-shape descriptors carry particularly strong temporally generalizable information. Applied to an experimental DNA hybridization assay in 1× PBS, the workflow reduced mean absolute percentage concentration error from 21.02% to 10.73%, a 48.9% improvement over conventional Δf calibration. Retaining resonance morphology therefore improves quantitative QCM biosensing beyond scalar frequency-shift calibration and provides an interpretable basis for AI-assisted electronic biosensors.

Título: Advancing Biosensing Through Artificial Intelligence: Overcoming Conventional Limitations Towards Intelligent Diagnostic Systems.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated with biosensors to improve signal processing, feature extraction, calibration, and clinical interpretation. However, analytical sensitivity and high internal validation accuracy do not necessarily translate into clinically useful or generalisable diagnostic performance. This review therefore reframes AI-enabled biosensing around clinical actionability rather than technological performance alone. We critically examine how AI can address signal noise, drift, matrix effects, and complex or high-dimensional biosensor outputs while evaluating how model selection should reflect data modality, dataset size, computational constraints, and intended deployment. Importantly, we distinguish the physical limit of detection (LoD) of the sensing system from algorithm-assisted effective detectability: AI cannot intrinsically lower the physical detection limit of a fixed transducer, but it can improve extraction and interpretation of weak signals near the noise floor. A central contribution of this review is a clinically actionable threshold framework that links representative biomarkers to decision-relevant concentration ranges, clarifying when further LoD reduction is clinically meaningful and when robustness, selectivity, dynamic range, calibration stability, and reproducibility matter more. We also critically appraise representative AI-enabled biosensor studies by sample size, validation strategy, reference standard, generalisability, interpretability, computational requirements, and evidence maturity, rather than headline accuracy alone. Across electrochemical, optical and spectroscopic, wearable, and point-of-care platforms, major translational barriers include biofouling, matrix interference, signal drift, dataset shift, insufficient external validation, privacy, and regulatory requirements. We conclude that progress in intelligent biosensing should be judged by reliable performance across clinically relevant ranges and demonstrated utility in real-world diagnostic workflows, rather than by progressively lower LoDs or isolated accuracy values alone.

We present a systematic investigation into two interdependent design principles─learned atomic representations and cross-element parameterization─that govern MLIP generalization. Using the diverse, multielement OC20 catalyst dataset, we evaluate chemically informed atomic embeddings against conventional 1-hot encoding within two distinct model architectures: the tensor-based LATTE descriptor and the MACE message-passing neural network. We demonstrate that embeddings such as Magpie and Matscholar reduce force mean absolute errors (MAEs) by 20-30% compared to 1-hot encoding, and improve data efficiency in low-data regimes by over 40%. Furthermore, by strategically sharing parameters across elements, we reduce the model sizes by up to 98% (from 23M to 400k parameters) without remarkably compromising accuracy, and even enable meaningful few-shot prediction for underrepresented elements. This work establishes a practical framework for building compact, transferable, and data-efficient MLIPs suitable for exploration across heterogeneous chemical spaces.

Título: Validation Strategy Dominates Model Choice in Chronological QSAR Evaluation.
Resumen: Quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models are commonly evaluated by random cross-validation or random train-test splits, but these retrospective procedures may overestimate performance when validation compounds are structurally or temporally close to the training data. In this study, we examined whether this optimism is primarily explained by structural redundancy, chronological data set evolution, or the choice of machine-learning model. Fourteen public ChEMBL bioactivity data sets were curated as binary classification tasks. Five validation conditions were compared: random validation, chronological validation by publication year, a size-matched randomly thinned control, structural filtering of the random validation set, and structural filtering of the chronological validation set. Model development was deliberately held fixed within the random-derived and year-derived comparisons, so that the effect of validation-set composition could be assessed without simultaneously changing the training cohort. Four standard QSAR model classes─random forest, support vector machine, XGBoost, and a feed-forward neural network─were evaluated under the same training-only model-selection workflow. Random validation produced closely aligned internal and external estimates, with mean MCC values of 0.75 and 0.72, respectively, while random thinning gave essentially unchanged validation performance (MCC 0.73). Structural filtering reduced validation MCC to 0.48 without changing the corresponding training-only CV estimate. Chronological validation produced a much larger generalization gap, with mean CV MCC of 0.73 and validation MCC of 0.19; additional structural filtering reduced validation MCC to 0.15. Model-class comparisons showed substantial overlap among classifiers, and no standard algorithm consistently overcame the chronological validation penalty. These results indicate that validation-set definition has a dominant influence on estimated QSAR generalization and that chronological data set shift is not reproduced by random or structure-only validation.

Título: ElemeNet: Multiscale Molecular Machine Learning with Uncertainty Quantification across the Periodic Table.
Resumen: Advances in deep learning architectures and representations have enabled ML-driven chemical property prediction, but state-of-the-art (SOTA) models have remained largely confined to independent codebases and lack support for diverse chemical species. This work introduces ElemeNet, a unified, general-purpose software package for molecular machine learning. The ElemeNet software package enables the training of advanced ML models for diverse properties and data sets with an enlarged range of elemental compositions. We define molecular representations compatible with elements 1-100, supporting diverse organometallic and biological systems in addition to organic chemistry already well served by the Chemprop ML toolkit. As well as more common atom-, bond-, and molecule-level predictions, we introduce and allow for moiety-level predictions. We also natively define optional conditioning on charge and spin states. Advanced E(3)-equivariant and transformer architectures are supported in addition to 2D models, with all classes including built-in uncertainty quantification through deterministic and statistical measures. We benchmark our protocols for ML model training against representative data sets from organic, inorganic, coordination, and biological chemistry, achieving competitive and SOTA performance relative to literature baselines and favorable scaling to millions of molecules. The entire workflow is exposed through a concise command-line interface, lowering the barrier to entry for nonexpert users. We anticipate ElemeNet will empower noncomputational researchers to leverage modern deep learning methods across the chemical and physical sciences.

Título: Predicting Protein Thermostability with Equivariant Graph Neural Networks and Contrastive Learning.
Resumen: Accurately predicting the thermostability changes induced by single-point mutations is a core challenge in protein engineering and industrial enzyme modification. However, current computational methods often struggle to jointly integrate evolutionary information, structural context, and the interactions between mutation sites and their local microenvironments, presenting obvious limitations in guiding protein modification practice. To this end, this paper proposes the Equivariant Contrastive Learning Network (ECL-Net) for effectively predicting protein thermostability changes. Firstly, this method employs a joint sequence-structure representation strategy, deeply integrating sequence embeddings extracted by protein language models (PLMs) with spatial structural information captured by residue interaction networks, while an Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) is utilized for feature propagation and structural modeling. Furthermore, the self-attention mechanism of the language model is utilized to determine critical residues highly correlated with the mutation, thereby introducing structural microenvironment information. Building upon this, a contrastive learning method jointly guided by the mutation site and local microenvironment is designed, aiming to guide the model to learn more robust feature representations. Experimental results demonstrate that ECL-Net outperforms existing baseline models. Among the four predicted transglutaminase mutants, the model's predictions for three mutants were consistent with the experimental outcomes, demonstrating the potential applicability of ECL-Net in guiding protein engineering.

Título: Dataset merging strategy for efficient construction of a machine-learning force field: A case of CeO2 surfaces with an oxygen vacancy.
Resumen: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the temperature during molecular dynamics simulations while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the merged MLFF was applied to ideal CeO2(111) slabs containing up to 5183 atoms, yielding only weak size dependence of the predicted vacancy-migration barrier. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

Título: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
Resumen: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical. Here we provide a computationally efficient tool, gTranslate, that uses an ensemble of five machine learning methods to accurately predict translation tables for prokaryotic genomes. The feature vector used by gTranslate takes advantage of differences in gene coding densities when predicting genes under different translation tables along with features that consider the number and ratio of UGA stop codon reassignments to tryptophan or glycine. gTranslate is freely available at https://github.com/cmc-aau/gTranslate and archived on Zenodo. We demonstrate that gTranslate correctly predicts the translation table of prokaryotic genomes >99.99% of the time (<i>i.e.</i>, <1 error per 10,000 genomes) and outperforms a more computationally expensive prediction method and a coding density heuristic used by popular bioinformatic tools. Using gTranslate, we identify a basal lineage of <i>Ca.</i> Stammera capleta that uses the standard bacterial genetic code instead of the UGA stop codon to tryptophan reassignment common to other members of this species. We also identify the first instances of UGA-to-tryptophan reassignment in the <i>Patescibacteriota</i> making this the first bacterial phylum with members capable of using translation tables 4, 11, and 25.

SomatiX showed particularly strong performance for low-VAF SNVs in ONT data while using a compact model and achieving the fastest runtime among the evaluated tools. SomatiX is available at https://github.com/colinliuzelin/SomatiX and archived at Zenodo under DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22062438. Título: Data heterogeneity and algorithmic bias in AI-based antimicrobial resistance prediction: a systematic review and mitigation framework.
Resumen: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents one of the most critical global public health threats of the contemporary era, contributing to millions of deaths and substantial morbidity worldwide. Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) have been increasingly applied to AMR detection, prediction, and management, demonstrating promising results in controlled research settings. However, clinical translation remains substantially constrained by fundamental methodological challenges, particularly data heterogeneity and algorithmic bias, whose extent and consequences are not yet adequately characterised. A systematic review with descriptive synthesis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library, covering studies published between January 2020 and April 2026. Eligible studies applied AI/ML approaches to AMR prediction using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), electronic health records (EHRs), surveillance datasets, and spectral data. Data were extracted using a standardized charting form and synthesized using descriptive and thematic methods. No meta-analysis was conducted owing to substantial methodological heterogeneity across included studies. A total of 68 studies published between 2020 and 2026 were included, of which 21 underwent detailed analysis. Studies demonstrated substantial heterogeneity across data modalities, patient populations, laboratory practices, and geographic settings. WGS-based approaches were most frequently represented, followed by AST- and EHR-based models. While many models achieved strong internal performance, generalizability across external settings remained limited. Key sources of heterogeneity included variability in data modalities, laboratory protocols, population composition, and temporal and geographic distribution. Major forms of bias identified included sampling bias, label inconsistency, structural confounding, and clinical context bias. Mitigation strategies demonstrated partial and context-dependent improvements. Data heterogeneity and algorithmic bias are the primary constraints on AI/ML-based AMR prediction, not algorithmic sophistication. The strong internal performance metrics reported across the literature do not reliably generalize to diverse populations, geographic settings, or clinical environments. Meaningful progress requires a deliberate shift in research priorities toward globally representative datasets, harmonized laboratory standards, mandatory external validation, and equitable model development. The proposed Heterogeneity Mitigation Framework offers a structured, evidence-grounded approach to these challenges; its empirical validation in diverse real-world settings is the most important next step for the field. Although this review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO, it was conducted using predefined eligibility criteria, structured data extraction, and transparent reporting in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Título: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
Resumen: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. Título: Integrative graph deep learning with directional decoding for robust gene regulatory network inference from single-cell transcriptomics.
Resumen: While gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are fundamental to understanding complex cellular mechanisms, the accurate inference from single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is hindered by the inherent noise, transcriptional dropout events, and dynamic nature of gene regulation. Current computational approaches often overlook long-range regulatory interactions, lack explicit modeling of regulatory directionality, and suffer from limited generalizability. To address these limitations, we introduce scGRAIL, a supervised deep learning framework that combines inductive local-aware graph aggregation (LGA) with an asymmetric relation decoder to enable robust GRN inference. Within this framework, LGA performs multi-hop neighborhood aggregation on a transcription factor (TF)-target graph, jointly leveraging topological structure and gene expression to capture long-range regulatory dependencies. A node reconstruction autoencoder (NAE) imposes gene expression reconstruction constraints on the latent embeddings, thereby enhancing robustness to noise and data heterogeneity and improving generalization. An asymmetric difference mechanism is introduced during decoding for distinct modeling of TFs and target genes; by computing an ordered difference vector between their embeddings, the model explicitly captures the directionality and target specificity of TF-target regulatory interactions, facilitating more accurate identification of potential causal regulatory relationships. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the model's superiority: it achieves optimal performance on 86.4% of benchmark datasets (38/44), surpassing state-of-the-art methods. Notably, scGRAIL achieves a 4.25% increase in average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) across four real-world networks compared to the graph contrastive link prediction (GCLink) model, yielding a 17.64% AUROC improvement for the TF500+ Non-Specific network in the mouse hematopoietic stem cells with lymphoid-lineage (mHSC-L) dataset, demonstrating its resilience to noise and scalability for large-scale GRNs. These results establish scGRAIL as a transformative tool for uncovering gene regulatory logic in single-cell transcriptomics. Overall, scGRAIL enhances structural modeling and directional discrimination in single-cell GRN inference by using multi-hop graph aggregation to capture long-range regulatory dependencies, expression reconstruction constraints to improve cross-dataset robustness, and an asymmetric decoding mechanism to explicitly model the regulatory directionality between TFs and target genes.

Título: Peripheral immune tolerance as a driver of tumor immune escape and therapy resistance.
Resumen: Peripheral immune tolerance, essential for preventing autoimmunity, is increasingly co-opted by tumors to drive progression, metastatic dissemination, and immunotherapy resistance. Whereas central tolerance eliminates autoreactive clones, peripheral tolerance remains dynamically regulated by antigen persistence, cytokine gradients, metabolic cues, and stromal architecture, a plasticity that tumors exploit to build a multilayered immunosuppressive ecosystem. This narrative review synthesizes multi-omic, spatial, cellular, and molecular evidence, emphasizing 2021 to 2025 publications alongside foundational studies, to propose tumor-induced peripheral tolerance (TIPT) as a unifying framework for immune escape and treatment failure. TIPT emerges from coordinated suppression by tumor-resident regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory B cells, M2-like macrophages, tolerogenic dendritic cells, and exhausted CD8? T cells, sustained by suppressive cytokine networks, metabolic deprivation, epigenetic fixation of dysfunctional states, and stromal-vascular exclusion barriers. Spatially organized tolerance niches are associated with immune evasion, metastatic seeding, and resistance to checkpoint blockade. Strategies targeting suppressive cell populations, metabolic pathways, chromatin regulators, and stromal barriers are in clinical development, but clinical benefit has been established for only a limited subset, and anti-TIGIT antibodies failed to meet primary endpoints in phase 3 lung cancer trials. Machine-learning models show promise for predicting tolerance states and guiding combination design, but prospective clinical validation is still needed. TIPT may represent an important, potentially actionable determinant of tumor evolution and immunotherapy response, and durable cancer control is likely to require combined strategies that dismantle this tolerance ecosystem.

Título: Decoding Alignment without Encoding Alignment: A Missing Component for Interpretability.
Resumen: RSA and CKA are standard metrics for comparing neural representations across brain regions, organisms, and deep learning models. We demonstrate a fundamental weakness: these decoding-based metrics are insensitive to <i>encoding manifold topology</i> - the internal functional organization of a neural population. In a controlled MNIST experiment, RSA, CKA, and Procrustes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow> <mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow> </msup> </math> remain statistically unchanged when encoding topology is causally manipulated via an auxiliary clustering loss, while the two model populations differ significantly in attribution patterns, weight-graph assortativity, and out-of-distribution robustness. Across biological systems and machine learning models, similar decoding behavior can arise from small, non-representative subpopulations, and alignment metrics are insensitive to encoding manifold topology even when it is fundamentally altered. These findings bear directly on mechanistic interpretability: standard alignment metrics cannot distinguish whether two networks share the same computational circuits or merely produce indistinguishable aggregate outputs. We propose encoding manifolds and Gromov-Wasserstein distance as complementary diagnostics for any decoding-based similarity claim, and provide a Neural Manifold Explorer tool for further experimentation.

Título: Credential farming in the age of generative AI: relocating trust from outputs to communities.
Resumen: Publications, affiliations and authorship positions began as proxies for qualities that cannot be observed directly: judgement, understanding and the capacity to contribute to shared inquiry. Generative artificial intelligence has weakened the inference those proxies depend on. Polished research outputs can now be produced by people who do not understand them, yet admissions committees and hiring panels still read an output as evidence of the competence that producing it once required. The result is faster credential farming, the extraction of the social trust held in credentials without contribution to the enterprise that gives them meaning. Refuse to convert those structures into new metrics. The argument matters most for researchers in low-resource settings, whose learning happens in informal spaces that credentialing systems do not see, and who are asked to make themselves legible in a vocabulary nobody taught them.

Prior machine learning models for OSA are heterogeneous, often developed on small or demographically narrow cohorts, frequently rely on physiologic signals that reintroduce a testing step, and are rarely validated across independent health systems.<b>What This Study Adds to the Field:</b> We developed machine learning models from routinely collected electronic health record data, comprising a full (106-feature) and a minimal (4-feature) model, to predict any OSA and moderate-severe OSA. The study is distinguished by multiple validation efforts, including temporal validation and external validation at a second health system. We further explored adaptation strategies for external adoption using transfer learning techniques. Finally, the models outperformed existing screeners such as STOP-BANG, and we describe a Bayesian framework that optionally incorporates select patient-reported symptoms to refine individual risk estimates. Título: MOSAIC: Learning Graph Node Embeddings from Spectrally Isolated Dominant Subspaces of Accumulated Diffusion Operators.
Resumen: Graph embedding transforms complex networks into low-dimensional representations for analysis and downstream machine learning. Existing methods often rely on eigenvalue ordering, random-walk sampling, or neural optimization. We introduce MOSAIC, Multistep Operator Spectral Accumulation with Isolated Components, an unsupervised framework that constructs an accumulated diffusion operator from successive powers of a graph transition matrix. MOSAIC uses Krylov subspace analysis to identify dominant spectral components according to their convergence behavior. This approach emphasizes persistent and spectrally separated diffusion modes rather than selecting embedding coordinates solely by eigenvalue magnitude. We evaluated MOSAIC using a biomedical graph projection derived from the Data Distillery Knowledge Graph that contained 5,171 human genes and 10,147 phenotypes. Across embedding dimensions from 16 to 128, MOSAIC achieved node-type classification AUROCs from 0.9863 to 0.9926 and exceeded FastRP, Node2Vec, HashGNN, and GraphSAGE. For gene-phenotype link prediction, validation and test associations were withheld before embedding generation. Under progressive removal of all edges or specific edge classes, MOSAIC retained more node-label information than FastRP, including after extreme graph sparsification. In a focused DICER1 analysis, 106 of 137 documented phenotype associations received scores above 0.90, demonstrating concordance with known pleiotropic biology and prioritizing additional relationships for independent evaluation. These results support MOSAIC as a fully unsupervised framework for learning informative graph representations. Although demonstrated using a biomedical graph projection, MOSAIC is domain independent and can be applied to other complex networks.

Título: Genotype-dependent behavioral signatures of opioid withdrawal revealed by automated behavioral quantification.
Resumen: Opioid withdrawal drives continued opioid use in opioid use disorder (OUD), which affected an estimated 4.8 million Americans in 2024. However, only one non-opioid medication is FDA-approved for withdrawal treatment, and there is great need for more diverse treatment options. Mice are powerful models to study opioid withdrawal because they allow for controlled drug and environmental exposure, express OUD-relevant phenotypes, and provide access to withdrawal-relevant tissue at exact time points. However, mouse models are hindered by their over reliance on a single genetic background (C57BL/6J). Using a single background risks limiting the translatability of preclinical studies as they are projected into genetically diverse human populations. Inferring withdrawal intensity in mice typically relies on single behaviors or indexes of behaviors, and applying these approaches across mouse genetic diversity faces a critical challenge: differing withdrawal responses could either encode differences in withdrawal severity, or differences in withdrawal-evoked behaviors independent of severity. To overcome this limitation, a more comprehensive assessment of opioid withdrawal behaviors across mouse genetic diversity is needed. Here we leverage computer vision and machine learning to automate the simultaneous quantification of many mouse behaviors during opioid withdrawal in eight diverse strains of mice. We reveal that all eight strains exhibit withdrawal-evoked behaviors, and these behaviors are sufficient to identify the withdrawal state of the mouse. However, the effect of withdrawal on individual behaviors or indexes of behaviors is not uniform across genetic diversity, and extending methods tuned in one strain risks misclassifying withdrawal in others. Finally our approach was able to distinguish graded withdrawal intensity, as defined by opioid exposure within 3 of 4 strains tested. We therefore conclude that opioid withdrawal behavior is profoundly shaped by genetic background, but withdrawal severity can nonetheless be established within a background. Combining automated computer-vision phenotyping with genotype-aware modeling provides a scalable path toward genetically informed withdrawal assessment in diverse mouse populations, with the ultimate goal of identifying the genetic and biological networks that modulate opioid withdrawal and may represent new targets for treating opioid use disorder.

Título: Imputation-Based Harmonization Mitigates Site Effects Without Data Leakage in Machine Learning Studies.
Resumen: Neuroimaging studies that pool data across clinical sites often suffer from site effects - variability in imaging measures that arises from technical heterogeneity across sites as opposed to true biological signal. We demonstrate that current approaches for integration either suffer from data leakage, fail to fully remove site effects from the target data, or attenuate true biological associations during the harmonization process. Resumen: Quantifying molecular complexity is a longstanding challenge with profound implications for chemical discovery, biological organization, and materials design. Wavefunction information was converted to Molden format and analyzed within the framework of the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) using Multiwfn. Bond, ring, and cage critical points together with associated topological properties were extracted from the electron density. The Quantum Assembly Index was constructed using custom Python implementations of graph-theoretic shortest-path algorithms and topological assembly contributions. Additional analyses included correlation, symmetry, ablation, ranking, contribution, and representative computational wall-time assessments.

Fourteen machine learning classifiers were evaluated, and the best-performing model was optimized and validated on the independent test set. Model performance was assessed using AUC, accuracy, recall, precision, F1 score, Kappa coefficient, and Matthews correlation coefficient. After LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression, 50 key features were retained. Random Forest showed the best preliminary performance and was selected for optimization. On the independent test set, the optimized model achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.9084, with favorable results across other metrics. Texture features contributed most strongly to prediction. This radiomics model enables robust preoperative ADG subtyping under the 2021 WHO classification and may support individualized surgical planning using routine MRI features. Owing to its retrospective single-center design, multicenter prospective external validation is required prior to widespread clinical application.
