Título: Pushing the Understanding of ns2 Lone-Pair Exposure in Zero-Dimensional Metal Halides: Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning Reveal Unseen Structural Controls of Emission.
Resumen: Combining density functional theory, ab initio molecular dynamics, machine learning, and excited-state analysis, we uncover structural factors governing ns2 lone-pair expression and emission across diverse inorganic and hybrid 0D metal halides, addressing an unresolved unified understanding of STE emission in high-symmetry systems, the stronger stereochemical activity of Sn than Pb, and halide-dependent energy-level alignment. We show that emission is controlled by valence-edge s-p mixing driven by lone-pair activation, with its extent governed by two distinct coordination-dependent structural modes. In highly coordinated octahedral systems, lone-pair exposure emerges through angular fluctuation-mediated transient off-centering, explaining finite luminescence in apparently centrosymmetric compounds. In lower-coordinate systems, intrinsic cage asymmetry produces persistent lone-pair exposure, often stabilized by organic cations, leading to stronger STE stabilization and enhanced emission. The higher stereochemical activity of Sn relative to Pb is rooted in greater dynamical structural degrees of freedom, opening more channels to activate the 5s2 lone pair. This coordination- and valence-shell-dependent effect is amplified in softer bromides with favorable energy-level alignment with ns2 cations. Overall, our results redefine the understanding of lone-pair stereochemistry, concluding that lone-pair stereochemistry in 0D metal halides is largely dynamical, activated by selective structural descriptors that govern excited-state localization and emission, providing a general design framework for efficient emitters.

Título: Enantioselective C-H Activations by Metallaelectro-Catalysis.
Resumen: Given the increasing awareness of the economic and environmental aspects of chemical syntheses, transformative catalysis platforms have emerged, with molecular electrocatalysis residing at the forefront. It enables sustainable oxidative transformations with high levels of energy efficiency and resource economy as well as scalability and inherent process safety. Hence, organic electrocatalysis has gained considerable momentum. Further, in terms of sustainable syntheses, the catalyzed activation of otherwise inert C-H bonds was identified as a particularly powerful strategy for the rapid assembly of chiral scaffolds, thereby preventing stoichiometric chemical waste. Despite indisputable advances, these strategies largely relied, until recently, on stoichiometric quantities of often expensive or toxic chemical oxidants. To this end, metallaelectro-catalysis has emerged as an enabling technology for C-H activations, using the traceless transfer of protons and electrons in lieu of chemical oxidants, while generating molecular hydrogen as the sole by-product via the synchronized hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Although distinct electrooxidative C-H activations were realized during the past decade, enantioselective electrochemical catalysis has thus far proven elusive. This Account summarizes our key advances until August 2026 in metallaelectro-catalyzed enantioselective C-H activation, streamlining the assembly of chiral molecules featuring various stereogenic elements. Thus, palladaelectro-catalyzed C-H alkenylation set the stage for oxidative C-H/C-H couplings toward atropochiral biaryls, leveraging chiral transient directing groups (TDGs). Subsequent research efforts have allowed us to broaden this platform. Since the pronounced complexity of the electrochemical space in these systems can complicate discovery and optimization, the implementation of a machine learning (ML) workflow was targeted. This was harnessed for the accelerated optimization of an enantioselective palladaelectro-catalyzed annulation reaction. Moreover, the versatility of rhodium catalysis in enantioselective electrochemical C-H activations was mirrored by the e construction of chiral spiropyrazolones and phthalides. Tailored ruthenium catalysts allowed for the selective buildup of atropostable indoles as well as chiral spirocyclic compounds. Taking into consideration the environmental implications and cost-efficacy of transition metal-catalyzed transformations, we further explored the utility of earth-abundant transition metals. On this note, enantioselective cobaltaelectro-catalysis enabled a broad range of highly efficient and enantioselective transformations, such as spirocyclizations, annulations with alkynes, allenes, and alkenes toward axial-, C-, and P-centered chirality, as well as decagram-scale synthesis realized in flow. The data-driven exploration of newly designed chiral ligands facilitated accelerated discovery in cobaltaelectro-catalyzed C-H activation. Moreover, cupraelectro-catalysis was employed for crafting planar chirality in ferrocene derivatives through versatile C-Het bond formations. Finally, we achieved an enantioselective desymmetrization through electrooxidative nickel catalysis inspired by ML, selectively constructing multiple contiguous stereocenters. Interestingly, comparative analysis revealed distinct reactivity for cobalt and nickel catalysts, whose mechanistic origins were elucidated.

ID (PMID): 42915802
Título: Design of an Intelligent Profiling Platform for Multiple Antibiotic Discrimination Enabled by Time-Resolved Histidine-Functionalized Cupric Oxide Nanozyme Sensor Array at Neutral pH.
Resumen: Nanozymes with peroxidase-like (POD) activity have broad applications in biosensing, but their catalytic activity is often optimal under acidic conditions, which severely limits their applications in neutral environments. Here, we constructed a histidine-functionalized cupric oxide (CuO@His) nanozyme via defect engineering. Relative to CuO, CuO@His exhibited enhanced POD activity at neutral pH and was capable of catalyzing 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) to generate blue oxidized TMB, which showed absorption peaks at 370 and 652 nm. Subsequently, we employed the recursive feature elimination strategy to screen the optimal wavelength-time combinations as the sensing channels and further established the characteristic "fingerprints" of different antibiotics. Moreover, with the assistance of machine learning algorithms, a concentration- and matrix-independent antibiotic identification model was established under neutral conditions. Finally, a visual intelligent sensing platform based on deep learning was constructed. This work provides a new strategy for the efficient identification of multiple antibiotics at neutral pH.


--- ARTÍCULO 2397 ---
ID (PMID): 42915723
Título: Transfer Learning Empowers the Development of Better-Performing Models for In Vivo Cardiotoxicity by Learning from In Vitro hERG Binding Data.
Resumen: Evaluating chemical hazards, such as cardiotoxicity, is critical for sound chemical management but is challenging due to the labor-intensive and time-consuming nature of in vivo testing. In silico models can efficiently and cost-effectively screen potential cardiotoxic compounds from a large number of chemicals. However, the available small-scale in vivo toxicity data sets prevent models from achieving superior prediction accuracy. Herein, a transfer learning-based graph neural network (TL-GNN) model for predicting in vivo cardiotoxicity was developed by fine-tuning from a pretrained model on a data set regarding the human ether-a-go-go-related gene binding, a molecular initiating event that may ultimately cause cardiotoxicity. The TL-GNN model not only outperformed the GNN without TL and classic machine learning models, but also those fine-tuned from GNN models pretrained on a nonmechanistic octanol-water partition coefficient data set and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers models pretrained on a data set with over a million unlabeled compounds. A structure-activity landscape-based method was adopted to characterize the applicability domains of the TL-GNN model. The TL-GNN model with defined applicability domains was applied to screen approximately 600,000 chemicals across diverse categories, identifying over 25,000 as cardiotoxic. The robustness of the TL-GNN model suggests the potential of the modeling strategy for complex in vivo toxicity by learning from adverse outcome pathway (AOP)-related in vitro targets.


--- ARTÍCULO 2398 ---
ID (PMID): 42915710
Título: Robust Chemometric Machine Learning Framework for Screening-Stage Triage in Antidoping Urine Analysis.
Resumen: Initial testing procedure (ITP) screening in antidoping requires rapid interpretation of high-throughput data under analytically complex and operationally demanding decision conditions. We developed a robustness-validated chemometric machine-learning framework─an integrated multivariate modeling workflow─for ITP triage using MassHunter-derived analyte-level peak-area response values for 148 GC-MS/MS analytes from 684 authentic urine casework samples, rather than raw GC-MS/MS chromatograms. Benchmarking 10,920 machine-learning pipelines, we selected a stacking-based ensemble optimized for rare-positive screening under severe class imbalance. On a fixed external-validation hold-out set (n = 137), the selected Rank 1 model achieved near-perfect recall across repeated evaluations. When applied post hoc to all 684 samples, the fixed implementation flagged all 56 reference-positive samples. SHAP analysis showed chemically meaningful analyte-response attribution patterns that were not determined solely by feature coverage. Covariate-adjusted analysis showed no independent association with sex, while exploratory sport analysis revealed no consistent sport-related pattern. This framework reduced estimated screening-review time by >99.8% relative to conventional manual review, providing scalable, interpretable support for prioritizing suspicious samples for expert review and confirmatory follow-up in routine regulatory antidoping laboratories.


--- ARTÍCULO 2399 ---
ID (PMID): 42915699
Título: Machine Learning-Assisted Discrimination of Isobaric Histone Acetylations by Nanopore.
Resumen: Histone acetylation, a post-translational modification, is associated with cancer progression, invasion, and metastasis, serving as a promising biomarker. The accurate discrimination of acetylation sites has strong potential for cancer diagnostics. Herein, we engineered an R220Q aerolysin nanopore to detect isobaric histone acetylations. By exposing the paired negative charge (D222) at the pore entrance, peptides with a higher positive charge density encounter a lower U* for pore entry and subsequent translocation. With the assistance of machine learning, we achieved direct discrimination of isobaric acetylations in histone peptides. Monoacetylated peptides H3K9ac and H3K14ac, as well as diacetylated peptides H3K4acK9ac and H3K4acK14ac were unambiguously identified in mixtures with identification accuracies of 99.4% and 98.8%, respectively. This work offers a label-free approach for analyzing acetylated biomarkers with potential applications in cancer detection and drug target development.

Título: Deep Learning-Enabled Interpretative SERS Analysis of Key Urinary Metabolites in Nephropathy Using Interfacial Charge-Engineered Silver Nanoparticles.
Resumen: The definitive diagnosis of kidney disease relies on the invasive gold-standard method of kidney biopsy, but this provides information only about local characteristics. In contrast, urine samples can be collected noninvasively and contain a variety of metabolites associated with kidney disease. However, obtaining high-quality, high-dimensional biological information and identifying specific diagnostic biomarkers in urine also pose significant challenges. This study developed a detection strategy that uses interface charge engineering with patient urine samples to diagnose diabetic nephropathy, IgA nephropathy, lupus nephritis, and nephrotic syndrome. Different sample types form biomolecular crowns of varying thicknesses at the detection interfaces. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) technology was employed to capture the urine metabolite fingerprints. We established a multiclassification model by combining urine spectral data with deep learning, conducted an interpretive analysis to clarify the basis for classification, and then used enrichment analysis to explore urinary metabolic information. This study establishes a highly sensitive, noninvasive, rapid, cost-effective, and patient-friendly classification method for kidney diseases, which is valuable for precision medicine.


--- ARTÍCULO 2401 ---
ID (PMID): 42915683
Título: Rapid Species-Level Classification of Urinary Pathogens from Raw LC-MS/MS Signals Using Machine Learning.
Resumen: Urinary tract infections are among the most common infections in humans, yet their diagnosis still depends on time-consuming workflows based on microbial culture, followed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Although LC-MS/MS offers the sensitivity and specificity needed to bypass culture, conventional pipelines depend on lengthy analyses and peptide/protein identification steps, limiting the throughput and hindering its adoption in clinical settings. Here, we introduce a direct, identification-free LC-MS/MS workflow that analyzes raw ion signal and produces species-level microbial identification in about 5 min after preparation, fast enough to meet clinical throughput requirements. Our machine learning-enabled raw-signal pipeline bypasses peptide identification entirely, preserving information and eliminating the traditional interpretation stack. Across 15 independent analytical batches covering 28 clinically relevant pathogens, the method achieved high-confidence classification (MCC = 0.86). Applied to 206 clinical urine specimens across three batches, the approach reached 91% accuracy at clinically actionable microbial loads (greater than 105 CFU/mL) and, critically, 0 false positives in control specimens. The performance was lower for specimens below this threshold. These results show that raw LC-MS/MS spectra contain sufficient biological information for direct microbial diagnosis, establishing an analytical framework for clinical mass spectrometry. This proof-of-concept demonstrates that rapid, culture-free, fast microbial identification is achievable and positions raw signal inference as a promising direction for next-generation diagnostic mass spectrometry.

ID (PMID): 42915680
Título: W-O-Ti Bridge Modulated MXene Heterostructures and Hydrogel Electrolytes Enable Asymmetric Machine-Learning Decoupling for Thermally Robust Molecular Quantification.
Resumen: Ambient temperature fluctuations impose a fundamental barrier to the field deployment of high-precision chemical sensors, as nonlinear thermal drift often overshadows subtle concentration-dependent signals. Here, we report a materials-to-algorithm paradigm that achieves intrinsic thermal robustness through interfacial engineering and asymmetric algorithmic compensation. We synthesize a W18O49-decorated MXene (MXene-W) cathode featuring strong W-O-Ti electronic coupling, which modulates the local electron density to stabilize redox kinetics against thermal perturbation. This is integrated with a carrageenan-polyacrylamide (CG-PAM) quasi-solid hydrogel electrolyte that ensures stable ion transport across a broad temperature window. Mechanistically, we uncover a critical asymmetry: bioluminescent transduction exhibits a pronounced nonlinear temperature dependence (combined Temp/Temp2 contribution of 0.35), surpassing the signal's intrinsic contribution, whereas electrochemical transduction is less temperature-sensitive. To resolve this, parallel response surface methodology streams feed into ensemble learners, effectively decoupling temperature-signal-concentration manifolds. The optimized platform achieves significant sensitivity and predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.9982). By deploying the inference pipeline as an offline application, we demonstrate cloud-free, on-site quantification of trace molecular analytes in complex matrices. This work provides a generalizable strategy for bridging nanoscale interfacial control with edge-intelligent computation to mitigate environmental noise in decentralized sensing networks.

Título: DeepCRISPR-Typer: Accurate CRISPR-Cas Identification and Subtyping in Metagenomes via Integrated Deep Learning.
Resumen: Accurate identification and classification of CRISPR-Cas systems are crucial for understanding microbial immune mechanisms and developing novel genome-editing tools. However, traditional homology-based mining methods face severe computational bottlenecks and assembly fragmentation challenges when processing massive metagenomic data. Here, we present DeepCRISPR-Typer, a comprehensive computational framework integrating a large protein language model (TEMC-Cas), a deep sequence feature extractor (CRISPR-RepTyper), and an adaptive targeted HMM profiling strategy. DeepCRISPR-Typer integrates array and Cas evidence and significantly reduces computational overhead by dynamically invoking subtype-specific HMM subsets. In metagenomic dataset evaluations, DeepCRISPR-Typer achieved a classification accuracy of 94.26% and demonstrated a significant acceleration of approximately 1 orders of magnitude compared to existing mainstream tools. This research provides a robust and scalable engine for metagenome-scale CRISPR system discovery, significantly expanding the mining toolbox for genome engineering applications.

Título: Harnessing Machine Learning for Enzyme Enantioselectivity: Toward Intelligent Biocatalysis Engineering.
Resumen: Enzyme enantioselectivity remains a central challenge in the biocatalytic synthesis of chiral pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals. Conventional evolution methods, constrained by prolonged experimental cycles and computationally intensive processes, struggle to comprehensively explore complex protein sequences. Although machine learning (ML) has been successfully applied to optimize enzymatic properties, such as catalytic efficiency and stability, its potential in enantioselectivity engineering remains underexploited. This review systematically evaluates how machine learning integrates multimodal datasets, including sequence, structural, and functional performance data, to advance the discovery and engineering of naturally enantioselective enzymes, and enable the de novo design of artificial enzymes for reaction-relevant applications. Overall, these advancements open new avenues for efficient chiral biosynthesis and provide theoretical foundations and technical blueprints for a paradigm shift toward intelligence-driven biocatalysis engineering.

Título: Engineering DNA-Targeting CRISPR and CRISPR-Like Effectors: Advances from Rational Design and High-Throughput Screening to AI-Driven Development.
Resumen: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and CRISPR-associated (Cas) proteins constitute adaptive immune systems in prokaryotes and have transformed life sciences, precision medicine, and synthetic biology as programmable genome-editing tools. Despite their broad utility, naturally occurring DNA-targeting Cas effectors remain constrained by several intrinsic limitations, including large protein size that complicates delivery, stringent protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements that restrict targetable genomic space, and mismatch tolerance that can lead to off-target activity and potential genotoxicity. These challenges have made Cas protein engineering and the discovery of novel CRISPR and CRISPR-like systems from metagenomic resources central to the development of next-generation genome-editing platforms. This Review places recent advances within an integrated synthetic biology engineering continuum that links natural effector discovery, structure-guided hypothesis generation, high-throughput functional screening, machine learning-enabled model construction, and iterative redesign. This Review summarizes progress in the screening, optimization, and functional engineering of DNA-targeting CRISPR and CRISPR-like effectors, with emphasis on structure-guided rational design, directed evolution coupled with high-throughput screening, bioinformatics- and evolution-guided mining of novel systems from large-scale sequence databases, and artificial intelligence-assisted development. By integrating these strategies, we highlight how CRISPR effector engineering is moving toward design-build-test-learn (DBTL)-inspired workflows that expand the functional landscape of genome-editing technologies and advance genome editing toward improved efficiency, safety, and programmability.

Título: Whole-Virus Screening Coupled with Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Enables Discovery of Virus-Binding scFvs.
Resumen: Discovery of virus-binding ligands against emerging viral pathogens is of broad interest for diagnostics and therapeutic development. Here, we present an integrated framework that combines whole-virus screening using yeast surface display with uncertainty-aware deep learning and in silico directed evolution for the discovery and optimization of virus-binding single-chain variable fragments (scFvs). Using dengue virus (DENV) as a model system, millions of scFv sequences obtained from iterative whole-virus selections were analyzed by an uncertainty-aware deep learning model to predict virus binding while quantifying prediction uncertainty. Guided by these predictions, an in silico directed evolution algorithm introduced targeted mutations within complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) to improve predicted binding together with developability-related properties, including solubility and humanness. Experimental validation demonstrated measurable DENV binding by two independently AI-designed scFvs, providing proof of concept for the proposed framework.

ID (PMID): 42915440
Título: Optimizing Ash Content in Biomass Hydrothermal Liquefaction through Machine Learning and Sustainability Assessment.
Resumen: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a highly promising thermochemical technology for converting wet biomass into bioliquid fuels. However, the effects of ash content in process performance and sustainability remain poorly understood. This study examined acid washing, alkali washing, and feedstock blending as methods for altering the ash content in a given biomass feedstock. Machine learning tools were employed in sustainability assessment for a 200 t/day plant, using life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis. Feedstock blending best reduced ash content (ash from 34.4 to 6.40 wt %). Ash content had opposing effects on product yield and oil quality. Across ash contents of 3.60-34.4 wt %, the oil higher heating value consistently rose, whereas oil yield initially increased then declined. The char yield followed an opposite trend. Integrated environmental and economic assessment identified 6.40 wt % ash as the optimal HTL condition for sludge and Chlorella. Under a boundary excluding biomass cultivation and harvesting, this condition gave an energy return on investment of 3.21 and a global warming potential of -317 kg CO2 eq/t dry biomass. The minimum fuel selling price was 0.517 $/L. These results show that reducing biomass ash content is not always advantageous. Feedstock blending demonstrated substantial benefits for large-scale oil production from high-ash biomass.


--- ARTÍCULO 2408 ---
ID (PMID): 42915432
Título: Predicting Bioconcentration Factors and Concentrations of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Plants with Machine Learning.
Resumen: Bioconcentration factors (BCF) and concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in crops were predicted by four machine learning models using a newly compiled data set composed of 11 crops, 11 plant tissue compartments, and 21 PFAS, as well as diverse soil properties and cultivation conditions. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best performance, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.951 for Log BCF and 0.943 for Log C. Feature importance analysis showed that soil pH and PFAS carbon chain length are key predictors of BCF. Soil PFAS concentration is the primary input feature for PFAS concentrations in plants and shorter growth-cycle plants accumulated higher PFAS concentrations. Root and leaf tissues were distinguished as the primary compartments of PFAS accumulation, exhibiting the highest BCF and concentration levels. Interestingly, although PFAS accumulation in plants generally shows a negative correlation with carbon chain length, root accumulation has a relatively weaker correlation with high levels of accumulation for both short-chain and long-chain PFAS. In contrast, above-ground tissues (particularly leaves) preferentially accumulate short-chain PFAS. These findings could provide valuable insights into the development of management and mitigation strategies to minimize PFAS accumulation in food crops and subsequently human exposure through the food chain.

Título: Ecological and Structural Drivers Underlying Species-Specific Estrogen Receptor α Responses to Estrogenic Chemicals in Mammals.
Resumen: Species-specific sensitivity to estrogenic chemicals complicates cross-species extrapolation in environmental risk assessment, yet its mechanistic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how ecological traits and amino acid variations in estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) mediate responses to estrogenic chemicals across mammals using an integrated New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) framework combining bioinformatics, in silico structural modeling, machine learning (ML), and in vitro transactivation assays. Two-way clustering of 169 mammalian ERα sequences and 107 ecological traits revealed distinct groupings associated with diet, habitat, and reproductive strategies. Homology model analysis showed that omnivorous species tend to possess larger ligand-binding pockets than carnivores and herbivores. In vitro assays of ERα from six mammalian species demonstrated substantial interspecies variability in response to natural and synthetic estrogenic chemicals. A cetacean-specific substitution from Asn to Ser at position 349 (corresponding to Asn349 in human ERα), which alters hydrogen bonding with Tyr537 in helix-12, was associated with aquatic lifestyles and altered receptor responsiveness. Additionally, ML models identified brain-to-body mass ratio as a candidate predictor of ERα-ligand binding domain sequence variation and ERα-mediated in vitro transactivation sensitivity across species. These findings identify ecological and structural drivers of species-specific estrogen sensitivity and provide a mechanistic framework for improving cross-species prediction of chemical effects in environmental risk assessment.

Título: Multisource Observation-Constrained Tuning for Air Quality Forecasting in a Machine Learning-Enhanced NOAA Unified Forecast System.
Resumen: Accurate near-real-time (NRT) air quality forecasting is critical for protecting public health but remains challenged by uncertainties in emissions, meteorology, and initial conditions within traditional chemical transport models (CTMs). We present an observation-driven machine learning framework that integrates multisource satellite products, including VIIRS aerosol optical depth and TEMPO NO2 with U.S. EPA AirNow measurements into a machine-learning surrogate of the NOAA Unified Forecast System (DeepAQM). A ConvLSTM-ResNet fusion module reconstructs spatially continuous surface PM2.5 and O3 fields from sparse observations, providing updated initial conditions for 72 h forecasts across the continental United States. DeepAQM reproduces UFS-AQM spatial patterns with strong agreement (R2 > 0.9 for O3 and up to 0.80 for PM2.5) while maintaining normalized mean bias within ±10%. Observation-updated initial conditions improve early forecast skill, increasing site-level R2 during the first 10 forecast hours from approximately 0.10-0.15 to 0.40-0.50 for PM2.5 and from approximately 0.40 to 0.50 for O3. Observation-based fine-tuning provides additional improvements throughout the 72 h forecast period, increasing overall R2 to 0.41 for PM2.5 and 0.82 for O3 during the independent evaluation period. These results demonstrate that integrating satellite and ground observations within DeepAQM can enhance NRT air quality forecasting and provide a scalable pathway toward globally deployable observation-driven prediction systems.

Título: High-Resolution Assessment of Terrestrial Carbon Storage and Restoration Benefits in China, 1990-2023.
Resumen: Terrestrial ecosystems serve as critical carbon sinks, playing an important role in the global carbon cycle and climate regulation. However, previous estimates of carbon storage in China's terrestrial ecosystems remain uncertain due to variability in data sources and methodological approaches. This study integrates multisource remote sensing data with extensive field-sampling data sets of carbon density, leveraging machine learning models to provide a comprehensive estimation of multiyear carbon storage and annual dynamics across multiple carbon pools. We estimated project-region carbon-stock changes using a scenario-based accounting framework. The total carbon storage, encompassing vegetation biomass and soil organic carbon, is estimated at 113.48 Pg C, with 20.4% in vegetation biomass and 79.6% in soil. National carbon stocks fluctuated over the study period but increased by 6.62 Pg C from 2014 to 2023. Scenario-based accounting indicates an additional baseline-adjusted project-region carbon-stock gain of 0.495 Pg C within major restoration regions during 2014-2023, equivalent to 0.050 Pg C yr-1. These results provide a high-resolution reconstruction of China's terrestrial carbon stocks and clarify recent carbon-stock changes across ecosystems, regions, and major restoration areas.

ID (PMID): 42915416
Título: From Detection toward Mitigation: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Methane Emissions Reduction.
Resumen: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas and a major contributor to near-term climate warming, yet emissions remain difficult to detect, quantify, and mitigate because they are spatially heterogeneous, temporally intermittent, and shaped by sector-specific measurement constraints. This review critically assesses artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) for methane monitoring and the translation of monitoring toward mitigation by synthesizing 63 studies published between 2018 and 2025, from which 93 model instances were coded across energy, agriculture/livestock, and waste management applications. We compare tree-based ensembles, classical machine learning methods, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, transformers, and hybrid/physics-guided architectures through a decision-oriented lens: data availability, validation type, uncertainty treatment, transferability, and operational relevance. Tree-based models remain attractive for structured predictors and interpretable driver ranking; deep learning dominates image- and video-based plume detection; and hybrid models are most useful when they fuse complementary sensors or enforce transport constraints. Across the reviewed evidence, AI/ML is most credible for screening and ranking large, persistent sources, while generalizable quantification of smaller, intermittent, or diffuse sources remains limited by wind uncertainty, small or proprietary training data sets, inconsistent metrics, and limited cross-region validation. Priorities for advancing AI-enabled methane mitigation include sector- and platform-specific benchmarks, calibrated uncertainty, physics-informed learning, explicit decision-support rules, and pilot demonstrations that measure avoided emissions rather than model accuracy alone.

Título: Long-Term Monitoring of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Interpretable Machine Learning Models for Methane Prediction in Dairy Cattle Slurry Storage.
Resumen: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from continuously filled dairy cattle slurry storage remain difficult to estimate under practical conditions. This study monitored methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, and slurry physicochemical properties for 15 months in laboratory-scale storage tanks designed to reproduce key features of on-farm storage, including continuous filling, farm-derived temperature dynamics, and periodic emptying events. N2O concentrations remained below 0.5 ppm and contributed negligibly to measured direct GHG emissions. In contrast, CH4 showed pronounced seasonal variability: 94.5% of annual CH4 emissions occurred during summer and autumn, whereas only 5.5% occurred during winter and spring. By combining cross-season monitoring with interpretable ML models, this study highlights the importance of long-term observations for characterizing CH4 emissions from continuously filled dairy cattle slurry storage estimation and targeted mitigation.

Título: Unveiling the Promoting Mechanism of Humic Acid in Photocatalysis via Bismuth Heavy-Atom Effect.
Resumen: Humic acid (HA) can contribute to photochemical transformation of organic pollutants in natural waters via triplet-excited states (3HA*). However, in HA-containing water matrices for practical photocatalytic treatment (e.g., surface waters or wastewater effluents), HA is conventionally regarded as a persistent inhibitor; its rapid quenching of reactive species dominates the process, while the beneficial 3HA* pathway remains restricted by spin-forbidden singlet-to-triplet conversion. Herein, a heavy-atom-effect-driven molecular assembly with a bismuth catalyst was designed to overcome the spin-forbidden barrier limiting 3HA* formation. This strategy converted HA into an in situ promoter and increased antibiotic degradation by 4.24-fold. The catalyst formed a close-contact electron donor-acceptor (EDA) complex with HA, through which the bismuth heavy-atom effect enhanced spin-orbit coupling in attached HA, accelerated intersystem crossing, and raised 3HA* steady-state concentration by 12.1-fold. Explainable machine learning and multidimensional spectroscopy further revealed the molecular selectivity of this enhanced pathway, showing that higher-molecular-weight HA components rich in oxygenated groups and conjugated aromatic skeletons preferentially participated in the Bi3-P-enhanced photochemical process and were transformed into smaller products. The mechanism was validated in real water matrices, indicating that heavy-atom-enabled intersystem crossing can be leveraged to improve photocatalytic tolerance to organic backgrounds and guide photochemical design for water treatment.

Título: Enhancing Global Cropland Soil Organic Carbon Stability Through Integrated Management Practices.
Resumen: The ratio of mineral-associated organic carbon to particulate organic carbon (MAOC:POC) can serve as an indicator for assessing relative soil organic carbon (SOC) stability, which is closely linked to climate change mitigation and sustainable agriculture. However, the potential for enhancing relative SOC stability in global croplands, and the corresponding optimized integrated management strategies, remain unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning model that captured the interactions among cropland management practices, soil, and climate factors using a compiled global data set of 2,029 field observations, enabling systematic geospatial analysis of MAOC:POC across croplands worldwide. Título: Data-Mechanism Fusion for Deep Learning-Enabled Membrane Performance Prediction and Material Discovery.
Resumen: Deep learning (DL) and related data-driven models are increasingly being used to predict membrane performance, guide material discovery, and optimize membrane processes. However, membrane separation is governed by coupled effects of material structure, solute properties, interfacial interactions, transport mechanisms, and operating conditions, making purely data-driven prediction difficult to generalize across membrane systems and water matrices. This review examines data-mechanism fusion as a membrane-science-oriented framework that integrates experimental data, molecular simulations, material databases, imaging information, process time-series data, and physicochemical knowledge throughout the modeling workflow. We first summarize membrane data types and assess how feedforward, convolutional, graph-based, recurrent, Transformer, and hybrid architectures align with data modalities and tasks. We then review recent progress in ion-selective separation, micropollutant and emerging contaminant removal, membrane material screening and inverse design, fouling diagnosis, and operational optimization. Particular attention is given to how mechanistic descriptors, physical constraints, hybrid coupling, simulation-informed surrogates, and closed-loop learning improve model reliability and interpretability. Finally, we discuss persistent challenges, including data scarcity, data set heterogeneity, limited transferability, uncertainty quantification, weak physical interpretability, and the gap between computational prediction and experimental or pilot-scale validation. Título: Benchmarking on-the-Fly Machine Learning Force Fields for Ion Hydration: Structure, Coordination, and Exchange Dynamics across Monovalent and Divalent Cations.
Resumen: Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) promise ab initio accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost of first-principles simulation, yet their fidelity for aqueous ion hydration across chemically diverse cation series remains systematically underexplored. Here, we benchmark an on-the-fly MLFF (OT-MLFF) framework, implemented in VASP via kernel-based Bayesian regression with adaptive DFT calls triggered when the estimated force error exceeds a set threshold, together with the pretrained, equivariant MACE foundation model applied off-the-shelf, against ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD; CP2K, PBE-D3) and classical MD (CMD; Madrid-2019/TIP4P-2005) for aqueous solutions of Li+, Na+, K+, Cs+, Mg2+, and Ca2+. MACE tracks AIMD most closely overall, its principal bias being a residual overcoordination of K+ and undercoordination of Cs+ in the diffuse monovalent shells. Angular distribution functions confirm accurate reproduction of the rigid octahedral geometry of Mg2+ but reveal systematic OT-MLFF smoothing of three-body features for more labile shells, including the O-Na-O shoulder near 65-70° and the O-Ca-O peak angle. Velocity autocorrelation functions reveal a related failure, the OT-MLFF underestimating the cooperative cage confinement of the large monovalent ions Cs+ and K+. In each of these cases, the pretrained MACE model recovers the AIMD behavior that the on-the-fly potential misses. Collectively, these results establish that the OT-MLFF is robust for an equilibrium solvation structure but fails for three-body angular sensitivity and exchange kinetics in chemically distinct edge cases and that a deeper, higher-body-order, pretrained model such as MACE systematically narrows these gaps even without system-specific training. Targeted improvements such as augmented transition-state sampling, higher angular-resolution descriptors, and long-range electrostatic corrections are identified as high-priority directions for kinetic fidelity in next-generation electrolyte force fields.

Título: Progress and Future Directions for Protein Corona Research.
Resumen: The protein corona refers to the proteins that adsorb on the surface of nanoparticles (NPs) exposed to biological environments. Proteins are described by many features reflecting size, structure, and sequence. The methods used to form and isolate the protein corona include how the NPs and proteins are combined and separated. The protein corona is often characterized by concentration, the amount of protein adsorbed on the NP, and composition, the inventory of proteins present in the corona. Determining the composition of the protein corona is the first step in understanding the underlying chemistry, physics, and biology that governs this nano-bio interaction. This review will first discuss the NP, protein, and experimental details that control the formation of the protein corona with a focus on unexpected details. I then discuss the biological complexity that impacts protein corona experiments. This includes the inherent complexity of biological fluids used to form the protein corona, the evolution of the corona as it moves through a biological system, and the influence of disease state on the protein corona. Corona formation depends on a highly multidimensional experimental space that lends itself to the tools of machine learning. We highlight our work in this area with modest success predicting the protein corona and point toward limitations in this area related to data sharing and overall goals in the field. In addition to this fundamental research on the nano-bio interface, two applications in protein corona research are discussed: the use of the protein corona as a diagnostic tool and corona-driven in vivo responses. In addition, I hope to highlight the value of in-person discussions for scientific progress.

Título: Evaluating Circle-Tracing Performance Using Machine Learning in a Haptic Interaction Framework.

So far, existing biomarkers of apple intake remain limited in terms of practical applicability. This study aimed to identify urinary biomarkers of apple intake with extended detection windows, compare their postprandial kinetics, and develop a multi-biomarker panel for identifying recent apple consumers. A randomized, controlled, crossover dietary intervention was conducted in 18 healthy adults. After a 2-day standardized run-in period, participants completed single-exposure, repeat-exposure and follow-up phases. XGBoost machine learning models were applied to establish an optimal multi-biomarker panel for assessing apple intake under free-living conditions. Five distinct metabolites were identified as candidate urinary biomarkers for apple intake. These metabolites remained significantly elevated at 24 h. In parallel, 28 early-responsive metabolites were discovered within the 0-6 h postprandial phase, which included several previously reported apple biomarkers, such as phloretin-2'-O-glucuronide. Individual metabolites showed limited predictive performance under free-living conditions, whereas a four-metabolite panel achieved the best discriminative performance (AUC = 0.80) for predicting apple consumption within 1-2 days compared to other panels. This study identified urinary biomarkers of apple intake with a detection window extending to at least 24 h and established a multi-biomarker panel for identifying recent apple intake.

Resumen: Negation in radiology reports (eg, "no evidence of dissection") is essential for accurately conveying diagnostic information. Transformer models have advanced detection capabilities but require costly expert labeling. Large language models (LLMs) may provide label-efficient alternatives through few-shot prompting or knowledge distillation. This study aims to systematically evaluate LLMs and transformer models under different supervision strategies, including comparisons of expert-labeled and LLM-distilled transformers, teacher LLMs (GPT-5.3 Chat, Gemma 4, and Qwen3.6-Plus), sampling approaches, and direct few-shot LLM inference, to determine whether LLM inference or LLM-based distillation can substitute for human labeling in radiology-report negation detection while reducing annotation costs. Teacher model choice had minimal effect on distilled performance. All 3 human-labeled transformer backbones (BERT, ALBERT, and Bio_ClinicalBERT) achieved high keyword-level F1-scores (0.982-0.985 under their best conditions; n=4200). In the 10-shot setting, GPT-5.3 Chat (F1-score 0.974) modestly underperformed human-labeled transformers in the large-sample range (ΔF1-score=0.009; adjusted P=.047) and significantly outperformed Gemma 4 (F1-score 0.957; adjusted P=.01) and Qwen3.6-Plus (F1-score 0.950; adjusted P<.001) in the bootstrap analysis. GPT-5.3 Chat labeled reports at approximately US $0.018 per report and became less expensive than manual annotation when expert hourly wages exceeded US $0.64-1.50. Human-supervised transformers remain the strongest baseline, but frontier LLMs such as GPT-5.3 Chat offer comparable performance with minimal supervision. LLM-based distillation offers a cost-effective alternative with only minor performance loss. Dataset scale proved more influential than sampling strategy. Additionally, superior teacher performance yielded no proportional gains through distillation, as open-weight or low-cost teachers achieved comparable results. If supported by external validation, the proposed label-efficient framework could enable accurate and affordable negation detection and rapid domain adaptation.

Título: HuKSA: A Machine-Learning-Based Framework for Predicting Human Kinome Selectivity and Polypharmacology.

Título: Dy/ZrO<sub>2</sub> synergy modulates sulfonic acid sites of flour-derived carbon for biodiesel preparation.
Resumen: A rare earth/ZrO<sub>2</sub> modified solid acid catalyst was prepared using flour as the carbon source and applied to produce biodiesel from waste cooking oil. Results show that ZrO<sub>2</sub> doping modulates graphitization to stabilize [C-SO<sub>3</sub>H] formation, but causes over-graphitization and low-valence sulfur accumulation, reducing -SO<sub>3</sub>H anchoring sites. Intriguingly, Dy doping concurrently suppresses excessive graphitization and blocks low-valence sulfur formation, such that the Dy/ZrO<sub>2</sub> synergy markedly elevates the acid content of carbon material to 5.25 mmol/g compared to that of the unmodified catalyst (3.75 mmol/g). Under optimal conditions (catalyst amount of 6 wt%, MOMR of 24, at 104 °C for 4h), the reaction conversion achieved 99.95 % and maintained > 95 % after six cycles. RSM, ANN and SVR models agreed well with the experimental results, and can be used for process optimization and prediction. Notably, kinetic studies reveal an activation energy(E<sub>a</sub>) of 142.688 kJ·mol<sup>-1</sup> and a pre-exponential factor(A) of 6.17213 × 10<sup>19</sup>h<sup>-1</sup>. The E-factor and PMI could decrease from 2.8734 to 0.7058 and from 3.8734 to 1.7058, respectively, and no heavy-metal or sulfur impurities, confirming economic and environmental feasibility. This work may provide a strategy for preparing of metal modified carbon-based solid acid and a reference for biodiesel process modeling.

Título: Spatial patterns, source apportionment, and environmental correlates of soil potentially toxic elements in an arid high-altitude mining area of Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China.
Resumen: Disentangling mining-related inputs from heterogeneous geological backgrounds remains difficult in arid mining regions. We analyzed eight potentially toxic elements (PTEs; As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in 155 surface-soil samples from an arid, high-altitude mining area in Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China. A staged framework combined a self-organizing map (SOM), improved absolute principal component scores-multiple linear regression (APCS-MLR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify multielement patterns, estimate potential-source contributions, and characterize nonlinear environmental associations. SOM resolved localized Cd-Pb-Zn co-enrichment, with class C3 concentrated near the waste-rock dump and processing plant. APCS-MLR separated five potential-source signals: mining-traffic Cd-Zn, mixed Hg-As deposition/agricultural, Ni parent-material, mixed Cr-Cu parent-material/industrial, and Pb traffic-deposition. In the 105 robust samples used for the final Huber-regression branch, F1 and F4 accounted for mean contributions of 29.7% and 27.5%, respectively. Spatial out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation of downstream LightGBM models identified F1 as the most stable factor (pooled OOF R<sup>2</sup> = 0.36; positive R<sup>2</sup> in all five folds), and its estimated contribution decreased with distance from the mining area. A full-sample, uncertainty-weighted, five-factor positive matrix factorization (PMF) sensitivity analysis recovered one-to-one correspondence with the APCS-MLR structure (cosine similarities, 0.724-0.977); all five profiles matched at cosine similarity ≥ 0.80 in 93% of bootstrap resamples. SHAP associations for F2-F5 remained exploratory because their spatial stability was weak. By separating pattern identification, statistical source apportionment, and association interpretation, the staged evidence chain supports targeted monitoring and improves the robustness of source-oriented environmental assessment in arid mining regions.

Título: Development and Evaluation of a Two-Stage Machine Learning Multivariable Model to Support Clinical Decision-Making in Thrombophilia Management.
Resumen: Thrombophilia is a disease characterized by an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. In this single-center, retrospective study, we evaluated the use of a two-stage machine learning (ML) model to predict the thrombophilia risk category and subsequent anticoagulation recommendation. The model was trained and tested using clinical and laboratory data obtained from 496 patients who underwent a complete thrombophilia work-up at the University Hospital Bonn between 2019 and 2024. The hybrid nature of the diagnostic categories, which combine ordinal classes including thrombophilia diagnosis, severity, and treatment recommendations and categorical classes (e.g. antiphospholipid syndrome), necessitated a two-stage approach. First, XGBClassifier was used to distinguish between the two classes, and then an ordinal-specific XGBOrdinalV2 model was used. Performance was assessed across 100 random 80/20 train-test splits. For exact class prediction (primary analysis), mean macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, and precision were 58%, 91%, and 56.2% for diagnosis and 54.4%, 91.3%, and 58.5% for treatment. Performance was highest for frequent classes and poor for rare high-risk classes. When predictions within one adjacent class were accepted (secondary analysis), macro-averaged sensitivity was 91.9% and 86.2%, respectively. Antiphospholipid antibody status, age at first thrombosis, and unprovoked thrombosis were the most influential features for diagnosis. Model predictions and physician decisions were concordant in 395 of 496 patients (79.6%). This study demonstrates that ML models can support standardized thrombophilia management and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

Título: Machine Learning Integrating Quantitative MRI and Clinical Features Predicts Loss of Ambulation in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
Resumen: Loss of ambulation (LOA) is a key milestone in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) with highly variable timing, complicating clinical counselling and trial design. Quantitative MRI non-invasively assesses muscle fat infiltration, yet few models have integrated MRI with clinical variables for individualized LOA prediction. We aimed to develop and validate a machine-learning model integrating quantitative MRI and clinical features to predict time to LOA and to derive interpretable, individualized risk estimates and candidate thresholds. This prospective study enrolled 188 boys with DMD (median age 9.10 years). Quantitative MRI parameters (T1, T2, fat fraction [FF]) of 19 hip/thigh muscles and clinical variables were measured. Patients were randomly split into training (80%) and test (20%) sets. Feature selection used LASSO, Boruta and recursive feature elimination based on random survival forest (RSF). Three survival models were compared: RSF and a ridge-penalised Cox model (both integrating clinical and MRI-derived features) and a multivariable Cox model restricted to clinical variables. Performance was assessed by concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), integrated Brier score (IBS) and decision curve analysis at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months. Over median 43.5 months follow-up, 66 patients (35.1%) experienced LOA. Six predictors were retained: NSAA score, MRC%, age and three FF parameters (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, obturator internus). In the test set (n = 40, 15 events), RSF achieved a C-index of 0.870 (95% CI, 0.764-0.957), outperforming the clinical Cox (0.804) and ridge Cox (0.853) model. Time-dependent AUCs of the RSF model were 0.984, 0.971, 0.913 and 0.850 at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months. RSF showed the best calibration, with the lowest IBS (0.076, 95% CI: 0.052-0.111), followed closely by the ridge Cox model (0.078) and the clinical Cox model (0.109). RSF stratified patients into low-risk, intermediate-risk and high-risk groups; no LOA events occurred in the low-risk group, with annual event rates were 7.2% and 34.6% in the intermediate- and high-risk groups (log-rank p = 0.0025). SHAP analysis identified exploratory thresholds (NSAA < 14.55, MRC% < 68.36%, rectus femoris FF > 32.30%, vastus lateralis FF > 58.00%, obturator internus FF > 7.43%). An interactive web application enables individualized risk prediction (https://westcndmd-timer-loa-risk-prediction-tool-8cygtrrbykvd9snmfcnhrp.streamlit.app/). A machine-learning-based RSF model integrating quantitative MRI FF metrics and clinical variables exhibited favourable predictive performance for time to LOA in DMD across short- and long-term horizons. It provided interpretable, individualized risk estimates and was deployed as an online tool to support clinical decision-making and trial enrichment.

Título: Transistor Biosensors: A Path to Accessible, Minimally Invasive Early Screening for Alzheimer's Disease.
Resumen: Current clinical diagnostic approaches for Alzheimer's disease (AD), including positron emission tomography and cerebrospinal fluid testing, face limitations related to invasiveness, high cost, and restricted accessibility. The identification of blood biomarkers, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and phosphorylated tau (p-tau) proteins, has arisen as a potential avenue for noninvasive, scalable, and cost-effective early screening. Transistor biosensors offer a compelling technological platform in this study. Capitalizing on ultrahigh sensitivity, rapid response, label-free operation, and potential for miniaturization and integration, these devices have demonstrated effectiveness in detecting ultralow concentrations of AD pathological proteins in blood, surpassing the detection limits of conventional method. This review systematically outlines the operational mechanisms of transistor biosensors and discusses performance optimization strategies. It further summarizes transformative advances in detecting key AD biomarkers, including Aβ proteins and p-tau isoforms, and highlights innovative directions such as multiplexed biomarker detection and machine learning-assisted diagnostic interpretation. Such integrated systems hold considerable potential to enable early risk warning, longitudinal monitoring, and precise, personalized intervention strategies for AD. Therefore, transistor biosensor represents a paradigm shift toward accessible, dynamic, and precision biomarker profiling, paving the way for next-generation AD screening and management frameworks.

Título: Transformer networks are robust learners of source localization for EEG measurements.
Resumen: EEG source localization is an ill-posed inverse problem complicated by measurement noise, electrode dropout from sensor miscalibration, and variability in the number of active sources. Classical methods such as eLORETA and LCMV beamforming impose regularization assumptions that degrade under realistic noise conditions and do not naturally extend to multi-source scenarios. Recent neural network approaches improve localization accuracy but are typically trained and evaluated under idealized conditions that limit their applicability to real-world EEG acquisition. This work aims to develop and evaluate a source localization model that generalizes across the noise levels, source counts, and electrode configurations encountered in clinical and experimental EEG settings.&#xD;&#xD;Approach: We present a transformer-based model for single- and multi-source EEG localization. Hundreds of thousands of simulated EEG measurements are generated from known source locations, spanning a range of noise levels, source counts, and electrode dropout configurations, to train and evaluate the model. We establish a systematic evaluation framework that explicitly factors in source region density, signal-to-noise ratio, and electrode availability, and benchmark the transformer against classical (eLORETA, LCMV beamforming) and deep learning baselines across these conditions. We additionally conduct a thorough ablation study on network architecture and training pipeline design.&#xD;&#xD;Main results: Across all tested conditions, the transformer consistently outperforms classical and deep learning approaches, with improvements as high as 12\,mm in mean localization error (MLE) for multi-source scenarios under high noise. Additionally, when number of sources is unknown, the transformer can correctly predict the number and location of sources and drastically out perform the threshold-based approach (e.g an F1 Score of 68\% vs 12\% when simulated at 25\% noise). The multiembedding transformers maintains reasonable performance under conditions such as electrode dropout and increased noise.&#xD;&#xD;Significance: By explicitly modeling the noise, electrode dropout, and multi-source variability that characterize real EEG acquisition, this work addresses a key gap between benchmark performance and experimental utility in EEG source localization. These results lay the groundwork for more robust localization techniques applicable to real EEG data, with potential relevance to applications such as brain-computer interfaces. The data and code for this work will be made publicly available to support further development and benchmarking in the field.

Título: A language-model approach to species distribution reveals alternative stable states.

ID (PMID): 42913562
Título: Domain-Wall-Mediated Ultralow-Barrier Sliding and Pinning in Ferroelectric Moiré Superlattices Revealed by Machine Learning.
Resumen: Sliding ferroelectrics built from stacked nonpolar monolayers enable out-of-plane polarization and unconventional switching via interlayer sliding, yet the microscopic sliding dynamics remain unclear. Using machine-learning molecular dynamics, we reveal spontaneous, thermally driven interlayer sliding in ferroelectric MoS2 moiré superlattices, with relative velocities on the order of 1 m/s at 300 K. Instead of rigid translation of the entire bilayer, the motion appears as a global drift of the moiré pattern. Such thermally driven sliding is inconsistent with a meV/atom-scale rigid-sliding barrier. In contrast, when constrained relaxation is allowed, the sliding proceeds along an almost barrierless pathway that directly reproduces the global drift of the moiré pattern. Furthermore, sulfur vacancies trigger a sliding-to-pinning transition, with ∼0.1% S vacancies already sufficient to convert the long-range sliding into localized oscillations. This pinning originates from the stacking-dependent vacancy energy, whose minimum at the nodes of domain-wall networks defines pinning centers, as further supported by the dynamical sliding-to-pinning process. Energetic analysis attributes the thermally driven sliding-to-pinning transition to competition between defect-induced pinning and moiré deformation. These results reveal that the sliding process in strongly reconstructed moiré superlattices is governed by a domain-wall-mediated collective reconstruction pathway with an ultralow barrier, rather than rigid layer translation, deepening the understanding of microscopic dynamics in moiré superlattices and sliding ferroelectrics.

ID (PMID): 42913540
Título: Revealing the Proton Slingshot Mechanism in Solid Acid Electrolytes through Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics.
Resumen: In solid acid electrolytes CsH2PO4 and CsHSO4, the origin of fast proton conduction has long been debated, attributed either to local proton hopping or to polyanion rotation. However, the precise role of polyanion rotation and its interplay with proton hopping remains unresolved. Nanosecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations, driven by equivariant neural-network force fields, reveal a nuanced proton slingshot mechanism: a rotating polyanion first carries the proton, O-H bond reorientation then extends its displacement, and the combined motion enables long-range jumps. This mechanism refines the conventional Grotthuss-type picture, revealing that long-range transport arises from significant O-H bond reorientation assisted by only limited polyanion rotation. Despite their structural similarity, CsH2PO4 and CsHSO4 exhibit qualitatively different transport behavior associated with their distinct proton concentrations. In CsH2PO4, two rotation rates with different activation energies emerge, while CsHSO4 displays a single-rate process with faster productive polyanion dynamics. The higher proton concentration in CsH2PO4 is associated with greater rotational frustration and slower dynamics of PO4 compared with SO4 in CsHSO4. In CsH2PO4, we further identify a unique correlation between oxygen sharing and proton transport, arising from the extra proton per polyanion. Together, our findings establish a unified framework linking polyanion rotation, proton coordination, and long-range transport, and suggest that tuning proton concentration could accelerate rotation and enhance conductivity.

Título: Discovery of Electron-Neutral Electrides with Pressure-Induced Superconductivity.
Resumen: Electrides have been largely restricted to electron-rich compositions, leaving the applications of electron-neutral electrides scarcely explored and poorly understood. Here we report the discovery of an electron-neutral ternary electride, LiAlGe, which undergoes an unusual pressure-driven evolution: a semiconducting, nonelectride F4̅3m-LiAlGe phase at ambient conditions transforms into metallic electride phases, F4̅3m- (6.4-13.7 GPa) and Cmmm-LiAlGe phase (13.7-40.0 GPa). First-principles calculations further predict superconductivity in both high-pressure phases. To extend this concept, we combined high-throughput computation with machine learning (ML) to identify ten additional electron-neutral electrides adopting the LiAlGe-type topology. ML analysis reveals that the cooperative interplay between distinct cation species and their atomic radii is a key descriptor governing electride formation in ternary neutral systems. We synthesized LiAlGe and experimentally verified its high-pressure behavior. Synchrotron X-ray measurements confirmed the predicted F4̅3m to Cmmm transition at 14.3 GPa, in excellent agreement with the calculated 13.7 GPa. Importantly, both high-pressure phases were found to be superconducting under appropriate pressures, validating the theoretical predictions and establishing electron-neutral electrides as a previously overlooked class of superconducting materials.

These results highlight the potential for data-driven approaches to enhance patient selection and optimize surgical decision-making in the treatment of CSM.

Título: Ultraflexible Multimodal Sensors with Stable Physical Sensing and Disposable Electrochemical Calibration for Long-Term Glucose Prediction.
Resumen: Wearable electrochemical biosensors offer direct biochemical readouts but often suffer from enzyme deactivation, biofluid fluctuation, fouling, and calibration drift during prolonged on-body use. Furthermore, in individual on-body tracking over one day and 15 days, the glucose predictions achieved an accuracy of at least 80%. This stable-physical-sensing/disposable-electrochemical-calibration architecture provides a practical strategy for personalized glucose prediction while mitigating the long-term instability of wearable electrochemical biosensors.

Título: From detection to prediction: AI-integrated molecular and biosensing approaches for psychrotrophic and thermophilic spoilage bacteria in dairy systems.
Resumen: Psychrotrophic Gram-negative bacteria and thermophilic or thermoduric spore-forming bacteria are major causes of quality deterioration and shelf-life loss in milk and dairy products. Their impact is mediated primarily by heat-stable peptidases and lipases, heat-resistant spores and biofilms that persist in processing environments; with the notable exception of toxigenic members of the Bacillus cereus group, most of these organisms are spoilage rather than safety hazards. Culture-based methods remain the reference standard but are slow and provide single time-point information. This review critically evaluates molecular and sensing methods, including quantitative and digital PCR, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-Cas assays, biosensors, viability assays, spectroscopy and (meta)omics, with explicit attention to whether performance has been demonstrated in naturally contaminated dairy matrices rather than in buffer or spiked samples, and examines how their outputs could inform predictive microbiology and machine learning. Validated dairy applications currently exist mainly for individual detection assays and for mechanistic or stochastic shelf-life models driven by culture-derived data; prospective, validated workflows in which molecular or biosensor outputs are used as model inputs to forecast spoilage have not yet been reported. Because heat-stable enzymes can spoil ultra-high-temperature products after the producing cells have been inactivated, viable counts alone are insufficient predictors of such defects. Key barriers include matrix effects, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, limited external validation and poorly defined intended use. Detection-to-prediction integration should therefore be regarded as an emerging research direction rather than an established industrial capability.

CatBoost achieved the highest interpolation accuracy (R<sup>2</sup>=0.9488), but unconstrained models and SoftPINN produced predictions that violated mass-balance bounds. HardPINN adapted an established constrained-output parameterization to the sample-specific adsorption bound, eliminating prediction-level mass-balance violations while retaining competitive accuracy (R<sup>2</sup>=0.9286). For the four group-wise evaluated models, transfer was relatively stable across water matrices and partial across chemical identities, whereas all four yielded negative median R<sup>2</sup> values for held-out adsorbent fingerprints (descriptor combinations excluded from training). These results indicate poor transfer to held-out adsorbent fingerprints for the four tested models, without implying corresponding behavior for GPR, FT-Transformer, or SoftPINN. The observed failure under joint distribution shift was consistent with incomplete, mechanism-relevant material descriptors, although material-level and source-level effects could not be separated. This biochar case study integrates an adsorption-specific, sample-dependent feasible output range with assessments of prediction error, physical admissibility and out-of-distribution transfer. Broader applicability to other adsorbent classes remains a hypothesis requiring class-specific external validation.

Título: T-ANALYZE as a Workflow for Matched Molecule Pair Analysis on Peptides.
Resumen: Matched molecular pairs (MMP) is an approach to finding local changes in structure that give rise to consistent changes in activity. Assuming molecules A and B are in a matched pair, one can imagine a "transformation", i.e., adding, removing, or exchanging a small set of atoms that changes A to B. Typical machine-learning algorithms are meant to handle individual molecules A, and model the activity difference between A and the average activity, and are agnostic to the presence of similar compounds in the training set. In contrast, MMP looks for differences between similar compounds A and B and is agnostic to the absolute value of the activities of A and B. Machine learning models tend to be poor at predicting activity cliffs, while MMP is designed to identify them. Previously, we (Sheridan et al., J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2006, 46, 180-192) suggested a workflow T-ANALYZE that organizes and displays sets of closely related drug-sized compounds such that any consistent MMP-based structure-activity in a data set can be easily seen. Nowadays, peptides are under consideration as candidate drugs and the MMP approach should be extended to them. Peptides are small enough that they can be treated as connection tables, i.e., atoms connected with bonds. Alternatively, they can be written as sequences, i.e., a one-dimensional list of monomer names. In this paper, we adapt the T-ANALYZE workflow to peptides represented both as connection tables and as sequences. We demonstrate this on the PAMPA activity of the CycPeptMPDB dataset.

Título: MARS-RNA: An Automated Pipeline for Correlating RNA Molecular Dynamics Trajectories with Chemical Probing Data.

Chemical probing methods, such as SHAPE (selective 2'-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension), provide structural insights in the form of one-dimensional (1D) nucleotide reactivity profiles. However, mapping these one-dimensional profiles back to the underlying dynamic structures remains a key challenge, as traditional analyses rely on a static view based on three-dimensional (3D) high-resolution structures from X-ray crystallography or nuclear magnetic resonance, rather than accounting for the dynamic nature of the system. In this Application Note, we introduce MARS-RNA (Molecular dynamics Analysis for Reactivity and Structure), an automated pipeline that extracts and integrates multiscale structural and geometric features from RNA Molecular Dynamics (MD) trajectories, combining them with secondary (2D) and 3D annotations from X3DNA-DSSR to identify features that correlate with experimental reactivity. MARS-RNA processes raw GROMACS trajectories, performs frame-by-frame structural annotation, calculates spatial centroids and physical distance fluctuations, computes Pearson/Spearman correlation coefficients against SHAPE data, and preprocesses results for machine learning pipelines. We show its value on the RNA 3'-UTR (PDB ID: 1AUD, chain A), by highlighting several single correlation with SHAPE reactivity.

Título: AGENTi: APCI-ESI Analyte Ionization Fidelity Pre-Screening Workflow using Multimodel Inference.
Resumen: Ionization sources convert neutral analytes into ions, enabling their subsequent separation and detection by mass spectrometry. Depending on the technique, this mechanism occurs within a solution or in the gas phase. The two most common methods to generate ions are electrospray ionization (ESI) and atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization (APCI), respectively. Both ESI and APCI can generate the same resultant ion species; however, it has been shown that preferential charge sites can change in response to an ionization source environment. Therefore, an additional quality control is warranted a priori to delineate erroneous analyte identification and/or unequivocal structural assignment. For protonation, protomer fidelity can be assessed by comparing the ion-mobility collision cross section (CCS) values obtained for both ESI and APCI. In this work, we utilized proxy standards (i.e., controls) derived from the available literature to develop a proof-of-concept multimodel inference application called AGENTi to probe differences in ionization for high-throughput protomer shift exploratory analysis. AGENTi uses in sequence the TensorFlow Autoencoder anomaly detection and the YDF Gradient Boosted Tree machine learning frameworks to generate more balanced and robust anomaly scores. We found that using a multimodel screening approach can reduce false positive capture at an acceptable loss of true positives. Moreover, we expect to achieve a better recovery of true positives with an improvement on the current Gradient Boosted Tree regression model for ΔCCS prediction as more ESI-APCI dual data are obtained for training. In all, we demonstrated in this pilot study that our foundation model for a priori probing of ionization pathway fidelity is feasible and efficient with AGENTi. The AGENTi prototype application and documentation are accessible at https://github.com/mitkeng/AGENTi.

Título: ML-RKIM: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Reaction Kinetics Identification and Modeling.
Resumen: Kinetic processes play a central role in structural transformations across natural, engineered, and biological systems, ultimately determining their final properties. Traditional kinetic characterization methods are often time-consuming and resource-intensive, and require prior assumptions about the reaction mechanism. In this work, we present a physics-informed machine learning framework to extract closed-form kinetic representations from time-series data without preselecting a single reaction mechanism. The framework combines neural networks, physics-informed features, and sparse regularization. The framework was applied to a range of processes, including thermally driven reactions such as polymer curing and crystallization, and nonthermal processes such as enzymatic browning. These results demonstrate the potential of this approach to accelerate kinetic characterization across polymer, food, and biomolecular processing applications, where accurate kinetic models are essential.

Título: CoTAR: Topology and Atomic State Reconstruction in Condensed Phases.
Resumen: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) enable performing condensed-phase molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accuracy approaching that of first-principles; however, their lack of explicit molecular topology limits bond-aware analysis and reconnection to classical force fields. This study presents CoTAR, a hybrid graph neural network (GNN)-hidden Markov model (HMM) framework that reconstructs bond connectivity and order, formal charges, and unpaired electrons from atomic species and coordinates by combining learned local environments, chemical constraints, and temporal smoothing. After joint fine-tuning with 20 labeled snapshots per benchmark system, CoTAR achieved category-macro bond and conditional bond-order F1 scores of 0.992 and 0.998 and chemically valid snapshots of 82.1% across 128 uMLIP systems. Zero-shot tests were successful for all tested nonionic systems but revealed persistent formal-charge errors in ionic mixtures. For successfully reconnected systems, the reconstructed-topology simulation results showed close agreement with the reference-topology results for the density, element-resolved diffusion, and intermolecular radial distribution functions. These results establish CoTAR as a practical route from topology-free uMLIP trajectories to chemically complete molecular representations within the present scope of nonreactive, topology-preserving systems.

Título: In-Context Molecular Property Prediction with LLMs: A Blinding Study on Memorization and Knowledge Conflicts.
Resumen: The capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have expanded beyond natural language processing to scientific prediction tasks, including molecular property prediction. This paper investigates whether LLMs perform genuine in-context regression on molecular properties or instead rely on verbatim retrieval of memorized target values. Furthermore, we analyze the interplay between pretrained knowledge and in-context information through a series of progressively blinded experiments. We evaluate nine LLM variants across three families (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5) on three MoleculeNet data sets (Delaney solubility, Lipophilicity, QM7 atomization energy) using a systematic blinding approach that iteratively reduces available information, complemented by 0-, 60-, and 1000-shot in-context sample sizes as an additional control for information access. We find no evidence of verbatim retrieval on the legacy benchmarks and show that blinding exposes conflicts between pretrained knowledge and in-context information. This work provides a principled framework for evaluating molecular property prediction under controlled information access.

Título: STELLAR: A Fragment-Based Docking Workflow for Highly Flexible Long-Chain Biopolymers.

Additionally, it scales linearly in computational time, runs primarily on CPUs with minimal GPU usage, avoids reliance on generative approximations, provides an accurate metric for ligand ranking, and reduces computational cost compared to similar tools. Its design also supports high-throughput screening of linear polymer-protein interactions by efficiently reducing the complexity associated with high conformational flexibility.

LOCO-CV demonstrated minimal performance variation across counties, indicating good internal geographic generalisability. At the same time, explainable artificial intelligence techniques consistently identified Chlorosis Intensity, Green-Yellow Ratio, and Necrotic Area as the most influential predictors. Considering predictive performance alongside computational efficiency, model size, and inference latency, LightGBM provided the most favorable balance for resource-constrained environments. In contrast, Logistic Regression offered a highly interpretable alternative with minimal computational requirements. Although the achieved performance indicates that approximately one in four samples may be misclassified and further external validation is required before operational deployment, the findings demonstrate that structured feature-based machine learning provides a transparent, computationally efficient, and interpretable framework for MLND detection and establishes a strong foundation for future field-based decision-support systems.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. Título: A machine-vision framework for electric vehicle charging hole localization based on contour-driven detection and geometric verification.

On an Intel Core i7-12700 CPU with 16 GB RAM and no GPU acceleration, the proposed framework achieves an overall mean localization error of 4.2 pixels and a 96.25% detection success rate, with an average per-image processing time of approximately 60 ms. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides accurate, robust, and engineering-deployable charging-hole localization for the target charging interface.
