Advanced survival modeling using joint modeling techniques provides deeper biological insights into child mortality dynamics, and machine learning and traditional survival models offered equivalent predictive discrimination and calibration in this analysis. These findings support targeted public health interventions focusing on birth spacing, maternal age, and enhanced monitoring for high-risk families as critical strategies for reducing under-five mortality in Zambia.

Título: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface.

All respondents of the BCI survey (n = 37) expressed strong support for the potential future use of BCI devices. Título: Learning global and local representations for generalized category discovery in neurodegenerative diseases.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved notable success in closed-set classification of neurodegenerative diseases, but its performance degrades significantly in more realistic open-set settings, such as discovering rare or novel disease subtypes from unlabeled data that are not seen during training. It aims to leverage labeled data from known categories to automatically identify novel categories within unlabeled datasets. We propose a GCD framework integrating semi-supervised contrastive learning with global-local representation learning to jointly optimize feature learning. Globally, we enforce consistency between weakly augmented views of the same instance by aligning their similarity relationships with other embeddings in a support queue. Locally, we treat neighborhood embeddings from the support queue as positive pairs for cross-instance contrastive learning, enhancing fine-grained discrimination. We evaluate our method on a benchmark dataset comprising six neurodegenerative diseases, with over 1500 patient samples. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms representative state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our method achieves 66.02% Accuracy and 60.59% Normalized Mutual Information on all categories, and 54.53% Accuracy and 16.67% Normalized Mutual Information on novel categories, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. Our framework underscores the model's robustness and its practical value in discovering new neurodegenerative disease conditions, highlighting its potential for advancing open-set diagnostic AI.

Título: Artificial Intelligence and Anatomical Variation: A Narrative Review of Detection, Classification, and Educational Applications.
Resumen: Anatomical variation encompasses non-pathological differences in the number, morphology, position, course, or relationships of structures and is not synonymous with rarity. Such variation affects imaging, surgery, procedural safety, dentistry, and anatomy education. This structured narrative review maps artificial intelligence (AI) applications that detect, classify, or segment variable anatomy across organ systems and distinguishes variant-specific evidence from general structure recognition. PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, publisher records, and preprint servers were searched iteratively on September 4, 2026, and updated on September 7, 2026, with citation chaining. The synthesis includes 14 principal empirical reports identified by this process: nine direct clinical imaging studies, three variation-relevant mapping studies, one direct multimodal preprint benchmark, and one contextual educational evaluation. Direct clinical evidence is concentrated in dental and cranio-maxillofacial imaging, with additional studies of lumbosacral transitional vertebrae and pulmonary, hepatic, or portal venous patterns. Segmentation performance does not establish named-variant classification, and evidence from anatomical proximity should not be transferred to untested variants. Educational outcome evidence is preliminary. Current AI may support narrowly specified tasks, but the identified literature does not establish a general, transferable understanding of human anatomical diversity. Progress requires explicit taxonomies, patient-level partitions, representative class distributions, clinically defensible reference standards, external validation, and dedicated educational evaluation.

Título: Dissecting polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome heterogeneity (PMOS): multi-omics, AI subtyping, and precision management.
Resumen: Polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is the most common endocrine disorder, affecting 8-12% of women of reproductive age and increasing the risk of infertility, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease. However, traditional symptom-based diagnostic criteria do not fully capture the underlying biological diversity of PMOS. Recent research using multi-omics and artificial intelligence (AI) has revealed that PMOS is best understood as a syndrome with multiple subtypes. Data-driven clustering of clinical variables consistently identifies four major subtypes: HA-PCOS, OB-PCOS, SHBG-PCOS, and LH-PCOS. Each subtype shows unique hormonal, metabolic, and genetic features, including distinct patterns in lipid, amino acid, and energy metabolism. Immune system disruptions and impaired blood clot breakdown in the ovarian environment are also notable features. Novel findings suggest that altered lactate metabolism and changes in histone lactylation may contribute to granulosa cell dysfunction, although further studies are needed to confirm these mechanisms. Machine learning models that integrate clinical, metabolic, and genetic data have achieved high diagnostic accuracy and can provide interpretable results. Potential targeted therapies, such as GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, N-acetylcysteine, and NK3R antagonists, have been proposed for specific subtypes, but have yet to be validated in clinical trials. Remaining challenges include small and homogeneous study cohorts, limited long-term data, and barriers to care in low-resource settings. Overall, recognizing PMOS as a syndrome with distinct subtypes highlights the promise of AI-powered, personalized approaches for more effective and equitable management.

Título: Electrocorticographic Network Feature Space Constriction as a Preictal Biomarker.
Resumen: In patients with epilepsy, seizures are associated with pathological neural synchronization. However, the preictal period preceding a seizure often exhibits reduced spatial synchronization compared to normal cognition. This observation aligns with the concept of the brain as a complex dynamical system, where a reduction in dimensionality and resilience can precede a phase transition. The Critical Brain Hypothesis suggests a connection between the loss of healthy scale-free behavior and various disorders, including epilepsy. Our study investigates preictal changes by utilizing network features, such as mean node degree and mean clustering coefficient, derived from thresholded correlation matrices of patient intracranial electrocorticographic electrode data. Logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM) models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). DCA suggested a potential net clinical benefit. SHAP analysis, in conjunction with multivariable regression results, consistently demonstrated that ADL score and lymphocyte count were associated with reduced risk of clinical deterioration, whereas CRP and neutrophil count were associated with increased risk. The SVM model developed in this study may help identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration among hospitalized lung cancer patients and may assist healthcare professionals in achieving early risk identification and potential clinical decision support.

Título: Sequence-activity mapping and model-guided engineering of the phenol-responsive DmpR-Po σ<sup>54</sup> promoter.

However, the transcriptional output of complex inducible systems, exemplified by σ<sup>54</sup>-dependent promoters, relies on long-range coordination among distal bacterial enhancer-binding proteins, DNA architectural proteins, and RNA polymerase. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting coupled with sequencing yielded a high-quality sequence-activity map covering 11,940 variants. At the regional level, identical UAS and IHF2 haplotypes generally preserved their relative activity rankings across single-region and joint-variant backgrounds, and the main effects estimated independently for UAS and IHF2 could approximately predict the activity of combined variants. At the nucleotide level, however, the effects of individual substitutions were strongly constrained by the overall DNA architecture and full-sequence context. Single-clone validation further showed that model-guided edits produced variable experimental outcomes, supporting candidate prioritization while indicating that individual engineering predictions require experimental validation. Collectively, this study characterizes the transferability and context-dependent constraints of regional sequence effects and establishes a data-driven framework for quantitative prediction and model-guided engineering of complex σ<sup>54</sup>-dependent promoters.

Título: Mapping the aging kidney: a bibliometric atlas of cellular senescence and future frontiers since the 20th century.
Resumen: Kidney disease is a major global public health challenge. The pathological mechanisms linking chronic kidney disease (CKD) and age-related kidney function decline are complex. Cellular senescence and its senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) act as key links between kidney aging and disease progression. Although publications in this field have surged, a systematic bibliometric analysis is needed to outline its knowledge framework, research hotspots, and future trends. This study aims to quantitatively analyze global publication trends, core contributors (countries, institutions, journals, and authors), and cooperation networks to map the dynamic evolution of this field. We conducted a comprehensive literature search across both the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases to retrieve original articles and reviews concerning cellular senescence and kidney aging published between 2000 and 2025. After merging the datasets and removing duplicates, a meticulous bibliometric analysis was executed using Excel 365, CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix (an R package) to map the knowledge framework and cooperation networks. This analysis included 2,191 relevant papers involving 16,545 researchers. The overall publication volume showed significant growth, reaching a peak in 2025. The United States leads the field with the most publications and the highest citation frequency. China ranks second in publications but fourth in citations, reflecting a gap in research quality. The collaboration network indicates that the United States is the core node, maintaining close ties with countries like China and Germany. The <i>American Journal of Physiology-Renal Physiology</i> ranked first in publication volume, while the <i>Journal of the American Society of Nephrology</i> achieved the highest citation frequency. Xiang-Mei Chen and Anette Melk were identified as core contributing scholars. Keyword analysis established "aging" (825 times) and "cellular senescence" (330 times) as the central concepts. Emerging topics such as "machine learning," "ferroptosis," and "Mendelian randomization" are rapidly rising as research hotspots. This study maps the evolutionary trends of research on cellular senescence and related kidney diseases, identifying current frontiers and providing data to support future research. The rise of concepts like machine learning, ferroptosis, and Mendelian randomization marks a deep shift in the research paradigm, offering new perspectives for future scientific exploration.


--- ARTÍCULO 2643 ---
ID (PMID): 42908600
Título: Coupling characteristics of endocrine regulation and system function under massage interventions.
Resumen: Massage may influence stress related endocrine activity and systemic physiological function, but its dynamic regulatory effects remain difficult to quantify. This study develops a VariationalMotionBayesian framework to model endocrine related physiological responses under massage intervention. The framework combines mathematical formulation of coupled endocrine and systemic variables, variational latent representation learning, motion field estimation, Bayesian evidence aggregation, and physiological constraint regularization. Multimodal wearable physiological time series are used to infer latent regulatory states and predict individual stress status. Experiments on WESAD and SWELL-KW show that the proposed model outperforms conventional machine learning, deep learning, and time series classification baselines in Accuracy, Macro F1, Balanced Accuracy, and AUROC. A controlled human massage intervention pilot study further shows coordinated changes in salivary cortisol, salivary alpha amylase, heart rate, RMSSD, electrodermal activity, respiration rate, and skin temperature after massage, and these measured responses are correlated with model derived latent dynamics. These results indicate that the proposed framework can capture physiologically meaningful temporal responses and provide a computational tool for analyzing endocrine related system regulation under massage intervention.


--- ARTÍCULO 2644 ---
ID (PMID): 42908598
Título: Classification of cystoid macular edema status from retinal vasculitis fluorescein angiography images using a convolutional neural network.
Resumen: Cystoid macular edema (CME) is a vision-threatening complication of retinal vasculitis, a rare inflammatory disease for which large imaging datasets are difficult to obtain. Detection of CME on fluorescein angiography (FA) requires expert interpretation, motivating automated image-based approaches to support clinical decision-making. Deep learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown strong performance in medical image analysis but are constrained by limited labeled data in rare diseases. Transfer learning may mitigate this limitation by adapting pretrained models to small, task-specific datasets. We analyzed 207 de-identified late-phase 55° FA images from 117 patients with retinal vasculitis. The primary target was concurrent patient-level CME status, established through specialist review of clinical records and optical coherence tomography obtained at the same clinical visit as FA. A patient was classified as CME-positive when CME was present in at least one eye. An ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 was evaluated using five-fold nested, patient-level cross-validation. Within each outer-development cohort, 144 candidate configurations were compared by four-fold inner cross-validation and selected according to mean inner-validation AUROC. Each selected configuration was evaluated only on its corresponding untouched outer-test fold. Across 117 pooled patient-level outer-test predictions, the model-selection pipeline achieved an AUROC of 0.708 (95% CI, 0.610-0.802), an AUPRC of 0.626 (95% CI, 0.493-0.755), and an accuracy of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.641-0.803). Sensitivity was 0.694 (95% CI, 0.558-0.822), specificity was 0.750 (95% CI, 0.643-0.853), and the F1 score was 0.680 (95% CI, 0.563-0.780). Exploratory Grad-CAM analysis visualized regions associated with model predictions. The nested model-selection pipeline showed moderate discrimination with a relatively balanced operating profile and slightly higher specificity than sensitivity. Clinically relevant false-positive and false-negative errors, together with the absence of external validation, preclude clinical deployment.

Título: Interpretable model using serum biomarkers and intra-/peri-aneurysmal CTA radiomics for discriminating ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms: an external validation retrospective study.
Resumen: To develop an interpretable model that integrates diverse machine learning algorithms, fusion strategies, intra-/perianeurysmal CTA radiomics, and serum biomarkers to differentiate ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms (IAs), and to investigate the underlying biological features associated with rupture status. Totally, 744 IAs patients who underwent CTA were retrospectively enrolled. Data from Center 1 (<i>N</i> = 423) served as the training set, and data from Center 2 (<i>N</i> = 321) served as the external validation set. Volumes of interest were delineated in intra-aneurysmal and peri-aneurysmal 1 mm regions. The serum inflammation score (SIS) was constructed using serum biomarkers. Seven machine learning classifiers were employed to develop models, and the optimal fusion model was developed by combining all classifiers using arithmetic mean, geometric mean, weighted mean, and logistic regression (LRSLM). Model performance was assessed by the area under the curve (AUC) and decision curve analysis (DCA), while interpretability was evaluated via SHAP, correlation, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses. Among the 11 models, LRSLM exhibited robust performance in the external validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.9177 with good calibration. It also demonstrated high accuracy (0.8847), recall (0.8171), and a low Brier score (0.0999), alongside greater clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities (10-85%). Correlation analyses revealed strong positive associations between intra-aneurysmal and peri-aneurysmal radiomic features (Spearman's <i>r</i> = 0.62, 0.72, and 0.84, respectively; all <i>p</i> < 0.001), as well as significant positive correlations between the intra-/perianeurysmal radiomics and SIS (Spearman's <i>r</i> = 0.32, 0.29, 0.32, and 0.34; all <i>p</i> < 0.001). RCS analysis further demonstrated a significant non-linear relationship between the intra-aneurysmal (IRSIAs) and peri-aneurysmal (PRSIAs) radiomic features and an increased incidence of IAs rupture (Non-linear <i>p</i> < 0.05; Overall <i>p</i> < 0.05). SHAP analysis highlighted key radiomics features contributors to the fusion model and supported model interpretability. The LRSLM model achieves robust discriminative performance for differentiating ruptured from unruptured IAs. SHAP analysis enhances the interpretability of the model and may assist in identifying high-risk phenotypic features, although prospective validation is required before predictive clinical application can be considered.

Título: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early acute kidney injury and altered consciousness in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a retrospective study.
Resumen: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and altered consciousness are common and serious complications following cardiac surgery, both associated with increased morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Early prediction of these complications is essential for timely intervention. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early AKI and altered consciousness risk in this population. We retrospectively extracted data from the MIMIC-IV database. Adult patients who underwent cardiac surgery within 24 h before ICU admission were included. The primary outcome was early AKI defined by KDIGO criteria within 48 h after ICU admission. The secondary outcome was altered consciousness within 24 h after ICU admission, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤12. A comprehensive set of candidate variables was screened using four feature selection methods (LassoCV, mRMR, mutual information, and <i>F</i>-test) with a voting strategy. Eight machine learning models were developed and compared. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to interpret the best-performing model. External validation was performed using data from cardiac surgery patients at Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2025. A total of 5,288 patients were included, with an AKI incidence of 76.2% (4,031/5,288) and an altered consciousness incidence of 22.8% (1,206/5,288). For the primary outcome of AKI, the XGBoost model achieved a training AUC of 0.787 (95% CI: 0.770-0.804) and an internal test AUC of 0.659 (95% CI: 0.629-0.688). For the secondary outcome of altered consciousness, the XGBoost model achieved an internal test AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.936-0.963). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis confirmed good calibration and clinical utility for both models. SHAP analysis identified SpO<sub>2</sub>, age, APSIII score, creatinine, and white blood cell count as the top 5 most important predictors for AKI. External validation was performed in an independent cohort of 395 cardiac surgery ICU patients from Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital, in whom the incidence of AKI and altered consciousness was 28.1% and 67.3%, respectively. The models retained acceptable discrimination in this external cohort (AKI: AUC 0.764, 95% CI: 0.711-0.818; altered consciousness: AUC 0.679, 95% CI: 0.615-0.737). We developed interpretable XGBoost-based prediction models for both early AKI and altered consciousness risk in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU. The models exhibited excellent discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, which may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide personalized interventions.

ID (PMID): 42908533
Título: Predicting cumulative live birth after IVF with growth hormone supplementation: the role of pretreatment duration and machine learning-based models.
Resumen: To investigate the association between growth hormone (GH) pretreatment duration and cumulative live birth (CLB), identify key prognostic factors, and develop predictive models using logistic regression (LR) and machine learning (ML) algorithms among women undergoing <i>in vitro</i> fertilization (IVF) with GH supplementation. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women undergoing IVF/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) with GH between February 2015 and June 2023 at a single tertiary center. Five models were developed: LR, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM). Performance was assessed with cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. AUROC and Brier scores evaluated discrimination and calibration. Among 1,782 women, 763 (42.82%) achieved at least one live birth. Maternal age, anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), the assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycle number, and GH duration were significant predictors. LR performed best (AUROC 0.782; Brier 0.187), showing strong calibration and interpretability. ML models had moderate discrimination but inferior calibration. AMH, AFC, and GH duration were key predictors across all methods. Both logistic regression and machine learning effectively predicted CLB after GH-pretreated IVF, but LR provided favorable discrimination, calibration, and interpretability. GH pretreatment ≥2 months was independently associated with higher odds of cumulative live birth.


--- ARTÍCULO 2648 ---
ID (PMID): 42908471
Título: Stellar white-light emission reveals two types of flaring light-curve patterns.
Resumen: Stellar flares are sudden magnetic eruptions that release intense energy and cause detectable variations in stellar light curves. These transient events offer windows into the magnetic field dynamics, plasma behaviour and reconnection processes in active stellar regions. Despite their importance, the diversity in flare morphology and its underlying physical origins remains poorly understood. To explore this variability, we analyse 2319 white-light flares observed by Kepler, extracting a comprehensive set of 22 time- and frequency-domain features from each event. Using unsupervised clustering, we identify two distinct flare populations that are not associated with global stellar parameters such as rotation period, temperature or mass. Instead, the separation is primarily driven by differences in frequency evolution, damping persistence and local magnetic activity (LMA). Our findings demonstrate that flare light-curve morphology can be quantitatively grouped, revealing internal dynamical contrasts without reliance on host star properties. This article is part of the theme issue 'Transferable mechanisms in the oscillatory processes of solar and stellar flares'.

ID (PMID): 42908460
Título: Detector for fast wave trains in the solar radio emission.
Resumen: Quasi-periodic fast propagating (QFP) wave trains observed in the solar corona after some energetic events (solar flares, coronal mass ejections, jets) open possibilities for diagnostics of spatial and temporal scales of the impulsive energy release processes that are absent in the standard model of a solar flare. In addition, the dynamics of the wave trains and their characteristic spatial and temporal signatures allow for localizing the initial energy release volume magenta and to perform fine diagnostics of the transverse structures of plasma inhomogeneities in the solar corona. However, the small number of such events registered significantly limits their promising diagnostic potential. The aim of this paper is to perform an automatic search for fast wave trains in radio data. We apply classifying neural network/machine learning methods. Dynamic radio spectra obtained by Hiraiso radio spectrograph (HiRAS) radio spectrographs within the 20 MHz-2.5 GHz frequency band during 2011 were used. We consider 50 global coronal extreme ultraviolet (EUV) waves as marker events for a more targeted search in HiRAS data. Our automatic detector revealed 50 independent QFP-candidate events with temporal signatures similar to those of the fast wave trains, with 13 candidates connected with the global waves. This article is part of the theme issue 'Transferable mechanisms in the oscillatory processes of solar and stellar flares'.

Título: [Discussion on the closed-loop regulation strategy for acupuncture "<i>Deqi</i>" based on brain-computer interface and its peripheral-central mechanisms].
Resumen: It is held that "<i>Deqi</i>" is the key to the therapeutic effect of acupuncture, but its evaluation has long relied on subjective feelings and lacks objective biological indicators. In the present article, we systematically review the current research status of brain-computer interface (BCI) technology based on electroencephalogram (EEG) in analyzing the peripheral-cerebral neural mechanism of "<i>Deqi</i>", and further explore how to utilize the closed-loop regulation ability of BCI to actively induce and maintain the "<i>Deqi</i>" state. By integrating domestic and foreign literature, we analyzed the peripheral initiation mechanism and central response characteristics of "<i>Deqi</i>", and explored its application value of EEG-BCI in the objective identification and the construction of closed-loop feedback systems. Studies have demonstrated that EEG, with its millisecond-level time resolution, can capture the dynamic changes of neural oscillations during the "<i>Deqi</i>" process in real time. The feature decoding method based on machine learning further realizes the objective identification of the "<i>Deqi</i>" state, while the closed-loop feedback system constructed by BCI technology provides an innovative path for precise acupuncture treatment. However, this field still faces some challenges such as signal artifact interference, insufficient decoding accuracy, and inconsistent research paradigms. The deep integration of EEG-BCI with acupuncture medicine provides a key technical platform for decoding the scientific connotation of "<i>Deqi</i>" and active regulation. In the future, efforts should be made to develop dynamic network decoding technology, further deepen the research on peripheral-cerebral coupling mechanisms, and promote the transformation of the system towards intelligence and standardization.

ID (PMID): 42908394
Título: Early Prediction of Cardiomyopathy in Pediatric Cancer Survivors Using Echocardiographic Video-Based Deep Learning.
Resumen: Cardiomyopathy (CM) is a leading cause of late mortality in childhood cancer survivors, but it is often identified only after irreversible cardiac remodeling has already occurred. In this proof-of-concept study, we assessed whether deep learning applied to routine echocardiographic videos can identify features predictive of future CM. We analyzed parasternal short-axis clips from cancer survivors ≤21 years old at cancer diagnosis. 3D deep convolutional neural networks were trained to classify CM-positive versus CM-negative studies from echocardiograms conducted up to five years prior to CM diagnosis. The performance was assessed on internal hold-out validation (Center 1) and external validation cohorts (Centers 2, 3). The model's prognostic value was evaluated by stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups for developing CM, and probability of future CM was assessed using cumulative incidence and proportional hazards regression analysis. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87±0.05 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.74±0.07 on the internal hold-out set. External validation showed near-chance single-study discrimination (AUROC 0.55±0.02 and 0.60±0.03; AUPRC 0.22±0.02 and 0.21±0.03 for Centers 2 and 3, respectively). Nevertheless, analysis of the external cohort showed significantly higher probability of CM in high- versus low-risk groups (hazard ratio 2.78, 95% CI = 1.52-5.10, p = 0.00056). Deep learning models have the potential to identify subtle echocardiographic markers years before CM diagnosis in pediatric cancer survivors and could serve as a preliminary step toward risk-guided CM surveillance. Further refinement and validation are needed to determine the utility of deep learning for early identification of pathologic cardiac remodeling in this population.


--- ARTÍCULO 2652 ---
ID (PMID): 42908344
Título: Causal inference in oral health research: Beyond statistical significance toward a causal framework.
Resumen: Oral health research has adopted sophisticated statistical methods, yet studies routinely present adjusted associations as causal effects. The problem is not statistical competence but the absence of explicit causal reasoning. This commentary proposes a principled framework for causal reasoning in oral health research. We conducted a narrative synthesis of foundational and recent literature on causal inference, drawing on texts describing the potential outcomes and counterfactual frameworks, the ICH E9(R1) regulatory addendum on estimands, study design, directed acyclic graphs, and recent applications of causal methods in oral health research; recurring principles were organized into a sequential four-pillar framework, illustrated throughout with a worked example examining periodontal treatment and cardiovascular disease. First, the question is framed through abductive reasoning and translated into a precisely defined estimand. Second, study design is aligned with that estimand by specifying the population, exposure contrast, and time origin so that the data reflect the intended causal comparison. Third, counterfactual reasoning and directed acyclic graphs clarify the conditions under which causal conclusions are warranted, guiding principled adjustment. Fourth, estimation and inference are used to evaluate evidence for the estimand, and results are interpreted with explicit attention to the assumptions required for causal claims CONCLUSION: We propose a cultural shift in oral health research where causal effects are precisely defined, identification assumptions are explicitly defended, and structural uncertainties are acknowledged. This framework reveals that statistical sophistication cannot substitute for careful causal reasoning. Advanced methods such as multivariable regression, propensity scores, and machine learning can allow robust estimation of causal effects but do not replace the need for a prior causal reasoning and identification assumptions. The question is not whether analyses are statistically correct, but whether causal effects are well-defined and assumptions are explicit. Applying this framework would make causal assumptions transparent, acknowledge uncertainty inherent in observational research, and clarify when experimental designs become necessary. This commentary argues that oral health research has a fundamental problem: studies use sophisticated statistics but still present associations as if they were causal findings. Better math alone doesn't fix flawed reasoning. The authors propose a four-pillar framework to address this. First, researchers should use abductive reasoning to frame a precise causal question that specifies the exposure, population, outcome, and comparison of interest. Second, study design should be aligned to that question. Third, causal assumptions must be made explicit using counterfactual thinking and directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), which clarify confounders, mediators, and colliders. Finally, statistical estimation and inference should come last, quantifying uncertainty about a pre-specified causal quantity, not generating causal meaning on their own. The bottom line: no statistical method, however advanced, can substitute for explicit causal reasoning. The real question in oral health research is not whether the analysis is statistically correct, but whether the causal effect is clearly defined and the underlying assumptions are honestly defended.

Título: Ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent extraction of polyphenols from <i>Sophora alopecuroides</i> L. seeds: process optimization, antioxidant evaluation and machine learning-assisted structure-activity interpretation.
Resumen: This study first applies ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvents (DESs) for green and efficient extraction of polyphenols from <i>Sophora alopecuroides</i> L. seeds. The process was optimised using Plackett-Burman design and response surface methodology, yielding optimal conditions: a choline chloride-to-glucose molar ratio of 1:0.57, a solvent moisture content of 42.5%, a liquid-to-solid ratio of 56.1 mL/g and a temperature of 57 °C, achieving a polyphenol yield of 55.71 mg/g. The extracted polyphenols exhibited concentration-dependent radical scavenging activity against DPPH and ABTS<sup>+</sup>, with clearance rates exceeding 80% within a defined concentration range. UPLC-IMS-QTOF-MS analysis identified 21 phenolic compounds. Besides, a machine learning model based on DPPH radical scavenging activity was developed, enabling the prioritisation of 10 compounds with high predicted activity. SHAP-based interpretability analysis revealed that aromatic moieties bearing phenolic hydroxyl groups were key structural determinants contributing positively to antioxidant activity. This provides an efficient DES extraction method and mechanistic insights into antioxidant structure-activity relationships, supporting future utilisation.

Título: An interpretable machine learning model integrating mucosal and cellular immunity to predict SARS-CoV-2 reinfection: a multicenter cohort study.
Resumen: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4<sup>+</sup> central memory T cells (T<sub>CM</sub>) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4<sup>+</sup> T<sub>CM</sub> cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.

ID (PMID): 42908281
Título: Charting Cervical Spinal Cord Morphometry Across the Lifespan.
Resumen: Spinal cord morphometry provides essential biomarkers of neurological health, but clinical interpretations are confounded by inter-subject variability and a lack of normative references across the full human lifespan. We address this gap by generating the first comprehensive lifespan charts for cervical spinal cord morphometry. From 78,269 T1-weighted brain MRI sessions, we identified a final cross-sectional cohort of 24,251 healthy or cognitively normal controls from 33 datasets (ages 0-100 years) with cervical cord coverage. To overcome contrast variability, we employed a state-of-the-art contrast-agnostic deep learning segmentation method, extracting cross-sectional area (CSA), anteroposterior (AP) and right-left (RL/transverse), and shape indices (AP/RL ratio, eccentricity, and solidity) from C1 to C7. Normative trajectories were modeled using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS). The resulting charts reveal distinct non-linear lifespan changes: rapid growth through childhood and adolescence, peak maturation occurring in early-to-mid adulthood (e.g., mid-30s for CSA), followed by gradual decreases. Significant regional variations along the cervical cord and consistent sex differences (males > females for size metrics) were quantified. Spinal cord trajectories showed strong temporal coupling with brain white matter and brainstem volumes, suggesting integrated CNS development and aging. These lifespan charts provide a robust normative framework, enabling age- and sex-specific centile scoring of individual spinal cord morphometry. This resource offers a critical tool for differentiating typical variation from pathological changes, enhancing the clinical utility of spinal cord MRI in studies of development and neurodegeneration.

Título: An early risk prediction nomogram for coronary artery lesions in Kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Resumen: Coronary artery lesions remain a major concern in Kawasaki disease. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical nomogram for early identification of children at risk for Coronary artery lesions. We retrospectively analysed 216 children with Kawasaki disease divided into a training cohort (n = 151) and a validation cohort (n = 65). Coronary artery lesions was defined as early coronary dilatation and/or coronary aneurysm. XGBoost and SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to explore age's nonlinear effect. Calibration and decision-curve analysis confirmed good consistency and favourable clinical net benefit. This nomogram integrates routine clinical variables and interpretable machine learning to identify nonlinear age-related Coronary artery lesions risk and provide individualised early risk estimation. External validation in large prospective multicentre cohorts is needed before wide clinical application.

Título: Quantifying Data Reuse in Proteomics Using PRIDE Downloads Statistics and a Semi-Supervised LLM-Based Framework.
Resumen: Understanding how scientific datasets are accessed and reused is essential for resource planning and impact assessment. Here we present the PRIDE Archive download tracking infrastructure and a comprehensive analysis of 159.3 million download records from the PRIDE proteomics database (2021-2025), spanning 35,528 datasets accessed from 235 locations. The infrastructure includes nf-downloadstats, a scalable Nextflow pipeline for processing download logs, and DeepLogBot, a machine-learning framework that classifies traffic into bots, institutional download hubs, and independent user downloads. DeepLogBot combines heuristic seed selection with multi-LLM annotation (Claude and Qwen3) to produce LLM-assisted consensus labels, achieving 92.2% bot classification accuracy on a held-out test set. After separating bot traffic, analysis reveals downloads from 214 countries/regions, 249 institutional download hubs, and a concentrated reuse distribution, with the top five countries (United States, United Kingdom, Germany, China, and Canada) accounting for over 54% of independent user downloads. These findings provide actionable insights for repository infrastructure planning and highlight the importance of distinguishing automated from individual access in scientific data resources.

Título: Automated classification of ignitable liquid profiles: Comparing machine learning and rule-based systems.
Resumen: In this work, two methods were developed for the automated classification of neat ignitable liquids and ignitable liquid residues. The performances of the two approaches were evaluated using laboratory-generated gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) data of various types of samples of ASTM E1618-19 classes. One method used machine learning with the Orange data mining software via image analysis for pattern recognition/comparison to known reference samples for the classification procedure. Five machine learning models, namely neural network, support vector machine, logistic regression, random forest, and k-nearest neighbors, were evaluated, and moderate classification accuracy (0.706-0.635), F1 score (0.703-0.626), precision (0.734-0.646), recall (0.706-0.635), and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (0.675-0.595) were achieved. The second method used a rule-based Python framework to automate the routine steps used by fire debris analysts for the interpretation of the GC-MS profile via identification of the major compounds (based on their mass spectra and retention times in the GC-MS chromatogram) in the sample, followed by classification using logic rules. The Python framework approach attained a higher classification accuracy (0.922), F1 score (0.924), precision (0.935), recall (0.922), and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (0.913). The two methods enabled the automated classification of ignitable liquid profiles and could serve as a preliminary assessment tool or an additional verification of the fire debris analysts' interpretations and conclusions of the analysis.

Título: Different Proportions of Round-Headed Spermatozoa: Impacts on Sperm Function and IVF/ICSI Outcomes.
Resumen: Although complete globozoospermia is well characterized, it is clinically rare. Partial globozoospermia is more prevalent, yet the impact of varying round-headed sperm ratios on disease severity remains unclear. Notably, even low proportions often signal compromised semen quality and spermatogenic dysfunction. This study investigates the impact of these proportions on sperm function and ART outcomes to provide evidence for individualized clinical management. This was a retrospective case-control study. After balancing baseline characteristics by propensity score matching (PSM), 728 subjects were included in both the round-headed sperm group (proportion ≥ 5%) and the control group. A machine learning-based automatic sperm morphology analysis system was used to quantify the proportion of round-headed sperm and their head parameters. Sperm function indicators (DNA integrity, acrosome function, mitochondrial membrane potential) were detected, and 166 couples from the round-headed sperm group who received IVF/ICSI were included for reproductive outcome analysis. After PSM, the round-headed sperm group showed significantly lower normal morphology rate, sperm kinematic parameters, nucleoprotein maturation, acrosome integrity, and acrosin activity compared with the control group. The sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) and high DNA stainability (HDS) were higher in the round-headed sperm group (p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis based on clinical pregnancy outcomes determined that the cut-off value for the proportion of round-headed sperm is 7.2%. The high-proportion group (> 7.2%) exhibited significantly lower IVF fertilization rate and high-quality embryo rate than the low-proportion group (≤ 7.2%) (p < 0.01). In ICSI cycles, the high-proportion group had significantly lower high-quality embryo rate (48.48% vs. 40.33%, p = 0.016), clinical pregnancy rate (58.82% vs. 41.43%, p = 0.048), and live birth rate (50.98% vs. 32.86%, p = 0.028) than the low-proportion group. The proportion of round-headed sperm can serve as an objective predictor for sperm function and outcomes before assisted reproductive technology treatment.

Título: Magneto-Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics.
Resumen: The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical-Mn/N-doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time-resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near-complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic "hot spots" at the Au-micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N-doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO<sub>4</sub> <sup>•‒</sup>-mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate-determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale-up conditions, with a machine learning model (R<sup>2</sup> = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno-economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value-added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.

Título: Multimodal Prediction in Robotic Surgery: The Incremental Value of Task-Level Kinematic Data.
Resumen: To determine whether multimodal predictive models incorporating task-level objective performance indicators (OPIs) alongside preoperative clinical variables improve prediction of surgeon experience, case complexity, and outcomes in robotic cholecystectomy. OPIs from robotic platforms enable automated assessment of intraoperative performance, but prior multimodal analyses have suggested limited incremental value beyond clinical variables. Whether this conclusion holds when OPIs are computed at task level and target specifically curated endpoints remains untested. We retrospectively analyzed 234 Calot's triangle dissections, 198 by attending surgeons and 36 by trainees. Three feature sets per target-clinical-only (10 preoperative variables), OPI-only (10 target-specific kinematic features), and combined-were evaluated using nested 5-seed×5-fold cross-validation across 5 algorithms (logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM). Discriminative performance was compared by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on fold-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Feature contributions were quantified with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. For surgeon experience and case complexity, OPIs alone matched the combined model (AUROC: 0.967 vs. 0.964; 0.791 vs. 0.792; both P>0.05) and outperformed clinical variables alone (P<0.001 and P=0.006). For outcomes, the combined model significantly exceeded both single-modality models (AUROC: 0.753 vs. 0.720 clinical and 0.720 OPI-only; P=0.015 and 0.005). OPIs contributed 90.7%, 73.3%, and 51.7% of total absolute SHAP value across the 3 targets, decreasing with distance from intraoperative kinematics. Task-level, target-specific OPIs carry independent discriminative information beyond routine preoperative clinical variables. Their incremental value is target-dependent, with multimodal integration offering statistically significant but modest gains for outcomes.

Título: Multiomics, multi-species profiling, and animal validation identify mitoxyperilysis as a conserved therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
Resumen: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by complex intercellular communication and regulated cell death pathways. Mitoxyperilysis, a recently characterized form of regulated lytic cell death, remains poorly defined in MASH. Here, we integrated multiomics, cross-species transcriptomics, machine learning, and in vivo models to dissect mitoxyperilysis activation and its therapeutic relevance in MASH. Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets from mouse and human MASH livers were analyzed. Cell-cell communication was inferred using CellChat, and metabolite‑mediated cell-cell communication (mCCC) was assessed with MEBOCOST. Mitoxyperilysis activity was scored via AUCell and AddModuleScore. Eleven machine learning classifiers identified transcriptomic signatures distinguishing MASH from controls, and key regulators were subjected to in silico knockout (scTenifoldKnk). A choline‑deficient, L‑amino acid‑defined high‑fat diet (CDAHFD) mouse model was used for in vivo validation. Single‑cell profiling revealed that mitoxyperilysis activity was highly enriched in myeloid cells, particularly monocyte‑derived macrophages (Mo‑Macrophages) and neutrophils, and was strongly induced by high‑fat high‑sucrose diet. CellChat and mCCC analyses demonstrated that Mo‑Macrophages served as central hubs of rewired inflammatory and metabolic crosstalk in MASH. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed the expansion of pro‑inflammatory hepatocyte subsets and conserved upregulation of mitoxyperilysis components (e.g. BAX, TLR4, NINJ1) in both mouse and human MASH. Cross‑species profiling across mouse, rat, hamster, non‑human primate, and human datasets demonstrated evolutionarily conserved activation of the entire mitoxyperilysis pathway. Machine learning identified Bax as the sole overlapping driver gene linking diet‑induced transcriptomic signatures to mitoxyperilysis. In silico Bax ablation perturbed lipid metabolism and immune pathways. In CDAHFD-induced MASH mice with typical pathological phenotypes, core mitoxyperilysis genes were transcriptionally upregulated, and Bax/Bid/Bak1 upregulation was validated at the protein level. While RhoA mRNA increased, total RhoA protein remained stable, with its ubiquitination elevated and activity suppressed. Mitoxyperilysis is an evolutionarily conserved, myeloid‑enriched pathway activated in MASH. Bax acts as a critical regulatory node, while RhoA is modulated via ubiquitination and functional suppression. Targeting this axis may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for MASH.

This study systematically elucidates the molecular landscape through which Cd exposure drives OA progression via the APP-mediated immune-inflammatory axis. These findings provide a novel theoretical framework for early screening and targeted therapeutic strategies in populations at high risk of environmental heavy metal exposure.

Título: Mechanism-aware benchmarking of large language models as learning aids in pediatric difficult airway training: true hallucinations vs. false contraindications.

Scenario inadequacy (score ≤ 2) increased with complexity: 32-98% for difficult intubation, 46-94% for difficult ventilation, and 52-92% for CICO. The contemporary generation of LLMs exhibits model-specific performance characteristics and error patterns in pediatric difficult airway management. Dosing-related failures manifest through different mechanisms of true hallucination vs. false contraindication. The findings reveal a marked inadequacy of the scenarios employed in these models, particularly as complexity and critical error rates increase. Current LLMs may have value as supervised supplementary learning tools, but not as autonomous sources of clinical or educational guidance.

Searches of four databases identified 8103 records (PubMed n = 2203, Web of Science Core Collection n = 2388, Embase n = 1790, and Cochrane Library n = 1722). After removal of 5652 duplicate records and 1251 non-full-text items, 1200 records underwent title/abstract screening, 25 full-text articles were assessed, and 14 studies comprising 1207 analyzable learners were included in the systematic review. Across the domain-specific pooled analyses, structured clinical performance showed the clearest positive signal (2 studies; 38 vs. 39 participants; SMD 3.39, 95% CI 1.43 to 5.35), strict knowledge acquisition showed a smaller but still positive signal (5 studies; SMD 0.80, 95% CI 0.07 to 1.53), and delayed retention showed no clear difference (2 studies; SMD 0.15, 95% CI -0.50 to 0.80). This structured clinical performance estimate was based on a very small evidence base and may be inflated by small-study effects, selective reporting, or measurement artifacts. An exploratory pooled synthesis of post-course score-based outcomes included 7 studies (248 vs. 251 participants) and suggested an advantage for LLM-based teaching (SMD 0.90, 95% CI 0.18 to 1.62, I² = 92.5%, P = 0.015), although heterogeneity across constructs, learner groups, and intervention modes was substantial. Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a larger effect in practice courses than in theory courses, although this signal was driven by only 2 practice-oriented studies and should be interpreted cautiously. Seven studies did not enter the pooled score-based synthesis directly; 1 was retained in the structured clinical performance supplementary meta-analysis and 6 were preserved through classification summary figures and single-study exploratory displays, thereby allowing all 14 included studies to remain within the overall results framework. GRADE-informed certainty ranged from very low to low across pooled domains. In medical education, current evidence provides low-certainty signals that some LLM-based teaching interventions may improve structured clinical performance and certain short-term knowledge outcomes, whereas delayed retention remains uncertain. The broader pooled score-based synthesis should be interpreted only as an exploratory summary across heterogeneous educational constructs, learner groups, and intervention modes, not as a single universal endpoint. Because several pooled domains were based on only 2 to 5 studies and overall certainty remained low to very low, these findings should be regarded as cautious signals rather than definitive estimates.


--- ARTÍCULO 2678 ---
ID (PMID): 42907838
Título: Quality assessment of synthetic data in healthcare: a critical appraisal with a focus on subgroup bias.
Resumen: The creation of synthetic data in healthcare research has emerged as a compelling solution to address challenges related to data privacy, in case of data-sharing and data scarceness for training machine learning models. The current paper aims to provide a critical landscape analysis of synthetic data quality metrics used in healthcare, mapping the state of the field, examining how current fidelity and utility scores often fail to capture weaknesses that appear in specific patient subgroups, and illustrating these blind spots with a lung-cancer case study. We specifically set out to highlight the need for assessing synthetic datasets not only at the aggregate level but also across clinically meaningful subgroups, to ensure reliability and fairness in downstream applications. By examining the landscape of synthetic data adoption in healthcare, we highlight the methodological and utility considerations that shape its integration into the research ecosystem. We elucidate how synthetic data can expedite research initiatives, support data-driven decision-making, and facilitate innovative methodologies while safeguarding sensitive patient information. Conversely, while many papers focus solely on the advantages of synthetic data, we aim to highlight also the potential constraints of using synthetic data in a real-world case involving lung cancer patient level data. Our analysis centers on identifying situations where synthetic data might introduce biases or inaccuracies that hinder the generation of meaningful clinical insights. We demonstrate the limitations of using synthetic data in a lung cancer case study, especially when dealing with small subgroups from the original dataset. While high values for fidelity and utility metrics are achieved when considering the entire synthetic dataset, significant discrepancies arise in cross-classification performance when examining subsets. Additionally, visual inspection reveals spurious correlations in the synthetic data that are not present in the real data. Global realism scores can give a false sense of security: in our case study, metrics that rate the full dataset as "high quality" overlook errors which appear once we zoom in on specific subgroups. We argue that future work must (i) design subgroup-aware fidelity and utility metrics, (ii) favor conditional generators that model rare strata explicitly, and (iii) report metric panels alongside qualitative, clinical sanity checks. Until such standards mature, our analysis highlights that researchers and regulators should treat synthetic data with caution.

Título: SFOA-based optimized SeResNet-BiLSTM network with an attention mechanism for the detection of exons.
Resumen: Detection of exons in eukaryotic DNA sequences is a challenging research area in computational biology. In this work, a Starfish Optimization Algorithm (SFOA) based hybrid deep learning architecture is proposed for the efficient detection of exons, which is the amalgamation of squeeze and excitation residual network (SeResNet), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and a customized attention (CA) mechanism. Firstly, SeResNet retrieves the deeply hidden features by performing recalibration and interdependencies between the channels. After that, BiLSTM is utilized to extract temporal information for a better understanding of the input data. Before applying the deep learning framework, the modified Gabor wavelet transform (MGWT) is used to extract the periodic feature information. The efficacy of the proposed model is validated using two benchmark datasets, namely the HMR195 and the Genscan training set. To verify the efficiency of the proposed method, its performance is compared with several pre-trained networks and various existing techniques using evaluation metrics. The simulation outcomes confirmed that the proposed SFOA-based hybrid optimized SeResNet-BiLSTM-CA model achieves superior performance than its counterparts.

Título: SOFEx: A Self-Organized Feature Extraction Approach for Detecting Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease using EEG Datasets.
Resumen: Early differentiation of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains difficult because diagnosis integrates cognitive, imaging, laboratory, and neurological evidence. EEG-based models may provide complementary information, but fixed descriptors can miss signal-specific structure. SOFEx was developed as an adaptive and interpretable EEG feature-engineering framework. The analysis used 1,905 EEG segments from 451 recordings of 168 participants (59 AD, seven MCI, and 102 controls). SOFEx combined self-organized rose pattern extraction, fold-wise feature selection, channel-wise classification, and iterative majority voting. Validation used leave-one-subject-out (LOSO), leave-one-record-out (LORO), and participant-grouped 10-fold cross-validation (CV). LORO and participant-grouped 10-fold CV achieved 93.65% and 96.38% accuracy, respectively, indicating substantial performance variation across validation schemes. Frontal and parietal electrodes contributed repeatedly to the selected configurations, providing sensor-space information on the signals supporting classification. SOFEx provides an adaptive and interpretable feature-engineering framework for EEG-based classification, combining input-specific pattern selection with sensor-level traceability. Participant-independent evaluation showed high sensitivity for AD, while discrimination of MCI remained more challenging. These findings support the potential of the proposed framework and motivate further validation on larger and independent cohorts to assess its generalizability across clinical settings.

Título: The anatomy of a personal health agent.
Resumen: Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored<sup>1,2</sup>. Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

ID (PMID): 42907476
Título: Global forest typology at 10-meter resolution for forest and land-use monitoring.
Resumen: Distinguishing forest types-primary, naturally regenerating, planted, and plantation forests-from agricultural tree crops and other land uses is essential for carbon accounting, biodiversity assessment, conservation planning, and supply-chain regulation. However, no existing global dataset resolves this typology at high spatial resolution. We present the Forest Typology (ForTy) v1 dataset, a global 10-meter resolution baseline map for 2020 that classifies all land into six categories aligned with FAO and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) definitions: Primary Forest, Naturally Regenerating Forest, Planted Forest, Plantation Forest, Tree Crops and Agroforestry, and Other Land. A cascaded deep learning pipeline, trained on 1.7 million globally distributed samples, generates per-class relative confidence maps from geospatial satellite embeddings by combining weakly supervised learning with active learning. Independent validation against 8,190 expert-labeled stratified random sites yields an overall accuracy of 90.2% for the six-class scheme, 94.8% for natural forest classification, and 95.5% for forest/non-forest classification.

Título: Five-country analysis of geographic and dietary drivers of gut microbiome composition and genomic variation.
Resumen: Human diet and lifestyle vary widely across cultures, shaping global diversity in gut microbiome composition and function. However, comparable cross-population studies have been limited by methodological heterogeneity. The Human Diets and Microbiome Initiative (THDMI) integrates standardized recruitment, dietary assessment, and shotgun metagenomics across 1,976 participants from the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, Mexico, and Japan to disentangle biological from technical variation. ID (PMID): 42907456
Título: Generating protein hydrogels with customizable stress relaxation behavior via deep learning-driven entanglement design.
Resumen: Protein hydrogels are promising artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) for 3D stem cell and organoid culture due to their favorable stress relaxation behavior (a decrease in stress in response to strain). Inter-chain entangled motifs, in which different protein chains are interlaced, represent a powerful strategy to synthesize such hydrogels. However, designing these motifs with tailored properties such as binding energy remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of simultaneously controlling these properties while ensuring entanglement. Here, we introduce TangleDiff, a deep learning framework for the de novo design of homodimeric entangled proteins with programmable features. TangleDiff generates diverse foldable entangled sequences with an in-silico success rate exceeding 70%, markedly outperforming current models (~1%). By conditioning TangleDiff on inter-chain binding energy, we generate novel protein dimers whose binding energies closely match the specified ranges, with approximately 70% of successful designs conforming to expected values. We experimentally validate TangleDiff by designing nine homodimers targeting various binding energies; seven successfully form hydrogels, with stress relaxation dynamics correlated with specified binding energies. This work establishes a general strategy for entangled protein design, opening avenues for entanglement-based biomaterial innovation.


--- ARTÍCULO 2691 ---
ID (PMID): 42907449
Título: Short-term memory of past caspase activity biases cell elimination in vivo.
Resumen: Apoptosis is triggered by the activation of Caspases leading to irreversible engagement in cell death. However, recent data outline numerous non-apoptotic functions of caspases as well as quite ubiquitous sublethal activation of effector caspases in vivo, opening the question of what drives the bifurcation between cell death and survival. Using quantitative live imaging combined with machine learning and optogenetics in the Drosophila pupal notum (a single-layer epithelium), we reveal the existence of a large heterogeneity of caspase activity thresholds between cells and distinct spatial domains with low or high sensitivity to caspases. We outline the central role of past exposure to sublethal caspase activity, which sensitises cells to apoptosis for several hours and reduces their threshold, and can bias single-cell elimination. Altogether, this work reveals the role of a cell's past history for apoptosis regulation in vivo, which can bias clonal selection and the spatial pattern of cell death.

ID (PMID): 42907299
Título: [Digital phenotyping in psychiatry: Concepts, systems, and clinical implications].
Resumen: Digital phenotyping uses smartphones, wearable devices, and embedded sensors to repeatedly quantify behavioral and physiological features in real-world settings. Its development in psychiatry raises conceptual, methodological, clinical, infrastructural, and ethical questions. This scoping review aimed to map the different understandings of digital phenotyping, their applications, and their main limitations. A scoping review was conducted. PubMed was searched for publications issued between January 1st, 2015, and December 31st, 2025. Publications directly addressing the conceptual foundations, methodologies, infrastructures, clinical applications, or ethical implications of digital phenotyping in psychiatry and mental health were eligible. The included publications were synthesized using thematic analysis. Forty-five publications were included and classified into five thematic domains: epistemology and epistemic injustice; clinical reasoning and decision models; sociotechnical systems and infrastructures; ethical considerations; and computational models and data-driven frameworks. Digital phenotyping enables the longitudinal assessment of mobility, sleep, activity, sociability, smartphone use, and selected physiological parameters. However, the resulting signals are shaped by device characteristics, sampling strategies, preprocessing decisions, and analytical models. Methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, platform dependency, and unresolved issues concerning clinical integration and data governance currently restrict generalizability. Digital phenotyping may complement clinical interviews and improve the study of individual trajectories, but it does not provide an exhaustive representation of mental states or constitute a validated biomarker in itself. Its clinical value depends on methodological reproducibility, robust infrastructures, demonstrable decision-making utility, and contextual interpretation by clinicians.

Título: [Artificial intelligence in child and adolescent psychiatry: A critical review of uses, evidence and relational stakes].
Resumen: To critically appraise the main current and emerging uses of artificial intelligence (AI) in child and adolescent psychiatry across three high-burden domains - autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and depression and suicide risk - and to examine the level of evidence, methodological limitations, and the ethical, safety and relational challenges specific to this population. Critical review of the literature. PubMed/MEDLINE and reference documents from international bodies (WHO, UNICEF, UNESCO) and the European regulatory framework were searched for 2018-2025, combining terms for artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital phenotyping and conversational agents with autism, ADHD, depression, suicide, child and adolescent. Studies were grouped into three domains: diagnostic and screening support; digital and AI-supported interventions; detection of depression and suicide risk. For depression and suicide, predictive models derived from electronic health records and digital phenotyping achieve fair discrimination (area under the curve often 0.80-0.86) but remain internally validated, with major concerns regarding bias, false positives and governance. Across domains, adolescents frequently describe conversational agents as available, non-judgmental and sometimes perceived as more "empathic" than human interlocutors, raising the question of a reconfiguration of the care relationship. AI offers genuine opportunities for detection, monitoring and some interventions in child and adolescent psychiatry, on the basis of evidence that remains limited and rarely tested in routine care. In a developing population, the integration of these tools must remain subordinate to clinical judgement, reinforced data protection and the centrality of the embodied encounter. AI should be conceived as an adjunct to care, not a substitute for the therapeutic relationship.

Título: Glow Up: a single-centre observational study protocol to develop digital biomarkers for prediabetes screening and digital phenotyping.
Resumen: Prediabetes, a key precursor to type 2 diabetes, is highly prevalent and underdiagnosed, particularly among adults aged ≥45 years with elevated body mass index (BMI). Early detection is critical because lifestyle interventions can delay or prevent progression to type 2 diabetes. The Glucose Observation and Wearable Use for Prevention (Glow Up) study aims to (1) test the feasibility of a digital biomarker for pre-diabetes screening using wearable- and smartphone-derived lifestyle factors (eg, sleep, physical activity and nutrition patterns) in daily life and to (2) characterise individual- and metabolic subgroup-level variability in lifestyle factors and glycaemic control. Specifically, we aim to examine how lifestyle factors relate to glycaemic status and identify personalised predictors of early metabolic dysregulation. Glow Up is a prospective, single-centre, observational case-control study conducted in Switzerland. Adults (n=200) aged ≥45 years with body mass index (BMI) ≥25 kg/m² will be recruited, including n=100 individuals with pre-diabetes and n=100 age- and sex-matched normoglycaemic controls. Participants will undergo 4 weeks of continuous monitoring using a blinded continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and commercial- and medical-grade wearables; for example, capturing physical activity, sleep and physiological markers (heart rate variability, heart rate and skin temperature), in addition to completing daily image-based meal logs using smartphones. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and body anthropometrics will be collected at the enrolment visit (T0) and repeated at follow-up (T3), approximately 5 weeks apart. The primary outcome is glycaemic status at T3, classified from HbA1c and FPG using prespecified thresholds. Secondary outcomes include CGM metrics, lifestyle profiling (sleep, physical activity, stress and nutrition) and adherence to image-based meal logging. The study received ethics approval from the Ethics Committee of Eastern Switzerland on 15 May 2025 (BASEC ID: 2025–00972). Título: Fast multi-view clustering via smooth low-rank tensor learning.

Additionally, this review addresses the use of AlphaFold models in major drug discovery processes including target identification, binding site prediction, molecular docking, virtual screening, lead optimization and structure-activity relationships (SAR). The possible utilization of AlphaFold in different areas of medicine, including oncology, antimicrobial resistance, neurodegenerative diseases and targeted protein degradation, is mentioned. Moreover, the collaboration of AlphaFold with new computational technologies, such as machine learning, generative artificial intelligence, molecular dynamics and multi-omics analysis, is described. An evidence-graded decision framework specifies when predicted structures are likely to suffice for hit finding, SAR interpretation, selectivity optimization, fragment-based design and degrader design and where quantitative evidence is still lacking. Even though AlphaFold has substantially advanced the field for example, in a prospective screen against the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) TAAR1, docking to AlphaFold2 models gave a 60% hit rate versus 22% for a homology model and a workflow combining an AlphaFold model with generative chemistry against the kinase CDK20 yielded a compound with an IC50 of 33.4 nM and an approximately eightfold antiproliferative selectivity window between cell lines-problems related to protein flexibility, conformational changes of proteins due to ligands, binding affinity prediction and biological complexity cannot be neglected and predicted structures still require experimental validation before guiding synthesis.

Título: Test-Retest Reliability of Large Language Models and Their Concordance With Human Experts in Rubric-Based Scoring of Clinical Summary Statements: Experimental Comparative Study.

Most VP systems provide little individualized feedback on the quality of learners' summaries, and earlier automated approaches have required complex natural language processing, limiting their scalability. Large language models (LLMs) may offer a more flexible, rubric-guided way to score summary statements and support feedback. Still, their test-retest reliability and concordance with expert ratings in this context remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate the test-retest reliability-specifically, whether the models produce stable ratings across repetitions-of LLM-generated medical summary statement ratings, and to measure their concordance with human expert assessments across different prompting strategies. Statements were evaluated along 4 ternary components (semantic qualifiers, transformation, narrowing, and global rating), and 2 binary components (factual accuracy and person). The test-retest reliability was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), Fleiss kappa (κ), and concordance with human ratings with accuracy (%) and chance-corrected interrater agreement (Gwet AC1 and AC2). Mistral 7B, a small open-weights model, had high ICCs (≥0.88) but low Fleiss κ (0.32-0.52). Concordance was higher for the binary rubric components (person and factual accuracy) than for the ternary components. Extreme deviations and invalid outputs were rare but more frequent in ternary components and the smaller local model. Large, general-purpose LLMs can function as reliable, rubric-guided raters of VP-based clinical summary statements, achieving high concordance with expert ratings under clearly defined criteria in binary rubric components and when using few-shot with CoT prompting. The performance on more nuanced, ternary reasoning dimensions was more variable. LLMs can support scalable, rubric-based formative feedback on clinical reasoning within VP systems but should complement rather than replace human judgment.

Three-dimensional molecular structures generated from SMILES strings were rotated around the x, y, and z-axes, converted into binary two-dimensional projections, and assembled into standardized multi-view tensors for CCS regression. Deep3DCCS was developed and evaluated using curated AllCCS and METLIN lipid CCS datasets containing 3948 molecule-adduct entries across [M - H]-, [M + H]+, and [M + Na]+ ions, and input optimization identified 32 × 32 pixel projections with five rotations per axis as a practical balance between prediction accuracy, model stability, and computational feasibility. In independent true-validation experiments, AllCCS-trained models achieved MRPE values of 3.27-3.79% on AllCCS validation data and 2.93-3.72% on METLIN validation data, whereas METLIN-trained models transferred less effectively to the broader AllCCS chemical space. Overall, these results support multi-view molecular projection tensors as a viable geometry-driven representation for CCS prediction and demonstrate that substantial CCS-relevant information can be learned directly from three-dimensional molecular morphology using a 3DCNN architecture, with low single-digit prediction errors across independent and cross-dataset validation experiments.

Self-MF provides an effective, self-supervised solution for high-fidelity MC-MRI reconstruction without fully sampled target-contrast labels. By combining contrast-aware self-supervision, frequency-domain conditioning, and diffusion-based reconstruction, the framework achieves superior image quality and robust anatomical preservation, representing a significant advancement for multi-contrast MRI in both research and clinical practice.
