Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were developed to predict suicidal ideation, suicide planning, and suicide attempts. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and related metrics. Feature importance was examined using gain-based measures, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots were used to explore the direction, strength, and nonlinear effects of key predictors. All three XGBoost models showed satisfactory predictive performance. Mental health factors, particularly persistent feelings of sadness and self-rated mental health, were the strongest predictors across all stages of suicidal behaviors. Lifestyle behaviors, including sleep duration, physical activity, diet, screen time, and substance use, also contributed meaningfully to risk prediction, although their relative importance differed by outcome. SHAP analyses indicated that greater sadness and poorer mental health were strongly associated with higher suicide risk, whereas adequate sleep and higher levels of physical activity were associated with lower predicted risk. Substance use, including alcohol, cigarette, and marijuana use, played an important role in predicting suicide attempts than suicidal ideation or planning. Partial dependence analyses showed nonlinear and threshold effects, especially for sadness, mental health status, and sleep duration. Mental health factors, especially persistent sadness and overall psychological well-being, were among the most prominent factors associated with suicidal behaviors among adolescents, while lifestyle behaviors showed important and stage-specific associations. Interpretable machine learning approaches help identify complex and nonlinear patterns associated with adolescent suicide risk and offer valuable insights to guide targeted, evidence-based prevention efforts.

Título: Predicting mental health risk in adolescents using interpretable machine learning: Evidence from SHAP analysis.
Resumen: Adolescent mental health is a critical public health concern; however, the combined contribution of emotional, demographic, and behavioral factors to poor mental health remains incompletely understood. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to assess feature importance and directional and non-linear patterns. SHAP analysis identified sadness/hopelessness as the dominant predictor, followed by sex, sleep duration, screen time, and breakfast frequency. In a sensitivity analysis excluding sadness/hopelessness, discrimination decreased (AUC 0.736; PR-AUC 0.510). The revised primary model achieved balanced sensitivity and specificity above 0.700 using a threshold selected entirely within the training data. Sadness/hopelessness was the strongest predictor, while demographic and behavioral factors provided additional predictive information. Because sadness/hopelessness is conceptually close to the current mental health outcome and the data are cross-sectional, the model should be interpreted as an auxiliary risk-stratification tool rather than a standalone clinical screening or diagnostic instrument.

Nanotechnology offers a route to reduce this diagnostic-therapeutic latency. Nanostructured biosensors and liquid biopsy platforms detect placental proteins, cell-free RNA/DNA, and extracellular vesicles at femtomolar concentrations and in a multiplex manner, enabling earlier risk stratification when integrated with machine-learning models. In parallel, placenta-targeted lipid-, peptide-, polymeric-, dendrimeric-, and small extracellular vesicle-based nanocarriers deliver angiogenic mRNA, antiangiogenic siRNA, antioxidants, and immunomodulators selectively to the trophoblast cells while limiting fetal exposure. Placenta-on-a-chip platforms and ex vivo placental perfusion models provide human-relevant test beds for these systems. We critically appraise these advances, examine the safety-by-design, manufacturing bottlenecks, and regulatory constraints unique to obstetric nanomedicine, and outline the convergence of theranostics and digital health that could move preeclampsia care from reactive symptom management toward proactive, placenta-targeted monitoring and therapy.

ID (PMID): 42904299
Título: Advancements in bottom-up synthesis routes for monolayer graphene: a review.
Resumen: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.

A useful subtype must be reproducible across cohorts, anchored to plausible biology, associated with a distinct clinical course, and able to improve diagnosis, therapeutic selection, or clinical-trial design. This Review examines the translational continuum from experimental HFpEF models to human patient subtypes, summarizes the main deep-phenotyping domains and AI approaches, and proposes seven clinically interpretable subtype families: cardiometabolic-inflammatory, hypertensive-vascular aging, atrial myopathy, pulmonary vascular-right ventricular, cardiorenal-congestive, peripheral-frailty, and specific etiologic phenocopies. Current evidence supports a layered treatment strategy in which broadly effective therapies, particularly sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, are combined with phenotype-directed management of obesity, diabetes, mineralocorticoid receptor activation, atrial fibrillation, congestion, pulmonary vascular disease, and physical deconditioning. The central next step is prospective validation of dynamic subtype assignments in external populations and phenotype-enriched trials. Phenogroup labels should therefore be regarded as pragmatic, transitional proxies for dominant mechanisms when those mechanisms cannot yet be measured directly at the individual-patient level; their value lies in improving decisions while the field moves toward fully individualized mechanism-based treatment. Deep phenotyping will be clinically valuable only when it changes a decision and improves an outcome, rather than merely increasing descriptive complexity.

Título: Subject-independent classification of ADHD from pediatric EEG: a leakage-aware deep learning framework with interpretable neurophysiological mapping.

Hand-engineered spectral features are highly vulnerable to identity leakage, whereas end-to-end convolutional models generalize across subjects with realistic, uninflated performance. Strict subject-wise validation is strongly recommended as standard practice for translational EEG research.

The reactivity of B[3] sites is strongly dependent on the type and number of second-nearest-neighbor cations, with boron sites linked to Al or Zr exhibiting markedly lower reactivity than those linked to Si or B[3], indicating site-selective and incongruent initial boron dissolution. These results provide a quantitative atomistic basis for understanding how glass composition controls boron dissolution at multicomponent glass-water interfaces.

Título: Dynamics-informed machine learning for recovering extensive missing systems dynamics.
Resumen: Inevitable missing values in observational time series often hinder reliable data-driven modeling of complex systems across diverse domains. Recovery is essential yet challenging, particularly in high-dimensional systems where most variables can exhibit extensive intra-series missingness and widespread inter-variable missingness simultaneously. In this study, we introduce a dynamics-informed imputation framework, termed Full-Partial Reconstruction Mapping (FPRM). In contrast to traditional approaches that directly fit time series interdependences, the FPRM embeds intrinsic dynamical priors via state-space reconstruction and recovers multiple incomplete series by learning diffeomorphic topology between attractors from complete and incomplete data. We validate the FPRM on paradigmatic model systems (e.g., an ecology system, the ordinary Lorenz system, a coupled 120-dimensional (120D) Lorenz system, and a coupled 120D Rössler system and real-world datasets (e.g., road occupancy rate from transportation system, electroencephalogram (EEG) signals from neuroscience, exchange rates from finance, and wind speed from climate systems). Even in high-dimensional systems where only one variable is fully observed and all others suffer from extreme missingness (e.g., 90%), the FPRM enables reliable imputation of multiple incomplete variables-a task that challenges most existing approaches. This dynamics-guided framework outperforms traditional approaches, alleviating substantial data gaps and enabling robust data-driven paradigms for complex dynamical systems.

Título: Bayesian bilevel operator learning with low-rank adaptation for efficient uncertainty quantification of PDE inverse problems.
Resumen: Uncertainty quantification in PDE inverse problems is essential in many applications. Scientific machine learning and AI enable data-driven learning of model components while preserving physical structure, and provide the scalability and adaptability needed for emerging imaging technologies and clinical insights. We develop a Bilevel Local Operator Learning framework for Bayesian inference in PDEs (B-BiLO). At the upper level, we sample parameters from the posterior via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, while at the lower level we fine-tune a neural network via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to approximate the solution operator locally. Numerical experiments across PDE models, including tumor growth, demonstrate that B-BiLO achieves accurate and efficient uncertainty quantification.

Título: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand.
Resumen: Climate change and technology diffusion will jointly drive future growth in building electricity demand. How this nonadditive response evolves over time with the pace of climate change and technology diffusion has not previously been examined, despite its importance for maintaining reliable power systems. We estimate electricity demand from residential and commercial buildings under climate change and/or technology diffusion across 183 counties in the United States through 2060. Our framework drives 209,352 machine learning models of building electricity demand with 100 spatiotemporally downscaled climate realizations across four climate models and three emissions scenarios, and 18 technology diffusion pathways of air source heat pumps and insulation. Internal variability accounts for a much larger share of climate-related uncertainty in peak demand than in temperature itself. Our results demonstrate that capturing nonadditive responses between climate change and technology diffusion is important for planning reliable power systems.

Resumen: To systematically review and characterize methodological heterogeneity in sepsis case detection using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) and eICU-CRD databases. Dependencies among several MIMIC-III repositories suggested propagation of implementation decisions across studies. Clinically validated sepsis definitions yield substantially different detection rates across studies using identical datasets. Statistical modeling showed that this variability is driven almost entirely by between-study implementation differences rather than sampling error or study characteristics. To improve reproducibility in sepsis research and the robustness of sepsis prediction models, we recommend standardized reporting of sepsis case detection methodology and the publication of version-controlled source code.

Resumen: Lower‑field 0.55 T MRI scanners with large‑bore design could offer patients more comfortable feeling and flexible position. With the advances in deep‑learning reconstruction and hardware optimization, 0.55T have greatly improved their image quality and cost‑effectiveness for musculoskeletal applications. However, its feasibility for shoulder evaluation remains unstudied. To evaluate the image quality of shoulder using 0.55T MRI in volunteers and patients with rotator cuff injury with comparison of conventional 1.5T. Fifty participants (25 volunteers, 25 patients) were prospectively enrolled. All participants underwent shoulder MRI both at open 0.55T with contour coils and deep learning (DL) and 1.5T MR without DL. The nonparametric method was utilized to compare image quality scores and quantitative metrics (signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (|CNR|)). Arthroscopy have been conducted in 16 patients. Kappa statistics was used to assess interobserver and interstudy agreement for lesion evaluation. Comfort feeling was also compared. The scan time was 11'25″ for 0.55T MRI and 11'42″ for 1.5T MRI. The interobserver analyses showed high consistency (κ = 0.771-1.000, P: 0.008 ∼ < 0.001) among 3 readers. The scores for coronal fat suppressed T2 weighted imaging (fsT2WI) and coronal T1 weighted imaging (T1WI) were significantly higher for 0.55T MRI. Most sequences at 0.55T demonstrated significantly higher SNRs (P:0.04 ∼ < 0.001). Additionally, |CNR| values for lesions were significantly higher in fs proton weighted imaging (PDWI) and fsT2WI at 0.55T. Perfect interstudy agreement between 0.55T and 1.5T was observed between 2 readers (Kappa = 1, P < 0.001) for lesion assessment. Agreement between MRI findings and arthroscopic results was perfect or good. The 0.55T system received higher scores in comfort ratings. The 0.55T MRI with DL, showed comparable or better image quality in healthy subjects and patients with rotator cuff injury to 1.5T MRI without DL.

Título: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models.
Resumen: Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy. A comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion. The integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning. Combining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.

Resumen: TODD-Graphene (TODD-G), a porous two-dimensional carbon allotrope composed of interconnected 3-8-10-12 carbon rings, has recently emerged as a promising candidate for nanoelectromechanical and adaptive nanodevice applications due to its metallic conductivity, mechanical compliance, and topologically engineered phonon structure. Fundamental frequencies were found to span 2.93-13.28 THz and follow the classical <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi> <mo>∝</mo> <msup><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow> <mrow><mo>-</mo> <mn>2</mn></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> scaling relation. Vacancy defects significantly degraded quality factors and resonance stability, whereas multilayer stacking improved energy retention despite modest frequency reduction. Boundary conditions strongly altered modal spectra, with clamped-clamped configurations producing the highest frequencies and quality factors. Phonon density-of-states analysis revealed distinct acoustic, mixed, and optical vibrational regimes with a maximum phonon cutoff frequency of 56.5 THz. Atomic-scale simulations were performed using classical molecular dynamics within the large-scale atomic/molecular massively parallel simulator (LAMMPS) package. Interatomic interactions were described using the adaptive intermolecular reactive empirical bond order (AIREBO) potential with activated Lennard-Jones and torsional terms, while multilayer van der Waals interactions employed a 12-6 Lennard-Jones potential. Structural relaxation was conducted using conjugate-gradient energy minimization. Thermal equilibration employed the Nosé-Hoover thermostat within the canonical (NVT) ensemble, followed by microcanonical (NVE) simulations for vibrational analysis using a timestep of 0.5 fs. Vibrational properties were extracted using impulse-response analysis, velocity autocorrelation functions, harmonic forcing, fast Fourier transform (FFT) spectral analysis, and phonon density-of-states calculations. Simulations systematically examined the effects of nanosheet size, temperature (1-1000 K), tensile strain (0-10%), vacancy-defect concentration (0.5-5%), multilayer stacking (1-5 layers), and boundary conditions (free-free, clamped-free, simply supported, and clamped-clamped). Machine-learning surrogate models including linear regression, support-vector regression with radial-basis-function kernels, random forest regression, and gradient-boosting regression were trained using an 80/20 train-test split and five-fold cross-validation to predict resonance frequency and quality factor across the multidimensional parameter space.

An ecological analysis was conducted using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data from 204 countries. Machine-learning-based feature selection was used to screen 68 risk factors. Título: Beyond Scalar Objectives: Expert-Feedback-Driven Autonomous Experimentation for Scientific Discovery at the Nanoscale.
Resumen: Self-driving laboratories or autonomous experimentation are emerging as transformative platforms for accelerating scientific discovery. Bayesian optimization (BO) is among the most widely used machine learning frameworks in self-driving laboratories, but these BO-based frameworks rely on predefined scalar descriptors to guide experimentation. This limits their ability to handle complex phenomena that are difficult to formalize as scalar descriptors. In many situations, the determination of an appropriate scalar descriptor can be challenging, and may fail to capture subtle yet scientifically important phenomena apparent to experts with interdisciplinary insight. This problem is particularly pronounced in nanoscale imaging experiments, where strong local heterogeneity, multidimensional observations, and emergent physical behaviors often cannot be effectively represented using scalar metrics. To overcome this limitation, here we develop deep-kernel pairwise learning (DKPL), an approach for autonomous microscopy experiments which incorporates human expertise and interdisciplinary scientific knowledge into an active learning loop. Instead of relying on explicit scalar objectives, DKPL enables experts to directly evaluate which experimental output is more promising using interdisciplinary knowledge. DKPL then learns a latent utility function from these expert judgments to guide subsequent autonomous microscopy experiments. We demonstrate DKPL's performance in learning physically meaningful nanoscale structures in lead titanate thin films while effectively prioritizing high-information measurement regions using an experimental model dataset with known ground truth. We further apply DKPL to analyze the character of ferroelectric domain walls, where we find DKPL capable of distinguishing between high and low characteristic domain-wall angles in lead zirconium titanate, and able to discover both head-to-head and tail-to-tail domain-wall character in erbium manganite. Autonomous experiments in mixed-phase bismuth ferrite also demonstrate DKPL's ability to link material structure with their properties in on-the-fly measurements. This development demonstrates an approach to integrate expert knowledge into autonomous microscopy experiments across a variety of material systems, and demonstrates a pathway toward expert-guided self-driving laboratories capable of addressing scientific problems beyond the limits of scalar-metrics-driven learning.

Título: Modeling Phase Separation in Polymer-Derived Silicon Carbonitride Ceramics through Extended Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics.
Resumen: Polymer-derived ceramics combine the thermal stability of ceramics with the versatile properties of carbon domains, but modeling their atomic-scale evolution during processing remains elusive because of the limitations of traditional computational methods. To address this issue, here, we develop and apply a machine learning interatomic potential for hydrogen-containing silicon carbonitride-based (SiCNH) ceramics, trained on a diversified database of over 9000 configurations─including amorphous models, high-temperature states, surfaces, and crystal structure predictions─to capture the full complexity of these materials. This potential enables large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of 8000-atom systems, revealing the atomic-scale evolution of the polymer-derived ceramic during thermal treatment. A key result of this work is the occurrence of a phase separation, where carbon domains progressively nucleate from the amorphous SiCN matrix during thermal processing, forming distinct graphene-like sheets while preserving the integrity of the ceramic network. The resulting models reproduce the experimental atomic pair distribution functions, supporting our approach and providing microscopic explanations for the material combination of the ceramic and graphitic properties. In this process, defective 5- and/or 7-member carbon rings mediate the transformation to stable 6-member aromatic structures. These findings provide atomic-scale information about the thermal stability and structural transformation pathways of polymer-derived ceramics and demonstrate the applicability of the methodology to complex amorphous systems at experimentally relevant scales.

Título: A fuzzy-enhanced broad learning framework with minority-class ensemble for ECG arrhythmia classification.
Resumen: Existing broad learning system (BLS)-based Electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia classification methods still face limitations in multi-source feature representation, sample reliability modeling, and minority-class recognition. To address these issues, this study proposes a combinational improvement framework built upon BLS, integrating uncertainty-aware gated fuzzy feature enhancement and a minority-class ensemble strategy for ECG arrhythmia classification. First, heartbeat waveform, QRS complex structural information, and RR rhythm features are integrated to construct a hybrid ECG representation that jointly captures morphological and rhythm characteristics. The framework trades a moderate training-time and memory footprint (an ensemble of tree models over analysis of variance-selected BLS features) for these minority-class gains, while inference remains a CPU-friendly single forward pass through the frozen pipeline. It improves minority-class recognition relative to the compared methods under severe class imbalance, while the recognition of fusion beats under the inter-patient protocol remains challenging (five-seed mean<i>F</i>1 of 6.722.69%) and is explicitly discussed as a limitation.

Título: Neglecting Changes in Salinity and Tidal Range Overstates Projected Increases in Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Mangrove Sediments.
Resumen: Mangroves are important coastal blue carbon ecosystems, but future sediment GHG emissions remain uncertain because global projections have largely emphasized atmospheric climate drivers, with less attention to coastal hydrology, particularly sea-surface salinity and tidal range. Here, we compiled 810 sediment GHG flux measurements from 294 mangrove sites worldwide and used machine learning to project emissions to 2050, distinguishing climate-driven changes from the additional effects of projected shifts in sea-surface salinity and tidal range. Título: Niche Divergence-Based Identification of Microbial Indicators Tracking Cyanobacterial Bloom Succession: A Metagenomic and Machine Learning Framework.
Resumen: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs) pose significant environmental and public health risks through toxin production, antibiotic resistance gene dissemination, and the disruption of biogeochemical cycles. Although extensive metagenomic investigations have explored microbial interactions between Cyanobacteria and coexisting members, the potential of incorporating functional indicators into early CyanoHAB monitoring systems remains underexplored. In this study, we employed metagenomic binning combined with machine learning approaches to analyze seasonal cyanobacterial succession and coexisting microbial communities across 19 sites in Erhai Lake across four seasons. We documented distinct niche shifts driven by the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in seasonal cyanobacterial succession alongside the formation of unique niches triggered by this asynchrony. Specialized microbial members (SN-MAGs) were identified as candidate bioindicators associated with early-stage cyanobacterial proliferation. Functional profiling showed r/K selection and metabolic adaptations in these SN-MAGs, including stress resistance and altered carbon metabolism, linked to cyanobacterial dynamics. Machine learning models leveraging these features were constructed and retrospectively evaluated. Cross-lake validation using an independent Lake Taihu dataset confirmed associations among these features and microbial community shifts preceding Microcystis proliferation. Our findings highlight the potential value of the dynamics of specific bacteria as a sensitive indicator of cyanobacterial dynamics. Moreover, we propose that these identified functional markers could potentially be developed into targeted molecular assays (e.g., qPCR assays), offering possible utility in predicting Microcystis population expansion.


--- ARTÍCULO 2919 ---
ID (PMID): 42899635
Título: Machine Learning Attribution of Atmospheric Black Carbon in a Coastal City: Source Variability and the Sea-Land Breeze Recirculation Mechanism.
Resumen: Black carbon (BC) variability in coastal environments reflects the combined effects of emission sources, regional transport, and mesoscale circulation. This study selected the typical coastal city of Qingdao as the study area, collected BC online observation data for one year in 2021, and integrated it with the Aethalometer model, trajectory analysis, and Random Forest (RF) machine learning framework to examine these mechanisms. The annual mean BC concentration was 1.78 ± 1.29 μg m-3, with fossil fuel combustion contributing 88.2% of the total mass, while the biomass burning contribution increased to 19% in winter. Source-resolved attribution showed distinct meteorological responses. Fossil-fuel black carbon (BCff) was more strongly associated with wind-controlled ventilation and transport, whereas biomass burning BC (BCbb) responded more strongly to low-temperature conditions. Under sea-land breeze (SLB) conditions, BC enhancement was most evident at wind speeds of 2.0 to 3.5 m s-1. Diurnal persistence, directional shifts in elevated fossil fuel BC, and interactions between wind speed and wind direction further supported return transport and reaccumulation within coastal circulation. These findings provide process-based insight into source-dependent BC variability and SLB-related reaccumulation in coastal environments.

ID (PMID): 42899634
Título: Wearable sensors and VOC monitoring: data fusion and machine learning for non-invasive disease detection.
Resumen: Emerging technologies that detect volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emanating from the body enable rapid and non-invasive detection of diseases. Respiratory illnesses, in particular, can be identified through measurement of VOCs in exhaled breath. However, the low specificity of some methods leaves room for improvement. By combining information from multiple data streams, we can potentially improve on the results obtained from using each data stream individually. Here we evaluate a novel data fusion approach combining a wearable vitals monitor and exhaled breath VOCs for the classification of asthma patients. The wearable vitals monitor or 'e-glove' measures key information such as skin temperature, trans-epidermal water loss, heart rate, and galvanic skin response, while the breath VOC data (measured by gold standard gas chromatography-mass spectrometry) provide insight into the biochemical and metabolic state of the body. Data fusion is a process used in many applications for combining information from disparate sources. We leverage data fusion in this case to achieve superior classification accuracy using the integrated data streams. The low-level data fusion achieved a higher ROC AUC score (0.88) in asthma classification than the breath VOC-only approach (0.72,<i>p</i>< 0.001). These results are promising for future data analysis workflows for non-invasive diagnostic and health monitoring.


--- ARTÍCULO 2921 ---
ID (PMID): 42899581
Título: Leveraging the Synergy between Mechanistic Insight and Machine Learning for Predictive Structure-Performance Relationships in Organic Synthesis.
Resumen: Understanding how molecular structure determines reaction performance is a central objective of physical organic chemistry and an increasingly important challenge in data-driven organic synthesis. As the frontiers of synthetic chemistry continue to advance, predictive structure-performance relationship modeling is expected not only to reproduce known reaction outcomes but also to guide new chemical design. In this Account, we summarize our efforts to integrate mechanistic insight with machine learning across data construction, model development, and discovery applications. At the data level, mechanistic understanding can help define reaction spaces and learning targets, allowing automated density functional theory calculations and literature-derived databases to become chemically consistent learning resources. This idea is illustrated by computed selectivity data sets for radical C-H functionalization and Cu(II)-mediated radical bond formation as well as literature databases for asymmetric hydrogenation of olefins and N,N'-dioxide/metal-catalyzed Michael additions. At the modeling level, mechanistic knowledge can be embedded into reaction representations and model architectures. Transition-state-based reaction encoding introduces pathway-specific stereochemical information into enantioselectivity prediction, while steric- and electronics-embedded molecular graphs incorporate physical organic effects directly into molecular deep learning. At the discovery level, mechanistic relatedness provides a basis for selecting historical data and transferring structure-performance relationships into low-data chemical space. This mechanism-guided transfer learning formalizes how chemists reuse related precedents, enabling few-shot catalyst ligand discovery for Ni-catalyzed atroposelective Suzuki-Miyaura coupling. A central lesson from these studies is that mechanistic insight is not a replacement for machine learning but the chemical foundation that makes it more reliable, interpretable, and extrapolative. By translating mechanistic understanding into data boundaries, reaction representations, and transfer strategies, machine learning can move beyond retrospective fitting and become a chemically grounded framework for predicting and discovering new organic reactions.

ID (PMID): 42899578
Título: Confined Growth of MOFs into Angstrom-Scale Defect-Free Membranes for Precise Molecular Separation.
Resumen: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), featuring ordered nanochannels and versatile pore chemistry, have emerged as promising materials for developing next-generation separation membranes. MOF-based membranes are typically synthesized either by the intergrowth of crystals to form polycrystalline membranes or by incorporating crystals into polymers to form mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). During the membrane formation processes, multiscale defects─ranging from microscale intercrystalline cracks and nanoscale interfacial gaps to angstrom-scale lattice defects─are prone to arise. These undesirable defects compromise the membrane structural integrity and molecular transport properties, thus impairing the separation efficiency and impeding the implementation of MOF-based membranes for precise molecular separation. In this Account, we present our group's efforts to construct defect-free molecular sieving membranes based on the "confined growth of MOFs". We first establish MOF design and selection principles by correlating molecular transport mechanisms with framework characteristics. We then demonstrate how confined growth enables the elimination of multiscale defects in both polycrystalline membranes and MMMs. For polycrystalline membranes, the elimination of angstrom-scale lattice defects has been a long-standing challenge. To address this, we proposed a high-probability theoretical coordination strategy that creates sufficient chemical potential to overcome the steric hindrance that occurs when connecting ligands to metal clusters. By further regulating the confinement of coordination reactants (e.g., ligands, metal cluster precursor), coordination environment (e.g., solvent, modulator), and coordination space (e.g., pore size, topology), we inhibited the linker-missing and metal cluster-missing defects and restored intrinsic lattice integrity in MOF membranes. This leads to a family of high-connectivity MOF membranes exhibiting outstanding molecular separation performance, not only for gases but also for water/ions and organic mixtures. By employing atomic-level characterizations (e.g., real-space high-resolution transmission electron microscopy) and molecular simulations, we revealed the underlying thermodynamics and kinetic mechanism of defect suppression and confined molecular transport through the lattice aperture. For MMMs, despite the structural integrity achieved in the as-synthesized crystals, incorporating these crystals into polymers remains another grand challenge because this process often introduces multiscale defects resulting from filler aggregation and interfacial incompatibility. Recognizing that the space between MOF fillers and the polymer matrix represents a typical confined environment, we pursued molecular-confined strategies to solve the dispersion and compatibility issues in MMMs. Recently, we proposed a solid-solvent processing strategy to fabricate an ultrathin and highly loaded defect-free MMM for molecular sieving. The polymer serves as a solid solvent, confining MOF nucleation and in situ growth on the polymer chains to avoid crystal aggregation and interfacial defects. This yields a new-generation nanocomposite membrane with MOF crystals as the continuous phase, enabling fast molecular transport through interconnected MOF nanochannels. Notably, this general polymer-confined growth allows for the scalable fabrication of MMMs toward diverse molecular separation applications including hydrogen separation, CO2 capture, and organic azeotropic separations. By integrating machine learning and high-throughput calculations, our group also explored the AI-accelerated design and customized synthesis of MOF-based membranes. We conclude this Account by discussing the remaining limitations, challenges, and opportunities of further exploring angstrom-scale defect-free MOF membranes. We hope that this Account can provide insights in developing next-generation molecularly selective separation membranes toward broad applications and stimulate or deepen interest in multiple disciplines crossing chemistry, materials science, and chemical engineering.

ID (PMID): 42899577
Título: Developing Sustainable Chemistry with AI.
Resumen: Today we are experiencing an unprecedentedly rapid transformation of science, driven by advances in computing and artificial intelligence (AI). At the same time, there are growing cumulative pressures of climate change impacts that not only affect economies but are creating significant societal challenges. The confluence of technology push and environmental-socioeconomic pressures is promoting the development of sustainable chemistry. The link between the transition to sustainability in chemistry and the digital transformation of R&D and manufacturing has been the long-standing focus in our research (Fantke, P.; et al. Chem 2021, 7, 2866 doi: 10.1016/j.chempr.2021.09.012). Sustainability is not a feature of a single chemical product or a process. It is incorrect to talk about "sustainable polyethylene", as such narrow framing will miss many issues in the more holistic system that not only includes the cradle-to-grave life cycle emission impacts of polyethylene but also considers all aspects of equity, impact on biodiversity, resilience of supply chains, etc. Sustainable chemistry makes sense only as a complex system. An analysis of complex systems requires large amounts of data and the use of appropriate analytical tools, such as advanced machine learning techniques. The chemical industry has been an early adopter of digital technologies, motivated by the inherent complexity of chemical systems and the need for efficiency to stay economically competitive. As early as the 1970s, cheminformatics tools were introduced to support structure-property analysis. In the 1980s, we saw the broad adoption of process modeling and simulation tools for design, scale-up, and optimization of chemical processes, paralleled with developments in the field of process system engineering and control. Today's digital transition is much deeper; everything from scientific discovery (molecules, materials, and phenomena) to chemical process development, analytical methods and process analytical technologies, and plant operation is being reshaped. This deep transformation includes the development of a radically different approach to data in chemistry. Advances in self-driving laboratories, agentic AI workflows, and digital factories require access to structured, semantically rich data. In this Account, we focus on three key areas of digitalization and AI technologies advancing chemistry and chemical process development toward net-zero targets. First, we discuss how data mining tools are used to analyze the existing value chains and identify opportunities to integrate net-zero feedstocks. When new molecules are introduced, data-driven route planning can be employed to design alternative synthetic pathways, which then need to be rigorously evaluated. Second, we focus on how to use AI to accelerate discoveries in chemistry, including the innovative design of catalysts, rational selection of solvents, and identification of optimal reaction conditions. By leveraging statistical modeling and data-driven optimization, these traditionally time-consuming tasks can now be performed much faster. Lastly, we discuss how to bring these innovations from the laboratory to manufacturing, which also requires advances in process technologies. We show that by leveraging AI agents, process modeling, and knowledge graphs, there is a potential to achieve automated process design and life cycle assessment, removing traditional choke points in scaling technologies and providing timely support for decision-making in early-stage development. In the end, we discuss the current challenges and future perspectives.

Título: Machine-Learning-Driven Dual-Mode Immunoassay Based on Nanobody and Natural Fluorescent Probe for Ultrasensitive Quantification of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Resumen: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative opportunistic bacterial pathogen posing severe threat to environmental safety and human health. To achieve rapid and accurate detection, we developed a nanobody-based colorimetric-fluorescent dual-mode sandwich immunosensor using natural fluorescent probe and further integrated machine learning to enhance the signal readout and improve detection sensitivity. Here, specific nanobodies toward P. aeruginosa were successfully developed for the first time by biopanning against an immune phage-displayed nanobody library. Natural fluorescent quinine, which possesses intrinsic fluorescence and undergoes fluorescence quenching via an internal quenching effect, was employed as the fluorescent probe. With the baseline LODs obtained by direct fitting of the raw optical signals (9.005 × 105 CFU/mL for colorimetry and 3.02 × 103 CFU/mL for fluorescence), an XGBoost model was introduced and further reduces the LOD to 3.269 × 103 CFU/mL and 3.96 × 102 CFU/mL, achieving a 275-fold and 7.6-fold improvement in sensitivity, respectively. Furthermore, following a brief pre-enrichment, this method enables detection of P. aeruginosa at concentrations as low as 10 CFU/mL. Recoveries in water samples ranged from 81.47% to 119.47%, with a coefficient of variation below 8.44%, showing good agreement with machine learning predictions (R2 = 0.957). No cross-reactivity was observed with closely related or heterologous bacteria. This method provides a technical approach for the precise quantitative monitoring of P. aeruginosa in complex environments.

ID (PMID): 42899531
Título: Physics-Informed Machine Learning Overcomes Particle-Size Nonlinearities That Confound the Raman Spectrometry of Granular Carbonaceous Materials.
Resumen: Raman spectroscopy supports multivariate regression models that can offer a rapid and nondestructive approach to quantifying the composition of granular materials. Soils constitute a class of such materials for which chemical analysis provides vital information for agriculture and environmental stewardship. However, soil samples typically present highly heterogeneous mixtures of varying particle size and diverse optical properties owing to light-absorbing constituents. Although particle-size effects on Raman spectrometry in scattering media have long been considered in the context of pharmaceutical analytical technology, the quantitative influence of particle size in opaque, absorbing materials remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effect of particle size and light absorption in controlled mixture systems that mimic soils. These mixtures, containing particles of varying sizes and optical properties, isolate the ways in which fluorescence, granularity and light absorption affect the accuracy of machine learning regression models. Using a dual-laser Raman system, we collected both conventional Raman and Shifted-Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS) spectra, showing that light-absorbing compounds attenuate Raman intensities nonlinearly to an extent that varies with particle size. Multivariate regression models link this behavior to optical extinction governed by the surface area of the absorbing grains. We account for this behavior in terms of a simple physical model that incorporates the physics of light scattering and absorption in heterogeneous systems of varying particle size. This hybrid, physics-informed machine learning framework outperforms purely data-driven approaches in predicting sample composition from Raman spectra, highlighting the importance of physical characteristics in the analysis of light-absorbing granular materials.

Título: Machine-Learning Surrogate Modeling of DFT-Calculated Binding Energies for Ionic Liquid Ion-Pairs.
Resumen: Ion-pair binding energy is a fundamental property that governs the physicochemical behavior of ionic liquids (ILs), influencing ion dissociation, transport, interfacial behavior, and field-driven extraction processes across a wide range of applications. Accurate prediction of this quantity is therefore essential for rational IL design. While density functional theory (DFT) delivers precise energetic characterization of ion pairs, its computational demands render it impractical for high-throughput evaluation of ionic liquid (IL) candidates. Here, we present a machine learning (ML) approach for direct prediction of DFT-derived ion-pair binding energies from SMILES strings of component ions. To resolve the mapping from molecular structure to binding energy, we considered seven machine learning surrogates: (1) kernel ridge regression (KRR), (2) Gaussian process regression (GPR), (3) random forest (RF), (4) XGBoost, (5) LightGBM, (6) CatBoost, and (7) graph neural network (GNN), trained on a set of 100 ion pairs and tested on a held-out set of 20 ion pairs. The gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost) achieved the best predictive performance, yielding an average coefficient of determination ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow><msup><mi>R</mi> <mn>2</mn></msup> </mrow> </math> ) of about 0.844 and an average Spearman's rank correlation coefficient ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>ρ</mi></mrow> </math> ) of about 0.879. The results from this study highlight the strong potential of descriptor-driven ML approaches to estimate ion-pair binding energies, establishing their utility as computationally efficient alternatives to DFT for preliminary screening of ionic liquids across varied application domains.

ID (PMID): 42899404
Título: Distinct trajectories of disease severity progression in juvenile systemic sclerosis.
Resumen: Juvenile systemic sclerosis (JSSc) often presents with overlapping features, making phenotypic classification and disease progression difficult to define. This study investigated whether JSSc comprises latent disease severity subgroups with distinct longitudinal trajectories and examined baseline predictors of class membership. Retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected data from 45 patients with JSSc between January 2005 and December 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory and disease severity data were collected. The primary outcome was progression-free survival (PFS), defined as percentage change in the Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity Score (J4S) over time. A Growth Mixture Model identified latent disease severity classes with distinct longitudinal trajectories and their baseline predictors. Thirty-eight JSSc patients (66% females), followed for ≥48 months, entered the study. PFS remained high in the fibrotic and limited cutaneous JSSc subtypes (80-100%) over the observation period, whereas the diffuse and sine scleroderma subtypes showed marked deterioration, with PFS decreasing to 54% and 25%, respectively. We identified two latent classes of disease severity: Class 1 showed low severity and good treatment response, Class 2 showed an active, progressive course with poor long-term outcomes. Baseline predictors of poor outcome were J4S >7.5, treatment initiation >9 months from disease onset, and >1.5 organs involved. Latent trajectory classes showed good concordance with JSSc clinical subtypes (κ = 0.660). We identified two latent classes of disease severity in JSSc with clear prognostic significance. High baseline J4S, delayed treatment and greater organ involvement predicted a more severe disease course, paving the way for precision health strategies and optimized patient management.

Título: P-WIN deployment: real-time personalized machine learning to predict critical deterioration in a pediatric intensive care unit.
Resumen: Early recognition of critical deterioration events (CDEs) in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) is crucial to improving outcomes, but the real-time performance of machine-learning (ML)-based alert systems is rarely assessed. We prospectively evaluated the performance, operational utility, and deployment feasibility of the PICU Warning Index (P-WIN), a personalized ML alert system predicting CDE in the PICU. In this prospective cohort study at a quaternary-care children's hospital, P-WIN estimated deterioration risk for PICU patients aged 0-24 years at 30-minute intervals between January 7 and April 7, 2026 using electronic health record data collected via Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources and proprietary EPIC API endpoints. CDEs included cardiopulmonary resuscitation, initiation of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, dilute (10 μg/mL) epinephrine bolus, or unplanned endotracheal intubation. P-WIN was compared to baseline workflows: an automated PICU Warning Tool and a clinician-huddle-based assessment. Primary measures were CDE-level sensitivity, admission-level positive predictive value (PPV), and alerts per patient-day. Among 1005 PICU patients, 99 CDEs were experienced by 62 patients. P-WIN detected 73% of these CDE 1-24 hours in advance, outperforming the PICU Warning Tool (39%, <i>P</i> < .05) and huddle workflow (23%, <i>P</i> < .05). P-WIN generated 0.21 (95% CI, 0.18-0.23) alerts per patient-day. The PICU Warning Tool and huddle workflow had similar PPV to P-WIN. P-WIN detected significantly more CDEs than existing PICU Warning tool and huddle workflows while maintaining a similar PPV. Our findings underscore the feasibility of ML-based personalized warning systems to enhance shared situational awareness of PICU deterioration.

Título: Predictive value of digital breast tomosynthesis based intratumoral-peritumoral radiomics and clinical features for benign-malignant breast microcalcifications.
Resumen: To investigate the value of clinical and radiomics features in distinguishing benign from malignant breast microcalcifications and develop a noninvasive model to reduce unnecessary biopsies. This retrospective study analyzed 181 microcalcification lesions from 172 patients. Lesions were divided into training/validation sets (7:3). Manual volumes of interest were delineated on digital breast tomosynthesis images. Radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral and peritumoral regions. Among 9 machine learning classifiers, the optimal performer was selected to develop 3 radiomics models: intratumoral model (RM0), intratumoral and peritumoral 1 mm model (RM1), intratumoral and peritumoral 3 mm model (RM3). Independent clinical risk factors identified by univariate and multivariate logistic regression were integrated with the optimal radiomics model to build a nomogram model (NM). Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. RM0 performed best. Independent risk factors included: Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) category (<i>P</i> < .001), history of diabetes (<i>P</i> = .023), and personal history of breast cancer (<i>P</i> = .034). In the training cohort, the areas under the ROC curve (AUC) were 0.884 (clinical model), 0.728 (RM0), and 0.942 (NM). In the validation cohort, AUCs were 0.881, 0.695, and 0.790, respectively. Single clinical features showed potential predictive value for microcalcifications, while the integrated model might not demonstrate adequate discriminative power. This study highlights the need for noninvasive differentiation of microcalcifications and suggests that while individual clinical factors have value, combined modeling requires further optimization.

Título: Applications of artificial intelligence in traditional Chinese medicine tongue diagnosis: a bibliometric review of research trends and hotspots, 2015-2026.
Resumen: This study aimed to characterize the development landscape of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tongue diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) by comparing publication trends, collaboration patterns, research hotspots, and emerging topics between CNKI-indexed and WoSCC-indexed literature. Publication trends were summarized descriptively, and CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used for collaboration-network, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, timeline, burst-detection, and journal citation analyses. CNKI-indexed and WoSCC-indexed records were analysed separately because of differences in database coverage, indexing characteristics, metadata structures, and publication practices. A total of 482 studies were included, comprising 295 WoSCC-indexed and 187 CNKI-indexed records. Publication output showed an overall upward trend in both datasets over the study period. The CNKI keyword clustering network showed high clustering quality (modularity Q = 0.7929; weighted mean silhouette S = 0.9413), as did the WoSCC network (Q = 0.8000; S = 0.9239). In CNKI, the strongest keyword bursts included "deep learning" (strength = 2.95), "image segmentation" (2.69), and "transfer learning" (2.61); in WoSCC, prominent bursts included "artificial intelligence" (2.13), "image colour analysis" (2.10), and "machine learning" (1.86). CNKI-indexed literature showed prominent themes involving tongue-image objectification, segmentation, and TCM-oriented diagnostic concepts, whereas WoSCC-indexed literature showed more differentiated themes involving AI architectures, tongue-feature analysis, computational modelling, and disease-related applications. Highly cited publications in both datasets further reflected the importance of tongue-image extraction and segmentation and the subsequent expansion toward disease-oriented modelling. Across both datasets, the temporal patterns suggested a shift in research attention from conventional image processing and feature extraction toward machine learning, deep learning, and more integrated AI-based approaches. The two datasets showed complementary but database-specific thematic structures in AI-assisted tongue diagnosis. Although the literature indicates a shift toward more advanced and disease-oriented AI applications, these bibliometric patterns do not establish the scientific or medical validity, diagnostic accuracy, or clinical readiness of AI-assisted tongue analysis. Further standardization, multicentre external validation, and clinically interpretable and reproducible research are needed before broader clinical application.

Título: Development and internal validation of machine learning models for identifying suicidal behavior in inpatients with mood disorders.

In the observed test set, AUC was 0.704 (0.597-0.803), AUPRC was 0.283 (0.198-0.453), and Brier score was 0.111. At the training-derived threshold of 0.111, sensitivity was 0.552 and specificity was 0.659. The leading SHAP contributions were onset-polarity category, previous SA, age, and previous SB, but all attributions were associational. Model performance was acceptable. These internally validated findings are exploratory and require prospective assessment, standardized outcome measurement, and external validation before clinical use.

Título: Egg fertility assessment system using deep learning technology.
Resumen: In the poultry industry, accurate distinction between fertilized, unfertilized, and hatching failure eggs is a key factor for improving hatching efficiency and reducing resource waste. This study comprehensively evaluated 12 CNN architectures for non-destructive egg fertility classification based on candling-style images captured on days 5-6 of incubation, under four experimental scenarios: Case A (image-level random split, three classes), Case B (egg-level separation, three classes), Case C (image-level random split, two classes), and Case D (egg-level separation, two classes). In Cases A and B, overall accuracy ranged from 93.65%-98.65% and 90.82%-95.79%, respectively. Per-class recall for fertilized eggs exceeded 98% across all models, while hatching failure egg recall was highly variable (5.88%-76.47% in Case A; 0%-27.78% in Case B), reflecting severe class imbalance and visual ambiguity. In Cases C and D (fertilized vs. unfertilized only), overall accuracy improved to 97.02%-99.80% and 95.84%-98.81%, respectively, with unfertilized egg recall ranging from 74.47%-97.87% (Case C) and 58.33%-87.50% (Case D). Egg-level evaluation (Cases B and D) consistently yielded lower accuracy than image-level splitting (Cases A and C), confirming that image-level splitting overestimates real-world generalization performance. CNN selection should be guided by the balance between computational resources and required accuracy: lightweight models (SqueezeNet: 4.7 MB; ShuffleNet: 5.5 MB) suit resource-constrained deployments, while larger models (Inception-v3, VGG-16, VGG-19) offer superior accuracy for high-performance applications. Classification of hatching failure eggs remains challenging due to their visual similarity to both fertilized and unfertilized eggs depending on the timing of developmental arrest, and represents an important direction for future research.

Título: CAMELLIA: an alignment-free pipeline integrating <i>k</i>-mer feature selection and supervised classification for genomic sequence subtyping.
Resumen: Scalable analysis of biological sequences is essential for functional characterization, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic and vaccine development. Alignment-based pipelines often fail to capture intraspecific variation and become computationally limited on large datasets, while alignment-free methods treat each class as homogeneous, ignoring sample heterogeneity. We present CAMELLIA (Combining AlignMent-free fEature seLection cLassIficAtion), an alignment-free framework that combines feature selection with explainable machine learning for genomic sequence analysis and classification. CAMELLIA identifies subgroups within classes and ensures underrepresented subgroups are captured by the selected features, yielding a more accurate and scalable data-driven representation. Sequences are represented as graphs, from which structural patterns are extracted as features for supervised classifiers, enabling accurate class discrimination. In an HIV-1 case study, CAMELLIA accurately classified sequences into eight subtypes, reduced processing time versus MEGA (MUSCLE) and FAMSA, matched CASTOR-KRFE under identical splits, and outperformed COMET and REGA in accuracy. Beyond predictive performance, CAMELLIA recovered structural patterns beyond class labels, improving feature selection and interpretability. We further examined feature-count sensitivity, showing how selected feature numbers relate to underfitting or noise-driven overfitting. By balancing scalability, accuracy, and interpretability, CAMELLIA offers a new lens for genomic sequence classification and sets a new standard for data-driven, heterogeneity-aware analysis.

Título: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
Resumen: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classification benchmarks-antimicrobial resistance (AMR) drug-class prediction from AMR gene sequences and multi-class oncovirus family classification from simulated 150 bp tumor-like reads-we systematically evaluate 25 weak/strong augmentation pairs constructed from biologically motivated operators, including reverse-complement, codon-level back-translation, mild masking/substitution (NN), high-rate substitution, and length-preserving insertion-deletion (indel). We find consistent trends: (i) moderate, sequence-preserving perturbations yield the best accuracy-stability trade-off, (ii) excessive masking or aggressive mutation increases variance and degrades performance, and (iii) short-segment masking (NN) for weak augmentation followed by an indel rate (around 5%) for strong augmentation emerge as a robust strategy to learn from unlabeled genomic data. We release implementations and recommended defaults to facilitate reproducible SSL for genomic sequence modeling under limited-label regimes.

This retrospective single-center exploratory study examined whether functional biomechanical indicators were associated with MRI-based morphological classification of LDH. A total of 58 patients were included, comprising 15 patients with disc bulging and 43 with disc protrusion or extrusion. Five predictors-lumbar extension, straight-leg-raising asymmetry, side-flexion asymmetry, gluteus medius asymmetry, and right Jiaji regional surface electromyography root mean square-were used to construct an interpretable L2-regularized logistic regression model. Model performance was evaluated using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, with participant-level out-of-fold probabilities averaged across repetitions. Predictors were selected before cross-validation; therefore, the reported performance may include selection-induced optimism. The model achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.705 (95% confidence interval: 0.537-0.851), a precision-recall area under the curve of 0.844, and a Brier score of 0.218. At the exploratory Youden threshold of 0.566, balanced accuracy was 0.714, sensitivity was 0.628, specificity was 0.800, positive predictive value was 0.900, and negative predictive value was 0.429. A prespecified threshold of 0.500 yielded a balanced accuracy of 0.692, sensitivity of 0.651, and specificity of 0.733. Calibration was suboptimal, with an intercept of 0.999 and a slope of 0.752. In a separate exploratory bootstrap analysis, coefficient sign stability ranged from 97.0% to 99.9%, although the intervals remained wide. These findings suggest preliminary associations between selected functional biomechanical indicators and MRI-based disc morphology. Given the small and imbalanced sample, predictor-selection optimism, limited negative predictive performance, suboptimal calibration, and absence of external validation, the model should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as a standalone clinical decision-support tool.

Título: Development of a master of science in digital health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Tanzania: a mixed-methods curriculum development study.

The approach provides a potentially adaptable model for curriculum development in LMIC settings. Future evaluation should assess program implementation, graduate competencies, employment outcomes, employer satisfaction, and contribution to national digital health transformation.

Título: IL18BP links antigen processing and presentation programs to a dendritic cell-enriched immunoregulatory state in colorectal cancer.
Resumen: Antigen processing and presentation (APP) is required for tumor immune recognition, but its relationship with the immune landscape in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains incompletely defined. In this study, APP-related transcriptional programs were used as the starting point to identify immune-cell-associated biomarkers with prognostic and immunotherapeutic relevance in CRC. Six public CRC bulk cohorts were analyzed to define APP-related molecular states. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and four machine-learning frameworks, including Boruta, LassoLR, Pamr, and XGBoost, were applied to prioritize genes linked to APP activity. Single-cell analysis was performed with an atlas of 121 samples and 169,427 cells to identify the cellular origin of the candidate gene. Immune infiltration, cancer-immunity-cycle activity, immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response, predicted drug response, somatic mutation patterns, and <i>in vitro</i> function were then evaluated. Two APP-associated patterns were identified and showed different survival outcomes and immune landscapes. Network- and machine-learning-based screening prioritized IL18BP as the main APP-associated candidate. Single-cell profiling showed that IL18BP was preferentially enriched in dendritic cells (DCs), linking the APP-derived bulk signature to a DC-centered immunoregulatory compartment. Across nine external ICB-treated cohorts, IL18BP showed response-classification performance. Drug-response prediction and somatic mutation analyses identified additional features associated with IL18BP-defined groups. In CRC cell lines, IL18BP knockdown increased proliferation, migration, and invasion. These findings identify IL18BP as a DC-enriched, APP-associated biomarker in CRC. By connecting APP programs in bulk tumors with DC-level expression patterns at single-cell resolution, this study positions IL18BP as an APP-associated marker of a DC-enriched immune state. These findings support further evaluation of IL18BP for prognostic and immunotherapy stratification in colorectal cancer but do not establish a causal APP-DC-IL18BP pathway.

Conversely, low-risk patients achieved virological suppression, HBeAg seroconversion, and biochemical response earlier than those classified as high risk. An interpretable three-variable prediction model based on CatBoost-guided feature selection accurately identified significant fibrosis in children with CHB while maintaining performance comparable to the machine-learning model. Baseline risk stratification was also associated with subsequent treatment outcomes, although external validation is needed before clinical implementation.

Título: Heterogeneity-aware risk-adaptive trajectory planning for UAVs in air-ground multi-agent interaction.
Resumen: Autonomous UAVs sharing low-altitude airspace with ground traffic must continuously interpret the heterogeneous and dynamically varying behaviors of ground agents, a challenge that conventional risk models, largely designed for static obstacles or aircraft-to-aircraft conflicts, are not equipped to address. This study formulates the air-ground interaction problem as a heterogeneous multi-agent risk perception task and proposes a three-stage computational intelligence framework for risk-adaptive UAV trajectory planning. First, a GMM-LightGBM model performs online identification of ground agent driving styles, which is coupled with a Full Velocity Difference (FVD) model to generate personalized agent trajectory predictions. Case studies across representative risk scenarios further demonstrate the framework's adaptive decision-making capability. By combining machine learning-based behavior identification, fuzzy reasoning, and learning-based trajectory generation, this work contributes a computational intelligence methodology for autonomous UAV decision-making in heterogeneous multi-agent environments.

Título: Representation, Transferability, and Trustworthy Uncertainty in Machine-Learning Prediction of the HOMO-LUMO Gap of Transition-Metal Complexes.
Resumen: The frontier-orbital (HOMO-LUMO) gap is a compact descriptor of the electronic structure of transition-metal complexes (TMCs) and a recurrent screening target for catalysis, photophysics, and functional material design; however, its evaluation by density functional theory (DFT) is costly at the library scale. Working entirely from the public tmQM database, with no additional DFT calculations and no experiments, we examine three questions that are seldom treated together: how much structural detail a model requires, whether it generalizes across the periodic table, and how far its uncertainty estimates can be trusted. For 108,541 mononuclear TMCs, we construct a hierarchy of representations of increasing cost: composition-and-coordination descriptors; the same descriptors augmented with inexpensive cheminformatics (RDKit) features; and a SchNet graph neural network that operates directly on the three-dimensional geometry. The predictive accuracy increases monotonically across the hierarchy (test R<sup>2</sup> ≈ 0.57 → 0.63 → 0.77; mean absolute error 0.44 → 0.30 eV), and Shapley value analysis attributes the predictions to chemically reasonable factors. We then show that this in-domain accuracy is a poor proxy for reliability. Leave-one-series-out and leave-one-metal-out evaluations reveal a sharp loss of accuracy on unseen chemistry (median leave-one-metal-out R<sup>2</sup> ≈ 0.34; worst case d<sup>10</sup> zinc, R<sup>2</sup> < 0), and, contrary to a natural expectation, neither of two geometry networks (SchNet, DimeNet++) extrapolates better than the simpler tabular model across metal series-both are often worse-although the directional architecture alone extrapolates with positive skill to a single withheld metal. Finally, although standard split-conformal intervals are well calibrated in the domain (≈90% coverage), they undercover (81%) for an unseen series; we demonstrate that series-conditional (Mondrian) calibration restores per-series coverage and that a distance-based applicability-domain filter flags essentially all out-of-domain complexes, recovering calibrated coverage on the retained subset. The study offers a transparent, reproducible recipe for deciding when and how confidently such models may be applied.

Resumen: Carotid vulnerable plaques (CVPs) represent a major cause of ischemic stroke, yet current diagnostic methods lack sufficient precision for early detection. Spectral computed tomography (CT) enables detailed plaque characterization, but its clinical utility depends on advanced analytical techniques. A Fourier Transform-enhanced U-Net model was developed using spectral CT data from 214 patients at Qiqihar Medical College. Transfer learning was applied for carotid segmentation, supported by extensive data augmentation and ten-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). A patient-level independent test set was reserved to evaluate model performance. The FTC-enhanced U-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.89 and an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.80, accurately delineating arterial and plaque boundaries. Ten-fold cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.88 ± 0.03, an accuracy of 85.3% ± 2.1%, and an F1-score of 0.84 ± 0.02, confirming strong robustness and generalizability. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive models derived from spectral CT imaging show substantial potential for early diagnosis and prognostic assessment of CVPs. The FTC-enhanced U-Net provides an efficient and reliable tool for clinical decision support, facilitating broader adoption of AI in vascular imaging and improving diagnostic precision and patient management.

Título: AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality in rural settings: a systematic review.
Resumen: Maternal mortality remains disproportionately high in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural settings with limited access to skilled obstetric care. Artificial intelligence and machine learning models offer promise for early risk prediction, yet their methodological rigour, applicability, and deployment feasibility in resource-constrained rural contexts remain inadequately synthesised. This systematic review evaluated AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality, with an emphasis on their suitability for rural and low-resource settings. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online for studies published from January 2015 to August 2025. Studies employing AI or machine learning to predict maternal mortality or severe maternal outcomes were included. The Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) assessed methodological quality across four domains: participants, predictors, outcomes, and analysis. Data extraction captured study characteristics, model architectures, performance metrics, validation strategies, and rural implementation considerations. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251174343) and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Twenty-eight studies met inclusion criteria, predominantly from sub-Saharan Africa (n = 12) and South Asia (n = 8). Dataset sizes ranged from 402 to over 31 million records from national surveys (n = 14), hospital registries (n = 9), and Internet of Things monitoring systems (n = 5). Random Forest (n = 14), ensemble methods (n = 11), and neural networks (n = 11) were most frequently employed. Reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values ranged from 0.70 to 0.95 (median 0.84), with sensitivity 70-92% and specificity 65-85%. PROBAST assessment revealed low risk of bias for participants (24/28), predictors (25/28), and outcomes (24/28), but substantial concerns in the analysis domain (14/28 low risk, 8/28 high risk). Key limitations included reliance on synthetic oversampling without external validation, inadequate reporting of calibration, and small sample sizes in IoT studies. Only 11 studies (39%) conducted external validation. Common predictors were maternal age, blood pressure, gestational age, parity, and antenatal care attendance. Rural implementation barriers included limited connectivity, data sparsity, workforce training needs, and the absence of explainability frameworks. AI-powered models demonstrate strong discrimination performance for maternal mortality prediction when trained on large, representative datasets. However, methodological weaknesses, particularly inadequate external validation and calibration assessment, limit confidence in generalizability. The underrepresentation of rural populations and the scarcity of implementation studies constrain real-world applicability. Future development should prioritise federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-site collaboration, lightweight architectures for offline deployment, explainable AI frameworks, and integration with community health worker workflows to achieve equitable, scalable solutions to reduce preventable maternal deaths in rural low- and middle-income country settings. PROSPERO CRD42025174343.

Título: Lactylation in cancer: a new frontier in metabolic-epigenetic regulation and clinical practice.
Resumen: The discovery of lysine lactylation (Kla) redefines lactate from a passive glycolytic by-product into a bioactive metabolic mediator that directly links cellular metabolism to epigenetic regulation. This emerging post-translational modification dynamically alters histone and non-histone proteins, thereby reconfiguring gene expression programs and immune responses within the tumor microenvironment (TME). It consequently promotes core malignant phenotypes including uncontrolled proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), metastatic dissemination, and resistance to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immune checkpoint blockade. Specific epigenetic signatures, notably histone H3K18la and H4K12la marks, serve as transcriptional anchors for oncogenic pathways across multiple cancer types. Multi-omics analyses have further yielded Kla-associated gene profiles with the potential to refine prognostic stratification and drug-target identification. These findings establish Kla as a central axis in tumor-associated metabolic-epigenetic crosstalk. Effective clinical application of KLAsKla biomarkers requires resolving technical detection limits and addressing the spatiotemporal heterogeneity that currently constrains machine learning-based prognostic models. Overcoming these bottlenecks is contingent upon leveraging advanced technologies such as single-cell multi-omics and spatial transcriptomics. This review characterizes the emerging roles of Kla in tumor metabolism, providing a framework for its future application as a diagnostic and therapeutic cornerstone in precision oncology.
