Título: Evolution of chronic diseases and multimorbidity clusters among the deceased in rural northeast South Africa (2012-2022): insights from verbal autopsy data.
Resumen: Rural South Africa is undergoing an epidemiological transition characterised by rising mortality from chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) alongside that from persistent infectious diseases. We aimed to investigate trends in the prevalence of chronic disease and multimorbidity clustering among deceased individuals in rural northeast South Africa from 2012 to 2022. Verbal autopsy data for 5,892 deceased individuals collected from the Agincourt Health and socio-Demographic Surveillance System (HDSS) study area in Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga Province, from 2012 to 2022 were analysed. We identified reported chronic diseases prior to death and applied cluster analysis, partitioning around medoids (PAM) and latent class analysis (LCA) to identify patterns of co-occurring diseases (multimorbidity clusters). Temporal trends in disease prevalence were assessed using descriptive statistics. Multinomial logistic regression models were used to examine associations of cluster membership with various behavioral factors. Over the 11-year period, the prevalence of hypertension among the deceased individuals rose from approximately 25% in 2012 to over 50% by 2022, that of diabetes increased from 10% and reached ~ 25% and that of dementia increased from 1% to over 5%. In contrast, the number of deaths that were reported to have had tuberculosis prior to their deaths declined markedly TB reducing from 23% to 11%. HIV prevalence fluctuated within a narrow range around 20% (approximately 18-22%). The proportion of deceased individuals with multimorbidity (≥ 2 chronic conditions) increased, and complex multimorbidity (≥ 3 conditions) nearly doubled between 2012 and 2019 (from 8% to 15%), with relative stability observed in the 2020-2022 period. Over time, multimorbidity clusters shifted from an initial dominance of HIV/TB comorbidity to later patterns dominated by cardiometabolic conditions (hypertension and diabetes), HIV-hypertension, and an emerging neurodegenerative illnesses cluster. Older adults (≥ 65 years) and females experienced the highest multimorbidity burden and were more likely to belong to complex disease clusters. Morbidity patterns in this rural population have shifted toward chronic NCDs and multimorbidity. Characterising these trends and identifying disease clusters is essential for targeting patient-centred care early on. Our findings underscore the importance of integrating care for NCDs and infectious diseases in rural health systems to address the growing multimorbidity burden, with particular focus on older adults and women.

Título: Development and a single-centre temporal validation of a machine learning-based model for early prediction of acute pancreatitis-associated liver injury.
Resumen: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a common acute abdominal inflammatory disorder characterized by premature activation of pancreatic enzymes, leading to pancreatic autodigestion, edema, hemorrhage, and even necrosis. The liver, as the first portal organ receiving pancreatic venous drainage, is one of the most frequently affected extra-pancreatic organs in AP. AP-associated liver injury (LI) is closely correlated with the intensity of systemic inflammation, the development of multiple organ dysfunction, and increased mortality. While machine learning (ML) models have been successfully applied to predict various AP-related complications such as acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, and infected pancreatic necrosis, effective tools for early prediction of LI before its clinical onset remain lacking. We retrospectively collected data from 1,184 patients diagnosed with AP at the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan University of Science and Technology between January 2018 and December 2023. After applying strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, 1,124 patients were included. The development cohort comprised 929 patients admitted between January 2018 and December 2022, randomly split into a training set (n = 650) and an internal test set (n = 279) in a 7:3 ratio. An independent temporal validation set consisted of 195 patients admitted from January to December 2023. Forty-nine clinical and laboratory parameters were collected within 24 h of admission to predict LI occurring after the first 24 h of hospitalization. Patients with any ALT/AST elevation > 3×ULN within the first 24 h were not counted as LI events; the outcome was strictly defined as incident LI emerging after 24 h. In the training set, LASSO regression was used to identify key predictive factors, followed by the construction of nine machine learning models: logistic regression (LR), decision trees (DT), random forests (RF), XGBoost, and LightGBM, among others. All feature selection and hyperparameter tuning were nested within 5-fold cross-validation on the training set only, with no use of test or validation set information. Model performance was primarily assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration metrics (Brier score, calibration intercept/slope), and decision-curve analysis (DCA). The SHAP method was employed for interpretability analysis of the optimal model. LASSO regression identified ten key predictors: amylase (AMY), lipase (LIP), total cholesterol (CHO), albumin (ALB), neutrophil percentage (N/W), serum calcium (Ca), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), gender, total bilirubin (TBIL), and drinking history. Among the nine models, the random forest (RF) model demonstrated superior predictive performance and temporal generalizability, achieving an AUC of 0.972 (95% CI: 0.954-0.989) with an accuracy of 0.921 in the internal test set, and an AUC of 0.935 (95% CI: 0.902-0.969) with an accuracy of 0.862 in the temporal validation set. The RF model showed a training-test AUC gap of 0.028 (1.000 vs. 0.972), indicating modest overfitting. Decision-curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across a range of thresholds. SHAP analysis revealed that pancreatic enzymes (AMY, LIP) and markers reflecting hepatic synthetic function (ALB, CHO) were the primary predictors influencing the model's output. Calibration was acceptable, with Brier scores of 0.070 and 0.101 in the test and validation sets, respectively; calibration slopes were 2.153 (test) and 1.367 (validation), indicating over-dispersion of predicted probabilities (over-confidence) that would benefit from post-hoc recalibration before clinical use. An RF model built using routine clinical data collected within 24 h of admission can effectively predict the risk of liver injury in AP patients and demonstrates promising temporal generalizability. The model offers a potentially useful tool for early identification of high-risk patients; however, prospective external validation and probability recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

Título: A deep learning framework for threshold-free relative gene expression ranking from histone modification signals.
Resumen: Current methods for predicting gene expression from histone modifications rely on arbitrary binary classification thresholds such as the median to distinguish between high and low expression for genes. This approach lacks biological justification, creates dataset-dependent classifications, and ignores the relative regulatory relationships between genes that are often more biologically meaningful than absolute cutoffs. We developed a deep learning method using pairwise ranking to determine the relative gene expression levels between gene pairs based on their histone modification signals. The approach adopted the DirectRanker architecture, which enforces antisymmetry by construction through a twin-subnet design with asymmetric subtraction, and was evaluated against three baseline classifiers (Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and SVM Linear) on identical features and data splits. Ablation testing across all 31 non-empty subsets of five histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K27me3) was conducted to identify their individual contributions. Datasets were strictly partitioned (80% training, 10% validation, 10% testing) with gene-level separation to prevent data leakage, and all experiments were repeated across five independent random seeds. Four datasets were analysed: two normal adult liver cell datasets (Donor 3 and Donor 4 from NCBI GEO GSE19465) and two HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cell line datasets (ENCSR134DWG and GSE76344). Multi-mark combinations anchored by active histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K9ac) consistently drove predictive performance, with the best combinations achieving AUROC values of 0.833-0.867 and test accuracies of 74-78% across datasets. DirectRanker attained AUPRC values of 0.819-0.856, closely matching or exceeding Random Forest on precision-recall performance. Repressive marks (H3K9me3, H3K27me3) consistently underperformed when used in isolation, with single-mark models achieving test accuracies of only 50-66%. DirectRanker produced substantially higher antisymmetry scores (0.961-0.983) than all baseline classifiers (0.787-0.851), confirming logically consistent pairwise predictions. Performance plateaued at four- to five-mark combinations, reflecting correlated predictive signal among the active marks within the promoter-proximal feature space. The pairwise ranking framework provides a principled alternative to threshold-based classification, enabling relative gene expression comparisons without arbitrary binarisation cutoffs. While Random Forest achieved marginally higher accuracy, DirectRanker's structural antisymmetry guarantee makes it the more suitable choice for applications requiring a globally coherent gene ranking. Active promoter marks carry the majority of the predictive signal, while the performance saturation with increasing mark combinations reflects overlapping information content rather than biological redundancy.

Título: Human-in-the-loop LLM-assisted thematic analysis: A validated, reproducible tutorial for large-scale qualitative research.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet clear methodological frameworks for integrating them into thematic analysis remain limited. A central challenge is how to scale qualitative coding with LLM assistance while preserving methodological rigor and reproducibility. This tutorial presents a structured, human-in-the-loop workflow for conducting large-scale thematic analysis with LLM support. Grounded in inductive and hybrid approaches to thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006), the workflow proceeds in three phases. First, researchers conduct manual thematic analysis on a subset of data to establish an initial codebook and assess relevance. Second, the same subset is analyzed using an LLM to iteratively refine prompts and evaluate alignment between human and model outputs. Third, the validated approach is applied to the full corpus using a modular four-step pipeline: key-idea extraction, chunk-level thematic coding, theme consolidation, and clustering, with iterative human verification through random sampling of outputs. We demonstrate the workflow using 2,952 publicly available Reddit posts. Structured prompt design and JSON-formatted outputs enable traceability between themes and source data and support reproducible analysis. Prompt engineering is treated as an iterative analytic process rather than a one-time instruction. Under controlled conditions, human and LLM coding showed high agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.91). All prompts, code, and reproducibility materials are openly available via an Open Science Framework repository. By providing detailed implementation guidance, embedded validation procedures, and safeguards against common failure modes such as hallucination and overgeneralization, this tutorial offers a practical and extensible framework for integrating LLMs into qualitative research across domains.

Título: Comparison of raw-signal, feature-based and hybrid representations for machine-learning classification of retinal diseases from pattern electroretinography.
Resumen: Pattern electroretinography (PERG) is a non-invasive test of macular and retinal ganglion cell function, but its low amplitude and inter-subject variability limit its diagnostic use. Engineered descriptors did not improve on the waveform, but they made the problem tractable for linear models, which gained 0.128 in mean AUC from the reduction in dimensionality. These internally validated findings indicate that absolute PERG amplitude should be preserved rather than normalised away; participant-independent, multi-centre validation is required before clinical application.

All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores). Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.

The findings support further prospective evaluation with standardized sampling and direct comparison with established clinical models before clinical translation.

Título: A single-loop bilevel deep learning method for optimal control of obstacle problems.
Resumen: Optimal control of obstacle problems arises in a wide range of applications and is computationally challenging due to the nonsmoothness, nonlinearity, and bilevel structure of the underlying problems. Classical numerical methods typically rely on mesh-based discretizations and require solving a sequence of computationally expensive subproblems, while deep learning approaches for this class of problems remain largely unexplored. In this work, we propose a bilevel deep learning framework whose core training algorithm is the computationally efficient Single-Loop Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Algorithm (S2-FOBA), which avoids nested optimization, uses only first-order information, and does not rely on restrictive lower-level uniqueness assumptions. The proposed method is mesh-free, scalable to high-dimensional settings and complex domains, and avoids the repeated solution of discretized subproblems. It employs constraint-embedding neural networks to approximate both the state and the control, thereby enforcing admissibility by construction while preserving the intrinsic bilevel structure of the problem. We further analyze the convergence behavior of S2-FOBA under mild conditions. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems, including two-dimensional examples with regular and irregular obstacles, a five-dimensional example, and a problem posed on a complex domain, demonstrate the effectiveness, efficiency, and robust constraint enforcement of the proposed approach.

The findings demonstrate successful cross-domain transfer to real-world US Department of Veterans Affairs clinical notes.

Título: RANGE-X: a gradient-free framework for the discovery of conical intersections and photochemical reaction pathways.
Resumen: Conical intersections (CIs), where two potential energy surfaces, such as those for the ground and first excited states, coincide, are quintessential in photochemistry. Nevertheless, it is usually difficult to find them without substantial chemical intuition and computational cost. As a solution to this problem, we present RANGE-X, a fully automated, gradient-free framework for locating CIs and their energy landscape, including ground- and excited-state minima, transition states, and reaction paths. The workflow is based on the hybrid artificial-bee-colony/genetic-algorithm global optimizer, RANGE (robust adaptive nature-inspired, global explorer), which performs gradient-free sampling with a choice of three cost functions targeting CIs, ground-state minima, and excited-state minima. An optional gradient-based conical-search refinement can be performed to achieve sub-meV accuracy in the CI energy gap. Candidate transition states are validated by a path-interpolation pipeline that distinguishes discrete-well topologies from broad-shoulder topologies that geometry-space clustering alone cannot resolve. The framework is method-agnostic for ground and excited states, as well as for reaction path validation approaches, and can be coupled with any <i>ab initio</i> software on classical or quantum hardware. In the present work, the GAMESS spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (SF-TDDFT) is used to study the ground and excited states. The reaction path validator is the nudged elastic band (NEB). Both choices are illustrative and can be replaced with other appropriate approaches. The framework is illustrated on eight systems spanning organic, d-block, heterometallic, multi-fragment metal-organic, and f-element chemistry.

Título: Microscopic origin of polytype-dependent melting in SiC revealed by machine-learning molecular dynamics.
Resumen: Predicting how crystal structure influences high-temperature stability remains a key challenge in materials modeling and design. Silicon carbide (SiC), one of the most thermally and chemically stable materials known, provides an ideal system for studying this problem because its many polytypes preserve similar local tetrahedral bonding while differing in long-range stacking geometry. To determine the impact of polytype structure on the high-temperature stability of SiC, we combine phase-coexistence machine-learning molecular dynamics with finite-temperature phonon analysis, enabled by a fine-tuned MACE interatomic potential that accurately describes crystalline, high-temperature, and disordered configurations across multiple SiC polytypes. We identify a clear stability ordering, 3C > 2H > 9R, reflected consistently in structural disordering, interlayer sliding, and finite-temperature phonon spectra. Across all polytypes, melting initiates through the formation of short C-C contacts and carbon-rich local regions, followed by a progressive loss of tetrahedral Si-C connectivity. The reduced stability of the long-period 9R polytype is associated with a denser manifold of low-frequency transverse-acoustic modes arising from its stacking periodicity and associated zone folding, which broaden and soften further at high temperature. These modes can provide additional low-energy channels for thermally activated lateral bilayer motion, consistent with the larger sliding amplitudes observed in 9R and their positive correlation with local structural disorder.

Título: Bond-Level Prediction of U-Donor Bond Lengths in Uranyl Coordination Complexes Using Machine Learning for Ligand Recognition.
Resumen: U-donor bond lengths in uranyl coordination complexes directly reflect metal-ligand interaction strength and provide important structural parameters for evaluating ligand recognition, selective complexation, and extraction/adsorption system design. To enable bond-level prediction, this study developed a DFT-derived machine learning framework for predicting U-donor bond lengths. A data set containing 15,177 coordination structures and 26,798 U-donor bond length data points was constructed from 3,330 unique ligands under a unified computational protocol. Five categories of models, including linear models, support-vector-based models, ensemble tree models, descriptor-based neural networks, and graph neural networks, were evaluated to compare representation strategies. Among descriptor-based models, XGBoost achieved the best performance, with R2, RMSE, and MAE values of 0.793, 0.057 Å, and 0.039 Å, respectively. Among graph neural networks, DimeNet++ performed best, with R2, RMSE, and MAE values of 0.821, 0.051 Å, and 0.036 Å. Functional-group-based evaluation and SHAP analysis indicated that donor atom type, neighboring atomic environment, local electronegativity difference, and local geometric features are key factors controlling U-donor bond length variations. External validation using unseen functional groups and uranyl structures demonstrated model generalization beyond the training space. This work provides a bond-level data set and a data-driven strategy for rapid U-donor bond length prediction and ligand screening in actinide coordination systems.

Título: Evaluating COPD care assistance: a comparative study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE bot performance.
Resumen: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to provide health information, yet their reliability in addressing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in the Chinese context remains unclear. We developed 40 COPD care questions spanning 7 prespecified domains relevant to patient education and self-management. All questions were submitted in Chinese in independent new chat sessions to minimise context carryover. Most responses were rated as 'good' for accuracy across chatbots. However, comprehensiveness scores for 'good' responses were low across all systems (mean ~ 1.4-2.0/5), and PEMAT actionability was limited, indicating that few responses included concrete, patient-executable steps. Our findings suggest that LLM chatbots may support basic COPD patient education in Chinese settings, but current responses often lack sufficient comprehensiveness and actionable guidance. Título: From innovation to implementation: a global scoping review of artificial intelligence applications, governance, and challenges in humanitarian contexts.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool for supporting humanitarian action through hazards and crisis prediction, real time monitoring of evolving crisis conditions and humanitarian needs, resource allocation, and decision-making. However, evidence on how AI is implemented, evaluated, and governed across humanitarian contexts remains fragmented. In this scoping review, we mapped the global evidence on the application of AI in humanitarian settings, including its distribution across the emergency management cycle, deployment maturity, and evaluation. We also identified any governance considerations, as well as enabling factors for and challenges to its implementation, with particular attention to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Gulf Cooperation Council countries (GCC), and Qatar. The methodology of this scoping review followed the framework set by Arksey and O'Malley, which comprises the formulation of the research question, selection of records, data charting, and synthesis of findings. We searched six databases (ProQuest, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus), queried Google Scholar, and ran targeted grey literature searches through the webpages of major humanitarian organisations for records reporting on the application, implementation, or governance of AI in humanitarian contexts. We descriptively and narratively synthesised the extracted data. We included 57 scholarly publications and 17 grey literature reports. Application of AI was most frequently reported in sudden-onset natural disasters, particularly floods and earthquakes, and was commonly used to support disaster monitoring, crisis informatics, search-and-rescue, logistics optimisation, hazard prediction, and geospatial analysis. Deep learning and machine learning were the most common model families. Across the emergency management cycle, most applications of AI focused on preparedness and response, while recovery was rarely addressed. Geographically, most evidence originated from Asia, while research from the MENA and GCC regions remained limited. Most reported systems remained prototypes or retrospectively validated models, with relatively few seeing operational deployment or field implementation. Governance issues were discussed more extensively in grey literature than in scholarly publications. Community participation, equity considerations, and formal governance frameworks were inconsistently reported. AI is increasingly being applied in humanitarian contexts, but it is heterogeneously distributed across regions, humanitarian contexts, and emergency management. Greater emphasis is needed on real-world deployment, implementation-focused evaluation, participatory approaches, and governance frameworks that support responsible, equitable, and context-sensitive AI adoption.

Título: FMCerNet: frequency-aware multi-label learning for fine-grained cervical cytology screening.
Resumen: Automated cytology screening is essential for early cervical cancer prevention, where gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) are typically partitioned into tiles for tile-level feature extraction and subsequent WSI-level diagnosis aggregation. However, existing tile-level methods remain constrained by limited input sizes, which frequently obscures sparse and morphologically subtle abnormal cells. Experiments on both public and private datasets demonstrate that FMCerNet improves the accuracy of positive screening and fine-grained subtype classification while maintaining high inference speed. Code at https://github.com/imAzhou/FMCerNet and archived on Zenodo (doi: 10.5281/zenodo.22886105).

Título: Closed Pores as Internal Stress-Regulation Units for Practical Silicon-Carbon Anodes.
Resumen: Silicon-carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation-induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Machine-learning-guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed-pore design. This work establishes closed-pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low-expansion silicon-carbon anodes.

Resumen: Immune-inflammatory dysregulation and cortical structural vulnerability have been increasingly implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). Título: Spatial Charge Separation in Porphyrin Metal-Organic Frameworks Enables Bifunctional Sites for Overall Water Splitting.
Resumen: Solar-driven overall water splitting provides a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuels, but its realization in porphyrin-based metal-organic frameworks (PMOFs) is limited by the difficulty of coupling reduction and oxidation chemistry within a single framework. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal a spatial separation of the frontier electronic states in two-dimensional M-Cu PMOFs (M = transition metal): the conduction-band edge is predominantly associated with the Cu2(COO)4 paddle-wheel node, whereas the valence-band edge is mainly localized on the porphyrin linker. Sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO) analysis further identifies total magnetic moment, electronegativity, group number, and d-electron count as physically interpretable descriptors of property variations within this M-Cu PMOF series. These results highlight cooperative linker-node electronic regulation as a computational design principle for porphyrin-based frameworks with spatially differentiated redox functions.

Título: Experiences developing structural biology tools with AI coding assistance.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) offer significant potential to accelerate scientific software development, yet their application to structural biology algorithms requires rigorous evaluation. This challenge is examined through the development of xcif, a new native parser for the crystallographic information file (CIF) format, designed to replace a stable but slow parser (ucif) in the Computational Crystallography Toolbox (cctbx). Using an expert-led, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted workflow, implementation time was reduced from an estimated several months to approximately one week of active human effort. However, this efficiency relied entirely on domain knowledge to specify constraints, intercept plausible but flawed machine-generated code and design adversarial tests. The machine assistance did not replace programming expertise but rather shifted the human engineering burden from writing code to independent validation. Applying the new xcif parser across a corpus of approximately 550 000 archive files confirmed that it produces output identical to both the legacy implementation and GEMMI, a modern high-performance parser. xcif parses roughly an order of magnitude faster than the legacy cctbx parser and 1.3-1.5 times faster than GEMMI, while reducing peak memory use for larger files. This case study demonstrates that AI assistance provides a highly practical, cost-effective pathway for the renewal of mature structural biology infrastructure, provided that the development is strictly governed by expert oversight and objective verification.

Título: A Simple Descriptor for Solid-State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries.
Resumen: The discovery of new solid-state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile-ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile-ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion-migration barriers spanning Li-, Na-, K-, and Mg-ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆d, a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile-ion-neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short-range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low- from high-barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆d in a high-throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast-ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast-ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆d links diverse ion-transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals and comparable frameworks outside the United States. We distinguish geographic discrimination, closed-set classification and source attribution, and show that reported accuracies in excess of 90 % derive from closed-set classification against small reference panels rather than from validated source attribution. We outline a minimum dataset that forensic microbial geolocation reports should contain before being offered in court. We conclude that the field has demonstrated promising discriminatory capability under defined conditions, but that forensic source attribution remains insufficiently validated, and that microbial profiling is best used alongside established soil examination rather than in place of it. We set out the infrastructural and empirical priorities that would close the gap between laboratory demonstration and routine evidentiary use.

Título: DiffUS: Differentiable Ultrasound Rendering from Volumetric Imaging.
Resumen: Intraoperative ultrasound imaging provides real-time guidance during numerous surgical procedures, but its interpretation is complicated by noise, artifacts, and poor alignment with high-resolution preoperative MRI/CT scans. To bridge the gap between preoperative planning and intraoperative guidance, we present DiffUS, a physics-based, differentiable ultrasound renderer that synthesizes realistic B-mode images from volumetric imaging. DiffUS first converts MRI 3D scans into acoustic impedance volumes using a machine learning approach. Next, we simulate ultrasound beam propagation using ray tracing with coupled reflection-transmission equations. DiffUS formulates wave propagation as a sparse linear system that captures multiple internal reflections. Evaluation on the ReMIND dataset demonstrates DiffUS's ability to generate anatomically accurate ultrasound images from brain MRI data. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/gduguey/DiffUS.

Our findings highlight the need for further research to establish whether metrics uniformly capable of state-of-the-art performance in causal model evaluation can be found.

The inversion was most pronounced for Klebsiella beta-lactam combinations. Título: Assessing the Potential Cumulative Effects of Longitudinal Interventions for Depression and Deviant Peer Association on Academic Achievement: a Causal Inference Approach.
Resumen: In various studies, depressive symptoms, deviant peer association, and academic achievement appear to be reciprocally and cumulatively related across the transition from childhood to adolescence. This study asks a hypothetical question: how much would grade 12 academic achievement improve if a preventive-intervention reduced depressive symptoms and/or deviant peer association across grades 5, 7, and 10? To answer this question, we used longitudinal datasets from 361 students in the LIFT project and employed the Longitudinal Modified Treatment Policies approach, which uses causal inference and machine learning analyses to estimate the total effect of shifting the trajectory(ies) of an exposure(s) while properly handling time-varying confounding. Implications of the findings for identifying key factors across critical developmental windows are discussed.

Título: From Linear-quadratic to Machine Learning in Radiobiological Modeling for Radiotherapy Planning: Resolving the Complexity-Utility Paradox with Hybrid Physics-informed Neural Networks.
Resumen: Radiobiological modeling for radiotherapy planning has evolved across three overlapping paradigms: postplanning biological evaluation using empirical dose-response relationships (c. 1960), biological optimization integrated into treatment planning system objective functions (c. 2000), and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven adaptive prediction (c. 2012-present). Despite this progression, increasing model complexity has not produced proportional clinical utility - a tension we describe as the complexity-utility paradox. A structured search of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science (January 1960 to March 2026) yielded 71 included studies; evidence is synthesized narratively with critical appraisal of landmark mechanistic models, consensus guidelines and recent meta-analytic data. We operationalize the paradox across three measurable gaps: A performance generalizability gap, in which external validation of machine-learning normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models is approximately 9% lower in relative terms (absolute difference 0.07; pooled internal area under a receiver operating characteristic [AUROC]: 0.76, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.73-0.78, versus pooled external AUROC: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.64-0.73), noting that 121 of the 225 pooled models were rated at high risk of bias on PROBAST and that the internal and external estimates derive from different model sets; an adoption gap, in which Quantitative Analyses of Normal Tissue Effects in the Clinic-derived Lyman-Kutcher-Burman constraints retain primary plan-evaluation authority despite demonstrated AI improvements; and an interpretability gap, in which regulatory and clinical-trust barriers penalize opaque model architectures. We argue that principled integration, rather than paradigm replacement, offers the most tractable resolution. Hybrid physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), anchoring data-driven learning to validated mechanistic priors within a federated multi-institutional training framework and uncertainty propagation compliant with the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement, may narrow all three gaps simultaneously. This position is explicitly caveated: PINNs inherit the bias of the embedded prior, and current radiotherapy-specific evidence remains preliminary. To our knowledge, no externally validated PINN-based NTCP model has yet been published, so the proposal is offered as a research direction rather than as an evidenced clinical solution. A tiered validation framework is proposed for structured clinical translation.

We define the cost of reproducibility as the resources required to reproduce the findings of a study and we propose five dimensions of cost, using objective characteristics such as code and data. We review 918 publications between 2022 and 2024 at top AI venues to evaluate the variation in reproducibility costs, with the hypothesis that publications at venues with stricter standards are less costly. Papers published at machine learning conferences are less costly to reproduce than publication from other venues, 12.91% less costly compared with journals, and 16.52% less costly compared with general AI conferences. Award-winning papers, however, are not less costly to reproduce than regular papers, and 6.72% of implementation repository links were broken. These findings suggest that reproducibility costs can be significantly reduced through compliance-based mechanisms-provided they receive community support. We recommend that venues require the inclusion of reproducibility checklists in their publications, permit appendices for comprehensive documentation, and adopt low reproducibility cost as a key criterion for awards.

Título: Neural Adjoint Inverse Design of Three-Dimensional Nanophotonic Devices.
Resumen: Volumetric meta-optics have emerged as a compact high-performance platform for advanced imaging, color routing in image sensors, and on-chip wavefront control. Realizing such devices depends on solving a high-dimensional nonconvex inverse-design problem governed by Maxwell's equations. Adjoint optimization is the standard route to gradients, yet broadband three-dimensional (3D) design typically requires thousands of full-wave forward/adjoint simulations, making industrial-scale optimization prohibitively slow. To address this bottleneck, a neural adjoint method is introduced, in which a solver-supervised Fourier neural operator (FNO) directly predicts dense, per-voxel 3D adjoint gradient fields from a voxelized permittivity volume. To preserve the sharp, resonance-driven sensitivity peaks that single-pass operator networks tend to oversmooth, a stage-wise FNO is proposed, in which successive stages refine residual errors with progressively higher-frequency emphasis. A domain-specific dataset is curated from paired forward/adjoint finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations spanning three volumetric tasks: spectral sorting (color routers), achromatic focusing (metalenses), and waveguide mode conversion. Across all benchmarks, the surrogate-driven optimization attains figures of merit within 86%-99% of rigorous FDTD-based adjoint optimization whilst reducing end-to-end design time from hours to seconds, with speedups exceeding <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn> <msup><mn>0</mn> <mn>4</mn></msup> <mo>×</mo></mrow> </mrow> </math> . These results establish a pathway toward fast large-scale volumetric meta-optical design enabled by neural-operator surrogates.

Título: Single-step Raman spectroscopy for maple syrup quality control.
Resumen: Maple syrup quality evaluation involves multiple parameters, including color classification, flavor assessment, and the measurement of sugar concentration, which are influenced by the complex chemical composition of the syrup matrix. As such, rapid techniques are needed to assess multiple quality control parameters from a single measurement. After spectral preprocessing, principal component analysis (PCA) was performed to investigate natural spectral variations among samples. PCA revealed differences associated with syrup color and flavor categories; however, the overlap observed among several groups indicated that the relationship between Raman fingerprints and maple syrup properties involves complex spectral variations that are not fully resolved by linear unsupervised analysis. For color classification, the CNN achieved prediction accuracies of 91%, 68%, 73%, and 92% for golden, amber, dark, and very dark syrups, respectively. VR13 showed a high classification rate in the evaluated data; however, the small number of independent VR13 samples prevents a robust estimate of general performance for this class. In addition to Raman fingerprints, fluorescence background variations were evaluated as an indicator of optical properties and were found to correlate with maple syrup light transmittance values used for color grading. The quantitative capability of Raman spectroscopy was further assessed by predicting sucrose concentrations using standard sucrose solutions (45-67%, w/w). Concentration-dependent Raman features were extracted and used to develop a random forest regression (RFR) model, achieving coefficients of determination (<i>R</i> <sup>2</sup>) of 0.87. Application of the model to real maple syrup samples yielded sucrose predictions with an average bias of 0.35%, indicating that Raman-derived spectral information can be used to evaluate both compositional and quality-related characteristics of maple syrup. Overall, the results reported demonstrate the power of Raman spectroscopy for a multiparametric analysis of maple syrup.

The SB@MFO composite retained 75.8% of its initial adsorption capacity after five adsorption-desorption cycles, demonstrating acceptable reusability. Owing to its adsorption performance, magnetic recoverability, and agricultural waste origin, SB@MFO shows promising potential for ammonium removal from aqueous systems. Further studies using real wastewater matrices and continuous-flow conditions are recommended to evaluate its practical applicability.

Título: Emerging innovative immunotherapies in malignant ascites: current landscape, challenges and perspectives.
Resumen: Malignant ascites is a common, severe complication of advanced solid tumors, driven by multifactorial pathogenesis, including impaired lymphatic drainage, vascular endothelial growth factor-induced vascular hyperpermeability, pro-permeability inflammatory cytokines, and profound peritoneal immunosuppression. Preclinical and early-phase clinical studies suggest that intraperitoneal oncolytic viruses can induce immunogenic tumor cell death and T-cell activation, with single-cell analyses indicating remodeling of the ascitic immune microenvironment. Future directions include integrating ascites immune phenotyping, patient-derived organoids for drug sensitivity testing, and machine learning-based decision support to guide personalized immunotherapy.

Título: First-principles phonon physics using the Pheasy code.
Resumen: Parameter-free calculations of lattice dynamics from first principles have achieved significant progress in the past decades, with a wealth of applications in thermodynamics, phase transitions, and transport properties of materials. Current approaches to derive the interatomic force constants (IFCs) of lattice potential become challenging and sometimes infeasible when going beyond third-order anharmonicity, due to the combinatorial explosion in the number of higher-order IFCs. In this work, we present a robust and user-friendly program, Pheasy, which reliably reconstructs the prescribed potential energy surface of crystalline solids via a Taylor expansion of arbitrarily high order. Given force-displacement datasets, the program enables an efficient and accurate extraction of IFCs using advanced machine-learning algorithms, and further calculates a wide range of harmonic and anharmonic phonon related properties. We show in three prototypical examples how the obtained IFCs have been successfully applied to study anharmonic lattice dynamics and thermal transport. Through these detailed benchmarks, we have also identified the optimal approach for IFC extractions and offered general guidelines for high-fidelity lattice-dynamical simulations, addressing the large uncertainties in the IFCs extracted from existing various schemes. Overall, the Pheasy project aims to create a phonon code ecosystem that connects diverse phonon simulation platforms and offers access to the broad research community.

Título: From inherited susceptibility to tumor state: toward a stage-aware architecture for genomic risk stratification in prostate cancer.
Resumen: Prostate cancer risk is currently represented by two largely separate genomic layers. Germline polygenic scores estimate inherited susceptibility before diagnosis, whereas tumor genomic and transcriptomic classifiers estimate biological aggressiveness and treatment response after tissue acquisition. These results suggest a physical perspective for generalization, arising from the interplay between flexible representations and boundary-induced constraints.

Título: Flexible simulation framework for polymer-attenuated Coulombic self-assembly.
Resumen: Polymer-Attenuated Coulombic Self-Assembly (PACS) is a flexible experimental approach for generating crystals from simple colloidal building blocks. The central components are charged spherical particles coated with a polymer brush that prevents irreversible aggregation. Whether oppositely charged colloids crystallize, and which structures they form, depends on several factors, including colloid concentration, charge, and size, as well as the salt concentration of the solution. Título: Evolutionary chemical learning in dimerization networks.
Resumen: We present a framework for chemical learning based on competitive dimerization networks (CDNs)-systems in which multiple molecular species, e.g., proteins or DNA-RNA oligomers, reversibly bind to form dimers. We show numerically that these networks can, in principle, be trained in vitro through directed evolution, enabling the implementation of complex learning tasks such as multiclass classification without digital hardware or prior knowledge of all microscopic association constants. Each molecular species functions analogously to a neuron, with binding affinities acting as tunable synaptic weights. A training protocol involving mutation, selection, and amplification of DNA-based components allows CDNs to robustly discriminate among noisy input patterns. Comparative analysis with in silico gradient descent training reveals closely correlated performance. These results establish CDNs as a promising platform for analog physical computation, bridging synthetic biology and machine learning, and advancing the development of adaptive, energy-efficient molecular computing systems.

Resolving the assembly from its callset requires processing the same reads through one pipeline against both references.

ID (PMID): 42887996
Título: Decoding in-situ plant stress physiology via bio-hydrogel microneedles.
Resumen: Electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide (H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) dynamics enables early monitoring of plant stress physiology, which is crucial for crop health management and yield optimization. However, invasive sensors damage plant tissues, whereas existing non-invasive approaches suffer from cuticular barriers and insufficient exploitation of dynamic biochemical signals, leading to high interfacial impedance, delayed responses, and low accuracy. Here, we introduce an integrated sensing and machine-learning framework (CRH-BMIS) that combines a highly specific Cs/rGO/HRP biohydrogel microneedle with algorithmic analytics. This system overcomes traditional barriers to in situ, tissue-level monitoring of abiotic and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000) stresses. By significantly lowering interfacial impedance, the microneedle exhibits a stable log-linear response over an ultra-broad range (0.01-8000 μM) with exceptional sensitivity (up to 12.46 μA cm<sup>-2</sup> decade<sup>-1</sup>, LOD 0.00109 μM) and robust anti-interference. Furthermore, utilizing an intelligent diagnostic model based on stress-evoked H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> dynamics, CRH-BMIS achieves competitive cross-plant classification of abiotic/biotic stress (96.97% accuracy) and disease-stage classification (91.47% accuracy). This superior performance stems from the deep synergy between minimally invasive microneedles and machine learning algorithms. CRH-BMIS not only delivers accurate, generalizable in situ stress diagnosis but also enables scalable early-warning decision support.


--- ARTÍCULO 3255 ---
ID (PMID): 42887976
Título: An electrochemical sensor platform for rapid nucleic acid detection of Influenza A in unamplified samples and machine-learning-assisted infection diagnosis.
Resumen: Influenza A remains a major cause of respiratory infection that demands for rapid, accurate and readily accessible diagnostic tools for timely clinical decision-making and outbreak control. Here, we report a smartphone-assisted electrochemical biosensor platform for amplification-free nucleic acid detection of Influenza A based on magnetic beads enriched target capture and methylene blue (MB)-mediated signal transduction. Under optimized conditions, the platform enabled sensitive detection of both synthetic complementary DNA and RNA, with limits of detection of 0.33aM and 3.32aM, respectively, while maintaining high selectivity against mismatched and non-target sequences. Additionally, the platform is also applied to the detection of RNA extracted from nasopharyngeal swab samples and shows superior discrimination ability between positive and negative samples as well as strong correlation with reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) results. Finally, an optimal machine-learning framework based on a support vector classifier (SVC) is developed to analyze DPV signal profiles and directly classify clinical samples without explicit comparison to blank-current responses, achieving an accuracy of 100% in the clinical cohort. Unlike conventional nucleic acid detection approaches that mainly rely on predefined thresholds or quantitative signal interpretation, this study establishes a machine-learning-assisted classification strategy for direct discrimination of influenza A nucleic-acid positive and negative samples based on electrochemical DPV signal profiles. This simple algorithmic framework is particularly suitable for portable devices with resource constrained microcontrollers to realize rapid result analysis. Our results shed a light on potential portable platform for decentralized rapid nucleic acid testing and promising technique for point-of-care infectious disease diagnostics.

Título: Discovery of thiol-reactive Staphylococcus aureus sortase A inhibitors from natural products by machine learning and thiocholine mass-shift profiling.
Resumen: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains a major clinical challenge, and Sortase A (SrtA), a cysteine transpeptidase involved in surface-protein anchoring and biofilm formation, represents an attractive anti-virulence target. In this study, we developed an integrated analytical workflow combining machine-learning (ML)-guided taxon prioritisation, affinity magnetic capture, mass-shift profiling, and biochemical target-engagement assays to identify natural-product SrtA inhibitors from complex botanical extracts. A random-forest classifier trained on ChEMBL SrtA bioactivity data was applied to the LOTUS natural-product database to prioritise Michael-acceptor-containing botanical sources, leading to the selection of Piper retrofractum for constituent-level analysis. Subsequent chemical profiling and affinity-capture experiments identified piperlongumine as a thiol-reactive constituent preferentially associated with active SrtA. Piperlongumine inhibited SrtA transpeptidase activity with an IC<sub>50</sub> of 27.83 ± 1.04 μmol/L and showed a higher TCI-adduct response and stronger SrtA inhibition than the structurally related alkaloid piperine. Time-dependent enzyme inhibition, competitive 5-FAM-LPETG bead imaging, and mPEG-maleimide thiol-occupancy analysis further supported thiol-dependent SrtA engagement under the assay conditions. Piperlongumine also inhibited biofilm formation across multiple S. aureus strains while exerting limited effects on planktonic growth at corresponding concentrations. These findings demonstrate an analytical strategy that links computational prioritisation, crude-extract chemical profiling, affinity capture, and target-engagement validation for the discovery of thiol-reactive natural products targeting SrtA.


--- ARTÍCULO 3257 ---
ID (PMID): 42887971
Título: Mislabeling (label noise) - an often overlooked issue in chemometrics.
Resumen: In supervised learning, errors can arise in label values. This fact is well known in machine learning (ML), where it has been studied since the late 1960s, but is often ignored in chemometrics. The main reason for mislabeling is human errors when supervision is carried out by a person. It is also inevitable in cases where a continuous process is divided into stages for their subsequent supervised discrimination. Another reason is the imperfection of an instrumental method, which poorly reflects the differences between classes. This paper pursues two goals. The first one is to introduce the concept of mislabeling in chemometrics. The second goal is to share our experience in solving mislabeling problems that arise in real-world examples. In our opinion, the most appropriate approach is the integration of the domain knowledge with the outlier detection methods, which should be based on probabilistic (soft) classifiers. This approach is used systematically and is illustrated by three cases that employ both well-established and new methods. Mislabeling is a real problem that can occur across a variety of applications, reaching up to 20%, and in some areas, such as medicine, this rate can be even higher. There is no doubt that mislabeling deserves investigation and correction. In mission-critical fields, particularly in medicine, the cost of an error caused by mislabeled data can be significant, measured not only in financial losses but also in human lives.

ID (PMID): 42887969
Título: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.
Resumen: Rapid and accurate analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar (CT) is essential yet challenging due to spectral overlap and matrix effects. Excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectral analysis using deep learning algorithms can address this challenge. Coal tar samples were extracted and diluted with cyclohexane. A dataset of 1173 EEM spectra covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and various concentration gradients was constructed. Seven machine learning algorithms were used for qualitative classification of PAHs, and the deep learning algorithm, ResNet18, achieved the highest accuracy, close to 90%. Quantitative analysis was performed using a convolutional neural network-based variational autoencoder (CNN-VAE) model, yielding Root mean square error (RMSE) and (Mean absolute error) MAE values as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate PAH quantification in complex coal-tar matrices. This new approach provides a cost-effective, rapid, and reliable alternative to conventional methods, mitigating issues such as Rayleigh scattering and spectral overlap. It offers a new strategy for detecting PAH molecules in complex matrices.

ID (PMID): 42887958
Título: Why choose between prediction power and mechanistic insight in QSRR modeling? A case study of artificial membrane chromatography and machine learning.
Resumen: Quantitative structure-retention relationship (QSRR) modeling of immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was performed on a chemically diverse set of 2003 analytes to determine whether mechanistically interpretable, descriptor-based models can match the predictive performance of advanced machine-learning approaches. Chromatographic hydrophobicity indices (CHI<sub>IAM</sub>) were measured under standardized fast-gradient IAM conditions and modeled using three molecular representation strategies: physicochemical descriptors, ECFP4 fingerprints, and a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) operating on molecular graphs. Among the descriptor- and fingerprint-based methods, the Gradient Boosting Regressor gave the best performance. The descriptor-based model achieved a test R<sup>2</sup> of 0.817, MAE of 4.43, and RMSE of 6.46 CHI<sub>IAM</sub> units, whereas the GIN model showed only a marginal numerical improvement (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.828, MAE = 4.27, RMSE = 6.25). In contrast, fingerprint-based modeling performed worse (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.771, MAE = 5.04, RMSE = 7.22). Statistical analysis of paired prediction errors showed no significant difference between the descriptor-based and GIN models, while the fingerprint-based model was the least accurate of the three. The observed differences among the best models were smaller than the long-term reproducibility of the IAM protocol. Applicability-domain analysis further showed that approximately 94-99% of compounds fell within the interpolation region. SHAP analysis identified lipophilicity, ionization, charge, and polarity as the major determinants of IAM retention, with cationic character enhancing retention and high polarity reducing it. These results demonstrate that descriptor-based QSRR modeling can achieve near-deep learning performance while preserving mechanistic interpretability, providing a practical and physically grounded strategy for IAM retention prediction.

Título: Machine learning-assisted fluorescent sensor array based on siloxane-derived porous polymers for high-throughput discrimination of multiple antibiotics in milk.
Resumen: Both simultaneous monitoring of multiple antibiotic residues for public health security and accurate single-analyte quantification for regulatory compliance are critically important, though the former remains challenging due to structural diversity among analytes. Título: AI-integrated iPSC multi-omics: advancing phenotype discovery and drug target identification in rare diseases.
Resumen: Rare diseases represent a major unmet medical need, yet the development of therapeutics for these diseases is limited by small patient cohorts, fragmented data, and uncertain disease mechanisms. ID (PMID): 42887837
Título: Decoding spatial attention in the cocktail party problem using whole-head high-density fNIRS.
Resumen: Spatial attention is critical for solving the cocktail party problem, a longstanding problem in neuroscience and artificial speech recognition. The ability to decode where humans are attending in a cocktail party like scene would empower applications in brain computer interfaces and assistive devices such as hearing aids. Here we demonstrate that, in an overt attention task, the attended spatial location can be decoded robustly from single trial hemodynamic responses, using a whole head high density fNIRS system. We also identify critical brain regions that make the highest contribution to decoding accuracy. Specifically, we find that decoding based on a small fraction of channels located within the left and right inferior parietal lobule (IPL) achieves maximal decoding accuracy comparable to all channels. Decoding fell close to chance in a covert auditory condition in which participants held central fixation while attending to the same talkers, indicating that auditory attention alone without orientation is not sufficient for decoding. Finally, control experiments suggest that overt-condition decoding is influenced by sustained eye position/gaze direction, not eye movement. These results support the development of fNIRS-integrated BCIs and assistive devices controlled by overt spatial attention.

ID (PMID): 42887809
Título: Uncovering spatially heterogeneous predictors of reported malaria cases in the Ashanti Region of Ghana: a triangulated framework integrating correlation analysis, random forest, and multiscale geographically weighted regression.
Resumen: Malaria remains a major cause of illness and death in sub-Saharan Africa. In 2023, WHO reported 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths globally. Ghana records a substantial malaria burden, and the Ashanti Region is among the regions contributing a large share of reported cases. Despite successive interventions, reported malaria incidence remains high. This study used a triangulated analytical framework to examine environmental and anthropogenic correlates of district-level reported malaria case counts in 2023 (n = 43 districts). Spearman's rank Correlation, Random Forest, and MGWR models were fitted to raw district-level laboratory-confirmed case counts, and a population-normalized incidence rate was used only for the descriptive spatial map. Spearman's rank correlation characterized global monotonic associations, Random Forest (RF) with partial dependence plots (PDPs) examined nonlinear marginal patterns, and Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) examined spatially varying local associations, following a variance inflation factor (VIF) screen for multicollinearity. Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) was the most consistently ranked correlate across the three analytical methods and was the only RF importance estimate distinguishable from the permutation null at the unadjusted 0.05 level (permutation p = 0.017; not adjusted for 11 comparisons). RF validation showed substantial overfitting and limited out-of-sample generalization (in-sample R² = 0.629; LOOCV R² = 0.056; MAE = 6897 cases; RMSE = 8851 cases; MAPE = 55.8%). Eight predictors had a bandwidth of 3 k-NN, suggesting strong estimated spatial non-stationarity under the MGWR model. With only 43 districts, these narrow bandwidths may also reflect coefficient instability rather than a confirmed spatial scale. Environmental and anthropogenic correlates of district-level reported malaria case counts varied across the Ashanti Region. These ecological associations are exploratory and hypothesis-generating, not evidence of causal transmission mechanisms or intervention effectiveness. Future studies should use reliable population denominators, facility-level coordinates, multiyear surveillance, entomological information, and socioeconomic covariates.

Título: Kinetics, radical chemistry and machine-learning-optimized abatement of capecitabine by UV/peroxymonosulfate: simultaneous micropollutant removal and attenuation of disinfection by-products formation potential.
Resumen: As a widely used anticancer prodrug, capecitabine (CAPT) is poorly removed by conventional treatment and may generate toxic transformation products and disinfection by-products (DBPs). This study systematically evaluated CAPT abatement by UV/peroxymonosulfate (UV/PMS), integrating reaction kinetics, energy analysis, reactive species quantification, machine learning, transformation products identification and subsequent disinfection assessment. UV/PMS reduced CAPT below the quantification limit within 4 min, with the pseudo-first-order rate constant (k<sub>obs</sub>) of 0.7854 min<sup>-1</sup> and the lowest electrical energy per order (EE/O) among the tested processes. SO<sub>4</sub>•<sup>-</sup> dominated CAPT oxidation, contributing 65.20% of the overall degradation. HO• contributed 23.92%, while direct UV photolysis and PMS oxidation accounted for 9.94% and 0.94%. The contribution of singlet oxygen was negligible. The second-order rate constants of CAPT with SO<sub>4</sub>•<sup>-</sup> and HO• were 4.02 × 10<sup>9</sup> and 7.48 × 10<sup>9</sup> M<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>, and UV/PMS exhibited strong process synergy effect. The PMS dose of approximately 200 μM under mildly alkaline conditions provided a favorable balance between degradation kinetics and energy consumption, whereas natural organic matter exerted the strongest matrix inhibition. XGBoost accurately predicted k<sub>obs</sub> and EE/O, and Pareto optimization identified a balanced operating point with k<sub>obs</sub>≈5.5 min<sup>-1</sup> and EE/O ≈ 1.88 kWh m<sup>-3</sup> order<sup>-1</sup>. Transformation products were tentatively identified and evaluated using DFT calculations, Fukui functions, frontier molecular orbital analysis and elemental ratio analysis. The results suggested that oxidation likely involved the fluoropyrimidine moiety and the aliphatic side chain, followed by hydroxylation, defluorination, deamination, hydrolysis and C-N bond cleavage. UV photodegradation alone increased the halogen reactivity of residual precursors, whereas UV/PMS minimized both total and toxicity-weighted levels of the four targeted DBPs during chlorination and chloramination. In conclusion, UV/PMS combined rapid, energy-efficient CAPT abatement with reduced DBPs formation and the related-toxicity burden.

Título: Molecular characteristics and formation mechanisms of chlorinated disinfection byproducts from diatomaceous organic matter: Deciphering intracellular vs. extracellular contributions via FT-ICR MS and machine learning.
Resumen: Diatom-derived algal organic matter (AOM), including intracellular organic matter (IOM) and extracellular organic matter (EOM), is an important precursor of disinfection byproducts (DBPs) in drinking water sources during diatom blooms. Clarifying the differences in the toxicity and formation mechanisms of chlorinated DBPs between IOM and EOM is crucial for identifying priority removal targets and optimizing drinking water treatment. However, these differences remain poorly understood. In this study, the toxicity, formation characteristics, and underlying mechanisms of IOM-derived DBPs and EOM-derived DBPs were systematically investigated and compared, with a focus on molecular-level interactions. At the same dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration (1.135 mgC/L), chlorinated IOM showed higher cytotoxicity than chlorinated EOM. IOM preferentially formed more nitrogenous DBPs, including (semi-)volatile and macromolecular species, whereas EOM produced more carbonaceous DBPs. Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry combined with machine learning revealed distinct molecular signatures of DBP precursors in IOM and EOM. Precursors of high-molecular-weight carbonaceous DBPs had lower unsaturation and oxidation degrees but higher aromaticity, whereas precursors of macromolecular nitrogenous DBPs showed the opposite pattern. Given the substantially higher DOC concentration of IOM than EOM at the same diatom density, IOM should be prioritized for removal. These findings provide molecular-level insight for controlling diatom-related DBP risks in drinking water treatment.

Título: Optical monitoring of inflammatory response in joint explant cultures using near infrared spectroscopy.
Resumen: To evaluate near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning (ML) for detecting and estimating inflammatory and matrix-related biomarkers released into the culture medium of an explant model. Bovine osteochondral explants and synovial tissues were co-cultured under inflammatory factor-treated (IF-treated) conditions that mimic osteoarthritis (OA) and non-IF-treated conditions. The co-cultures were maintained for seven days with the culture medium collected and replaced daily. The samples were subjected to NIR spectral measurements (900-1700 nm), followed by measurement of sulphated glycosaminoglycans (sGAG), nitric oxide (NO), interleukin (IL)-6, and IL-8 released into the culture. Acquired spectra were preprocessed and analyzed for classification and estimation of biomarkers using ML-based models. Feature importance analyses were performed to identify key wavelength features that contribute to classification and prediction of biomarkers. Biomarker release showed a substantial increase in the OA-like setup compared to the non-IF-treated setup. During classification, the IF-treated and non-IF-treated spectra showed distinct patterns, with noticeable differences in the 1440-1520 nm and 1600-1700 nm regions. Using these spectral variations, the best performing classifier achieved an accuracy of 95.3% in distinguishing OA-like from non-IF-treated samples. The regression analysis also showed good regression performance with R² values of 0.44 (sGAG), 0.48 (NO), 0.42 (IL-6), and 0.36 (IL-8). This study showed that NIR spectroscopy combined with ML can detect and quantify OA-related spectral signatures in explant media, thereby demonstrating its potential as a non-destructive and rapid method for monitoring inflammatory activity in ex vivo OA models.

ID (PMID): 42887666
Título: Type 1 diabetes metabolomics and multi-omics: Current applications, limitations, and future directions - A narrative review.
Resumen: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disease characterized by immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, resulting in absolute insulin deficiency and lifelong dependence on exogenous insulin. This disease, if not treated, leads to acute and chronic complications affecting the cardiovascular, renal, and retinal systems and introduces significant psychosocial burdens. But even with advances in insulin therapy, optimal glycemic control remains difficult to achieve. T1DM progression spans from autoantibody seroconversion to overt diabetes, accompanied by dynamic metabolic perturbations, contributing to β-cell dysfunction. These metabolic alterations correlate with glycemic markers and provide integrated signatures of gene-environment interactions and disease heterogeneity. Therefore, metabolomics has emerged as a promising approach for identifying metabolic dysregulation associated with T1DM, with some studies reporting metabolite alterations detectable before clinical onset or autoantibody positivity; targeted and untargeted approaches enable comprehensive profiling of disease-associated metabolic pathways, although these findings largely reflect associations from observational cohorts rather than validated early-detection tools. Here, the analysis of biofluids with advanced platforms such as UPLC-MS and NMR provides high-resolution insights into systemic metabolism, supporting the discovery of candidate biomarkers that may, pending further validation, contribute to earlier diagnosis and precision medicine strategies in T1DM. Even though current metabolomic studies have substantially improved the classification of metabolic alterations associated with T1DM, the field still necessitates clarification of causal mechanisms, standardization of methodologies, validation of findings across diverse populations, and integration of metabolomics with other omics platforms in robust longitudinal designs. These gaps highlight a clear necessity of moving beyond descriptive profiling toward systematically standardized and validated metabolomic markers embedded within multi-omics and longitudinal frameworks.

Título: Augmenting electronic health records for adverse event detection.
Resumen: Adverse events (AEs) resulting from medical interventions are significant contributors to patient morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Detection of these events using electronic health records (EHRs) can facilitate timely clinical interventions. However, effective detection remains challenging due to severe class imbalance, missing labels, and the complexity of EHR records. Classical machine learning approaches frequently underperform due to insufficient representation of minority adverse event classes and limited capacity to capture interactions among patient demographics, administered medications, and associated complications. This study aims to develop and evaluate a lightweight, NLP-inspired data augmentation framework for structured EHR data that improves minority-class adverse event detection without requiring complex generative models or pre-trained clinical language models. We introduce TASER-AE (Tokenized Augmentation for Structured EHR-Adverse Events), a novel data augmentation pipeline tailored for structured EHR data, coupled with transformer-based classification. TASER-AE addresses these issues through an NLP-inspired data augmentation framework adapted for EHR, enabling effective minority-class representation in sparse and imbalanced clinical datasets. The augmented records produced by TASER-AE alleviate class imbalance by enriching the representation of minority adverse event classes, which enhances the robustness and predictive performance of the classifier. TASER-AE yields minority-class F1 scores up to 0.67, substantially surpassing classical machine-learning baselines and generative augmentation, and consistently improving on prior edit-based augmentation methods, across multiple adverse event tasks. Experiments conducted on two distinct EHR datasets confirm TASER-AE's ability to substantially improve adverse event detection. These results demonstrate the potential of structured, NLP-inspired augmentation methods to overcome data limitations in clinical predictive modeling, ultimately contributing to improved patient safety outcomes. TASER-AE is available at https://github.com/Kingsford-Group/taserae.

Título: An efficient convolutional neural network model for classifying positive affective states from EEG data considering sleep condition.
Resumen: The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience.

Título: Physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction for limited-angle CBCT.
Resumen: <i>Objective.</i>Limited-angle cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is attractive for image-guided radiotherapy and imaging-guided procedures when full-arc acquisition is impractical, but the incomplete angular sampling leads to severe streaking, shading, and structural distortion. This study aimed to develop a physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction framework for recovering anatomically faithful volumetric CBCT from short-arc limited-angle projections.<i>Approach.</i>We propose a physics-constrained and geometry-aware network (PCGA-Net), a dual-domain reconstruction framework that combines projection completion, analytic geometric reconstruction, and image-domain refinement within a unified cross-domain design. Specifically, a projection completion module first estimates missing-angle information from the measured limited-angle projections. A geometry-aware reconstruction module then maps the completed projections into image space using differentiable cone-beam forward and backward-projection operators. Finally, a volumetric refinement module suppresses residual artifacts and restores anatomical detail under geometry-guided cross-domain consistency supervision. The framework was evaluated on three clinically distinct cohorts: gynecologic (GYN) high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy, abdominal liver four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT), and head-and-neck (H&N) CBCT.<i>Main results.</i>Across all three cohorts, fully adapted PCGA-Net consistently outperformed conventional limited-angle Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstruction and the compared learning-based baselines, a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) and PatRecon-Net, in both qualitative and quantitative evaluation under matched patient-specific adaptation conditions. On the GYN HDR brachytherapy cohort, PCGA-Net achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 34.47 ± 6.28 Hounsfield units (HU), a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.87 ± 0.04, and a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 35.79 ± 0.95 dB, compared with 178.63 ± 31.58 HU, 0.51 ± 0.03, and 18.97 ± 1.31 dB for FDK. On the abdominal liver 4DCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 39.27 ± 6.10 HU MAE, 0.82 ± 0.03 SSIM, and 36.85 ± 1.16 dB PSNR, versus 195.21 ± 40.08 HU, 0.50 ± 0.06, and 18.50 ± 1.50 dB for FDK. On the H&N CBCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 28.42 ± 4.88 HU MAE, 0.91 ± 0.05 SSIM, and 38.52 ± 0.95 dB PSNR, compared with 165.30 ± 25.40 HU, 0.61 ± 0.05, and 21.13 ± 1.14 dB for FDK. In all three cohorts, PCGA-Net also exceeded cGAN and PatRecon-Net across all evaluated metrics.<i>Significance.</i>These results indicate that jointly enforcing projection-domain completion, analytic imaging geometry, and image-domain refinement is an effective strategy for limited-angle CBCT reconstruction. PCGA-Net provides a robust short-arc reconstruction framework across multiple anatomical sites and clinical workflows, supporting its potential utility in constrained image-guided therapeutic and procedural settings.

Título: Physics-informed machine learning-based dose calculation for patients undergoing fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures.
Resumen: <i>Objective.</i>To develop and evaluate a physics-informed machine-learning framework for rapid organ-dose estimation in fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures without requiring patient-specific imaging.<i>Approach.</i>We used 385 adult radiation dose structured reports (RDSRs) from three procedure types-bilateral carotid angiography, percutaneous biliary drainage, and liver chemoembolization-comprising more than 50 000 irradiation events. A body-size-matched computational phantom was selected using patient sex, height, and weight. RDSR-derived beam parameters and engineered descriptors of beam-organ geometry and attenuation were used to train organ-specific XGBoost models for localized organs and a multi-output multilayer perceptron model for four distributed tissues.
