The corresponding proportions were 88.2% and 98.0% for the distributed-tissue estimates and 87.6% and 98.3% for detriment-weighted dose. The median relative prediction error across organs and tissues was 0.37% (interquartile range, -3.68% to 4.99%). A reliability score was developed to support uncertainty-aware interpretation. The framework required approximately 0.3 s per irradiation event, corresponding to an approximately 290-fold acceleration relative to conventional MC simulation under the benchmark conditions.<i>Significance.</i>The proposed image-free framework enables rapid organ-dose estimation when patient imaging is unavailable and may support large retrospective epidemiological studies and uncertainty-aware dose monitoring. Because development and validation were limited to three procedure types and relied on reconstructed phantom-beam geometry, external validation is required before application to other procedures or high-precision individual clinical decisions.

--- ARTÍCULO 3276 ---
ID (PMID): 42887473
Título: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
Resumen: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

Título: ConsistDiff: Training-free reinforcement learning for semantically consistent text-to-image generation.
Resumen: Diffusion models have become a leading paradigm for text-to-image generation owing to their promising capability to produce photo-realistic and diverse images from text prompts. Despite these advances, state-of-the-art models often fail to maintain faithful semantic consistency, particularly when handling complex descriptions with multiple entities and attributes. These shortcomings manifest as object omission, attribute leakage, or inaccurate binding between textual concepts and visual elements. To address these challenges, particularly for deploying generative models on resource-constrained devices, we propose ConsistDiff, an inference-time optimization framework that enhances Stable Diffusion without requiring computationally expensive fine-tuning. Specifically, we integrate a context-aware attention mechanism to refine inter-token relations by leveraging character-level spatial distances. This context-aware design provides a fine-grained structural signal that sharpens attribute-entity binding, suppresses spurious long-range couplings, and adds negligible computational overhead. Further, we formulate prompt-specific token reweighting as a reinforcement-learning problem and optimize it with an attention-separation reward that explicitly penalizes cross-entity attention overlap while preserving the saliency of key objects. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that ConsistDiff consistently improves semantic alignment between the input text prompts and the generated images while maintaining highly efficient inference as well as mitigating common issues such as attribute leakage and entity inconsistency.

Título: Architecture-agnostic knowledge distillation for machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Resumen: Atomistic foundation models can achieve near-ab-initio accuracy and strong transferability across molecular and materials systems, but their large parameter counts lead to high inference latency and memory cost, limiting long-time-scale molecular dynamics and resource-constrained deployment. In many practical studies, only a narrow chemical subdomain is required, motivating compact students that preserve the teacher's physical priors. Existing distillation for Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) is still limited by architecture mismatch or incomplete geometric supervision. We propose an architecture-agnostic framework, Joint Atomic Energy-Energy Hessian Distillation, that requires no architecture-specific feature projection. Across teacher-student pairs, it also reduces parameter counts by 79%-98%, enabling fast and deployment-friendly specialized MLIPs for targeted chemical subdomains.

Resumen: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. Título: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems.
Resumen: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.

Hard-prompting showed particular effectiveness in the 1-shot scenario compared with standard fine-tuning for GatorTron-Base. Overall, Decoder-based models generally outperformed encoder-based models under QLoRA-based adaptation. However, under the most resource-constrained setting, where both training data and trainable parameters were highly limited, encoder-based models achieved better performance than decoder-based models. This study provides a controlled benchmark for adapting LLMs to CTRE under different data and parameter constraints. Our findings suggest that QLoRA targeting only the query and value projection layers is a computationally efficient and competitive adaptation strategy. Decoder-based LLMs generally achieved stronger performance under QLoRA-based adaptation, whereas domain-specific encoder-based models showed advantages under the most resource-constrained soft-prompting setting. These results highlight the importance of selecting adaptation strategies according to both model architecture and available computational resources.

Título: Testing Group Differences in Nonlinear Growth Curve Modeling with Penalized Spline.
Resumen: Longitudinal data analysis in social and behavioral sciences often assumes a linear change over time, but human behavior is complex and frequently exhibits nonlinear patterns. Regression spline is a popular approach in machine learning to model nonlinear trajectories. While traditional machine learning prioritizes prediction, researchers in social and behavioral sciences focus on testing and interpreting the significance of group differences. This study compares six spline models for evaluating group differences in group-mean trajectories across multiple time points: the frequentist truncated power basis model, the frequentist piecewise basis model, the frequentist B-spline basis model, the Bayesian truncated power basis model, the Bayesian piecewise basis model, and the Bayesian B-spline basis model. Título: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Composite Materials: A Review.
Resumen: Composite materials are not easy to model using traditional experiments and physics-based approaches due to their diverse properties and multiscale nature. It combines their possible use across the prediction of their properties, damage detection, structural health monitoring, and materials design. Searches were performed in Scopus and Google Scholar for articles published using combined keywords such as "(artificial intelligence OR machine learning OR deep learning OR Generative AI) AND (composite OR fiber reinforced) AND (prediction OR optimization OR characterization)". For each selected article, relevant information was extracted in a structured and consistent manner, including the type of composite material, AI methodology, input parameters, dataset characteristics and size, validation methods, and application domain. AI is shifting composite materials research from trial-and-error toward data-driven, predictive design. Título: Securing AI-Driven Systems for Environmental Sustainability in IoT Applications: A Lightweight Message-Authentication Scheme Against Telemetry Poisoning.
Resumen: Machine-learning models for environmental monitoring are only as trustworthy as the field measurements that train them, yet raw or custom LoRa telemetry links-unlike a correctly configured LoRaWAN network-carry no application-layer authentication, letting any in-range transmitter inject fabricated readings and poison the training pipeline. We propose a lightweight, unidirectional, encryption-free scheme in which each message carries an HMAC-SHA-256 tag over the device identifier, a timestamp, a monotonic counter, and the sensor payload; the server accepts a message only if its tag verifies and its counter exceeds a durable, transactionally updated high-water mark, giving origin authentication, tamper evidence, and duplicate or stale rejection without encryption. A ten-seed illustrative poisoning study on two public environmental datasets shows a value-based defence can increase PM2.5 forecast RMSE by up to about 104% by discarding genuine extremes, whereas our scheme holds the clean baseline exactly, since forged rows are rejected before training. The tag grows an example message from 34 to 99 bytes (about 2.9×) and roughly doubles airtime (about 2.2×); per-message CPU time and energy are not quantified here. Under independent per-device keys and rate limits, partial key compromise bounds admitted forged traffic to the compromised devices' share of total traffic.

Título: Driving-Context Classification from Wearable Physiological and Motion Signals During Real-World Driving.
Resumen: Wearable physiological sensing is widely used in driving research to infer drowsiness and stress, but whether driving context itself is reflected in wearable signals, independent of any drowsiness label, is rarely examined directly; any such signal reflects the driver's physiological response to context, not the road environment itself. Driving context is statistically distinguishable from wrist-worn wearable signals once analyzed at the correct statistical unit, but the signal is diffuse across sensor channels, and person-independent classification remains weak at this sample size; naive cross-validation and uncorrected pairwise-multiplicity designs common in this literature can substantially overstate both classification and statistical testing results.

Título: Quantifying Subject-Identity Variance in Spectral EEG Features and Its Role in Machine Learning Evaluation Leakage.
Resumen: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to study cognitive states and clinical biomarkers, yet the contribution of stable between-subject differences to common EEG feature representations is rarely quantified directly or incorporated into evaluation design. Título: Prognostic Models for Incident Hypertension: Time to Move from Development to Implementation-An Umbrella Review.
Resumen: Hypertension represents a major modifiable cardiovascular risk factor with increasing global prevalence. While numerous prognostic models for incident hypertension have been developed, their clinical implementation remains limited, suggesting a gap between model development and practical application. This study aimed to synthesize evidence from systematic reviews on multivariable prognostic models estimating the future risk of incident hypertension among initially normotensive individuals, evaluating methodological quality, predictive performance, validation status, calibration reporting, and clinical utility. Stronger independent evaluation, calibration/Brier assessment, and decision-curve analysis were reported in only 18/67, 23/67, and 10/67 reports, respectively. <b>Conclusions:</b> ML shows promising post-TAVR discrimination, particularly for mortality, but substantial heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and sparse calibration and decision utility assessment constrain clinical translation. Título: Research Activity and Subspecialty Imbalance of Artificial Intelligence in Orthopaedics: A Bibliometric Analysis.
Resumen: <b>Background</b>: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a major research domain in orthopaedics, driven by advances in computational methods and the widespread availability of digital clinical data. Although AI-related orthopaedic publications have increased substantially, the extent to which this growth reflects a balanced distribution of research activity across clinical subspecialties and AI modalities remains unclear. <b>Purpose:</b> The aim of this study was to evaluate temporal trends, subspecialty distribution, and methodological characteristics of AI-related orthopaedic research activity using a bibliometric approach. <b>Methods:</b> A bibliometric analysis was performed using publications indexed in two major scientific databases between 2016 and 2025. AI-related orthopaedic articles were identified using predefined search terms. Publications were analyzed according to annual publication trends, orthopaedic subspecialty classification, AI methodology, and proxy indicators of study design and evidence development. Subspecialty assignment was performed using a standardized taxonomy, and descriptive analyses were used to characterize research patterns. <b>Results:</b> AI-related orthopaedic publications increased exponentially during the study period. Research output was unevenly distributed across subspecialties, with adult reconstruction and spine surgery accounting for the largest share of publications, whereas foot and ankle surgery, pediatric orthopaedics, hand & wrist, and shoulder & elbow surgery remained underrepresented. Deep learning-based imaging studies predominated, while studies incorporating structured clinical data, longitudinal outcomes, and external validation were comparatively limited. Much of the literature remains exploratory, primarily focusing on early-phase model development. <b>Conclusions:</b> AI research in orthopaedics has expanded rapidly but remains methodologically heterogeneous, with research activity heavily concentrated in data-rich subspecialties such as adult reconstruction and spine surgery. The predominance of early-phase studies indicates that current publication volumes are largely driven by data accessibility rather than a balanced distribution across all orthopaedic domains. Future research should encourage multicenter collaboration, standardized reporting, and targeted studies in underrepresented subspecialties to ensure a more balanced development of orthopaedic AI tools.

Título: Artificial Intelligence in Emergency Medical Call-Taking and Dispatch Operations: A Scoping Review.
Resumen: <b>Objective:</b> This study aimed to systematically review worldwide research on artificial intelligence (AI) applications in emergency medical service (EMS) call-taking and dispatch operations and identify current research trends and research needs. <b>Methods:</b> This scoping review was reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, KoreaMed, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library were searched for studies published from January 2021 to August 2026. Data were synthesized descriptively. <b>Results:</b> Eighteen studies from 13 countries and one multinational setting were included; eight (44.4%) were conducted in Europe. Patient Recognition and Classification was the predominant domain (11/18, 61.1%), followed by Dispatch Support and Operational Decision-Making (5/18, 27.8%) and Other Methodological Applications (2/18, 11.1%). Structured clinical or dispatch data were used in 11 studies, textual data in eight, and call audio in five; four applied multimodal integration. Deep learning (DL) was used as a primary model in 11 studies and classical machine learning (ML) in eight, including three using both; large language models (LLMs) were used in two. Eleven studies involved retrospective model development and internal validation, whereas only two were randomized controlled trials. None of the 11 model-development studies conducted independent external validation or calibration assessment, and the two randomized trials, one with high risk of bias and the other with some concerns, showed no consistent improvement across dispatch outcomes. <b>Conclusions:</b> AI applications span diverse clinical and operational tasks, with multimodal integration, speech technologies, and LLMs broadening their potential scope. Evidence remains dominated by retrospective model development and internal validation; prospective and real-world implementation studies are needed to establish safety and clinical utility before integration into EMS systems.

Título: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Spirometry in Primary Healthcare: Opportunities for Early Detection of Small Airway Dysfunction.
Resumen: Spirometry underuse and persistent limitations in its technical quality and interpretation in primary healthcare (PHC) contribute to delayed and inaccurate diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Artificial intelligence (AI) has recently demonstrated, at the randomised controlled trial level, that it can improve spirometry interpretation by primary care clinicians. Maximal mid-expiratory flow (MMEF), a spirometric measure routinely derived from every forced expiratory manoeuvre, has been associated with subsequent airflow obstruction and lung function decline, particularly when conventional spirometric indices remain preserved, suggesting that it may contribute to earlier recognition of small airway dysfunction. However, no existing review has examined whether AI could specifically address the challenge of MMEF interpretation, and the incremental value of MMEF within AI-assisted spirometry models remains unestablished. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on AI-assisted spirometry in PHC across three evidence domains, diagnostic classification, quality control, and computational small airway assessment, and examines the potential for integrating MMEF with conventional spirometric indices, flow-volume curve morphology, technical quality, clinical characteristics, and longitudinal data to support its clinical interpretation. The available evidence supports the feasibility of the individual components underpinning this proposed framework, including AI-assisted spirometry interpretation, automated quality assessment, and computational extraction of small airway information from spirometric data. However, the contextual integration of MMEF within AI-assisted models has not yet been prospectively evaluated, and validation of its incremental predictive value and clinical utility is needed before implementation can be recommended.

ID (PMID): 42881472
Título: Peri-operative goal-directed haemodynamic therapy and high-risk patients: what's going on? A narrative review.
Resumen: Goal-directed haemodynamic therapy (GDHT) is a comprehensive haemodynamic optimisation strategy rather than simple fluid optimisation. It guides peri-operative haemodynamic management towards predefined physiological targets to reduce post-operative complications in high-risk surgical patients. This review asks whether GDHT retains clinical value in 2026, which patients are most likely to benefit, which targets are most appropriate, and what its relationship to Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) programmes should be. The physiological basis of GDHT links surgical injury to an inflammatory cascade that impairs vascular integrity and tissue perfusion and draws on Shoemaker's seminal observation that prompt restoration of oxygen delivery during surgery or in the first post-operative hours predicts survival. RCTs and meta-analyses have reported reductions in post-operative complications, most consistently acute kidney injury, surgical site infections, and gastrointestinal morbidity, with the benefit most consistent in patients at the highest peri-operative risk. Recent evidence has complicated this picture. OPTIMISE II and iPEGASUS, two large pragmatic trials, produced neutral results, and the incorporation of fluid optimisation into ERAS protocols raises a practical question: what does GDHT add when good peri-operative care already includes haemodynamic attention? These uncertainties converge on a single practical difficulty: there is no universally accepted definition of "high risk", which limits both trial comparability and clinical uptake. Artificial intelligence tools, in particular closed-loop haemodynamic management systems and machine learning models for preoperative risk stratification, are appraised here as potential means of supporting more individualised implementation. GDHT retains clinical value in 2026, but the benefit appears most evident in patients at the highest peri-operative risk, while in intermediate-risk populations the evidence for added value beyond well-implemented ERAS remains uncertain. The most effective strategy is a multiparameter-based one, combining dynamic preload indices, cardiac output monitoring, and metabolic endpoints rather than fixed single-variable targets. Validated risk stratification is the critical prerequisite for both rational clinical implementation and meaningful future trials.

Título: Interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of deep vein thrombosis in elderly ICU patients: multicenter development and external validation.
Resumen: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a frequent complication in elderly intensive care unit (ICU) patients, while reliable prediction tools for this population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of DVT in critically ill elderly patients. In this multicenter retrospective study, ICU patients aged ≥ 75 years from two tertiary medical centers in China were enrolled. Patients with pre-existing DVT were excluded. A development cohort (Suzhou, n = 1,717) and an external validation cohort (Xi'an, n = 533) were established. Clinical variables collected within 24 h after ICU admission were used to predict incident DVT during ICU stay. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was applied for feature selection, and four machine learning models were developed and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and interpretability were evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). DVT occurred in 15.2% and 21.0% of patients in the development and external validation cohorts, respectively. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance, with AUCs of 0.843 in internal validation and 0.811 in external validation. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risks. Key predictors included D-dimer, C-reactive protein, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, procalcitonin, mechanical ventilation, and mechanical thromboprophylaxis. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of individual predictors. We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early DVT prediction in elderly ICU patients. The model may support risk stratification and clinical decision-making in critical care settings.

Título: Explainable machine learning and unsupervised anatomical phenotyping of mitral valve prolapse in patients with severe mitral regurgitation.
Resumen: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) is increasingly recognized in mitral valve prolapse (MVP), but its anatomical embedding within degenerative MVP remains incompletely defined. We assessed whether explainable supervised learning and unsupervised clustering could identify MAD-associated MVP phenotypes. We analyzed a public surgical cohort of 979 patients with MVP and clinically significant mitral regurgitation. Etiology was classified as Barlow disease (BD) or fibroelastic deficiency (FED). Logistic regression, Random Forest and XGBoost were evaluated for MAD prediction using nested cross-validation with threshold optimization, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit (decision-curve analysis). XGBoost explainability was assessed using SHAP. UMAP-based clustering using anatomical and clinical variables (excluding MAD and etiology from the input) was performed, with prespecified cluster-number and stability sensitivity analyses. Unsupervised phenotyping identified three anatomical clusters. The smallest cluster (n = 91, 9.3%) showed the highest MAD prevalence (36.3% vs. 12.0% and 15.8%), marked BD enrichment (95.6%), universal bileaflet prolapse and ≥ 4-scallop involvement, larger MV diameters and less chordal rupture; this phenotype was reproducible across UMAP settings. Supervised models showed only moderate MAD discrimination (XGBoost AUROC 0.695 ± 0.057; PR-AUC 0.314 ± 0.066), with modest calibration (Brier 0.13-0.20; slopes < 1) and limited net benefit, and were therefore interpreted as explanatory rather than diagnostic. SHAP identified BD status as the strongest contributor, followed by number of prolapsing scallops, mitral valve diameters, LV volumes and bileaflet prolapse. Explainable and unsupervised analyses concordantly identified a MAD-enriched, BD-dominant bileaflet/multiscallop MVP phenotype, supporting the concept that MAD is embedded within broader annular-leaflet remodeling rather than being an isolated binary abnormality. These findings require prospective, multimodality, outcome-linked external validation before clinical application.

Título: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
Resumen: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

Título: Evaluating the effect of griseofulvin on the disintegration properties of tablets.
Resumen: Understanding how active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) influence tablet disintegration remains essential for optimising oral drug product performance. In this work, we present an integrated, data-driven framework that combines deep-learning-based image segmentation, automated regime detection and mechanistic modelling to characterise liquid absorption and swelling behaviours from sessile drop experiments. Using this workflow, we investigated the effect of incorporating griseofulvin into directly compressed tablets containing a variety of excipient combinations. For griseofulvin, the method was sensitive to changes in absorption and swelling behaviour, highlighting its potential as a high-throughput formulation screening approach. Further studies involving a wider range of APIs are needed to determine whether these observations are generalisable and relevant to disintegration and dissolution performance.

Combined machine learning, molecular dynamics, and density functional theory analyses indicate distinct inhibition modes, including coordination of Fe<sup>III</sup>, Zn<sup>II</sup>, and Sn<sup>II</sup> at the LanM EF4 hand loop and favourable binding of [Al(OH)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>-</sup>/[Ga(OH)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>-</sup> near the TEM-1 substrate-recognition region. Consistent with these predictions, citrate reduced inhibition from hydrolysing metals, especially Al<sup>III</sup> and Sn<sup>II</sup>. Together, these findings define matrix-dependent operating envelopes, mechanistic design rules, and practical mitigation strategies for deploying REE biosensors in chemically complex waters.

Título: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
Resumen: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational capacity, analogous to scaling up parameters in machine learning models. By contrast, the steering subsystem (hypothalamus, pallidum, and brainstem) scales via diversification of bespoke cell types to encode innate drives and reflexes, functioning as a high-dimensional biological "reward function." This framework explains the divergence in how evolution has influenced these subsystems and offers a unified lens for understanding brain architecture and the etiology of brain disease; furthermore, it may inform model designs for artificial intelligence.

Título: KAPI-LM: kernel-adaptive physics-informed learning machines for PDEs.
Resumen: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as mesh-free approaches for solving partial differential equations, but their learned representations are often difficult to interpret. RBF-kernel-based formulations such as sparse, physics-based, and interpretable neural networks (SPINNs) make the geometry of the physical kernels explicit and show that kernels adapt coherently around dominant solution features, motivating the question of whether all kernel geometries need to remain independent. To investigate this question, we introduce kernel-adaptive physics-informed learning machines (KAPI-LMs), a general framework for solving PDEs with structured RBF representations in which a large physical kernel dictionary is organized through a smaller set of geometric variables while retaining all physical kernels and independent expansion coefficients. The resulting hypothesis class provides explicit control over the degree of geometric sharing and can be combined with different physics-informed learning strategies. To demonstrate this flexibility, we develop compressed SPINN (cSPINN) using joint geometry-coefficient optimization, compressed physics-informed extreme learning machine (cPIELM) using variable projection for coefficient-linear PDEs, and Meta-cSPINN using task-conditioned learning for parametric PDEs. We establish approximation guarantees and quantify the effect of geometric sharing. Numerical studies across linear, nonlinear, parametric, coupled, and multiscale PDEs demonstrate substantial geometric compression at fixed physical basis resolution and reveal problem-dependent limits to sharing. They also show that different optimization strategies can discover markedly different geometries within the same hypothesis class. For parametric PDEs, Meta-cSPINN supports one-shot prediction and suggests additional organization across solution families, while PDE residuals identify where geometric sharing should be released or local resolution added. KAPI-LM thus provides a physics-informed PDE-solving framework in which geometric complexity is explicit and controllable, allowing the solution representation to be interpreted, compressed, and adaptively refined according to the physics.

Título: JTCSE: Joint tensor-modulus constraints and cross-attention for unsupervised contrastive learning of sentence embeddings.

Título: Leveraging AI and Machine Vision in Telephysiotherapy for Promoting Physical Activity and Reducing Sedentary Behavior: Scoping Review.

This scoping review aimed to map and systematize current evidence on the use of AI and machine vision in telephysiotherapy to promote PA and reduce sedentary behavior among healthy adults. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and was reported according to the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Título: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity.
Resumen: A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation. A powerful framework for understanding neural computation uses neural dynamics - the rules that govern how neural activity evolves over time - to explain how goal-directed input-output transformations occur. As dynamical rules are not directly observable, we need computational models that can infer neural dynamics from recorded neural activity. We typically validate such models using synthetic datasets with known ground-truth dynamics, but unfortunately existing synthetic datasets don't reflect fundamental features of neural computation and may therefore be poor proxies for neural systems. Further, the field lacks validated metrics for quantifying the accuracy of the dynamics inferred by models. The Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit (CtDToolkit) addresses these critical gaps by providing: 1) synthetic datasets that reflect computational properties of biological neural circuits, 2) interpretable metrics for quantifying model performance, and 3) a standardized pipeline for training and evaluating models with or without known external inputs. In this manuscript, we demonstrate how CtDToolkit can help guide the development, tuning, and troubleshooting of neural dynamics models. In summary, CtDToolkit provides a necessary framework for model developers to better understand and characterize neural computation through the lens of dynamics.

Título: Changing contributions of emotion and reward information to learning through adolescence.
Resumen: From childhood to adulthood, individuals' learning and decision-making may be differentially impacted by two salient value signals for adolescents: emotions and rewards. Título: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the "oxide gatekeeper" in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation.
Resumen: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

The porosity parameter decreases the velocity of fluid by approximately 12%, whereas the modified Hartmann number increases the fluid velocity by 15-17%. Additionally, SWCNTs exhibit 8-10% higher thermal conductivity compared to MWCNTs. The ANN-LMBP model demonstrates excellent predictive performance with a coefficient of determination R<sup>2</sup> > 0.998 and a mean squared error on the order of 10<sup>-4</sup>. These results confirm that the proposed ANN-based framework is a fast, accurate, and computationally efficient tool for modeling nonlinear thermal fluid systems, with significant applications in thermal management, cooling technologies, energy systems, and industrial fluid flow processes.Clinical trial number not applicable.

Título: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with survival outcomes via a deep survival learner.
Resumen: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects in survival settings is complicated by right censoring as well as the time-varying nature of the estimand. While the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) provides a natural target, most existing approaches focus on a single prespecified time point and do not account for temporal trajectory, leading to instability in estimation. We propose a deep survival learner (DSL) for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with right-censored outcomes. The method is based on a doubly robust pseudo-outcome whose conditional expectation identifies time-specific CATEs under standard assumptions. This construction remains unbiased if either the outcome model or the treatment assignment model is correctly specified, when properly accounting for censoring. To estimate CATEs over a clinically relevant time spectrum, DSL employs a multi-output deep neural network with shared representations, enabling joint estimation of treatment effect trajectories. From a theoretical perspective, we derive error bounds for both pointwise and joint estimation over time. We show that joint estimation can leverage temporal structure to control estimation error without incurring much additional approximation cost under smoothness conditions, leading to improved stability relative to separate estimation. Cross-fitting is incorporated to reduce overfitting and mitigate bias arising from flexible nuisance estimation. Simulation studies demonstrate favorable finite-sample performance, particularly under nuisance model misspecification. Applied to the Boston Lung Cancer Study, DSL reveals heterogeneity in the effects of perioperative chemotherapy across patient characteristics and over time.

Título: Development and Exploratory Evaluation of a Large Language Model-Supported Scoping Review Workflow.
Resumen: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated human-level performance in literature review screening phases and have been evaluated in systematic-review workflows. Título: Exploring the Application of Machine Learning for Daily-Life Near-Fall Detection in Older Adults.
Resumen: Falls are a health concern among older adults, and near-falls may serve as an early indicator of future falls, functional decline, and the need for targeted preventive interventions. Data from the SeFallED study was used, which followed up on individuals aged ≥ 60 years who presented to the emergency department following a fall. Título: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
Resumen: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total <i>N</i> = 6,584). Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. Título: Best subset selection meets resampling: tackling selection instability at very low numbers of events per variable.
Resumen: Trust is a basic necessity for translating machine learning models from bench to bedside. Título: DiFVM: A Vectorized Graph-Based Finite Volume Solver for Differentiable CFD on Unstructured Meshes.
Resumen: Differentiable programming has emerged as an important tool for gradient-based inverse problems and end-to-end hybrid physics-machine learning in computational fluid dynamics. Forward accuracy is assessed through analytical and canonical benchmark problems, comparisons with published reference data, and independent solver comparisons, while end-to-end differentiability is demonstrated through proof-of-concept inverse modeling examples. DiFVM provides a differentiable CFD framework for gradient-based optimization, inverse modeling and future physics-integrated machine learning on complex unstructured geometries.

Título: Exploratory microbiota-metabolite alterations associated with cognitive impairment after repeated low-dose sevoflurane exposure in mice.
Resumen: Repeated low-dose sevoflurane exposure may affect cognition, but the relationship between such exposure, gut microbial composition, and circulating metabolites remains unclear. This study examined an experimental proof-of-concept exposure model and treated microbiota-metabolite findings as exploratory associations. Mice were exposed to 100 ppm sevoflurane for 2 h/day over 7 consecutive days, followed by Morris water maze testing without a long-term recovery follow-up. Gut microbiota and serum metabolites were profiled by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and LC-MS metabolomics, respectively, and machine-learning analyses were used only for exploratory feature ranking. Sevoflurane-exposed mice exhibited poorer Morris water maze performance (Day 6 escape latency: 28.6 ± 3.4 s vs. 12.5 ± 1.8 s in controls, p < 0.01), although interpretation is limited by unequal behavioral sample sizes. Serum metabolomics suggested nominal and exploratory alterations in bile acid- and sphingolipid-related pathways. Shotgun metagenomics (n = 3/group) identified preliminary relative-abundance shifts, including a lower <i>Bacteroidota/Bacillota</i> ratio and lower relative abundance of <i>Akkermansia</i>. In this proof-of-concept model, repeated low-dose sevoflurane exposure was associated with impaired spatial learning and memory and with exploratory serum metabolic and gut microbial alterations. The findings do not establish persistent long-term deficits, routine occupational risk, or causal microbiota-metabolite mediation. Larger cage-aware studies, an ambient-air comparison group, targeted validation, and interventional experiments are required.


--- ARTÍCULO 3610 ---
ID (PMID): 42877094
Título: Beyond detection: developing probabilistic hemodynamic phenotyping after a positive point-of-care pulmonary hypertension test.
Resumen: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a heterogeneous condition in which hemodynamic subtype directs management and specialist referral. PH can be identified non-invasively at the point of care by a previously developed, regulatory-cleared machine-learned diagnostic (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.95, sensitivity 82%, specificity 92%), but a positive test result raises a second clinical question: which patients have pre-capillary disease and therefore warrant referral to a specialist PH center. A probabilistic post-test phenotyping model was developed to estimate hemodynamic subtype probabilities and support rule-out of pre-capillary PH among test-positive patients. Subjects with right heart catheterization (RHC)-confirmed PH [mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) ≥25 mmHg] enrolled in a prospective multisite trial (NCT04031989) who tested positive on the previously validated point-of-care PH diagnostic formed the analysis cohort (<i>n</i> = 139). Hemodynamic subtypes were assigned per 2015 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) criteria. A one-vs.-one (OvO) Gaussian mixture model (GMM) framework, combining unsupervised clustering with <i>post hoc</i> supervised assignment of subtype probabilities was applied to features derived from non-invasive orthogonal voltage gradient and photoplethysmographic signals to generate subject-level subtype probability estimates. Blinded validation in a large dataset has not yet been performed; development results are reported, supported by a small blinded independent dataset. At an exemplar <i>post-hoc</i> rule-out threshold of 16% pre-capillary probability, the GMM OvO approach yielded sensitivity 86% (95% CI: 71%-95%), specificity 51% (95% CI: 41%-61%), negative predictive value 88% (95% CI: 73%-96%) at an assumed pre-capillary prevalence of 34%, and a negative likelihood ratio (LR-) of 0.27 (95% CI: 0.07-0.70) on the development cohort. Supportive out-of-sample discrimination was observed in the blinded independent cohort. A GMM OvO probabilistic model applied to non-invasive point-of-care signals can generate PH subtype probability estimates and may support rule-out of pre-capillary disease among true-positive patients. The model reuses signals already acquired for PH detection and can therefore be implemented as a software addition to an existing point-of-care workflow. Independent blinded validation is required to comprehensively characterize model performance.

Título: The predictive value of machine learning for the response to anti-TNF-α therapy in patients with Crohn's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Resumen: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of machine learning (ML) in predicting the response to anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) therapy in individuals with Crohn's disease (CD), providing an evidence-based basis for the construction or update of prediction tools. PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science were comprehensively searched for studies published up to November 18, 2025 on ML predictive models for the therapeutic response to anti-TNF treatment in individuals with CD. The Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used to assess the risk of bias in the eligible articles. Model performance was assessed using the concordance index (C-index), and a meta-analysis was conducted. A total of 29 studies involving 6,697 patients with CD were included. Of these studies, 22 focused on the response to anti-TNF-α therapy, 6 on mucosal healing, and 1 on other outcomes. The meta-analysis demonstrated that for predicting the treatment response to anti-TNF-α treatment, in the validation dataset, the C-indices were 0.762 for ML models based on clinical features (CFs), 0.852 for models based on radiomic features, and 0.854 for models based on CFs combined with radiomic features. In internal validation, the C-indices for models based on CFs, radiomics, and CFs combined with radiomics were 0.773 (95% CI: 0.711-0.841), 0.840 (95% CI: 0.781-0.904), and 0.830 (95% CI: 0.780-0.883), respectively. In the external validation set, models based on radiomics (0.865, 95% CI: 0.783-0.955) and models based on CFs combined with radiomics (0.883, 95% CI: 0.816-0.955) outperformed models based on CFs (0.733, 95% CI: 0.645-0.833). Furthermore, the C-index of models based on endoscopic mucosal response was 0.794. hile ML shows promise in predicting the therapeutic effects of anti-TNF-α treatment in individuals with CD, there are some methodological limitations. Future research should integrate multi-center, geographically diverse datasets to enhance the generalizability of models. Improving model robustness will help identify non-responders early, ultimately promoting the development of personalized therapeutic strategies and precision medicine. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251276470.

ID (PMID): 42877037
Título: Machine learning prediction of deep vein thrombosis before staged surgery in lower-leg and ankle fractures treated with temporary external fixation.
Resumen: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) detected between temporary external fixation and staged definitive surgery can complicate perioperative management of lower-leg and ankle fractures. We developed machine-learning models to estimate DVT probability during this interval. This retrospective cohort included adults admitted during 2015-2025 who underwent staged fixation and bilateral lower-extremity venous ultrasonography. A stratified 70:30 split defined development and validation sets. Development-set imputation, Boruta feature selection, and five-fold cross-validation were used to develop 12 classifiers. Algorithms were compared in the validation set. The selected Naive Bayes pipeline underwent 500 development-cohort bootstrap replications for optimism correction. Discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, and decision curves were evaluated. SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) and a bilingual research prototype web application supported interpretation. Among 356 patients, 55 (15.4%) had DVT, including 40 with calf muscular vein thrombosis. The development and validation sets comprised 250 patients (39 events) and 106 patients (16 events). Boruta retained nine predictors. Naive Bayes had the highest validation receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC), 0.807 (95% confidence interval, 0.705-0.909). Precision-recall AUC was 0.343, sensitivity was 0.875, and specificity was 0.589. Beta calibration reduced the Brier score from 0.135 to 0.116 without changing discrimination. The apparent AUC was 0.858, mean bootstrap optimism was 0.084, and optimism-corrected AUC was 0.773. Injury-to-admission time, calcium, age, platelet count, fibrinogen, and hemoglobin had the largest mean absolute SHAP values. The model may support risk stratification for an ultrasound-detected composite DVT endpoint in this staged-treatment population. Its proposed use is to inform surveillance timing and intensity while retaining routine bilateral ultrasonography. Prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

ID (PMID): 42877016
Título: Multimodal biomarkers and prediction models for stricturing and penetrating progression in Crohn's disease.
Resumen: Crohn's disease can progress from non-stricturing, non-penetrating inflammation (B1) to stricturing (B2) or penetrating (B3) complications, yet risk is commonly recognized only after structural damage is established. This narrative review examines clinical, endoscopic, genomic, circulating, stool, tissue, imaging, radiomic, and computational biomarkers relevant to behavioral-progression risk and separates direct B1-to-B2 or source-defined B3 evidence from related prognostic and mechanistic evidence, while distinguishing internal penetrating from perianal fistulizing disease when source reporting permits. Structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation tracking, informed the selection of longitudinal human studies, prediction models, and mechanistic studies relevant to candidate feature selection. Ileal involvement, perianal fistulizing disease, persistent inflammatory burden, and endoscopic severity provide reproducible risk enrichment but insufficient individual-level precision. Genomic scores, plasma and stool proteins, tissue transcriptomics, shear-wave elastography, radiomics, and machine-learning models suggest potential value for multimodal risk stratification, but most lack independent external validation, calibration, transportability, and demonstrated incremental value over routinely available clinical variables. Direct prospective evidence is substantially more developed for B2 stricturing progression than for incident internal B3 penetrating progression; internal penetrating disease and perianal fistulizing disease are treated as distinct outcomes. Mechanistic studies suggest divergent fibrostenotic and tissue-destructive programs that provide biological guidance for biomarker selection. No biomarker or multimodal model identified in this review was ready to support routine biomarker-guided treatment escalation. Future studies should use well-characterized B1 baselines, prespecified structural outcomes, and prospective decision-impact testing that quantifies overtreatment.

ID (PMID): 42876976
Título: Pangenomic and machine learning approaches to divergent pathogenic strategies in avian <i>Mycoplasma</i> species: evidence and limitations.
Resumen: Avian mycoplasmosis, mainly caused by <i>Mycoplasma gallisepticum</i> (MG), <i>Mycoplasma synoviae</i> (MS), and <i>Mycoplasma gallinarum</i> (MGn), remains a persistent constraint on poultry production. These species co-circulate in flocks but differ in tissue tropism, host responses, and clinical outcomes. This review examines how pangenomic analysis and machine learning (ML)-based feature prioritization can clarify these differences while separating computational associations from experimentally supported mechanisms. We first summarize genome reduction, structural variation, accessory gene content, and antimicrobial resistance architecture, and then evaluate ML applications in classification, feature selection, network inference, and candidate prioritization. The evidence is strongest for MG, which combines respiratory adhesion, TLR2/MyD88/NF-κB-mediated inflammation, NLRP3 activation, and oxidative injury. MS appears more synovium-adapted, with evidence of fibroblast reprogramming, ER stress-related responses, and interference with antiviral signaling. MGn remains insufficiently characterized because complete reference genomes, standardized infection models, and functional validation data are lacking. We conclude that pangenomics and machine learning are useful only when linked to validation: They can define candidate repertoires and rank testable hypotheses, but they do not establish pathogenic mechanisms. A controlled three-species comparison and a complete, well-annotated MGn reference genome are the most immediate priorities for addressing the gaps that currently prevent confident cross-species comparison.

ID (PMID): 42876975
Título: An innovative framework based on GMV-ALFF multi-modal MRI and Gaussian data augmentation for psychiatric disorder classification.
Resumen: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit significant overlap in clinical symptoms, posing substantial challenges to accurate diagnosis. This study proposes an innovative multi-modal fusion framework based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), integrating structural and functional MRI biomarkers-gray matter volume (GMV) and amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF). Total 31 patients with schizophrenia, 48 patients with bipolar disorder, and 38 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled and underwent resting-state fMRI scans. The framework comprises three core components: Gaussian data augmentation to mitigate the limitation of small sample sizes; a dedicated CNN architecture for processing GMV and ALFF features to generate class probability outputs for SZ, BD, and HC; and DempsterShafer (D-S) evidence theory for robust multi-modal decision fusion. Extensive 5-fold cross-validation confirms the framework's efficacy: it achieves superior performance metrics (Accuracy: 0.9656 ± 0.0324, Precision: 0.9698 ± 0.0319, Recall: 0.9656 ± 0.0324, F1-Score: 0.9661 ± 0.0324) and outperforms traditional machine learning methods (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, KNN). The findings demonstrate that the proposed multi-modal fusion approach enhances the ability to differentiate among SZ, BD, and HC compared to unimodal classification methods, providing a reliable technical support for the auxiliary diagnosis of psychiatric disorders.

ID (PMID): 42876973
Título: AI and the future of teachers: predicting stakeholders' expectations of teacher job loss from AI-related institutional conditions.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming educational work, although claims that it will replace teachers often overlook the institutional conditions that make teacher job loss appear more or less likely. This study examined whether current AI-related institutional risk conditions predict stakeholder expectations of teacher job loss over the next decade. A purposive sample of 300 education and AI stakeholders rated the extent to which 11 conditions were currently present and provided a separate 0-10 score indicating the extent to which they expected AI to contribute to teacher job loss. Overall job-loss expectations were low to moderate, and the institutional AI condition indicators showed good internal consistency. The machine learning model showed good predictive performance in the original held-out test set (<i>R</i> <sup>2</sup> = 0.683) and stable performance across 100 repeated train-test splits (mean <i>R</i> <sup>2</sup> = 0.598). The explainable AI analysis showed that the strongest contribution band consisted of automated feedback, large-scale AI adoption, and standardized content delivery. The findings suggest that the extent to which stakeholders perceive AI-related institutional risk conditions to be currently present in educational settings is associated with the extent of teacher job loss they expect. They further indicate that this risk is not an inevitable technological outcome, but is embedded in a broader institutional ecology, with expectations clustering more strongly around direct forms of AI-mediated instructional restructuring than around indirect institutional or governance-related vulnerabilities.

ID (PMID): 42876971
Título: Functional magnetic resonance imaging in neuropathic pain: a bibliometric analysis incorporating machine learning.
Resumen: Neuropathic pain (NP) affects 6.9%-10% of the global population. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has become central to NP investigation, yet few studies have systematically mapped this literature. We used bibliometric and machine-learning methods to chart the fMRI-NP research landscape. We retrieved 1,866 fMRI-NP articles (2005-2025) from Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus. Following PRISMA guidelines, we analyzed publication trends, citation metrics, and collaborative networks with CiteSpace and VOSviewer, complemented by exploratory topic modeling based on term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) and non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), and by community detection combining GraphSAGE node embeddings with density-based spatial clustering (DBSCAN). The corpus amassed 94,160 citations, with an average of 50.46 per article and a corpus h-index of 139. Annual output rose from 35 articles in 2005 to 156 in 2025, following a power-law trend (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.862). The United States and China were the most productive countries. Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital were the most prolific institutions. NeuroImage and Pain were the most productive journals, and NeuroImage, the Journal of Neuroscience, and Pain were the most frequently co-cited. Text-mining of titles and abstracts indicated that stimulus-evoked activation, brain-connectivity/default-mode, and post-herpetic/regional themes were the most prevalent, with the limbic and sensorimotor systems the most frequently mentioned pathways. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric mapping of the fMRI-NP research landscape, characterizing its growth trajectory, the most productive countries, institutions and journals, the most co-cited references, and the recurrent themes in the literature. The mapping indicates increasing attention to brain connectivity, multimodal imaging, and computational text analysis. These bibliometric patterns delineate active and emerging areas of research activity and may help orient future literature-based inquiry and collaboration in the field.

ID (PMID): 42876947
Título: AI-enabled and comparator digital interventions for adolescent mental health (2020-2025): early detection, human-AI collaboration, and ethical governance-a PRISMA-ScR scoping review.
Resumen: Mental health difficulties among adolescents and youth (ages 10-24) are increasing globally, yet early intervention remains impeded by stigma, service shortages, and cultural barriers. AI-enabled technologies including chatbots, automated screening tools, and machine learning-based predictive models have been proposed as scalable approaches to address these gaps, alongside non-AI digital interventions such as therapist-guided internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) and smartphone-based CBT applications, which are examined as comparator evidence given their stronger controlled-design evidence base. This scoping review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) reporting guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. A systematic database search across six databases (PubMed, Scopus, ProQuest, SpringerLink, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect), supplemented by manual and forward-citation searching, yielded 10,962 records, of which 19 studies met the predefined inclusion criteria. A Human-AI Collaboration Role framework comprising a four-level continuum from fully human-led to fully automated delivery was applied as a predefined coding dimension across all included studies. Most studies focused on depression and anxiety among mid-to-late adolescents in high-income countries (68.4%). Therapist-guided iCBT was the most rigorously studied format using randomized and controlled designs; AI chatbots, predictive models, and large language model (LLM)-based systems demonstrated feasibility or engagement outcomes in a limited number of studies and contexts, though randomized diagnostic chatbot trials specifically remain absent for participants under 18 years; at least one randomized non-diagnostic chatbot trial (a body-image intervention) has been conducted in this age group. Equity-related reporting was inconsistent: socioeconomic status was reported in only 10.5% of studies and cultural adaptation in 42.1%; restriction to English-language publications may further underrepresent non-Western and low- and middle-income-country evidence relevant to these equity findings. Key implementation challenges included inconsistent safeguarding protocols for minors, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and insufficient integration with clinical and educational systems. The evidence base remains preliminary and methodologically heterogeneous, insufficient to support conclusions about clinical effectiveness or generalizability to diverse adolescent populations. These findings represent a descriptive map of the current evidence landscape rather than an assessment of effectiveness. Future research should prioritize adequately powered adolescent-focused trials, participatory co-design approaches, culturally informed adaptations, and transparent ethical governance frameworks to ensure responsible development of AI-enabled digital mental health tools for youth. Because the included studies were heterogeneous and no formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken, this review does not establish comparative clinical effectiveness, safety, or superiority of AI-enabled interventions. https://osf.io/sbpk2, doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/SBPK2.

Título: Machine learning-based screening for Ascertain Dementia 8-defined suspected cognitive impairment leveraging routine health check data in South China.
Resumen: Timely detection of cognitive concerns can facilitate further assessment, referral, and management; however, cognitive impairment often remains under-detected in primary care settings, representing a missed opportunity for early detection for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. We aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning-based cross-sectional concurrent classification model that utilizes routine health check data only, supporting concurrent identification of individuals with Ascertain Dementia 8 (AD8)-defined suspected cognitive impairment who warrant further clinical cognitive evaluation. This cross-sectional study included 7440 adults (aged ≥65 years) from the 2021 Elderly Health Check Program in Shenzhen, China. Suspected cognitive impairment was defined as an AD8 score ≥2. At the clinically optimized threshold of 0.034, the model achieved a sensitivity of 60.6%, a specificity of 73.4% and a NNS of 51.9. DCA indicated a positive net benefit across a threshold range approximately from 0.03 to 0.20, suggesting potential clinical utility for triage in this setting. This cross-sectional model provides a pragmatic, low-cost tool for concurrent case-finding of individuals with AD8-defined suspected cognitive impairment in primary care. However, further external validation in diverse geographic regions is mandatory before clinical implementation.

ID (PMID): 42876942
Título: Benchmarking deep learning-based reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography with clinically relevant synthetic datasets.
Resumen: Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality (IQ) metrics that may lack clinical relevance. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT. A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT. The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods. The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments. The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.

Título: Identifying influential environmental drivers of Alzheimer's disease at the county level using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence.
Resumen: Alzheimer's disease (AD) prevalence varies substantially across United States (US) counties, yet the combined influence of environmental and socioeconomic factors remains incompletely characterized. This study bridges this gap by employing machine learning combined with explainable artificial intelligence to identify and interpret key environmental drivers of AD prevalence across US counties. Utilizing county-level AD prevalence data linked with comprehensive environmental and socioeconomic indicators, we applied an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regression framework. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to evaluate global and local feature contributions. The final model demonstrated stable performance (RMSE: 0.89 ± 0.04; R<sup>2</sup>: 0.62 ± 0.03). Among 15 selected factors, chloride precipitation and median household value emerged as the most influential predictors. Additional significant drivers included land-use metrics (open land, walkability), atmospheric deposition, and localized industrial exposures. SHAP analysis revealed nonlinear, threshold-like increases in predicted AD prevalence at higher chloride levels, while geographic mapping identified regionally distinct exposure profiles. Geospatial analysis and explainable AI demonstrate that AD prevalence is driven by interacting environmental toxicants and socioeconomic disadvantages. This "exposome" perspective highlights that mitigating environmental hazards and systemic inequities is critical for reducing the neurodegenerative disease burden.

Título: Lung cancer classification and severity estimation using vision transformer-IPCNN with enhanced U-Net segmentation.
Resumen: The death rate due to lung cancer is increasing because of late detection. Several automated lung cancer diagnostic techniques based on Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have been developed for early detection. However, existing methods have limitations, including higher false-positive rates, lower sensitivity, and greater time consumption, which can affect early lung cancer diagnosis. To address these limitations, the Lung Cancer Classification and Severity Estimation-Improved Parallel Convolutional Neural Network-Vision Transformer (LCCSE-IPCNN-ViT) model is proposed. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed LCCSE-IPCNN-ViT model provides accurate and efficient lung cancer classification and severity estimation, indicating its potential for supporting early lung cancer diagnosis.

Título: Comprehensive Molecular Profiling for Precision Diagnostics: Integrating Genomic, Proteomic, and Epigenetic Landscapes in Human Pathology.
Resumen: Comprehensive molecular characterization may enhance diagnostic assessment in complex human diseases by capturing biological heterogeneity beyond conventional single-layer approaches. This review examines the integration of genomic, proteomic, and epigenetic profiling for precision diagnostics and clinical interpretation. Major advances include comprehensive genomic characterization, high-throughput proteomic profiling, clinically informative epigenetic biomarkers, machine-learning-assisted data integration, and single-cell and spatial multiomics for resolving cellular and tissue-level heterogeneity. Evidence across diverse disease models indicates that integrated molecular data may enhance biomarker identification and provide additional information for disease classification, prognostic assessment, and prediction of therapeutic response; however, comparative measures of diagnostic performance are not consistently available. Future priorities should focus on harmonized analytical standards, reproducible pipelines, scalable computational infrastructure, improved model interpretability, robust clinical validation, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration across oncology, rare genetic disorders, neurodegenerative disease, and other clinically heterogeneous conditions in routine practice. Integrative molecular profiling therefore represents a major direction for next-generation diagnostics, with its potential clinical value depending on analytical validation, clinical validity and utility, reproducible implementation, and prospective comparison with established diagnostic pathways.

Resumen: Anemia represents a frequent and clinically burdensome complication in patients with primary lung cancer receiving platinum-based regimens, yet robust risk stratification tools that integrate multidimensional clinical data and undergo external validation remain scarce. Título: Performance of large language models in postoperative hip fracture rehabilitation counseling for older adults: a comparative evaluation of safety, accuracy, reliability, readability, and empathy.
Resumen: To compare the performance of five widely used large language models in answering public questions about postoperative rehabilitation after hip fracture in older adults, focusing on safety, accuracy, reliability, readability, empathy, and overall information quality. This cross-sectional comparative evaluation used a 42-question bank addressing general postoperative rehabilitation after proximal femoral fracture treated with internal fixation or hip arthroplasty. All questions and the standardized safety-oriented prompt were submitted in English, and all responses were returned and analyzed in their original English form without translation. Between May 1 and May 10, 2026, each question was submitted once to five generative artificial intelligence-driven chatbots through their official public interfaces, yielding 210 responses. LLMs may serve only as supervised adjunctive educational tools, with outputs framed as complementary to procedure-specific professional care.

A total of 648 sepsis patients with T2DM admitted to Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital between January 2020 and October 2024 were included in this retrospective cohort study, an internal validation cohort of 303 patients was retrospectively collected from Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital between November 2024 and December 2025, and an independent external validation cohort of 260 patients was retrospectively collected from Xi'an No. 3 Hospital (a separate tertiary care center) between November 2023 and December 2025. Six machine learning algorithms-Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest-were developed and compared. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm combined with forward sequential feature selection. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC), calibration (calibratin plots and Brier scores), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Model interpretability was enhanced using SHAP analysis. Among the 648 internal patients, 115 (17.7%) developed VTE. The Boruta algorithm and forward sequential feature selection identified five key predictors: D-dimer, C-reactive protein (CRP), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), international normalized ratio (INR), and fibrin degradation products (FDP). Among the six algorithms, LightGBM achieved the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.9025 in the test set, 0.8048 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.8902 in the external validation cohort. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis confirmed positive net clinical benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis revealed that elevated D-dimer, CRP, INR, and FDP, together with shortened APTT, were the strongest drivers of VTE risk. Sensitivity analyses excluding D-dimer-driven cases, removing the D-dimer feature, and restricting to symptomatic VTE yielded consistent results (AUC range: 0.84-0.89). The LightGBM model incorporating five readily available coagulation and inflammatory markers accurately predicts in-hospital VTE in sepsis patients with T2DM, with robust discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. SHAP-based interpretability enhances transparency and may facilitate personalized risk stratification and informed thromboprophylaxis decisions in this high-risk population.

This study aims to predict end-of-season team points using Serie A data from the 2015-2025 period and to generate forward-looking performance forecasts for the 2026 season. The study combines financial, sporting, and managerial variables within a Bayesian machine learning framework and compares different statistical and machine learning methods for football performance prediction. Nine independent variables were included in the analysis: squad market value, previous season points, net transfer expenditure, number of new transfers, managerial change, proportion of foreign players, average age, Serie A experience, and participation in UEFA competitions. Variable importance was evaluated using the Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) approach. Linear Regression, Elastic Net, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) models were applied and compared using MAE, RMSE, and R<sup>2</sup> performance measures. The BMA results showed that squad market value, managerial change, and participation in UEFA competitions were the most important variables associated with team performance. Among all prediction models, the BART model achieved the best predictive performance, with the lowest error level (RMSE = 7.28) and the highest explanatory power (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.863). In addition, an ensemble forecasting approach was used to provide a more balanced interpretation of model uncertainty. Forecasts for 2026 suggest that teams with high squad value and technical stability, particularly Inter, are expected to occupy the top positions in the league standings. The findings indicate that financial structure, managerial stability, and participation in European competitions play an important role in football performance. Overall, the study demonstrates that Bayesian and machine learning-based approaches can provide effective results in football performance prediction. The proposed framework may contribute to the literature on football performance analysis and provide useful insights for strategic planning and performance management in professional football clubs.
