Título: A multi-model LLM framework for AI-assisted psychological scale development: initial psychometric evaluation of the Emotion Regulation Scale (ERS).
Resumen: Emotion regulation is a key construct in mental health, yet existing measures differ in conceptual coverage, with some focusing on specific strategies or regulatory difficulties rather than broader cognitive, behavioral, and contextual regulation processes. This study aimed to develop an Emotion Regulation Scale (ERS) grounded in Gross's Process Model, using large language models (LLMs) as assistive tools within an established psychometric framework. This cross-sectional study included 743 adults recruited through convenience sampling. Participants were randomly divided into two non-overlapping subsamples, one used for exploratory factor analysis and the other for confirmatory factor analysis. Multiple LLMs and AI-based tools assisted with item generation, refinement and bias screening, translation, and post-EFA construct interpretation, with human oversight throughout development. An initial pool of 25 items was generated and refined to produce the final 17-item ERS. The ERS revealed a preliminary four-factor structure, with EFA explaining 50.85% of the variance. CFA provided preliminary support for a post hoc refined 17-item model (χ²/df = 1.95, CFI = 0.934, TLI = 0.918, IFI = 0.935, RMSEA = 0.050). Known-groups validity indicated significant differences across depression and anxiety levels (MCR: F(4, 738) = 39.32; 64.49, p < 0.001). The findings provide preliminary psychometric evidence for the 17-item ERS and suggest that it may complement existing measures by capturing broader cognitive, behavioral, and contextual emotion regulation processes. The study illustrates the potential for LLM-assisted scale development within established psychometric procedures and human oversight. Further research using diverse samples is needed to evaluate the scale's psychometric properties, generalizability, and broader utility.

Título: Mismatch between urban eco-sanitation improvement and health service supply capacity: evidence from Chinese city panel data and interpretable machine learning.
Resumen: Health service supply capacity depends not only on medical resource stocks but also on urban eco-sanitation conditions and resource-allocation mechanisms. Existing studies focus mainly on environmental exposure and health outcomes, with limited attention to whether eco-sanitation improvements can be converted into health service supply capacity. This study constructed a panel of Chinese prefecture-level and above cities for 2002-2024, using the health service supply capacity index as the dependent variable and the eco-sanitation environment index as the core explanatory variable. Two-way fixed effects models, dimension-specific analysis, mechanism tests, heterogeneity analysis, robustness checks, and interpretable machine learning identified mismatch mechanisms and boundary conditions. The mechanism analysis was extended to two- and three-year ESE lags and one- and two-year lagged investment variables. Carbon-emission comparability was reassessed on exact CEADs-matched samples for 2002-2019. Hu Huanyong line subgroup models were additionally estimated with city and province-year fixed effects. The eco-sanitation environment, green infrastructure, and municipal sanitation facilities improved continuously, whereas health service supply capacity increased more slowly. The baseline model does not support a stable positive conversion from eco-sanitation improvement to stronger supply capacity. Dimension-specific results reveal differentiated roles. The positive PPI coefficient must not be read as a pollution benefit; it is consistent with a demand-induced or compensatory resource-allocation response. Neither two- to three-year ESE lags nor one- to two-year lagged investment variables produced a stable urban construction investment transmission chain. The positive CEADs interaction was confirmed only within the 2002-2019 matched sample and therefore represents pre-pandemic evidence. The southeastern Hu-line coefficient attenuated and lost conventional significance after province-year policy shocks were absorbed. Machine learning indicates the relationship is shaped by development stage, population size, fiscal capacity, and nonlinear boundaries. Eco-sanitation improvement is not a sufficient condition for enhancing health service supply capacity. Healthy city development should integrate eco-sanitation governance, infrastructure investment, workforce allocation, and fiscal arrangements into a unified governance framework. Because HSC is a supply-side proxy based on resource counts, these implications concern resource availability and network density rather than quality of care, realized utilization, accessibility, or overall health-system performance.

Título: Machine learning model for the prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

Through the combination of imaging and clinicopathological features, our machine learning model shows a promising approach to improve the prediction of pCR in breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant treatment. Título: Predicting Hospital-associated complications in older adults: methodological considerations.
Resumen: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict post-surgical complications, but predictive performance does not guarantee clinical readiness. Shimizu and colleagues developed a promising model for older adults undergoing tibial fracture surgery using a large Japanese database. However, four methodological pitfalls warrant attention. First, the composite outcome was not validated in this population, and excluding in-hospital deaths introduced survivorship bias, underestimating the true burden of severe complications. Second, days to surgery, a variable not known at admission, created target leakage that inflates performance and undermines the admission-time claim. Third, using the test set for feature selection violated TRIPOD guidelines and likely overstated the scorecard's utility. Fourth, the Super Learner exhibited substantial overfitting, with a 0.110 drop between training (AUC = 0.850) and test (AUC = 0.740) performance, while offering only marginal improvement over simpler models. We suggest redeveloping the model with proper internal validation, excluding leakage-prone predictors, treating death as a competing risk, and prioritizing interpretability when complex ensembles offer limited added value. External validation remains essential before clinical implementation.

Título: Development and external validation of an AI pipeline for automated estimation of a radiographic DMFT (rDMFT) score from panoramic radiographs: a feasibility study.
Resumen: To assess the feasibility of estimating a radiographic Decayed-Missing-Filled-Teeth score (rDMFT), a proxy for the clinical DMFT index, from a single panoramic radiograph with a position-aware deep-learning pipeline. A tooth-status detector and a tooth-numbering detector (32 FDI positions), trained on DENTEX 2023, were combined in a position-aware read-out (one tooth per FDI position, third molars excluded, missing teeth = 28 - occupied positions) and validated on 100 panoramic radiographs from an independent hospital against a two-dentist, radiograph-based reference (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC; mean absolute error, MAE; Bland-Altman analysis). Against the reference, the pipeline reached an ICC of 0.84 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.90) and an MAE of 2.38, below the between-dentist agreement in point estimate (ICC 0.88, MAE 2.13), with larger errors against each dentist alone (MAE 3.00 and 2.73) and a bias of + 1.14 units from caries over-detection; agreement was highest for filled (r 0.90) and lowest for decayed teeth (r 0.34; dentists 0.16). In the 26 radiographs with missing teeth the missing count was exact in 42% (62% within ± 1 tooth), and missing teeth were over-called in 15 of 74 complete dentitions; tooth loss was no longer overlooked (26 of 26 detected), but the overall ICC was 0.84 versus 0.90 without numbering. Automated rDMFT estimation is feasible, but agreement was lower in point estimate than between two dentists, with larger errors against each dentist. The missing component now responds to actual tooth loss but remains imprecise and is over-called in some complete dentitions; the decayed component is unreliable. The pipeline is a research building block, not a decision-support or triage tool. rDMFT is a radiographic proxy, not a clinical measure, and the pipeline is not proposed for clinical use; any application would first require validation in unselected cohorts against clinically determined reference standards.

Título: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation.
Resumen: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology<sup>1,2</sup>. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes<sup>1,3,4</sup>. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

Título: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning.
Resumen: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes<sup>1-3</sup>. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models<sup>4-10</sup>. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2-6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere<sup>11-15</sup>. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System<sup>16</sup> and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model<sup>17</sup> for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF<sup>18</sup>, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities<sup>19</sup>.

Título: Improving coupled cluster theory for strongly correlated molecules with Kohn-Sham density encoding.
Resumen: Coupled cluster theory using a Kohn-Sham density functional reference can dramatically outperform the standard Hartree-Fock-based approach for strongly correlated systems, but the origin of these improvements has remained unclear. We show these improvements arise from differences in the one-particle density as encoded into the Fock matrix, not from the nature of the orbitals themselves, as is commonly assumed. Exploiting this insight, Kohn-Sham references enable near-chemical accuracy for electronic and thermochemical properties of transition metal dimers and main group compounds. Notably, Kohn-Sham coupled cluster qualitatively recovers the entire chromium dimer potential energy surface, a notorious failure case for conventional methods. We further introduce a density difference diagnostic that detects multireference character and guides the selection of optimal references at mean-field cost. Together, these results establish a practical route to treating strong correlation within quantum chemistry's "gold standard" framework, with immediate implications for machine learning potential development and materials research, which rely heavily on density functional theory.

Resumen: Passive microfluidic mixing is fundamentally constrained by the dominance of laminar flow, a limitation commonly addressed using embedded obstacles or surface modifications, often at the cost of increased fabrication complexity and hydraulic resistance. Here, we introduce a conical helix micromixer (CHM) that combines circular and helical microchannel topologies into a monolithic geometry capable of passively generating progressively intensified Dean vortices through continuously varying curvature. This curvature-driven mechanism induces strong transverse transport and achieves  a mixing index (MI) > 95% in the first turn of the CHM across varying flow rates (1-2500 µL min<sup>-1</sup>) without requiring any internal roughness structures or external energy inputs, as validated by field-based mixing simulations. A central methodological contribution is a reduced-order planar representation of the full three-dimensional (3D) CHM geometry for flow-field analysis and optimization. Direct geometrical validation against the original 3D conical-helix centreline demonstrated projection-induced deviations below 2% across all investigated configurations, with most cases remaining below 1%, confirming that the planar representation preserves the dominant geometric characteristics of the true 3D flow path with negligible loss of fidelity. This reduced-order strategy lowered computational costs by approximately an order of magnitude, while preserving a strong correlation with full 3D field-based calculations across the investigated ranges of Reynolds numbers. Geometric and flow parameters were systematically explored using a Taguchi framework, while gradient-boosted machine-learning models were employed as mechanistic analytical tools to quantify parameter sensitivity. Both analyses consistently identified the inlet curvature radius as the dominant design variable governing Dean vortex onset and mixing-length compression, with tighter curvature significantly accelerating the development of transverse mixing. The results prove that controlled curvature modulation alone can function as an efficient passive mixing engine, providing a compact, fabrication-ready platform for microreactor synthesis, point-of-care diagnostics, and scalable lab-on-a-chip applications.

Título: In-laboratory polysomnography as the reference standard in sleep research: a bibliometric overview of human studies.
Resumen: In-laboratory attended Polysomnography (PSG) is the reference standard for objective sleep assessment. Although portable and wearable sleep technologies have advanced, the evolution of PSG research over the past decade has not been systematically characterized. Bibliometric data from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015-2025) were retrieved using a search strategy focused on in-laboratory, full-night PSG studies, yielding 462 publications for analysis. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Microsoft Excel were used to conduct visual and quantitative analyses of publication trends, country- and institution-level co-authorship, journal distribution, author keywords, and keywords bursts. Annual publications exhibited a steady increase, with the United States and China as the leading contributors. Prominent institutions included Eindhoven University of Technology and Seoul National University. PSG research was predominantly published in specialized sleep medicine journals. Keyword analysis revealed a stable thematic core encompassing sleep monitoring, sleep staging, and sleep apnea, alongside emerging trends in machine learning, wearable devices, and brain modeling. Within the corpus of included in-laboratory PSG studies, research outputs demonstrated a sustained trajectory, exhibiting a pattern of parallel development between clinical applications and technical refinement. While PSG remains a foundational methodological pillar in this specific domain, its evolving integration with advanced computational methods underscores a continued commitment to bridging clinical relevance and technological progress within PSG-focused research.


--- ARTÍCULO 3699 ---
ID (PMID): 42874486
Título: Development and external validation of a non-laboratory model to predict early-onset cardiovascular disease risk: a multicohort machine learning study.
Resumen: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a questionnaire-based model for two related tasks in adults younger than 65 years: classification of incident early-onset cardiovascular disease (EOCVD) among participants without cardiovascular disease at baseline, and time-to-event prediction of all-cause mortality among participants with EOCVD at baseline. Longitudinal data were obtained from CHARLS, HRS, KLoSA, ELSA, and SHARE. The incidence classification analysis included 37,082 participants, and the prognostic survival analysis included 19,478. Eighteen questionnaire or routinely obtainable predictors were used. No laboratory biomarker or imaging measurement was entered into either model, although reported diagnoses may have depended on earlier clinical testing. CatBoost achieved an AUROC of 0.6869, an AUPRC of 0.1438, a precision of 0.1105, and a recall of 0.6512 in the independent SHARE cohort. The Cox proportional hazards model achieved a test-set C-index of 0.7175; its 3-, 5-, and 7-year AUROCs were 0.7314, 0.7348, and 0.7350. P-EOCVD provides questionnaire-based risk stratification for incident EOCVD and subsequent mortality. Its low precision precludes diagnostic use. The model may support first-step screening where laboratory testing is not immediately available, but prospective validation and recalibration are required before use in under-resourced populations.


--- ARTÍCULO 3700 ---
ID (PMID): 42874479
Título: Concentration of injury and fatality harm at repeat-active highway-rail grade crossings: A multi-state permutation and machine learning analysis.
Resumen: Highway-rail grade crossing incidents remain a transportation safety concern, yet prior studies have focused mainly on crash occurrence, severity, and hotspot detection, leaving limited evidence on how injury-or-fatality harm concentrates at crossings with repeated incidents. Using Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) Form 57 records from six U.S. states during 2013-2025, this study quantified repeat-site harm concentration and evaluated leakage-controlled surveillance ranking. The final cohort comprised 8,286 incidents, of which 3,250 involved at least one injury or fatality. Repeat-active crossings, defined as crossings with at least two incidents, accounted for 56.3% of documented harm and exceeded the randomized benchmark (p = 0.013; false-discovery-rate-adjusted p = 0.026). The harm-count Gini coefficient across all observed incident-involved crossings was 0.630, indicating an unequal distribution of documented harm. Leakage-controlled rolling-origin histogram gradient boosting validation yielded a mean area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.721, while unseen-crossing evaluation yielded 0.693; separate leave-one-state-out logistic validation yielded 0.674. Conceptually, the study formalizes repeat-site harm concentration as distinct from incident frequency and separates surveillance prioritization from causal safety mechanisms. The framework supports repeat-site screening and prioritization for further inspection and engineering assessment without implying causal infrastructure deficiencies or intervention effectiveness.

ID (PMID): 42874475
Título: Fe<sup>3+</sup>-mediated fluorescence switching of biomass-derived carbon dots integrated with PVA microneedles for smartphone-assisted determination of ascorbic acid in fruits and vegetables.
Resumen: Rapid and accurate determination of ascorbic acid (AA) is important for evaluating the nutritional quality of fresh produce. In this study, biomass-derived carbon dots (CDs) were synthesized from pomelo peel in a green deep eutectic solvent, and Fe<sup>3+</sup> was subsequently coordinated with the CDs to construct an off-on fluorescent probe based on Fe<sup>3+</sup>-induced quenching and AA-triggered fluorescence recovery. The probe was incorporated into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) microneedle (MN) patch to enable localized sampling and in situ sensing in fruits and vegetables. Fluorescence images were acquired using a smartphone, and multidimensional RGB-derived features were analyzed using LightGBM for quantitative prediction. The platform exhibited a linear response to AA over 0-10 mM (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.9979) with a limit of detection of 0.2 μM, while the direct sampling, fluorescence sensing, and smartphone readout could be completed within 10 min. In real produce samples, the microneedle measurements showed good agreement with the reference method, supporting the potential of this portable platform for on-site AA quantification.


--- ARTÍCULO 3702 ---
ID (PMID): 42874472
Título: Machine-learning-assisted ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy for low-level multi-component adulteration identification in Coptis chinensis.
Resumen: Low-level adulteration of botanical ingredients is difficult to detect because weak adulterant signals are often masked by the dominant matrix spectrum. Here, Ultraviolet-Visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy combined with machine learning was investigated for identification of low-level multi-component adulteration in Coptis chinensis. Scutellaria baicalensis, Rheum palmatum, and Curcuma longa were used as adulterants to construct 29 classes, including pure, single-, binary- and ternary-adulteration samples, at a fixed total adulterant content of 3 wt%. Twenty independently prepared samples were included in each class, resulting in a total of 580 independent samples for model development and evaluation. The spectra showed strong overlap, nearly unchanged peak positions, and subtle intensity variations, making visual inspection and single-wavelength analysis insufficient for detailed discrimination. Multiple spectral preprocessing methods and machine-learning models were systematically compared using stratified five-fold cross-validation at the independent sample level. Following this systematic comparison, moving-average preprocessing combined with either random forest or extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest overall classification accuracy of 95.9%. Spectral-window analysis further showed that broader wavelength regions provided higher accuracy than narrow peak-centered windows, indicating that the discriminative information is distributed across the spectral profile rather than confined to isolated absorption peaks. Even though the study was limited to three model adulterants under the present controlled laboratory conditions, these results demonstrate the feasibility of extracting weak composition-dependent information from highly overlapping UV-Vis spectra and highlight the need for further validation using more diverse adulterants and sample sources.

ID (PMID): 42874426
Título: Machine learning-based prediction of hospital-acquired malnutrition at discharge using the GLIM criteria: A multicenter real-world study.
Resumen: This study aimed to investigate the incidence and clinical impact of hospital-acquired malnutrition (HAM) and develop a machine learning model for early risk prediction. This secondary analysis included prospectively collected data from a multicenter observational study involving 34 tertiary hospitals in China. Adult patients hospitalized for 7 to 30 days were enrolled. Patients without malnutrition at admission were evaluated for HAM at discharge according to the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria. Machine learning models were developed using clinical and nutritional variables available at admission, and model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility analyses. Among 4746 hospitalized patients, 1364 (28.7%) had malnutrition at admission. Of the 3382 patients without baseline malnutrition, 731 (21.6%) developed HAM during hospitalization. Patients with HAM had significantly higher rates of hospital-acquired complications (9.0% versus 2.9%), longer hospital stays (14.93 versus 13.53 days), and higher healthcare costs (¥48 980 versus ¥20 640) compared with those without HAM (all P < 0.001). Male sex, older age, pre-admission weight loss, reduced calf circumference, decreased handgrip strength, reduced muscle mass phenotype according to GLIM, and malignant tumors were associated with HAM. The XGBoost model demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.857-0.906) in the independent test set. HAM is common among hospitalized patients without malnutrition at admission, and the developed machine learning model may enable early identification of high-risk patients for timely nutritional intervention.

ID (PMID): 42874412
Título: MCLE: Multimodal collaborative learning and enhancement with similarity-based modal purification for pretrained features.
Resumen: Multimodal recommendation has become a crucial framework for leveraging various data modalities to boost recommendation performance. However, existing methods still face several limitations when exploiting multimodal features. Relying solely on limited raw features prevents full exploitation of the rich semantic information inherent in various modalities, while unfiltered noise in multimodal data can degrade recommendation quality. Moreover, naive modal feature fusion strategies struggle to address the significant differences in preferences for different modalities among various users. To address these limitations, we propose a Multimodal Collaborative Learning and Enhancement framework (MCLE). Specifically, we utilize a pretrained language model to augment user profiles and item attributes, and propose an adaptive fusion mechanism that combines the enhanced user profile features with interaction-derived user representations, rather than simply relying on either source alone. A Similarity-based Modal Purification (SMP) module is then designed to filter out modal feature noise using learnable reference vectors that evaluate feature quality through similarity computation, producing purified multimodal representations. On this basis, a Multimodal Adaptive Feature Aggregator (MAFA) employs difference-aware attention and dynamic modal gating to achieve personalized multimodal feature integration. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

Título: Bio-inspired zero-shot learning with hierarchical fault-trait knowledge transfer for cross-domain diagnosis.
Resumen: Fault diagnosis methods for complex mechanical systems often face challenges in adapting to unseen fault types and varying operating conditions. Existing techniques typically suffer from limited cross-domain adaptability and weak zero-shot recognition capabilities. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a bio-inspired zero-shot learning framework that incorporates hierarchical fault-trait knowledge transfer and domain adaptation. A biomimetic network is designed to quantify domain discrepancies and generate transferable domain factors, using a hierarchical fault-trait description framework inspired by the differentiation process from general to specialized features. This approach enables fault diagnosis of previously unseen fault types by leveraging labeled data from the source domain only. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for cross-domain zero-shot diagnosis and suggest its potential applicability to complex mechanical systems.

Título: TMRKP: Trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction framework for stroke-associated pneumonia and hemorrhagic transformation.
Resumen: Prediction of stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is critical for improving the prognosis of acute ischemic stroke patients. However, current brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models narrowly focus on generic visual patterns, and frequently overlook the radiology-informed knowledge critical for predicting SAP and HT. To address this limitation, we propose a trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction (TMRKP) framework equipped with radiology knowledge-aware masked modeling (RKMM) and evidential multi-sequence fusion (EMF). Specifically, TMRKP first organizes four MRI sequences into a 2 × 2 super-sequence configuration, mimicking the diagnostic perspective of radiologists who simultaneously analyze multiple imaging modalities. Second, to introduce radiology knowledge into representation learning, we focus on white matter hyperintensities (WMH), a well-established biomarker of chronic small-vessel disease and long-term ischemic injury that is clinically relevant to SAP and HT. During pre-training, RKMM segments WMH masks from the MRI sequence to steer the model toward WMH regions, enabling it to learn meaningful representations of these clinically relevant pathological areas. Third, for SAP and HT prediction, EMF models the predictive uncertainty using evidence derived from both the super-sequence and the WMH-aware masked super-sequence, and fuses the resulting multi-sequence evidence based on Dempster-Shafer theory (DST). Extensive experiments on the collected Jiangdu dataset, together with independent external validation on the Zhongda dataset, demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of TMRKP over the state-of-the-art models.


--- ARTÍCULO 3707 ---
ID (PMID): 42874408
Título: Topology-aware dynamic co-evolution for robust graph learning.
Resumen: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Our code is available at https://github.com/robustgcn/TADC.

Título: Machine learning-assisted dual-channel FeZnCu@CNP nanozyme sensor array for qualitative and quantitative analysis of multiple pesticides.
Resumen: To fulfil rapid identification and quantification of various pesticide residues, we first synthesized a FeZnCu@CNP nanozyme with dual laccase- and peroxidase-like activities, enabling differential responses to eight pesticides (Gly, Car, Met, TBZ, CBZ, PCNB, ACE, and MCPA) via coordination and hydrogen-bonding interactions. The dual-channel nanozyme sensor array based on machine learning was developed, successfully discriminating these pesticides at 0.1-100 μg/mL for both qualitative and quantitative detection with an LOD of 0.013 μg/mL. Principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) confirmed effective differentiation of eight individual pesticides and their mixtures at varied concentrations and ratios. The concentration-independent discrimination model based on the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm demonstrated outstanding accuracy in pesticide detection and differentiation. Importantly, this model demonstrated strong anti-interference and high feasibility for fruit/vegetable and blind sample identification. This sensor array enables concentration-independent qualitative identification and accurate quantitation of eight residues, offering a supplementary rapid-screening strategy for multi-pesticide detection.


--- ARTÍCULO 3709 ---
ID (PMID): 42874375
Título: Unraveling membrane protein conformational landscapes: Enhanced sampling, membrane regulation, and artificial intelligence-assisted simulation.
Resumen: Membrane proteins undergo functionally essential conformational transitions that couple local chemical events and changes in the membrane environment to large-scale structural rearrangements. These transitions are often difficult to capture with conventional molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly in complex protein-membrane systems. This mini-review discusses how recent MD studies have resolved transition pathways and conformational intermediates and revealed regulatory mechanisms involving substrates, ions, lipids, and membrane mechanics. A recurring theme is that membrane protein function is determined not only by the stability of experimentally resolved endpoint structures but also by the accessibility of intermediate states and the pathways connecting them. We further highlight how enhanced sampling, machine learning, complementary simulation approaches, and experimental constraints are increasingly being combined to construct more robust mechanistic models. Together, these advances are moving MD from retrospective interpretation toward predictive models of membrane protein function.

Título: Machine learning-driven prediction of Salmonella enterica virulence for enhanced risk assessment in poultry in Mexico.
Resumen: Strain-level heterogeneity in Salmonella enterica pathogenic potential is not routinely incorporated into quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA), where homogeneous virulence assumptions are commonly applied. This study evaluated whether supervised machine learning (ML)-based genomic classification could provide a structured approach to integrating strain-level variation into risk modeling. Publicly available S. enterica genomes annotated with clinical metadata were used to train classifiers assigning isolates to clinically derived risk categories. Two genomic feature representations were compared: pangenome-wide gene presence/absence matrices and curated functional gene sets. Ensemble models trained under nested cross-validation achieved strong predictive performance, with pangenome-based models outperforming models restricted to curated functional gene sets. Feature importance analyses indicated that accessory genome variation contributed substantially to class discrimination. The trained classifiers were applied to an independent cohort of poultry-derived isolates to examine out-of-sample prediction patterns. Model-derived classifications were subsequently incorporated into an established QMRA framework representing high-risk chicken consumption scenarios in central Mexico. Integration of virulence categories modified dose-response assumptions and redistributed prevalence across risk strata, producing scenario-dependent differences in estimated probabilities of illness and projected case numbers. The median estimated risk varied according to the genomic stratification approach and scenario. For the ML pangenome-based model, risk estimates ranged from 5.84 × 10<sup>-10</sup> to 1.02 × 10<sup>-3</sup>. The ML model based on curated functional genes produced estimates from 5.7× 10<sup>-10</sup> to 1.67 × 10<sup>-3</sup>. These were compared with a previous 13-gene model (5.72 × 10<sup>-10</sup> to 1.70 × 10<sup>-3</sup>) and a serotype-based approach (1.42 × 10<sup>-9</sup> to 6.00 × 10<sup>-3</sup>). These findings indicate that genome-informed stratification can be operationally embedded within QMRA and, importantly, that the way strains are classified directly influences estimated risk levels. Because predicted risks varied substantially depending on whether isolates were categorized as high-, moderate-, or low-virulence, accurate genomic classification is critical for appropriately capturing strain-level heterogeneity can influence predicted public health outcomes within modeled scenarios.

Título: Not all artificial intelligence large language models are created equal: heterogeneous performance in therapeutic decision-making for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer.
Resumen: To evaluate the concordance between therapeutic recommendations generated by 3 widely used consumer large language models (Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT) and the decisions of a multidisciplinary tumor board in the management of the first recurrence of high-grade serous ovarian cancer. Secondary objectives were to characterize recurrent error patterns and to assess the safety of model-generated recommendations using a 3-tier taxonomy. A retrospective observational analysis was conducted on 44 consecutive patients with a first recurrence of high-grade serous ovarian cancer treated at a tertiary referral center. For each case, an identical, anonymized, structured zero-shot prompt was submitted to the 3 models. The multidisciplinary tumor board decision served as the reference comparator. Overall concordance and concordance for the chemotherapy backbone, maintenance or targeted-agent class, and surgical indication were compared between models using Cochran's Q test and pairwise McNemar tests (Holm-adjusted). Discordant recommendations were categorized as true hallucinations, unsafe, or suboptimal but guideline-concordant. Concordance varied substantially across models (Cochran's Q p<.001): Gemini 77.3% (95% confidence interval 62.2 to 88.5), Microsoft Copilot 36.4% (95% confidence interval 22.4 to 52.2), and ChatGPT 18.2% (95% confidence interval 8.2 to 32.7); Gemini differed significantly from the other 2 models (Holm-adjusted p<.001), whereas the difference between Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT did not reach significance after adjustment (p=.057). Component-level analysis localized the divergence to systemic therapy: surgical-indication agreement was uniformly high (93.2% to 95.5%, p=.85). All 3 models generated unsafe recommendations for the re-use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase) inhibitors in patients with documented prior progression on poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor maintenance, with marked differences in frequency (Microsoft Copilot 10, ChatGPT 3, and Gemini 2; 15 of 74 total discordances). The remaining discordances were suboptimal but guideline concordant. Consumer large language models showed heterogeneous and clinically meaningful differences in reproducing Multidisciplinary Tumor Board decisions in recurrent ovarian cancer; none were free of unsafe recommendations. Their current performance does not support independent clinical use, and expert supervision is required to ensure patient safety.

Título: Quercetin confers protection against psoriasis by inhibiting AKR1B10-mediated glycolytic reprogramming in keratinocytes.
Resumen: The anti-psoriatic effect of quercetin has been observed. However, the involved mechanism remains poorly explored. Hence, the study investigated the therapeutic effects of quercetin against psoriasis and elucidated its underlying molecular mechanisms, with a focus on AKR1B10-mediated glycolytic reprogramming. An imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model and an interleukin-17A (IL-17A)-stimulated keratinocyte model were established as psoriasis-like models. Therapeutic effects of quercetin on psoriasis-like lesions were evaluated by gross lesion observation, PASI scoring, histopathological staining, and immunohistochemistry. Flow cytometry as well as ELISA were performed to assess T helper 17 (Th17) cell proportions and systemic inflammatory responses. Candidate therapeutic targets of quercetin in psoriasis treatment were obtained by integrating GEO database analysis, target prediction, and machine learning algorithms. A series of assays were harnessed to measure AKR1B10 expression and glycolysis-related enzymes, lactic acid, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR). AKR1B10 overexpression experiments were performed to validate the function of AKR1B10. Quercetin markedly alleviated psoriasis-like skin lesions and repressed inflammation in IMQ-treated mice, accompanied by significantly inhibited Th17 cell expansion and keratinocyte hyperproliferation and reduced levels of inflammatory cytokines. AKR1B10 was identified as a potential mediator of quercetin activity in psoriasis, which was upregulated in psoriasis. Mechanistically, quercetin lowered AKR1B10 expression, downregulating key glycolytic enzymes and lactic acid and reducing ECAR. Overexpressing AKR1B10 largely negated suppressive impacts of quercetin on keratinocyte glycolysis and proliferation. Quercetin alleviates inflammation and abnormal keratinocyte proliferation in experimental psoriasis-like models, potentially through modulation of AKR1B10-associated glycolytic reprogramming.

Título: Therapeutic efficacy and dosing regimen evidence synthesis of Ursolic Acid for liver injury: A preclinical systematic review with machine learning.
Resumen: Ursolic acid (UA), a pentacyclic triterpene, shows hepatoprotective efficacy and favorable safety in various animal models of liver injury. However, robust preclinical evidence remains scarce. To synthesize the preclinical evidence for UA and explore how UA dose and treatment duration are associated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) improvement in animal models of liver injury. This preclinical systematic review integrating meta-analysis and machine learning followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). An exploratory HED range of approximately 5-7 mg/kg was associated with greater predicted ALT improvement. The study indicates that UA exerts hepatoprotective effects in animal models of liver injury. Potential mechanisms include modulation of the gut-liver axis, attenuation of hepatic and systemic oxidative stress, and suppression of inflammation and fibrosis. Given the exploratory nature of these preclinical findings, the translational potential of UA warrants further rigorous validation.

Título: Predicting eating quality of pork shoulder butt using Vis/NIR hyperspectral imaging and machine learning models.
Resumen: This study proposed a framework for predicting eating quality clusters (EQCs) of pork shoulder butt using visible/near-infrared hyperspectral imaging (HSI). HSI data from 189 samples were acquired, and their EQCs were defined by applying k-means clustering (k = 2 and 3) to an integrated feature matrix composed of results from sensory and electronic tongue analyses. Three datasets, including muscle, fat, and whole-meat regions, were generated using a partial least squares-discriminant analysis-based segmentation procedure. The muscle region outperformed other datasets in both class classification tasks. Optimal feature selection and data augmentation methods were then explored. In the binary classification, the combination of uninformative variable elimination, combined transformation, and a logistic regression model achieved the best performance. In the three-class classification, the combination of a support vector machine with all variables and scale and noise addition showed the best performance. Consequently, HSI would serve as a rapid and non-destructive tool for predicting pork EQCs.

Título: Artificial intelligence-enabled drug discovery: A growing but largely early-stage clinical pipeline.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into pharmaceutical discovery, yet the extent to which AI-enabled assets have translated into clinical-stage programs remains incompletely characterized. AI-enabled therapeutics are entering clinical testing at increasing scale, but most programs remain early in development, with few having advanced beyond Phase 2. This dataset provides a baseline for future evaluation of whether AI-enabled discovery ultimately improves regulatory approval rates and clinical outcomes.

Título: Viral regulation of N<sub>2</sub>O emissions depends on soil acidity.
Resumen: Acidification generally enhances N<sub>2</sub>O emissions from soils. Yet, the adaptive responses of denitrifiers and the regulatory roles of soil viruses in denitrifier-mediated N<sub>2</sub>O emissions under persistent acidity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined D<sub>2</sub>O-labeled single-cell Raman spectroscopy, <sup>15</sup>N tracing, metagenomics, machine learning, and virus-addition experiments to examine virus-denitrifier interactions across soils with contrasting long-term acidity conditions maintained for > 17 years. Acidic soils showed the highest N<sub>2</sub>O emissions despite the lowest potential denitrification rate and highest microbial anabolic activity. Denitrifiers and viral populations in acidic soils exhibited reduced microdiversity, stronger purifying selection, and distinct functional specialization, while viruses showed a lower virulent-to-temperate ratio and greater genetic potential for host interaction and persistence. Host antiviral defense capacity was the strongest genomic predictor of abundance responses to active virus. In acidic soils, active viruses increased N<sub>2</sub>O reductase level by 33.2% without altering nosZ abundance and reduced N<sub>2</sub>O accumulation by up to 62.5%, indicating an efficiency-optimized response. Neutral soils showed a quantity-driven response, whereas alkaline soils showed no significant reduction in N<sub>2</sub>O accumulation. These findings reveal acidity-dependent viral regulation of N<sub>2</sub>O emissions, strongest in long-term acidic soils.

Título: CoilDrop-MRI: Self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction with coil dropout.
Resumen: Self-supervised deep learning-based methods have shown great promise for accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction, achieving high image quality without requiring fully sampled data for training. Resumen: To map artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed for triage in primary care and describe their characteristics, performance and clinical applicability. The framework offers an interpretable approach to identifying disease-associated transcriptomic patterns and may support future precision diagnostic research.

This review combines a CiteSpace-based bibliometric analysis of Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) records with a structured qualitative synthesis of ML-assisted studies on zero-dimensional nanoparticles, one-dimensional high-aspect-ratio nanomaterials, two-dimensional layered nanomaterials, functional nanomaterials, carbon dots, and emerging hybrid systems. Annual output increased from four publications in 2012 to 268 in 2025, and ML showed the strongest recent keyword burst (strength = 22.57). Across representative studies, reported test-set coefficients of determination commonly ranged from 0.858 to 0.995, although validation designs and data independence varied markedly. Tree-based ensembles were generally effective for small-to-medium tabular datasets, whereas deep learning was most defensible for images, spectra, and time-series data. Prediction estimates properties for a specified formulation; optimization uses a validated surrogate model to search the formulation or processing space and therefore requires independent experimental verification. Nano-SiO<sub>2</sub>, carbon nanotubes, and graphene oxide dominate the evidence base, while durability, microstructure, uncertainty quantification, and multifunctional co-optimization remain underrepresented. Matrix-aware standardized databases, physically constrained models, grouped or external validation, and closed-loop experiments are required for reliable intelligent design. The bibliometric component covers 1324 Web of Science Core Collection records published during 2012-2026, whereas the qualitative component applies explicit criteria for construction relevance, definition of the ML task, and sufficiency of performance and validation reporting. Bibliometric patterns and qualitative evidence are therefore reported and interpreted separately.

ID (PMID): 42872975
Título: Dictionary learning for kernel EDMD.
Resumen: Studying nonlinear dynamical systems through their state space behavior can be challenging, and one possible alternative is to analyze them via their associated Koopman operator. This turns the nonlinear problem into a linear, infinite-dimensional one. To approximate the operator in finite dimensions, extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) is a commonly used algorithm. It requires a finite list of functionals and a set of snapshots from the system to compute an approximation of the operator and its corresponding spectrum. Instead of choosing the list of functionals directly, it can be implicitly defined via kernels, a method known as kernel extended dynamic mode decomposition (kEDMD). However, one still needs to define the kernel and choose its parameter values. In this paper, we aim to streamline this process by extending dictionary learning for EDMD to kernel learning in kEDMD. By simplifying kEDMD, we show how to perform gradient-based optimization over the learnable kernel parameters and demonstrate that this method leads to useful kernels for the original kEDMD. The focus of our work is a method that takes a weighted list of kernels with randomly initialized values as input and outputs a list of kernels and parameter values suitable for approximating the Koopman operator of the underlying system. We demonstrate that unimportant kernels can be removed from the list by analyzing the weights in the weighted sum. We evaluate the method across several experiments, including the Duffing oscillator and the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, showcasing the method's different strengths.

Título: Noninvasive assessment of the anaerobic threshold in endurance athletes: an evidence-based narrative review of methods, validity, and field feasibility.

Título: A Combined Network Toxicology and Docking Study to Identify Putative Molecular Targets Linking Styrene Exposure to Atherosclerosis.
Resumen: Styrene is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound linked to hematologic and vascular alterations; however, the molecular mechanisms connecting exposure to atherosclerosis remain poorly characterized. We integrated peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic profiles (GSE23746) with toxicogenomic data from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, applying support vector machine recursive feature elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator machine learning algorithms to identify core targets at the styrene-atherosclerosis intersection. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and molecular docking evaluated binding potential. Four model genes-CCND3, CCR1, MYC, and MYD88-were identified and constituted a diagnostic signature with high accuracy (area under the curve > 0.9). These genes were enriched in IL-17 and NF-κB inflammatory pathways and correlated with distinct immune cell alterations, particularly neutrophils and T cell subsets. Molecular docking predicted direct, moderate-affinity binding of styrene to CCND3 (Vina score = -6.4 kcal/mol), involving multiple contacts within the cyclin domain. The convergence of transcriptomic screening and molecular docking identifies CCND3 as a putative target for styrene-protein interaction and suggests a mechanistic hypothesis linking styrene to atherosclerosis via inflammatory and immune dysregulation. The computational framework provides a basis for future experimental validation. This computational framework generates the hypothesis that styrene may contribute to atherosclerosis through coordinated perturbations of immune signaling and cell cycle regulation, with CCND3 representing a candidate molecular target for future experimental validation in styrene-exposed populations.

ID (PMID): 42872636
Título: Reliability of Machine Learning Approaches Towards the Identification of Novel PI4KIIIβ Inhibitors.
Resumen: The type III Phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4KIIIβ) serves as a key host factor that mediates the replication of RNA viruses and is involved in essential membrane trafficking events. The development of PI4KIIIβ-specific inhibitors could give insights into the enzyme's function and contribute to the treatment of viral diseases. However, the molecular features that determine inhibitor activity and selectivity remain unclear. PI4KIIIβ inhibitors with reported biological activities (pIC50) were systematically analyzed using machine-learning methods. Molecular characterization was performed using RDKit, Chemopy descriptors, and PubChem fingerprints. Multiple classification and regression models were developed and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation to establish robust structureactivity relationships. It was suggested that the PubChem fingerprint-based linear regression, SMOreg, and GaussianProcesses models were more appropriate for the studied dataset to deliver the best predictive ability, which showed a correlation coefficient value > 0.7 in the 10-fold crossvalidation. PubChemFP389 and PubChemFP572, representing amidine-like fragments or guanidine- related motifs, and the aromatic amine fragment showed a negative correlation with respect to biological activity. The study describes predictive models and provides insights into essential structural features in chemical compounds relevant for inhibitory activity, which could assist in the design and optimization of novel PI4KIIIβ inhibitors for antiviral and anticancer applications. A similar approach may be extended to a larger dataset of molecules or to other related drug targets. The findings suggest that excessive basicity and certain polar functionalities may be detrimental to PI4KIIIβ inhibition, providing important insights into the structural features influencing ligand binding and activity.

ID (PMID): 42872629
Título: Development of a Risk Prediction Model for Arteriovenous Fistula Restenosis Following Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients Using SMOTE Algorithm.
Resumen: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) restenosis after percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) affects hemodialysis in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients. Data imbalance limits predictive model accuracy. To identify risk factors and develop a SMOTE-based risk prediction model for AVF restenosis within 12 months after PTA. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 241 consecutive MHD patients with AVF stenosis undergoing PTA between July 2022 and July 2025. Each patient contributed one index PTA. Patients were divided into restenosis (45 cases) and nonrestenosis (196 cases) groups according to whether AVF restenosis occurred within 12 months after PTA. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified risk factors. The SMOTE algorithm addressed data imbalance. Model performance was evaluated by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Original-data multivariate analysis identified multisegmental stenosis, cannulation method, platelet count, and C-reactive protein (CRP) as independent risk factors. After SMOTE, intradialytic hypotension and serum albumin also became significant; however, these variables should be interpreted as exploratory because SMOTE does not create additional independent clinical information. The SMOTE-based model (P2) achieved AUC of 0.934 (training set) and 0.868 (validation set), outperforming the original model (P1). The SMOTE-based model may help predict AVF restenosis within 12 months after PTA, but it is an exploratory internally validated tool and requires external validation before clinical use.

Título: Can Forensic Crime Scene Investigation be Aided by Spectroscopy and Chemometric Techniques?-A Comprehensive Review.
Resumen: This review examines the forensic applications, advantages, and limitations of key spectroscopic techniques, including Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), and mass spectrometry, in crime scene and laboratory investigations. These techniques are discussed in the context of analyzing evidence, detecting illicit substances (including biological fluids, explosives, and narcotics), and reconstructing crime scenes. The benefits and limitations of each method are highlighted, along with their potential for enhancing forensic investigations. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) with spectroscopic techniques is also briefly explored, noting their role in improving data analysis and interpretation. Challenges such as sensitivity, specificity, and implementation in field settings are discussed, alongside future directions for advancing spectroscopic applications in forensics. This review aims to provide a balanced overview of spectroscopic techniques in forensic science for researchers, forensic scientists, and law enforcement agencies.

ID (PMID): 42872582
Título: Machine learning-driven risk screening for Chinese developmental dyslexia in children: Theoretical framework, feature selection, and simulation-based methodological illustration.
Resumen: Developmental dyslexia affects Chinese children's reading development, and school-based risk screening may help identify children who require further assessment and support. However, interpretable screening-oriented models remain limited by small samples, insufficient standardization, limited longitudinal evidence, and weak cross-school validation. This study proposes a simulation-based methodological framework for organizing and evaluating multidimensional cognitive indicators of Chinese developmental dyslexia. The framework integrates phonological processing, orthographic processing, attentional control, and working memory indicators within a feature-selection and explainable machine-learning pipeline combining statistical screening, LASSO-based embedded selection, ensemble-model importance analysis, and SHAP-based interpretation. Simulated experiments informed by prior empirical distributions were used to illustrate the pipeline's internal behavior, methodological coherence, and interpretability under predefined data-generating assumptions. The simulation reproduced expected risk-feature patterns, including the prominence of rapid automatized naming, phonological awareness, orthographic processing, and cognitive-control indicators. These patterns, however, reflect recovery of predefined simulation signals rather than independent empirical identification of dyslexia predictors. Similarly, the reported AUC values, SHAP rankings, and threshold estimates are simulation-internal results, not evidence of real-world screening accuracy, clinical utility, or school-based readiness. The study therefore provides an illustrative methodological framework, rather than validating a practical screening tool.

ID (PMID): 42872575
Título: Accuracy of Machine Learning in Differential Diagnosis of Multiple System Atrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Resumen: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is frequently misdiagnosed as Parkinson's disease (PD) or progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), posing significant diagnostic challenges. The aim of the study was to systematically evaluate the efficacy of machine learning (ML) in differentiating MSA from other neurodegenerative disorders. We conducted a systematic search in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (up to July 5, 2025), including ML-based MSA diagnostic studies. QUADAS-2 assessed bias risk, and a bivariate mixed-effects model synthesized diagnostic metrics. A total of 51 studies (comprising 3595 MSA patients and 18,189 total cases) were included in the systematic review. Of these, 38 studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis, whereas the remaining 13 studies were summarized qualitatively. In the primary analysis comparing MSA with PD, the pooled sensitivity was 0.86 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.81-0.90), specificity 0.87 (95% CI: 0.83-0.90), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve (AUC) 0.93 (95% CI: 0.90-0.95). Overall, pooled sensitivity was 0.85 (95% CI: 0.82-0.88), specificity 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89-0.94), and AUC 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92-0.96). Positron emission tomography (PET)-based models achieved optimal performance (sensitivity: 0.90, specificity: 0.96, AUC: 0.97), whereas deep learning models outperformed others (sensitivity: 0.93, specificity: 0.98, AUC: 0.99). ML models integrating PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for MSA. Future work should prioritize prospective multicenter validation and standardized external testing to facilitate clinical implementation.

Título: Non-Perturbative Bacterial Identification Directly From Solid Agar Plates Using Raman Micro-Spectroscopy and Machine Learning.
Resumen: Raman spectroscopy is a promising tool for microbial identification, yet its implementation in microbiology and clinical workflow is still restricted due to the accompanying additional preparation required to focus on microbial signals. Here, we demonstrate Raman-based bacterial identification directly from unopened, inverted agar plates, the same conditions used during incubation. Our approach enabled sensitive identification using two Escherichia coli variants, differing only in green fluorescent protein (GFP) expression, across diverse media and substrate material conditions, despite the interrogation path traversing 3-4 mm thick background material. We integrated traditional density functional theory (DFT)-based material computation with machine learning analysis, achieving over 97.7% classification accuracy, surpassing the performance of standard measurements from opened plates by 10.8% higher mean accuracy and 0.76% less variance. We further demonstrated Raman mapping-based colony identification via Raman peaks characteristic to GFPmut3 chromophore structure generated by DFT. Our approach is robust to changes in algorithms or substrate materials and promises real-time, non-perturbative monitoring of bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and antimicrobial resistance development.

Título: H<sub>2</sub>TiO<sub>3</sub> ion-sieve modified pencil graphite electrode integrated with artificial neural network calibration for broad-range quantitative detection of lithium ions.
Resumen: The widespread use of lithium (Li) has resulted in lithium-ion (Li<sup>+</sup>) contamination across a wide range of concentrations in the environment, posing potential risks to environmental safety and ecological health. However, the accurate and reliable quantification of Li<sup>+</sup> over such a broad concentration range remains challenging. Herein, a lithium ion sieve (H<sub>2</sub>TiO<sub>3</sub>)-engineered electrochemical sensing platform was developed by integrating selective ion recognition with artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted signal modeling. Lithium titanate (Li<sub>2</sub>TiO<sub>3</sub>) was prepared <i>via</i> a sol-gel route and subsequently converted to H<sub>2</sub>TiO<sub>3</sub> through proton exchange in an acidic medium. The resulting H<sub>2</sub>TiO<sub>3</sub> was then immobilized onto a pencil graphite electrode to obtain a working electrode for Li<sup>+</sup> detection. Electrochemical characterization revealed that the working electrode markedly enhanced the redox peak currents of potassium ferrocyanide and lowered the charge-transfer resistance after incubation in a lithium-ion solution. To overcome the difficulty of pinpointing signals when the entire cyclic voltammetry curve varies rather than individual peak intensities, an ANN module was applied to correlate the cyclic voltammetry response with the Li<sup>+</sup> concentration. The electrode exhibited a concentration-dependent response toward Li<sup>+</sup> in an ultra-wide dynamic range of 1.0 × 10<sup>-11</sup> to 1.0 × 10<sup>-4</sup> g L<sup>-1</sup>. The sensor exhibited excellent stability and reproducibility, with relative standard deviations remaining below 8%, and delivered recoveries between 97.9% and 103.9% when applied to water samples. The integration of ion-sieve recognition with machine learning modeling enabled Li<sup>+</sup> quantification across an unprecedentedly wide concentration window.

Título: ESIPT promotion or inhibition: gold cluster orientation in alanine.
Resumen: An orientation-dependent regulatory mechanism whereby gold (Au) clusters influence the excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) process in biomolecules is revealed for the first time in this study. Using alanine (ALA) as a model system with multiscale theoretical calculations, we reveal that the orientation of Au clusters can precisely modulate both the reaction pathway and thermodynamic feasibility of proton transfer. Theoretical screening of clusters with different numbers of Au atoms and excited-state dynamics studies indicate that pristine ALA hardly undergoes spontaneous proton transfer in the excited state; however, upon sulfurization and bonding with clusters, ESIPT is activated. IR and Raman vibrational analyses demonstrate that the alanine-Au<sub>5</sub> cluster (ALA-Au<sub>5</sub>) exhibits the most significant intramolecular hydrogen bond regulatory effect and achieves an optimal balance between capturing orientation-specific vibrational features and maintaining computational efficiency. A machine learning-assisted conformational search identified stable configurations, which lay a foundation for subsequent calculations. Electronic structure and energy analyses confirm that Au cluster binding to the acceptor blocks ESIPT while binding to the donor boosts it, elucidating how the spatial orientation of metal clusters modulates electronic structure and excited-state dynamics and providing a theoretical foundation for the rational design of metal-bio hybrid photofunctional systems.

Título: An AuNPs/CNT electrochemical aptasensor for accurate cortisol level discrimination assisted by machine learning.
Resumen: Cortisol levels provide valuable information regarding physiological stress and abnormalities associated with endocrine and mental health disorders. In this study, an AuNPs/CNT-modified electrochemical aptasensor integrated with machine learning was developed for sensitive cortisol detection and accurate discrimination of cortisol levels. A porous CNT network supported a large specific surface area with high conductivity, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed the AuNPs modified the electronic structures of CNTs and further accelerated the charge transfer efficiency. Once cortisol specifically binds to the aptamer, target-triggered conformational rearrangement could destabilize the aptamer/cDNA duplex and release the aptamer from the electrode surface. The reduced surface nucleic acid density alleviated steric and electrostatic hindrance for the diffusion of the [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3-/4-</sup> probe, which resulted in an accelerated interfacial electron transfer and yielded an enhanced electrochemical signal. The proposed cortisol aptasensor exhibited a good linear relationship between the current variation and the logarithm of cortisol concentration in the range of 10-5000 nM, with a limit of detection of 1.61 nM. Simultaneously, supervised machine learning was applied to classify cortisol concentrations with low, normal, and high levels, thus providing a promising strategy for intelligent stress assessment.

ID (PMID): 42872475
Título: scChronos: hierarchical temporal context learning for missing snapshot prediction in single-cell time series.
Resumen: Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensitive to sampling noise and cell-to-cell variability. We introduce scChronos, a hierarchical temporal context learning framework that formulates missing-snapshot prediction as target-conditioned population distribution prediction rather than individual-cell propagation. Unlike cell-centric propagation approaches, scChronos explicitly captures dual-level dynamics: (i) within each observed snapshot, scChronos compresses cell populations into cluster-representative cell representations with a transcriptomic encoder, preserving population information while reducing noise and (ii) across reference snapshots, the dual-branch temporal context integration module fuses information from all available and nearby time points into a temporal representation, which is then decoded with learnable cell-generation seeds to predict the target distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that scChronos improves both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting compared with state-of-the-art methods. Beyond reducing distributional discrepancy, scChronos better preserves developmental topology and maintains cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs. The code and data are available at https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283.

Among them, SVM exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance in accuracy, prediction confidence, and model stability, while all three algorithms achieved perfect identification accuracy for the QB/XJ adulteration pair. Nevertheless, the method still has limitations in low-concentration adulteration detection, with a minimum detectable adulteration level of 20%, which is mainly attributed to the non-chromatographic separation characteristic of TAPI-TOFMS and the high chemical similarity between authentic and counterfeit FB species. This rapid and robust methodology provides promising technical support for the quality supervision and authenticity identification of commercial FBs.

Título: Integrative long-read sequencing, RNA-seq and machine learning framework characterizes and predicts autosomal silencing in unbalanced X-autosome translocations.
Resumen: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) equalizes dosage between females (XX) and males (XY), yet its functional and clinical consequences remain challenging to interrogate in humans. Evaluating this spread and possible mediating factors is therefore essential for accurate clinical management. Using allele-resolved long-read sequencing and RNA sequencing, we investigated DNA methylation and gene expression across autosomal regions involved in unbalanced X-autosome translocations. Título: Integrated serum metabolomics and machine learning for classification of <i>Datura stramonium</i> L. exposure using plant part-specific metabolic signatures.
Resumen: <i>Datura stramonium</i> L. (DS) poisoning remains a significant toxicological concern in clinical and forensic contexts. This study developed a serum metabolomics strategy integrating machine learning to viably discriminate between seed- and leaf-derived <i>Datura</i> exposure using metabolic signatures. These results demonstrate that the integration of serum metabolomics and machine learning enables accurate and interpretable forensic source attribution of Datura poisoning. The proposed framework extends traditional toxicological analysis from exposure confirmation to data-driven forensic reconstruction, offering a novel approach to high-resolution forensic toxicology in complex plant poisoning cases.

Título: Examinations of the heterogeneity in the structural brain connectome in schizophrenia.
Resumen: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by widespread brain dysconnectivity, yet it remains unclear whether variable structural dysconnectivity patterns reflect biologically and clinically meaningful subtypes. We recruited 105 SCZ patients and 97 healthy controls, collecting magnetic resonance imaging, clinical assessment, and laboratory test data. Double generalized linear models were first applied to estimate group differences in the mean and inter-individual variability of structural connectivity between SCZ and controls. Subsequently, nonnegative matrix factorization was used to identify SCZ subtypes according to dysconnectivity profiles. We observed a significantly altered subnetwork that exhibited increased inter-individual variability in SCZ, with its connections and regions predominantly enriched in the ventral-attention, frontal-parietal, and default-mode networks that support higher-order cognition. This subtype also demonstrated distinct neuroanatomical features, including a subtype-specific cortical thickness change pattern unrelated to SCZ or bipolar disorder, as well as subtype-specific brain epicenters, such as left posterior cingulate and rostral middle frontal regions. Our study demonstrates increased inter-individual variability in the structural connectome of SCZ and highlights the potential of connectome-based subtyping approaches for characterizing disease heterogeneity related to pathophysiological processes.

Título: Aging rate indicators and the search for anti-aging drugs.
Resumen: Evidence that drugs, diets, and single-gene mutations can slow aging and extend the healthy lifespan of mammals has begun to convert biogerontology from an observational science into one based on interventions that could provide people with additional years of healthy, productive life. However, the research and development of anti-aging drugs is hampered by the lack of instantaneous and continuous measures of the rate of aging itself. This article presents recent work on anti-aging drugs that are effective in mice, provides evidence for candidate "aging rate indicators" (ARIs), and outlines a roadmap for translating these into clinical research to slow aging in humans. Thus far, 14 agents or combinations have significantly increased the lifespan of mice in studies conducted under the Interventions Testing Program (ITP) of the National Institute on Aging, often when initiated in late adulthood. Recent evidence suggests that many, perhaps all, interventions that slow aging in mice induce common, shared changes in physiological status and molecular pathways. We have proposed 12 such mechanisms as candidate ARIs, i.e., measurable outcomes that reflect a slow-aging state and that could discriminate between normal mice (and perhaps humans) and those exposed to effective anti-aging interventions-thereby accelerating research. Research priorities now include testing the robustness of these ARIs, extending them to include plasma constituents, elucidating the mechanisms through which diverse interventions alter them, uncovering the links between the ARIs and late-life diseases, and extending research to dogs, non-human primates, and humans. The growing recognition of the legitimacy and promise of evidence-based interventions resulting from aging biology should elevate this field to a level of urgency and respect comparable to that of current research on individual age-related conditions.

Título: Investigating the role of artificial intelligence in predicting risk factors after liver transplantation: A systematic review.
Resumen: Liver transplantation (LT) is the treatment of choice for patients with end-stage liver disease, yet its success is often compromised by serious complications such as acute kidney injury (AKI), graft failure, recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and infections. Recent advances in AI-especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL)-offer promising tools for predicting these outcomes and supporting early clinical interventions. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the performance and limitations of AI-based models in predicting key post-LT complications. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were comprehensively searched from January 2000 to December 2025. Studies applying AI algorithms to predict post-LT outcomes in humans were included. Non-English-language articles, non-original studies, and articles without predictive modelling were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, including study design, AI type, input data, validation method, and performance metrics. Due to high heterogeneity, no meta-analysis was performed. Of 6,744 articles identified, 14 met the inclusion criteria. ML models (eg, random forest, XGBoost, support vector machines, and neural networks) were used in most studies; DL architectures (eg, CNNs, DeepSurv, and CapsNets) were used in a few, and reported AUROC ranges were 0.61-0.96. Only four studies used external validation. Commonly predicted outcomes included AKI, HCC recurrence, sepsis, graft-versus-host disease, and malignancy. AI algorithms show strong potential for predicting post-LT complications, particularly when ensemble or imaging-based DL models are used. However, limited validation and interpretability remain challenges. Future research should focus on multicentre validation, transparent reporting, and clinical integration.

Título: Advancing Near-Term Water Quality Forecasting with Explainable Machine Learning and Probabilistic Uncertainty Quantification.
Resumen: Phytoplankton blooms threaten drinking-water security, yet translating high-frequency monitoring data into timely, reliable, and interpretable forecasts remains challenging. To address these limitations, we present here an end-to-end framework integrating an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) ML with automated hyperparameter optimization, bootstrap-ensemble uncertainty quantification, and interpretability through SHapley additive exPlanations (SHAP), which we applied to forecast phytoplankton in a water-supply reservoir. This lightweight transferable framework advances mechanistic understanding of phytoplankton dynamics and supports proactive, risk-informed water-quality management.
