Título: A deep learning-based silhouette gait detection framework for fall risk classification in Parkinson's disease.
Resumen: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a rapidly growing neurodegenerative disorder associated with gait impairment, functional decline, and increased fall risk. Conventional clinical assessments rely heavily on brief observational scales and are limited by subjectivity and environmental bias. There is a pressing need for objective, quantitative, and scalable digital assessment tools to support precision management of PD. This study aimed to develop and validate a smartphone-video-based gait assessment system aligned with a clinically meaningful pathway encompassing PD screening, functional evaluation, and fall risk classification. Gait videos were recorded using smartphone cameras and processed through a silhouette extraction pipeline. For S&E ADL functional grading, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 88.5% across three functional categories (80, 90, and 100%). For fall risk classification, the model achieved an accuracy of 91.1%, a sensitivity of 68.4%, a specificity of 98.3%, and an AUC of 0.909. Overall, the framework demonstrated robust performance across PD screening, functional stratification, and fall risk classification tasks. This study developed a smartphone-video-based gait assessment framework using computer vision and deep learning. The proposed framework demonstrated strong performance in PD identification, severity estimation, and fall risk classification. Future work will expand validation across diverse populations and disease stages, while advancing toward multimodal integration and long-term home monitoring.

Título: CatRange enables robust prediction of enzyme variant kinetic regimes.
Resumen: Predicting enzyme kinetics directly from sequence remains a central challenge in computational biology, particularly for mutations at catalytically essential residues. Existing models often default to wild-type predictions even when mutations cause substantial activity loss. This limits their utility for enzyme design and mechanistic inference. This formulation reflects the order-of-magnitude scale at which enzyme kinetics are commonly interpreted. It reduces sensitivity to assay variability while preserving distinctions among functional catalytic and binding states. Using joint enzyme-substrate representations and gradient-boosted classifiers, CatRange predicts kinetic ranges for wild-type and mutant enzymes across held-out, out-of-distribution, and few-shot mutation settings. The model achieves robust order-of-magnitude recovery and class-balanced discrimination. Moreover, it captures mutation-induced transitions across kinetic regimes, including activity losses caused by perturbations of annotated catalytic residues. CatRange also identifies nonenzyme sequence inputs. Together, CatLog and CatRange provide an interpretable, mutation-sensitive framework for enzyme engineering and kinetic metabolic modeling.

PRISM therefore provides a framework for reproducibly assigning blood count-based risk thresholds to prioritise clonal haematopoiesis screening in populations at risk for myeloid neoplasia. Título: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
Resumen: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. We critically synthesize evidence across diverse chemical classes (flavonoids, polyphenols, pentacyclic triterpenes, alkaloids, anthraquinones, tannins, polysaccharides, and marine bioactive metabolites), bridging computational predictions with established mechanistic milestones. Furthermore, we provide a deep critical appraisal of core methodological bottlenecks-target prediction bias, publication bias of over-studied hub genes, arbitrary pharmacokinetic cutoffs, circular virtual docking, and lack of renal bioavailability validation. Finally, we formulate a forward-looking translational roadmap integrating single-cell transcriptomics, humanized 3D organoid co-cultures, spatial multi-omics, reverse validation in longitudinal clinical registries, and machine learning feature selection, providing rigorous guidance for precision anti-urolithic drug discovery.

Título: Pulmonary malignant lymphoma requiring surgical lung biopsy for diagnosis following coronavirus disease 2019 infection: a case report.
Resumen: Pulmonary involvement by peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS), is an exceedingly rare extranodal manifestation with nonspecific radiological and clinical features. Prospective external validation, standardized image acquisition, transparent model reporting, calibration assessment, and evaluation in diverse populations are required before clinical deployment. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261444857, PROSPERO CRD420261444857.

Título: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
Resumen: Windowed electroencephalography (EEG) pipelines can produce misleadingly high performance when segments from the same participant occur in both training and testing. We define this contamination as <i>window leakage</i> and test it in two clinically and technically distinct public cohorts: 121 children (61 attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder [ADHD], 60 controls) and 149 adults (100 Parkinson's disease, 49 controls). Signals were harmonized to 18 common channels and 128 Hz. All primary models used stratified 8-fold participant-disjoint evaluation, 50%-overlapping windows, participant-level probability aggregation, and validation participants drawn exclusively from each outer-training fold. A deliberately contaminated Random Forest audit contrasted random-window and participant-disjoint splitting. Random-window balanced accuracy reached 95.59% in ADHD and 92.02% in Parkinson's, but fell to 60.98% and 56.17%, respectively, when participants were held out. Thus, the inflation replicated across disorders, ages, recording tasks, and acquisition systems. Under correct evaluation, CNN-LSTM achieved the highest ADHD subject-level balanced accuracy (73.21%), whereas EEGNet achieved the highest Parkinson's balanced accuracy (63.75%). No architecture comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction. One-, 2-, 4-, and 8-s windows produced no consistent cross-cohort ranking. Removing ATCNN-SA components also yielded dataset-dependent changes, and no ablation difference was significant after correction. Participant-bootstrap intervals remained wide despite tens of thousands of windows, indicating that inferential precision was governed by participant count rather than segment count. Window-level random splits contaminate clinical EEG performance estimates and must not be used to claim generalization to unseen individuals. Participants should be separated before model fitting, results should be reported at subject level, and split, windowing, aggregation, and uncertainty procedures should be disclosed explicitly.

The cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets using stratified sampling. Recursive feature elimination identified eight predictors: age, prealbumin, albumin, cholinesterase, lymphocyte percentage, platelet count, fibrinogen and serum calcium. Eight conventional machine learning algorithms, TabICLv2 and SuperLearner ensembles were evaluated using discrimination, calibration and decision curve analyses. SHapley Additive exPlanations were used for model interpretation. Among 1196 patients, 507 (42.4%) developed postoperative mGPS=2. In the internal validation cohort, TabICLv2 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.753 (95% confidence interval, 0.701-0.804) and a Brier score of 0.197. SuperLearner-W and SuperLearner-SR showed comparable discrimination, with areas under the curve of 0.752 and 0.751, respectively. Lymphocyte percentage, platelet count and fibrinogen were the leading contributors to model predictions. Learning-curve analysis revealed suboptimal convergence behaviour, with relatively flat cross-validation trajectories and persistent separation from training performance across increasing training fractions. A web-based research prototype was developed to provide individualised risk estimates, patient-level feature attribution and an applicability-domain assessment indicating the level of support from the model-development data. An interpretable model based on routinely available preoperative variables provided moderate discrimination for postoperative inflammatory-nutritional deterioration after colorectal cancer surgery. The suboptimal learning-curve convergence indicates that the model is not suitable for clinical deployment without further development and independent external validation.

Título: Condition-dependent success of resource-based reproductive tactics across both sexes in <i>Drosophila prolongata</i>.
Resumen: Because reproductive tactics vary in their energetic and fitness costs, individuals may increase their reproductive success by aligning their tactics with their physical condition. In resource-based mating systems, monopolizing valuable patches is energetically costly, yet potentially highly rewarding for males. In females, mating near resources may reduce the cost of mate search and assessment. However, the balance of costs and benefits associated with a given tactic may shift with an individual's condition. Here we studied this in the fruit fly <i>Drosophila prolongata</i>. In arenas containing resource-dense areas (RDAs) typically used as territories, we tracked the individual positions and behaviors of flies in groups using machine-learning-based pose estimation and behavioral classification. We found that large, high-condition males achieved elevated mating success through territoriality and courtship, whilst small males obtained copulations through high mobility, consistent with a scramble competition tactic. Female behavior was also condition dependent: large females spent more time in RDAs, mated sooner at those sites, and thus reinforced territory-based sexual selection, whereas small females mated later and more frequently outside RDAs, potentially avoiding harassment costs. In addition, we detected size-disassortative pairings, suggesting that the complex cost-benefit interactions encountered by females of varying condition can lead to counter-intuitive associations. However, given the limited duration of our observations and the high remating rate in this species, the prevalence of this disassortative mating pattern over longer time scales warrants further investigation. Our findings reveal how resource distribution and individual condition may interact to maintain multiple reproductive tactics in both sexes. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s00265-026-03739-z.

Título: From metric to model: a five-stage pipeline for building and sustaining valid AI predictive systems in consumer neuroscience.
Resumen: The application of machine learning to consumer neuroscience has made it possible, in principle, to predict consumer responses from media assets alone. However, the pursuit of model sophistication has outpaced attention to a foundational constraint: the quality of any predictive artificial intelligence (AI) system is bounded by the quality of the neurophysiological and biometric data used to train it, and by the rigor of the modeling procedures applied to those data. This article argues that persistent problems of low metric reliability, poor cross-metric consistency, and the broader replication crisis have left the field building predictive systems on an insecure measurement foundation. Anchored in the framework for neurometric validation established by Ramsøy (2019), the paper offers a conceptual synthesis and agenda-setting framework for the AI era: a five-stage pipeline comprising (1) Metric Mapping, the theory-driven identification and pre-screening of candidate neurophysiological and biometric measures; (2) Psychometric Validation, the formal assessment of each metric's sensitivity, specificity, validity, and reliability; (3) Discriminatory Ability, an assessment of whether a metric produces meaningful score distributions across real-world commercial stimuli; (4) Principled Data Scaling and Model Development, covering both the large-scale data collection and the modeling and validation procedures required for robust prediction; and (5) Model Governance and Drift Prevention, the ongoing monitoring, retraining, and calibration required to maintain predictive validity over time. The individual components draw on established practice in psychometrics, measurement science, and applied machine learning; the contribution lies in integrating them into a coherent, domain-specific architecture for consumer neuroscience, and in making explicit a criterion-Discriminatory Ability-that is widely assumed but rarely tested in applied advertising research. The pipeline is offered not as a validated standard but as a structured research agenda and a basis for future work on standardization, certification, and governance, with the aim of shifting the field from a model-centric toward a validation-centric culture.

These findings reflect participants' perceptions rather than objectively measured diagnostic performance. Four machine learning survival models-decision tree, random survival forest, gradient boosting survival analysis, and an XGBoost-based accelerated failure time model (XGBAFT)-were trained for OS prediction and interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Performance was assessed by Harrell's concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis, and benchmarked against the eighth-edition American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) TNM staging system. The development cohort was predominantly male (53.2%) and aged over 65 years (61.6%); 28.9% underwent radical resection of the primary site and 47.6% received chemotherapy, with a median observed survival of 8 months. For CSS, the corresponding C-indices were 0.726 and 0.710, with AUCs of 0.813/0.797/0.760 and 0.792/0.712/0.702. Both nomograms outperformed the eighth-edition TNM system (OS C-index, 0.585; CSS C-index, 0.635) and showed good calibration and net clinical benefit. Among the machine learning models, XGBAFT achieved the highest discrimination (AUCs, 0.861/0.834/0.831 internally and 0.807/0.803/0.789 temporally). SHAP identified chemotherapy, primary-site radical surgery, regional lymph node surgery as the most influential predictors. The nomogram stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups with significantly divergent survival curves (P<0.001). Within the SEER population, our dCCA-specific nomograms and the XGBAFT model provided accurate, well-calibrated, and interpretable predictions of OS and CSS, outperformed eighth-edition TNM staging, and supported effective risk stratification. Because both cohorts were drawn from SEER, these results constitute internal and temporal validation; prospective multicenter studies in geographically and ethnically diverse cohorts are required before clinical implementation.

However, reconstructing high-fidelity 3D volumes from extremely noisy projections, particularly under the interference of structural heterogeneity, remains a challenging task. Traditional Fourier-domain methods often suffer from frequency-dependent signal attenuation and uneven information distribution. While recent deep-learning-based frameworks attempt to predict high-frequency components directly in frequency space, they are highly susceptible to noise and often introduce artifacts. State-of-the-art (SOTA) real-space method circumvents Fourier-domain defects, yet remains constrained by the inherent spectral bias of multi-layer perceptrons, as fixed positional encoding fails to sufficiently capture intricate high-frequency details. We propose cryoTriplane, a real-space 3D homogeneous reconstruction network that utilizes a hybrid spatial representation to adaptively capture fine structural details. By combining fixed positional encoding for noise-robust structural initialization with structure-aware positional encoding for high-frequency refinement, our method achieves 3D reconstructions that are simultaneously globally consistent and locally fine-grained. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations across five simulated and four real-world datasets demonstrate that cryoTriplane significantly outperforms existing methods in resolving fine structural features. Furthermore, validation through downstream atomic modeling underscores cryoTriplane's ability to recover high-quality density maps. Specifically, our method achieves sequence coverage improvements of 4.6% and 5.5% on the EMPIAR-10005 and EMPIAR-10492 datasets over the SOTA approach, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/chengyr1999/CryoTriplane. The real datasets used in this study are publicly available from EMPIAR.

Título: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives.
Resumen: Molecular Hessians, the second derivatives of the potential energy, are fundamental to many workflows in computational chemistry. Usually, accurate Hessians are computationally expensive to calculate and scale poorly with system size, whether computed using quantum chemistry methods or machine learning interatomic potentials. Here we introduce Hessian Interatomic Potentials (HIPs), a deep learning model that directly predicts Hessians without relying on automatic differentiation or finite differences. To do so, we construct SE(3)-equivariant, symmetric Hessians from irreducible representation (irrep) features up to degree l = 2, computed by a graph neural network. HIP Hessians are one to two orders of magnitude faster, more accurate, more memory efficient, easier to train and exhibit favorable scaling with system size. We validate our predictions across a wide range of downstream tasks, demonstrating consistently superior performance in transition state search, geometry optimization, zero-point energy corrections and vibrational analysis. We open source the HIP code and model weights.

Collectively, these findings show that cRCC constitute intensive structural properties of protein interfaces, remaining invariant to the molecular weight of the interacting partner. Consequently, this framework provides a novel computational strategy to prioritize druggable PPI targets for small-molecule discovery and guide the rational design of synthetic protein interfaces.

Título: Language extinction and diversification: The two sides of the same coin.
Resumen: Language extinction is conventionally treated as a conservation crisis to be arrested, and language diversification as a historical explanandum to be reconstructed. The two phenomena are studied separately, by different communities, with different methods. This separation is theoretically incoherent. Extinction and diversification are reciprocal outcomes of a single evolutionary dynamic operating on four nested scales of linguistic organisation. Whether a given dynamic is labelled "extinction" or "diversification" depends on the observer's reference frame, not on the mechanism. I integrate lexical diffusion (Wang), utterance selection (Croft), feature-pool ecology (Mufwene), iterated learning (Kirby), agent-based simulation (Gong et al.), and the Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (Laland et al.). A worked numerical example, using a Pólya-urn model with the Price-equation decomposition, demonstrates that identical micro-dynamics produce divergence or replacement depending on a single pair of ecological parameters (inter-group contact × prestige alignment). Five falsifiable predictions follow, each with a concrete operationalisation, from symmetric sign-reversal of endangerment predictors in phylogenetic diversification data, to measurable Large Language Model (LLM) induced diversity collapse in post-2022 corpora. The framework reframes revitalisation policy (target niche conditions, not feature prescription), Artificial Intelligence (AI) design (diversity as a reward signal, not an afterthought), and the conceptual status of endangered languages (ecologically reconstructible, not ontologically tragic). Language extinction and language diversification are not opposing phenomena; they are the same evolutionary process running in two directions. A single multi-level selection framework that spans sub-lexical, feature-pool, population, and machine-mediated scales predicts both divergence and death, and a tractable Pólya-urn simulation shows how identical micro-dynamics flip between the two under one ecological parameter.

Título: Demystifying the influence of ion-surface interface science for the effective design of hydrogen storage tanks.
Resumen: Hydrogen storage tank design has traditionally been described through separate mechanical, thermal, structural, and regulatory frameworks that share no common physical vocabulary. This review argues instead that these descriptions rest on a single underlying layer, the ion-surface interface, and develops that argument through an explicit four-tier dependency hierarchy rather than a flat enumeration of coupled interfaces. Tier 1 establishes the material-hydrogen interface as the domain in which ion-surface interface science applies in the literal, mechanistic sense, governed by hybridization-dependent dissociation barriers, defect-mediated trapping, and, only where a genuine electrolyte is present, electric-double-layer behavior; electric-double-layer language is deliberately withheld from dry gas-phase and solid-state systems, for which charge-transfer and orbital-hybridization descriptions are shown to be the physically correct alternative. Tiers 3 and 4 are shown to be connected to this physical core only indirectly, as an engineering-response layer and a statistical risk-governance layer respectively, correcting the logical inconsistency of treating structural, safety, and regulatory constraints as coequal expressions of interfacial physics. Within this framework, hydrogen embrittlement is resolved mechanistically across hydrogen-enhanced decohesion, localized plasticity, strain-induced vacancy formation, and hydride-induced cracking, with condition-dependent thresholds established across four independent alloy systems, quantitative isosteric-heat and ionic-modifier comparisons are developed for material-based storage, and route-specific rate-limiting mechanisms are stated explicitly in place of a single blanket claim. The review closes by developing a cross-scale parameter-passing framework linking first-principles, atomistic, continuum, and data-driven methods, illustrated by a demonstrated closed-loop machine-learning materials-discovery example, and by identifying the specific, named gaps, in tank-level integration of physisorptive materials, in strategy-specific cost data, and in a fully quantitative design-rule synthesis, that remain open for the field.

The H insertion in SrMnO2.5 stabilizes high-spin Mn2+ (d5) without requiring strongly distorted tetrahedral or planar MnO4 coordination associated with the VO•• formation, while the large exchange splitting in SrFeO2.5 raises the energy of the electron-accepting states and limits H insertion. These findings establish the mechanism by which the electronic structure of transition metals governs the competition between hydrogenation and VO••formation in TMOs.

The model directly predicts per-frequency-bin occupancy masks from normalized PSD vectors, thereby simultaneously achieving signal detection and parameter estimation (center frequency and bandwidth). Extensive experiments on 67,200 synthetic broadband PSDs and 820 real-world UAV PSD samples demonstrate the effectiveness of SpecUNeSt-MLP. Across all tested SNR levels (from -4 dB to 8 dB), SpecUNeSt-MLP consistently outperforms LAD, FCN, SS-CNN, and SS-LSTM in terms of detection probability, false alarm rate, and average localization error. Compared with the recent RMP baseline, SpecUNeSt-MLP achieves better performance under low-SNR conditions while maintaining comparable performance at higher SNR levels, with only one-sixth of the parameter count of RMP. These results demonstrate that SpecUNeSt-MLP provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for fine-grained spectrum sensing in complex electromagnetic environments.

Título: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials.

Título: Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging.
Resumen: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.

Título: Machine learning based spectral fitting and atomic physics corrections for the main ion charge exchange recombination spectroscopy system on the DIII-D tokamak (invited).
Resumen: Rapid and accurate machine learning (ML) based analysis of the Doppler broadened and shifted Balmer-α spectra from the main ion charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (MICER) diagnostic on the DIII-D tokamak has been developed to provide raw measurements of the main ion (typically D+) temperature, toroidal rotation, density, and beam emission based measurements directly from the active Balmer-α spectra. The temperatures and toroidal rotations are typically within 150 eV and 10 km/s of those obtained from the standard least squares fitting approach. The complexity of the MICER spectra and associated corrections has historically limited analysis to high priority discharges, despite the wealth of information contained in the spectra. These advances have dramatically reduced the analysis time for single discharges from several hours to seconds. The speed-up now allows bulk analysis of thousands of historical discharges acquired by the diagnostic during its 12+ years of operation on DIII-D, enabling a variety of studies, such as those involving H-mode main ion pedestal profiles.

Compared with histopathology, magnetic resonance spectroscopy achieved a sensitivity of 87.5%, specificity of 46.2%, positive predictive value of 83.3%, negative predictive value of 54.5%, accuracy of 77.4%, F1-score of 85.4%, and balanced accuracy of 66.8%. The seven false-positive cases were characterised as metastasis in three cases, abscess in three cases, and other non-high-grade pathology in one case. The best exploratory ML model was Random Forest with magnetic resonance spectroscopy diagnosis included, achieving an accuracy of 73.6% and an AUC of 0.646. However, this did not improve upon the diagnostic performance of radiologist-derived magnetic resonance spectroscopy diagnosis alone. In this small fully histopathology-confirmed neuro-oncology cohort, magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated good sensitivity but limited specificity for predicting high-grade glioma. Rather than presenting this pattern as a new diagnostic phenomenon, this study contributes a clinically grounded confirmation with complete tissue verification, a clearly characterised false-positive mimic profile, and a transparent negative ML result. These findings support the use of magnetic resonance spectroscopy as an adjunctive metabolic neuroimaging tool and provide a cautious data point for future larger studies evaluating spectroscopy-guided and ML-supported diagnostic pathways.

ID (PMID): 42866681
Título: Validation design and experimental provenance shape apparent machine-learning transferability in legacy Mössbauer spectroscopy.
Resumen: Machine-learning models in chemistry are increasingly trained on values compiled from many published papers and are usually validated by splitting the records at random or by publication; the latter assumes that each publication is an independent experiment. We tested this assumption in a legacy <sup>57</sup>Fe Mössbauer corpus. All 45 source publications were re-examined against their original tables and figures, and papers reporting the same alloy composition with the same fitted spectral areas were identified and checked against the sources. Eleven publications reported measurements on three shared specimen series, so the corpus formed 37 experimental-provenance groups containing 171 model-eligible sample states. The target was an operational high-field ferromagnetic spectral fraction, not a martensite phase fraction. At a matched test-set size, median <i>R</i> <sup>2</sup> fell from 0.670 under random state-level splitting to 0.322 when publications were held out and 0.287 when provenance groups were held out. With the test states held fixed, retaining related publications in training was associated with a median reduction in apparent error of 6.72 percentage points, which varied strongly between clusters and partly reflects the larger training set. The flexible chemistry-and-temperature model reached a pooled <i>R</i> <sup>2</sup> of 0.422 against 0.354 for a calibrated martensite-start comparator but had the lower error in only 17 of 37 groups (group-balanced difference in mean absolute error -1.73 percentage points; 95% CI -7.87 to +4.52). Transferability improved as the evidence base expanded, although provenance-group count could not be isolated as the cause, and a retrospective open-access audit added only 12 model-eligible states. Thus, a publication identifier, which records the paper a value came from, does not guarantee experimental independence, validation design can change the apparent <i>R</i> <sup>2</sup> by more than a factor of two, and a pooled advantage need not hold when each experiment is weighted equally. We provide practical recommendations for machine learning on literature-derived chemistry data and release the curated corpus, provenance assignments and code.

Título: MXene-Based Lithium-Ion Anodes: An Outlook on Computational Predictions and Experimental Validation.
Resumen: First-principles studies have produced extensive predictions of MXene-anode capacities, voltages, and diffusion barriers over the past decade. Yet, a gap remains between these predicted metrics and the performance observed in operating cells. We suggest that this gap reflects not a limitation of computation itself but the absence of a sustained feedback loop between computational and experimental work. Computational predictions are often communicated and cited as performance forecasts even though they describe idealized systems (bare or uniformly terminated surfaces, equilibrium conditions, and the absence of electrolyte, interphase, and cycling history) that differ from the environment of an operating anode. We propose that the progress of MXene-anode research be measured by how closely computation and experiment inform each other.

Título: Visual cues in MI-BCI induce biases in EEG classification models with deep learning but not with standard machine learning.
Resumen: Deep learning classification methods are increasingly popular in the brain-computer interface (BCI) field due to their ability to learn complex, non-linear representations from EEG data. Unlike traditional machine learning approaches, which typically rely on hand-crafted features, deep learning models autonomously extract spatio-temporal features directly from the raw or minimally preprocessed signal. However, this flexibility may come at the cost of reduced interpretability and increased susceptibility to confounding factors. This study aims to investigate whether the inclusion of task-related visual cues in the input EEG window biases deep learning models by leading them to exploit irrelevant features, thereby compromising their neurophysiological validity. This study investigates how including EEG signals measured during visual cue presentation on classification accuracy and feature extraction in motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs. Three classification pipelines were evaluated: CSP+LDA, a traditional machine learning approach; DeepConvNet, a convolutional neural network for EEG classification; and REVE, a Transformer-based EEG foundation model. All methods are trained and tested on two large scale open-access EEG datasets using two epoching strategies, with or without including the visual cue onset, to assess their impact on model performance and neurophysiological relevance. Attribution maps (e.g., Saliency maps) and CSP patterns are used to interpret the features learned by each model. Including the visual cue onset significantly improved the classification accuracy of DeepConvNet and REVE. However, attribution analysis showed that the model mainly relied on early parietal activations, most likely cue-related visual evoked potentials, rather than MI-related sensorimotor rhythms (ERD/ERS), which were more prominent when the cue onset was excluded. In contrast, CSP+LDA showed minimal accuracy changes across conditions, with consistent motor cortex activation patterns. These findings demonstrate that higher classification performance does not necessarily imply neurophysiological validity. In particular, deep learning models may exploit confounding signals, such as visual cue processing, which undermines their interpretability and applicability in asynchronous or real-world BCIs, in which there is no such cue. We advocate for systematically applying explainability tools in BCI research to ensure classifiers rely on task-relevant brain activity. Additionally, we emphasize the importance of excluding visual cue periods from EEG segments containing reposenses evoked by the visual cue onset from the input to deep learning models.

Título: Applications of artificial intelligence in personalized nutrition interventions.
Resumen: Unhealthy dietary patterns remain a major modifiable contributor to the global burden of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, individuals can respond markedly differently to identical foods, limiting the effectiveness of one-size-fits-all dietary guidance. This review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to personalized nutrition interventions across three interconnected layers. At the biological level, inter-individual variability can be characterized by three mechanistic dimensions: nutrigenomic variation, which influences nutrient metabolism and disease susceptibility; metabolomic biomarkers, which objectively capture dietary exposure and early metabolic alterations; and the gut microbiome, which bidirectionally mediates diet-host interactions. At the technological level, AI integrates these dimensions into multimodal digital profiles. Machine learning models predict individual postprandial glycemic and lipemic responses, with reported correlations of up to r = 0.77 in large cohorts; deep learning and computer vision automate dietary assessment; natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) support nutrition counseling; knowledge graphs enable constraint-aware food recommendations; and digital-twin and adaptive closed-loop systems incorporating continuous glucose monitoring and wearable-device data support real-time nutritional interventions. However, the strength of clinical evidence varies across disease domains. Glycemic management in T2DM and prediabetes currently has the most mature randomized controlled trial evidence: an AI-enabled personalized intervention combining algorithmic dietary personalization with CGM-linked feedback improved glycemic endpoints compared with a Mediterranean diet, while a fully automated AI-delivered diabetes prevention program achieved outcomes non-inferior to those of human coaching. In obesity, cardiovascular disease, oncology, and gastrointestinal disorders, the evidence remains mixed or preliminary. Clinical translation also faces substantial challenges, including biased and inconsistently standardized dietary and multi-omics data; the underrepresentation of non-European populations, which limits model generalizability and raises concerns about health equity; limited model explainability; privacy and data-governance challenges; immature regulatory pathways for adaptive software as a medical device; and specific risks associated with LLMs, such as hallucinated or guideline-discordant dietary advice. AI-enabled personalized nutrition is therefore progressing from proof of concept toward clinical translation. Realizing its potential equitably will require multi-ethnic nutrition-omics cohorts, privacy-preserving multicenter collaboration, dietitian-led human-AI collaboration, and lifecycle safety governance for generative models.

Título: FAMUS: a few-shot learning framework for large-scale protein annotation.
Resumen: Gene function prediction is pivotal in genomic and metagenomic data analysis. Here, we present Functional Annotation Method Using Supervised contrastive learning (FAMUS). FAMUS compares query sequences to a full array of profile Hidden Markov Models, encoding each sequence's complete similarity profile, rather than only its top-scoring hit, into a condensed vector space that minimizes the distance between proteins from the same family. Título: An Extensive Review of Recent Progress In Kinase-targeting Antimalarial Drug Discovery.
Resumen: Malaria remains a major global health challenge, with the rise of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains necessitating the development of novel therapeutic strategies. Kinases, which regulate essential processes throughout the parasite life cycle, including invasion, egress, development, proliferation, gametogenesis, and transmission, have emerged as promising drug targets, leading to significant advances in kinase inhibitor development over the past five years. This review examines recent advances in kinase-targeted antimalarial drug discovery, with particular emphasis on inhibitor scaffolds, SARs, target selectivity, biological efficacy across multiple parasite life stages, and mechanisms of kinase inhibition. A literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 2019 and 2024. Studies reporting computational, biochemical, cellular, or in vivo evaluations of inhibitors targeting P. falciparum kinases were examined. Particular attention is given to inhibitors of calcium-dependent protein kinases, AGC kinases, including PKA, PKB, and PKG, CMGC kinases, phosphoinositide lipid kinases, NIMA-related kinases, aurora-related kinases, and orphan kinases. The integration of high-throughput screening, molecular docking, virtual screening, machine-learning approaches, and structure-guided optimization has accelerated the identification of lead compounds. Several inhibitors demonstrated nanomolar enzymatic or cellular potency, multistage antiplasmodial activity, and encouraging selectivity over human kinases. Nevertheless, challenges involving target validation, kinase selectivity, pharmacokinetic properties, toxicity, resistance liability, and translation from computational or biochemical activity to in vivo efficacy remain. Continued research integrating biological validation, selectivity profiling, and pharmacokinetic optimization is crucial for translating promising kinase inhibitors into innovative, effective, and durable antimalarial treatments capable of reducing the global burden of malaria.

ID (PMID): 42864796
Título: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence-driven Approaches in the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetes and Diabetes-Associated Complications.
Resumen: Diabetes mellitus is a global health issue with escalating metabolic dysfunction, clinical heterogeneity, and rising microvascular and macrovascular consequences. Traditional diabetes diagnosis, risk assessment, treatment selection, and complication surveillance rely on periodic clinical measures and population-level risk models, which may not fully capture dynamic, individualized disease pathways. Precision diabetes treatment is being transformed by Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and multimodal data analytics. This review critically examines AI-driven approaches to diabetes management, including early disease prediction, diagnostic support, glycemic monitoring, treatment-response prediction, and the prevention and detection of diabetes-associated complications. The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has sanctioned multiple AI/ML-based medical devices for automated retinal screening, clinical diagnostic assistance, and patient self-management applications. For clinically meaningful patterns and disease progression prediction, AI-enabled analysis of continuous glucose monitoring data, retinal images, electronic health records, wearable device signals, laboratory parameters, and multi-omics datasets is prioritized. The use of AI for detecting diabetic retinopathy, kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, neuropathy, and foot disorders is also highlighted.Data quality, algorithmic bias, interpretability, privacy, cybersecurity, model drift, regulatory monitoring, clinical validation, and equitable access prevent widespread application despite promising results. This study offers a thorough and critical assessment of the developing roles of AI, specifically ML and DL, in the prediction, diagnosis, and management of diabetes and its related complications. Real-world validation, standardized evaluation frameworks, trustworthy AI, and effective human- AI collaboration will drive advancement. AI could transform diabetes management into predictive, tailored, continuous, and complication-preventive care.

ID (PMID): 42864751
Título: Ultrahigh Interfacial Thermal Conductance across GaN/BAs Interfaces via Atomic-Level Engineering.
Resumen: The integration of gallium nitride (GaN) with ultrahigh-thermal-conductivity boron arsenide (BAs) substrates represents a promising pathway for developing next-generation high-power devices. The heat dissipation capability of such integrated systems is fundamentally governed by thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces, and buffer layers such as Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> have been widely adopted to accommodate lattice mismatch and facilitate heterointegration. However, the atomic-scale structural factors governing thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces remain unclear, limiting further improvements in interfacial thermal conductance. Herein, we propose an atomic-scale interfacial structural-uniformity strategy for engineering ultrahigh thermal conductance across GaN/BAs interfaces using molecular dynamics simulations augmented by machine-learning interatomic potentials. We show that interfacial structural uniformity plays a more important role than individual bond strength in determining thermal transport across the investigated GaN/BAs interfaces. For instance, the As-N-terminated coherent interface exhibits the highest interfacial structural uniformity and achieves an ultrahigh interfacial thermal conductance of approximately 2000 MW·m<sup>-</sup> <sup>2</sup>·K<sup>-</sup> <sup>1</sup>, representing a nearly eightfold enhancement over the experimentally reported Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>-mediated interface (250 MW·m<sup>-2</sup>·K<sup>-1</sup>). Finite-element analysis indicates that this atomic-scale optimization directly translates into device-scale performance, leading to a substantial improvement in overall heat dissipation efficiency. These findings suggest that engineering interfacial structural uniformity offers a promising strategy for achieving high-efficiency thermal management in next-generation high-power electronic devices.

ID (PMID): 42864667
Título: Micro-CT radiomics reveals the microcalcification-surrounding tissue interface as the diagnostic epicenter of breast microcalcifications.
Resumen: In clinical breast imaging, microcalcifications (MCs) are routinely interpreted as small radiological signs, typically analyzed in clusters. They guide radiologists in assessing breast lesions and determining the likelihood of malignancy. Yet, increasing biological evidence indicates that active processes occur not only within the calcified core but also in the microcalcification-surrounding tissue microenvironment (MCST). This raises the possibility that current assessments may overlook critical diagnostic information embedded in the MCST. However, conventional mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) lack the spatial resolution required to determine where diagnostic information truly resides. We used a high-resolution (≈8 μm) 3D micro-CT scanner to scan 94 paraffin-embedded breast biopsy blocks, from which 3504 individual MCs were segmented to obtain a binary 3D mask ([Formula: see text]) for each MC. Unlike previous studies analyzing clustered MCs at mammographic resolution, our analysis operates at the level of individual MCs. Radiomic features were extracted from each MC and used to train machine-learning classifiers to predict the histopathological label (benign or malignant) of the lesion in which each MC occurred. To determine (i) whether discriminative information arises predominantly from the calcified core or from the MCST and (ii) to separate genuine tissue signal from preprocessing or segmentation effects, we conducted three complementary analyses. First, we held [Formula: see text] constant and varied only the size of the rectangular preprocessing window around [Formula: see text], i.e. the 3D region of grayscale data considered for feature computation. Second, we assessed robustness to segmentation by making small, incremental changes to [Formula: see text] (erosions to restrict the calcified core; dilations to extend into immediately adjacent tissue). Third, to test MCST-only signal, we classified MCs using features computed exclusively from concentric shells defined at incremental offsets from the [Formula: see text]: outer shells (thin layers of MCST just outside [Formula: see text]) and inner shells (thin layers within the calcified core, inside [Formula: see text]). Increasing the size of the preprocessing window around a constant [Formula: see text] improved classification performance (AUC ≈ 0.688 → 0.811), revealing strong contextual effects in radiomics feature extraction. Moderate mask dilations likewise improved performance (AUC ≈ 0.689 → 0.813), indicating that the diagnostic signal extends beyond the calcified core into the MCST. Remarkably, even when using only concentric shell features, classification performance remained high (AUC ≈ 0.81). This study provides the first imaging-based evidence - at micrometer scale and in 3D - pinpointing where the discriminative information of breast MCs arises: within the calcified core and/or the MCST? From a radiomics and technical standpoint, the preprocessing window matters: it should be controlled and reported, as it directly affects extracted features and can influence diagnostic performance. We find that MCST is the dominant source of discriminative information for classifying individual MCs as benign or malignant: classification using features computed exclusively from concentric shells performs on par with maximally dilated mask (encompassing both the core and MCST) but clearly exceeds calcified-core-only. These findings shift the interpretative focus of MC analysis from the calcified deposits themselves to their immediate microenvironment, suggesting that future biomarkers and quantitative features should target MCST.

ID (PMID): 42864658
Título: Using machine learning to evaluate a non-selective enhanced recovery pathway for hip and knee arthroplasty: perioperative factors associated with same-day and early discharge.
Resumen: Same-day and early discharge after total hip and knee arthroplasty (THA/TKA) depend not only on patient characteristics but on the perioperative pathway itself. This study used supervised machine learning (ML) to evaluate a universal, non-selective enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway at a high-volume tertiary centre, identifying the perioperative factors most strongly associated with failure of Day 0 or Day 1 discharge, and of same-day (Day 0) discharge. All patients undergoing primary THA, TKA, or partial knee replacement (PKR) within a universal, non-selective ERAS pathway (April 2024-May 2025) were included, with no exclusion on the basis of age, comorbidity, or anticipated day-case suitability. ML models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree) were developed in Python using the full set of preoperative, anaesthetic, and postoperative pathway variables, with SHAP used for interpretation. A total of 3,025 patients were included (median age 70.1 years, IQR 62.3-76.6). With discharge failure as the positive class, test ROC-AUC for failure of Day 0 or Day 1 discharge ranged from 0.66 to 0.76 (PR-AUC 0.34-0.50; baseline failure prevalence 18%). For same-day discharge failure, ROC-AUC ranged from 0.76 to 0.82 (F1 0.76-0.83; PR-AUC 0.89-0.93; baseline prevalence 73%). SHAP analysis ranked the factors most strongly associated with discharge failure. For same-day discharge, time to mobilisation was the most significant factor, followed by postoperative radiography before return to the ward and mobiliser designation. For Day 0 or Day 1 discharge, the strongest associations were ASA grade, sex, operative side, and time to mobilisation. Supervised ML is an effective framework for evaluating a non-selective ERAS pathway. Time to mobilisation dominated same-day discharge and was a leading factor for Day 0 or Day 1 discharge; it warrants prospective confirmation as a modifiable target.

Título: Machine learning-guided leaf margin classification and discovery that BcPHB promoter selection rewires a BcPHB-BcLMI1 module to shape leaf margins in Brassica campestris.
Resumen: The morphological diversification of leaf margins reflects the evolutionary reshaping of conserved developmental programs. However, fully deciphering the underlying molecular basis remains challenging due to difficulties in phenotype quantification and the incomplete characterization of complex regulatory networks. In this study, we established a computer-vision framework to decode leaf lobe trait and identified the HD-ZIP III factor PHABULOSA (BcPHB), combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and selective sweep analysis in Brassica campestris. We found that promoter variation defines two major haplotypes, BcPHB<sup>HapI</sup> and BcPHB<sup>HapII</sup>, driving divergent expression levels associated with entire and lobed leaves. Functionally, BcPHB knockdown lines (BcPHB<sup>ami</sup>) exhibited lobed margins, whereas complementation of lobed accessions with the BcPHB<sup>HapI</sup> promoter partially restored the entire-leaf phenotype. Similarly, overexpression of LATE MERISTEM IDENTITY 1 (BcLMI1), a conserved regulator of leaf lobation, phenocopied the BcPHB<sup>ami</sup> lines. Mechanistically, BcPHB and BcLMI1 form a reciprocal negative feedback loop that stabilizes margin patterning. Furthermore, domestication-driven selection of BcPHB<sup>HapI</sup> facilitated the transition from ancestral lobed leaves to cultivated entire forms. This study reveals a pivotal developmental module and illustrates how regulatory evolution drives morphological diversification in crops.

ID (PMID): 42864610
Título: Charting the rise of artificial intelligence in medical education: a global bibliometric and network analysis, 2000-2026.
Resumen: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral curiosity to a core feature of modern medical education through adaptive learning, simulation-based training, automated assessment, and large language models such as ChatGPT. Publication activity has accelerated rapidly, but the structure of this expanding literature has not been comprehensively mapped. Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy that combined medical education terms in the title field with artificial intelligence terms in the topic field. Articles, review articles, and data papers published from 2000 to 2026 were included. A total of 2,298 records were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analyses, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct keyword co-occurrence, country collaboration, and institutional collaboration networks. Data for 2026 represent a partial calendar year. Publication output remained limited until the late 2010s and rose sharply after 2021. Of the 2,298 records, 2,066 (89.9%) were published from 2021 to 2026, with the highest complete-year output in 2025 (821 publications). The United States led in publication volume (918 records) and raw citation count (14,582 citations), followed by the People's Republic of China (367 records; 4,404 citations). The Journal of Surgical Education published the most articles. Harvard Medical School led institutional output, whereas Stanford University and the University of California San Francisco had higher raw citation totals despite fewer publications. Artificial intelligence, medical education, ChatGPT, medical students, and machine learning were the most prominent keywords. Artificial intelligence in medical education is a rapidly expanding but geographically and institutionally concentrated field. Raw citation patterns differed from publication volume, although these unadjusted measures should not be interpreted as direct comparisons of research quality. Thematic patterns emphasize learner-facing applications, assessment, and generative AI, while responsible curricular integration and empirical evaluation remain important priorities. These findings are especially relevant to emergency medicine education, where simulation, time-sensitive decision-making, and competency assessment are central.

ID (PMID): 42864609
Título: A PCA-based deep feature optimization framework for explainable orange fruit disease classification.
Resumen: Accurate classification of orange fruit diseases is important for precision agriculture and yield protection. This study develops and rigorously benchmarks a hybrid deep-feature framework for classifying Black Spot, Canker, Fresh, and Greening oranges (1,090 images), combining deep feature extraction, PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and classical machine-learning classification. Eight backbones (seven CNNs and a Vision Transformer, ViT) and four classifiers (32 configurations in total) were evaluated under 5 × 5 repeated stratified cross-validation, with PCA fitted exclusively on training-fold features in every iteration to eliminate data leakage. The proposed ViT + PCA+SVM configuration achieved the highest mean accuracy, 99.12%±0.71%, significantly outperforming every CNN-based backbone, including DenseNet201 + PCA + SVM (98.48%±0.81%, p < 0.001). A dedicated variance-retention sensitivity analysis justifies the 98% threshold used throughout, and ablation experiments confirm that PCA substantially reduces feature dimensionality (by ~ 55.7% for ViT and ~ 76.6% for DenseNet201) without a significant loss of accuracy for either backbone. Explainability analysis - occlusion sensitivity and SHAP for the proposed ViT model, and Grad-CAM and SHAP for the DenseNet201 comparison model - shows that both configurations base predictions on biologically relevant, disease-affected regions of the fruit rather than spurious cues. These results identify ViT + PCA+SVM as the most accurate configuration evaluated, with DenseNet201 + PCA + SVM as a closely competitive, more compact convolutional alternative for intelligent orchard disease-monitoring systems.

ID (PMID): 42864600
Título: Deep learning reveals persistent individual signatures in bat echolocation calls of the greater leaf-nosed bat.
Resumen: Intraspecific variation is a prerequisite for natural selection and can manifest in various phenotypic traits, including vocal signals. However, classifying individuals based on their vocalizations, or acoustic individual identification (AIID), remains a significant challenge. This is particularly true for species that use rapidly varying echolocation calls for orientation. Here, we demonstrate that deep learning can overcome the limitations of traditional methods and reveal persistent individual signatures within bat echolocation calls. We recorded 17 584 echolocation calls from 34 individuals of the greater leaf-nosed bat ( <i>Hipposideros armiger</i>) under controlled laboratory conditions, with 19 individuals recorded repeatedly over three months. We show that a convolutional neural network (CNN) significantly outperforms a traditional method, achieving an average identification accuracy of 84% for single calls and 91% for call sequences. In contrast, the traditional discriminant functional analysis method achieved accuracies of only 39% and 47%, respectively. By systematically altering the temporal structure of echolocation calls in input sequences, we found that temporal patterning enhances individual classification accuracy, suggesting it contributes to the encoding of individual-specific information. This study reveals that echolocation calls of <i>H. armiger</i> can contain stable, individual identity information that was previously undetectable. Our findings highlight the potential of deep learning for non-invasive AIID and provide a methodological basis for future studies aiming to monitor animals in more dynamic environments.

ID (PMID): 42864568
Título: Biomachining in manufacturing: mechanisms, processes, applications and future perspectives.
Resumen: Biomachining (BM) is an emerging bio-assisted manufacturing approach that uses microbial metabolism and bioelectrochemical reactions to remove material under mild conditions. Due to its low mechanical loading and limited thermal effects, BM has potential in low-damage microfabrication, surface functionalization, microfluidic mold fabrication, abrasive tool dressing, and functional device modification. This review critically summarizes BM with respect to removal mechanisms, process technologies, modeling and optimization strategies, manufacturing applications, and engineering challenges. The biological and electrochemical mechanisms of BM are discussed first, followed by conventional and hybrid BM processes and their comparison with conventional and non-conventional machining technologies. Current applications are reviewed with emphasis on the gap between laboratory demonstrations and scalable industrial implementation. Major challenges include low removal efficiency, limited dimensional accuracy, unstable microbial activity, weak process controllability, contamination risk, waste treatment, and biosafety management. Future development should focus on standardized evaluation, microbial stability control, mechanism-data fusion modeling, hybrid process intensification, and dedicated equipment. Machine learning-assisted prediction, Internet of Things-enabled monitoring, digital twin-based closed-loop control, and sustainability/techno-economic validation are also important for moving BM toward controllable and scalable manufacturing.

ID (PMID): 42864435
Título: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models.
Resumen: Predicting properties from coordinate-category data-sets of vectors paired with categorical information-is fundamental to computational science, manifesting in materials science as predicting formation energies or elastic moduli from crystal structures. While large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied to such tasks, optimal strategies for achieving reliable predictions remain elusive. Here we report fundamental limitations in LLM's ability to learn from coordinate information in coordinate-category data. Through systematic experiments using synthetic datasets with tunable coordinate and category contributions, and a comprehensive benchmarking framework (MatText), we find that LLMs consistently fail to capture coordinate information while excelling at category patterns. This geometric blindness persists regardless of model size (up to 70 billion parameters), dataset scale (up to 2 × 10<sup>6</sup> structures) or text representation strategy. For material property prediction tasks dominated by structural effects, specialized geometric architectures consistently outperform LLMs, as evidenced by a clear 'Graph Neural Network Language Model (GNN-LM) wall' in performance benchmarks. Our analysis provides concrete guidelines for architecture selection in scientific machine learning.

Título: Interpretable machine learning framework for peptide lead optimization in ultralarge design spaces.
Resumen: In modern peptide drug discovery, the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) has become a powerful strategy to improve potency and key developability properties, including stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability. This shift has expanded peptide chemical diversity and design spaces well beyond natural residues, creating fundamental challenges for predictive methods (e.g., quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling) used in lead optimization: limited transferability from natural residues to novel ncAAs, limited interpretability, and poor scalability to ultralarge peptide spaces (>10<sup>50</sup>). We present PepOpt, an interpretable machine learning framework that unifies molecule-based and sequence-based peptide representations in linear models and exploits dynamic programming to efficiently explore ultralarge peptide spaces. PepOpt achieves high predictive accuracy and interpretability, supports training and inference across diverse ncAAs, including ncAAs absent from the training set whose constituent substructures are represented in the training data. Its linear structure decomposes predictions into residue-specific contributions, enabling systematic optimization without exhaustive sequence enumeration. Notably, PepOpt is inherently capable of multi-parameter optimization without specialized modifications. Together, these capabilities position PepOpt as a valuable platform for prediction, interpretation, ideation, and rapid exploration in ncAA-rich ultralarge peptide chemical spaces, accelerating the rational design of novel peptide therapeutics.


--- ARTÍCULO 4062 ---
ID (PMID): 42864349
Título: Predictability can be dynamically constructed in deterministic systems.
Resumen: A deterministic system's future can be fixed from the start yet remain unpredictable because of chaos or computational irreducibility. Here we reveal another source of unpredictability for non-chaotic deterministic systems: collective entities making the future legible are initially absent but dynamically constructed. In a generalized cellular automaton, disordered lattices evolved into static configurations, rectilinear waves, or spiral waves. Although initial configurations fixed each fate, machine-learning models did no better than randomly guessing fates from them. Recoding cell states geometrically revealed self-organization of prediction-enabling topological entities: vortices, non-contractible-loop strings, and, most generally, a winding field describing how same-state regions wrap the lattice. As the winding field self-organized, initially unpredictable fates became increasingly legible. Static and rectilinear-wave fates became progressively predictable, whereas spiral-wave fate became accurately predictable only near wave formation. These results establish that self-organization can build not merely order but entities that make certain futures visible, revealing a gap between determinism and practical predictability.

Título: Mapping high resolution, multidimensional phase diagrams of near-physiological protein condensates.
Resumen: Biomolecular condensates are membraneless compartments, crucial for organising and regulating diverse cellular processes. Current approaches to study condensate biology either use simplified recombinant protein systems with limited physiological relevance, or complex live-cell models with restricted experimental control and scalability. Here, we present ExVivo PhaseScan, a droplet microfluidics platform that couples mammalian lysate-based reconstitution with scalable analysis to generate high-resolution phase diagrams of compositionally complex protein condensates. We apply this approach to study two multicomponent condensate systems, stress granules and nucleoli, and dissect the physicochemical interactions that influence their stability. We further developed a machine learning pipeline to analyse condensate morphology which we use to reveal how mutations in the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-linked protein Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) remodels condensate properties. We identify liquid-to-solid transitions of mutant FUS within stress granules and nucleoli, and show that these transitions can be reversed by RNA aptamer-based interventions. Together, these findings establish ExVivo PhaseScan as a versatile tool for dissecting the physicochemical and pathological regulation of condensates, with potential to inform therapeutic strategies for diseases driven by aberrant phase transitions.

Título: Metastable CeZrO<sub>4-δ</sub> polymorph for high-sensitivity nitrogen dioxide detection.

These findings demonstrate that metastable phases offer an effective route to tune sensing materials, and the current example provides a platform for sensitive and stable NO<sub>2</sub>-resolved monitoring relevant to Euro 7-oriented emission diagnostics.

Título: Navigating machine learning and classical statistics in sarcopenia screening for community-dwelling older women.
Resumen: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used for sarcopenia screening, but its added value over conventional models remains uncertain when datasets are moderately sized and predictors are few. Sarcopenia was defined as handgrip strength <18 kg and bioelectrical impedance-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index <5.7 kg/m<sup>2</sup>. SVM, CART, and MLP showed lower discrimination. The three-predictor LR model achieved an AUROC of 0.852. With nested tuning, full-model AUROCs were numerically similar for LR (0.835), SVM (0.843), and MLP (0.840); corresponding three-predictor AUROCs were 0.865, 0.850, and 0.852. LR remained competitive with the evaluated ML models, and the previously identified three-predictor model showed good discrimination. Relative performance depended on model configuration and training procedures. Independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

Resumen: Oropharyngeal dysphagia (OD) is highly prevalent in ageing and neurological populations. Despite its impact, current gold-standard assessments such as videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) and fibreoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES) are not widely accessible and require specialised expertise. Moreover, conventional evaluation focuses primarily on bolus transport during eating and does not fully integrate the broader pharyngolaryngeal functions involved in airway protection such as coughing, breathing and phonation. These limitations contribute to delays in diagnosis and insufficient clinical management. The primary objective is to model a pharyngolaryngeal effectiveness (PhLEs) multidomain composite index based on signals collected from non-invasive sensors. Secondary analyses will explore the ability of this indicator to predict severity and clinically relevant complications during follow-up. This multicentre, observational, prospective and longitudinal study aims to operationalise the concept of PhLEs, which integrates four key functions of the pharyngolarynx: swallowing, breathing, airway protection and phonation. A non-invasive multisensor device incorporating a cervical microphone, accelerometer, surface electromyography, nasal thermistor and pulse oximeter will record multimodal signals during standardised clinical tasks. Reference assessments include VFSS or FEES, cough reflex testing with citric acid, phonation analysis and meal observation. A total of 520 adults will be recruited from four French university hospitals: 440 patients with suspected or confirmed OD and 80 healthy volunteers. Participants will undergo monthly follow-up for 6 months to identify the onset of OD-related complications such as pneumonia, weight loss, dehydration and psychological burden. Recorded signals will be annotated and processed using machine learning methods. These models will be developed to automate the detection of pharyngolaryngeal events, predict severity of swallowing impairment and estimate complication risk based on PhLEs. Data, electronic case report form entries and raw signals will be centralised on a dedicated server for storage and analysis and managed by a certified healthcare data hosting provider. This study introduces a novel comprehensive approach to OD evaluation using objective multisensor data and artificial intelligence. The expected outcomes include earlier identification of swallowing disorders, improved severity stratification and enhanced prognostic evaluation, ultimately supporting timely clinical decision-making. If validated, this tool could expand access to swallowing assessments by offering a non-invasive, portable and automated solution that complements gold-standard techniques and enhances prevention strategies across common aetiologies of dysphagia. Título: Artificial intelligence-enabled mental health applications for adolescents: a scoping review of safety, effectiveness and clinical implementation.

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and ScienceDirect were searched from 1 January 2014 to 17 June 2026. English-language peer-reviewed sources addressing AI-enabled screening, prediction, assessment, monitoring, therapeutic support, care navigation, safeguarding or implementation for adolescents or school-aged youth were eligible. Adult-only studies, non-AI digital tools, protocols without results and unverifiable or promotional sources were excluded. Structured-data machine learning was the dominant modality (42/95, 44.2%), and risk prediction or prognosis was the leading clinical function (45/95, 47.4%). The field is dominated by prediction and internal validation, whereas symptom-level benefit, prospective safety, workflow integration, scale-up and sustainability remain largely untested. Future applications should be evaluated as supervised, human-in-the-loop systems with explicit safeguards for consent, privacy, fairness, accountability and crisis escalation.

Título: [Driving mechanisms and research challenges of phytoplankton community structure shifts in the coastal China seas.].
Resumen: The coastal China seas are a representative marine region jointly influenced by global climate change and human activities. As primary producers in marine ecosystems, phytoplankton community structure strongly influences ecosystem stability. Here, we summarized the spatiotemporal patterns, driving mechanisms, and modeling approaches of phytoplankton community structure shifts in the coastal China seas. Phytoplankton communities exhi-bit pronounced regional heterogeneity. In nearshore waters, eutrophication and changing nutrient regimes have generally weakened diatom dominance and increased the relative abundance of dinoflagellates and small-sized phytoplankton, accompanied by an increased risk of harmful algal blooms. In offshore and shelf-edge regions, ocean warming and enhanced stratification have promoted a trend toward smaller phytoplankton in size classes. Transitional zones are regulated by the combined effects of water-mass exchange, frontal dynamics, estuarine plumes, and upwelling currents, which collectively drive enhanced spatiotemporal variations in phytoplankton community structure. Community succession is driven by interactions among resource supply, environmental filtering, and biological processes, with temperature, light, nutrient stoichiometry, and microzooplankton grazing playing key roles. Current predictions of phytoplankton community dynamics still face challenges, including limited understanding of ecological mechanisms, simplified functional-group representations, difficulties in parameterizing key processes, and inadequate resolution of mesoscale and submesoscale dynamics. Future studies should strengthen long-term observations and mechanism-based experiments, and develop multi-scale coupled models integrating multiple nutrient forms, high-resolution physical processes, and machine-learning approaches to improve predictions of phytoplankton community dynamics and ecosystem responses.

Novel trends in 2023-2025 included substance use, lifestyle psychiatry, evidence synthesis and non-suicidal self-injury. Most studies were conducted in Western countries. Underrepresented research areas included the involvement of youth with lived/living experience in identifying meaningful outcomes, open science, implementation research, economic evaluations, machine-learning approaches, and social determinants of mental health.

Título: Online continual Fréchet distance learning.
Resumen: Task-Free Continual Learning (TFCL) represents a realistic yet challenging learning scenario, aiming to train a model capable of capturing all previously seen important information without forgetting while the task information is not available. Título: Adaptive parameter manifold learning for low-dimensional neural network optimization.
Resumen: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success across diverse domains, yet their massive over-parameterization introduces significant optimization challenges, particularly susceptibility to overfitting and noise memorization. While traditional stochastic gradient descent treats all parameters equally in the native parameter space, recent evidence suggests that neural network optimization occurs within much lower-dimensional subspaces. Existing parameter subspace methods either rely on random projections that ignore parameter space structure or employ linear dimensionality reduction that cannot capture complex geometric relationships. Through empirical analysis of training trajectories, we demonstrate that neural network parameters evolve along continuous, low-dimensional non-linear manifolds whose intrinsic dimensionality is substantially lower than the original parameter space. We propose Adaptive Parameter Manifold Learning (APML), a novel optimization framework that leverages Local Tangent Space Alignment to discover the underlying manifold structure from training trajectories and optimize neural networks on the parameter manifolds. Our method dynamically adapts the manifold throughout training to accommodate the changing geometry of the loss landscape. Extensive experiments on noisy label learning tasks across vision and language domains, as well as federated learning scenarios, demonstrate that APML achieves superior robustness and communication efficiency compared to existing subspace optimization methods.

Título: Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees.
Resumen: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system's strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model's ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation.

This review systematically evaluates the computational SL landscape across three core dimensions. First, we examine how diverse GNN architectures integrate multi-layered biological data. Second, we address model interpretability, contrasting intrinsically transparent architectures with post-hoc explanation methods, as a requirement for clinical trust. Finally, we explore the emerging role of Generative AI and large language models to leverage their zero-shot reasoning and broad biomedical knowledge.

The MLP successfully reproduced the experimentally observed synchronization boundaries and achieved prediction accuracies exceeding 93% for experimental data and 98% for theoretical data, demonstrating its capability to identify complex nonlinear lock-in dynamics. These results highlight the potential of combining physics-based reduced-order models with data-driven approaches for improved prediction and analysis of flow synchronization phenomena.
