Título: 3dcon: tomogram denoising by deconvolution.
Resumen: Cryo-electron tomography is an expanding technology for the study of macromolecules, viruses and cells. It is often applied to specimens that are too large or heterogeneous for methods based on 2D image averaging such as single-particle analysis, for example intracellular membranes or organelles. Current practice records a tilt series of projection images in rotation. Reconstruction is normally an ill-posed mathematical problem. Particularly for the under-determined case of sparse data, discrete tilt angles and a limited tilt range, characteristic artifacts appear in the reconstructed slices. Much of what appears as noise is in fact structural: the projection of contrast from different planes. Various schemes are employed to regularize the reconstruction, including machine-learning frameworks built on neural networks. To the extent that the noise is structural, based on the geometry of the tilt series, it might be suppressed by deconvolution with a suitable kernel. This was demonstrated and has been used regularly in cryo-STEM tomography of thick specimens where the under-sampling problem is particularly acute. Here, we present 3dcon as an open-source extension of the entropy-regularized deconvolution algorithm that had been adopted from fluorescence microscopy. It takes advantage of modern computing hardware for convenient and fast processing. Deconvolution is entirely algorithmic, meaning that successful processing of the data does not depend on the data itself. As such, it should be robust in a wide variety of applications.

Título: Using large language models to probe the limits of atom-centered structural descriptors.

Título: Impact of ligand bulk on conformational rearrangement in supported organometallic complexes.
Resumen: Measuring the dynamics of surface organometallic species, let alone connecting these to catalysis, is highly challenging. Resumen: Electrode-electrolyte interphases (EEIs) govern battery performance, yet the interplay between their chemical composition and spatial organization remains challenging to resolve. Título: Extreme conformal prediction: Reliable intervals for high-impact events.
Resumen: Conformal prediction is a popular method to construct prediction intervals with marginal coverage guarantees from black-box machine learning models. In applications with potentially high-impact events, such as flooding or financial crises, regulators often require very high confidence for such intervals. However, if the desired level of confidence is too large relative to the amount of data used for calibration, then classical conformal methods provide infinitely wide, thus, uninformative prediction intervals. In this paper, we propose a new method to overcome this limitation. We bridge extreme value statistics and conformal prediction to provide reliable and informative prediction intervals with high-confidence coverage, which can be constructed using any black-box extreme quantile regression method. A weighted version of our approach can account for nonstationary data. Título: Addressing hypersensitivity in density functional theory for reliable machine learning.
Resumen: In principle, machine learning (ML) can be used within density functional theory to obtain any electronic property of a time-independent many-body system from its ground-state electron density alone. However, when the target quantity (the output) is highly sensitive to small variations in the density (the input), accurately learning the mapping between them is highly challenging in practice. We identify this 'hypersensitivity' in two classes of density functionals that contain observables central to most electronic structure calculations: (1) any observable that varies subject to a global constant shift in the external potential (such as the total energy); (2) any observable of the <i>N</i>-electron system that depends on the properties of the (<i>N</i> + 1)-electron system (such as the electron affinity). We demonstrate that the accuracy with which widely used ML models approximate density functionals in these two classes is significantly limited by the pathological nature of the mapping from the density to the observable, even when the reference level of the external potential is fixed to prevent constant shifts. In addition, we find that providing the external potential as input to the ML model resolves this issue, in some cases reducing the error by up to three orders of magnitude when predicting quantities in these two classes.

Título: Sex and gender in digital mental health: why the data are not neutral.
Resumen: Digital tools, including smartphone sensors, wearable devices, and conversational artificial intelligence, have moved mental health assessment beyond the clinic and into everyday life, offering the possibility of earlier detection and broader access. However, these benefits are not distributed equally between women and men. Drawing on recent evidence, this review traces sex and gender across four layers of the digital mental health pipeline: who reaches these tools, how algorithms interpret the data, how effectively interventions perform, and how raw sensor signals are understood. At each layer, biases that may appear to be technical details instead reflect sex- and gender-related patterns. ID (PMID): 42859739
Título: AI and speech-based identification of cognitive impairment in maintenance haemodialysis-the ASPIRE study.
Resumen: Cognitive impairment (CI) is common among individuals receiving maintenance haemodialysis and is associated with impaired treatment adherence, reduced quality of life, and mortality. However, CI often remains under-recognized in nephrology care because existing diagnostic approaches are resource-intensive. Speech-based artificial intelligence (AI) is a promising approach for identifying CI through analysis of speech characteristics. This proof-of-concept study investigated whether a speech-based AI model could identify Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA)-based CI and distinguish individuals receiving haemodialysis from clinically relevant controls. Adults receiving maintenance haemodialysis and controls completed the MoCA and speech tasks. Participants were categorized into low-, moderate-, and high-risk CI groups according to MoCA scores. Acoustic, linguistic, and multimodal speech features were extracted using machine-learning models. Model performance was evaluated. Speech-based AI differentiated individuals receiving haemodialysis from controls (<i>n</i> = 40). Multimodal models achieved the highest performance, with accuracies ranging from 0.78 to 0.80 for uraemia classification. For MoCA-based cognitive risk classification (<i>n</i> = 63), verbal fluency tasks yielded the strongest results. The best-performing model was the two-task fusion, which identified the high-risk group with a weighted F1-score of 73%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) of 79%, and Matthew's correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.43. Moderate MoCA-based cognitive risk was more difficult to classify. Speech-based AI suggested potential as a scalable, non-invasive, and low-burden approach for identifying CI. Verbal fluency tasks and multimodal speech analysis showed the strongest classification performance. Although larger multicentre studies are needed, these findings provide proof of concept that speech may serve as a clinically relevant biomarker of CI in nephrology and support further validation using comprehensive neuropsychological assessment as a reference standard.

ID (PMID): 42859637
Título: Machine learning quantification of hepatobiliary lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio in benign hepatocellular tumors: a feasibility study.
Resumen: To evaluate the feasibility of a machine learning derived semi-automatic quantification of the lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio following hepatobiliary contrast agent injection for the characterization of benign hepatocellular tumors. Precontrast, arterial, portal venous and hepatobiliary phases of liver magnetic resonance images were coregistered, then the liver was automatically segmented by a pretrained U-Net network. Each lesion was then manually segmented on the arterial phase, while different regions of interest were automatically placed in the liver parenchyma (ring shape, circular). Two-dimensional and three-dimensional lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratios were automatically calculated using each different regions of interest and the whole liver volume. All the calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio were compared to a manual lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio and correlated to organic-anion-transporting polypeptide expression. Moreover, the ability of each calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio in classifying the two lesions was investigated. A total of 23 hepatocellular benign tumors were analyzed including nine focal nodular hyperplasias (39 %) and 14 hepatocellular adenomas (61 %). The correlation between each calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio and the manual value was strong (Pearson coefficient ranging between 0.69 and 0.87). Regarding correlation with organic-anion-transporting polypeptide expression, the highest correlation values was obtained with two-dimensional ring region of interest lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio (Pearson coefficient = 0.56). All lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio values were effective in classifying between focal nodular hyperplasia and hepatocellular adenoma, with the best results in terms of inverse Fisher discriminant ratio obtained with ring-shaped region of interest (0.34 2D, 0.28 3D) and uniform liver region of interest (0.28 2D, 0.37 3D). Semi-automatic quantification of the hepatobiliary lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio both using a two- or a three-dimensional approach is a promising tool for benign hepatocellular characterization.

Título: Machine Learning Accurately Predicts Costs and Identifies Disparities for Common Outpatient Hand Surgeries.
Resumen: Costs of outpatient hand procedures vary widely, and the influence of social determinants of health is not well characterized. Machine learning (ML) offers a way to quantify cost drivers and identify disparities. We sought to (1) assess whether ML models can accurately predict the costs of common outpatient hand procedures (2) identify cost determinants and (3) assess whether socioeconomic or racial disparities exist in cost patterns. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the New York State Ambulatory Surgery and Services Database (2015-2018) including patients undergoing open carpal tunnel release, endoscopic carpal tunnel release, trigger finger release, and distal radius fracture open reduction and internal fixation. ML models were trained to predict total procedure costs, and feature importance analyses identified key cost drivers. Associations between costs, Social Deprivation Index quintiles, and racial/ethnic composition were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's tests and Pearson/Spearman correlations. ML models trained on 61,460 patients demonstrated strong predictive performance. Patient zip code and hospital identifier were consistently top cost predictors. Significant disparities were observed: higher costs were associated with both high and low extremes of Social Deprivation Index, as well as higher proportions of Asian, Black, and Hispanic patients. In contrast, White patients were overrepresented in lower-cost quartiles. ML accurately predicted procedure costs and revealed consistent socioeconomic and racial disparities in cost patterns for common outpatient hand surgeries. These findings highlight the need for value-based policies designed to reduce inequities and improve access to high-quality, affordable surgical care. Therapeutic III.

Título: Biomarkers and Risk Prediction in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome: A Comprehensive Review.

Título: Clinicopathological Machine Learning Models for Mortality Risk Prediction in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis of the The Cancer Genome Atlas Head-Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC) Cohort.
Resumen: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a leading contributor to global cancer mortality, yet outcome prediction in routine practice still relies almost entirely on anatomical staging. We evaluated whether readily available clinicopathological variables, and their combination with tumour transcriptomic data, can support machine learning (ML)-based mortality risk stratification in HNSCC. We analysed clinical records for 528 patients from the Cancer Genome Atlas Head-Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC) cohort, obtained from the National Cancer Institute's (NCI's) Genomic Data Commons (GDC). Ten clinicopathological features were used to train four classifiers: logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and support vector machine to predict vital status, evaluated by stratified five-fold cross-validation. Time-to-event outcomes were separately modelled with Kaplan-Meier estimation and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. In a matched subset of 500 patients with available tumour RNA-sequencing data, we additionally incorporated expression of four HNSCC driver genes (CDKN2A, EGFR, FAT1, and E2F1) identified from the TCGA landmark genomic analysis, together with the first five principal components of a 4,465-gene expression panel, and re-evaluated the same four classifiers on this matched cohort with and without the genomic features. The cohort included 224 deaths (42.4%). Using clinicopathological variables alone, random forest achieved the highest discrimination (area under the curve (AUC) 0.698), followed by logistic regression (AUC 0.689), support vector machine (AUC 0.686), and gradient boosting (AUC 0.666). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed clear separation of overall survival by stage (log-rank Stage I vs. IV, p = 0.005), and multivariable Cox regression confirmed Stage IV disease (HR 4.07, 95% CI 1.50-11.03, p = 0.006) and older age (HR 1.02 per year, p = 0.005) as independent predictors of mortality (concordance index 0.608). Adding genomic features in the matched 500-patient cohort improved discrimination for every classifier, most notably random forest (AUC 0.708 → 0.727) and logistic regression (AUC 0.688 → 0.704); expression-derived features accounted for eight of the 15 most important predictors in the augmented model. Routinely collected clinicopathological data provide a modest but genuine and statistically robust prognostic signal in HNSCC (AUC 0.67-0.70). Supplementing this with a small panel of driver-gene expression values and an unsupervised transcriptomic signature further improves discrimination (best AUC 0.727) without resolving the underlying prognostic ceiling, supporting stepwise, transparently benchmarked multi-omic model development rather than reliance on any single data modality.

Título: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Early Warning Systems for Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration in Hospitalized Patients: Current Clinical Applications and Future Directions.
Resumen: Early recognition of clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients is essential for preventing adverse events such as cardiac arrest, sepsis, respiratory failure and unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Traditional Early Warning Systems (EWS), including the Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) and National Early Warning Score (NEWS), are widely used to support bedside assessment through standardized evaluation of physiological parameters. However, conventional EWS are limited by intermittent monitoring, manual data entry and variable clinical interpretation. Recent advances in electronic health records, continuous physiological monitoring and artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of AI-enhanced Early Warning Systems capable of real-time risk assessment and prediction of clinical deterioration before overt clinical manifestations occur. Machine learning algorithms can analyze large volumes of clinical data, identify subtle physiological trends and support earlier clinical intervention. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced EWS may improve rapid response activation, reduce ICU transfers, decrease in-hospital mortality and optimize workflow efficiency. This narrative review examines the evolution of EWS from traditional scoring systems to AI-driven predictive models, focusing on their current clinical applications in hospitalized adult patients. Particular emphasis is placed on practical implementation in routine clinical care, the role of nurses and multidisciplinary teams, interpretability of AI algorithms, ethical considerations and barriers to adoption. In addition, the review discusses the integration of AI-enhanced systems into clinical decision support pathways and highlights the importance of maintaining clinical judgment alongside technological innovation. AI-enhanced EWS should be viewed as decision-support tools that complement rather than replace healthcare professionals. Successful clinical implementation requires robust validation, interdisciplinary collaboration, organizational readiness and continuous staff education. When appropriately integrated into clinical workflows, AI-supported predictive systems may significantly contribute to earlier intervention and improved patient safety in acute hospital settings.

Título: First-trimester non-invasive prediction of preterm birth using cell-free DNA fragmentomics.
Resumen: Spontaneous preterm birth (PTB) remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet accurate prediction in asymptomatic women during early gestation remains a critical unmet clinical need. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) obtained through the same maternal blood collection used for routine first-trimester non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) represents an underutilized substrate for early PTB risk identification. To develop and validate a cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomic classifier for the early prediction of spontaneous preterm birth (PTB) using routine first-trimester non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) data. A case-control study was conducted within a multicenter Vietnamese cohort comprising 286 pregnancies, including 82 spontaneous PTB cases and 204 term controls. Maternal plasma cfDNA collected during routine first-trimester NIPT (median gestational age, 12 weeks) was sequenced to a depth of approximately 20 million reads per sample. Five fragmentomic feature categories including copy number alterations, end-motif composition, nucleosome distance, fragment length, and joint fragment-length × end-motif were evaluated for PTB prediction. Consistent with these findings, the EM-based classifier demonstrated the highest discriminative performance in the internal validation cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.970 (95% CI, 0.912-1.000). At a specificity >90%, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94% (95% CI, 78%-100%). These findings demonstrate that cfDNA EM signatures derived from routine first-trimester NIPT can accurately identify pregnancies at risk of spontaneous preterm birth, using only a routine maternal blood sample, supporting the potential to extend the clinical utility of existing prenatal screening infrastructure pending prospective validation at production sequencing depths.

ID (PMID): 42859440
Título: triangulax: Differentiable Simulations with Triangular Meshes across Soft Matter Physics.
Resumen: Many physical and biological systems -foams, membranes, elastic shells, or tissue sheets- can be mathematically described as 2D surfaces. These surfaces can host complex dynamics, like reaction-diffusion systems, and undergo drastic deformations. Here, we present triangulax, an open-source Python library for simulations and geometry processing that discretizes surfaces using triangular meshes available at https://github.com/nikolas-claussen/triangulax. It combines two features. First, discrete differential geometry provides coordinate-free discretization, which allows simulating strongly deforming surfaces. Second, the library is built on the machine-learning framework JAX, so mesh-based energies and entire simulations can be differentiated automatically (including simulations with stochastic forces or topological modifications). This simplifies multi-physics simulations by computing forces automatically and allows fitting model parameters to experimental data or design objectives. We implement an algorithm to preserve mesh quality in strongly deforming surfaces and apply it to a model of membrane mechanics coupled to an on-membrane concentration field. We validate our approach against exact solutions and existing software, and demonstrate triangulax across a range of problems, including membrane mechanics, vertex models, and inverse design of a shape-morphing elastomer sheet.

ID (PMID): 42859431
Título: How are European small enterprises dealing with the circular economy?
Resumen: Environmental sustainability and energy savings are crucial for economic development, yet European SMEs account for 63.3% of total CO2 firms emissions. Understanding how these businesses behave when transitioning to a Circular Economy is essential for policymakers to design appropriate measures and incentives for preventing negative environmental externalities. The study analyzed data from the fifth wave of the "SMEs, resource efficiency, and green markets" survey conducted in late 2021, which included 14,008 enterprises across 27 European Union member states. To categorize the companies, researchers applied a K-modes clustering algorithm-a machine learning method designed specifically for categorical data- to evaluate six qualitative business characteristics and nine environmental actions. The analysis identified three distinct business behavior clusters. Cluster 1 (6,195 firms) primarily provides services to other businesses and focuses heavily on energy savings and waste minimization. Cluster 2 (4,002 firms) is the least environmentally proactive group, predominantly selling products directly to consumers, with 21.14% taking no environmental action at all. Cluster 3 (3,811 firms) is the most active and diverse group, exhibiting the highest participation in minimizing waste and saving energy but also reporting the most difficulties. Regardless of the cluster, the primary barrier to sustainability is the complexity of administrative or legal procedures, followed by the high costs of environmental actions. Consequently, the support most requested by these companies consists of grants or subsidies along with greater cooperation between companies across sectors and consultancy. The transition to sustainable practices remains a significant challenge for most European SMEs, who often perceive current macro-level environmental regulations (such as the Circular Economy Action Plan) as bureaucratic hurdles rather than sources of help. To effectively foster a sustainable economy, policymakers must focus on simplifying administrative procedures, providing financial support, and encouraging inter-firm cooperation and technological consultancy.

Título: Filtering Out Defects in Open-Source Meat Freshness Datasets: A New Leak-Free Benchmark and a Comparative Analysis of Four Different Mobile Deep Learning Models.
Resumen: Image-based, nondestructive classification of hourly meat-freshness stages is important for food-quality monitoring and supply-chain management. However, detailed audits of open-source datasets and their preprocessed subsets can reveal methodological defects that artificially inflate model performance. In this study, a Mendeley Data dataset for hourly meat-freshness classification was audited at the file and original-image levels. Two major defects were identified: The 36- and 48-h beef classes contained byte-identical images, as verified by MD5 hashes, and offline augmentation performed before data partitioning distributed variants of the same original images across the training, validation, and test sets, causing cross-partition leakage. A leak-free nine-class benchmark containing 1849 verified original images was therefore constructed. The duplicated beef stages were represented as a single 36+ h beef class, whereas the distinct 36 and 48 h mutton stages were retained separately. MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2, and MobileNetV2 were trained using online augmentation, focal loss, inverse-frequency class weights, and five prespecified random seeds. MobileNetV3-Large achieved the highest mean test accuracy (98.51% ± 0.58%) and macro F1 score (98.54% ± 0.55%) and ranked first in four of five runs. However, its advantage over EfficientNet-B0 was not significant in any seed-wise exact McNemar comparison after Holm correction. These findings demonstrate the risks of uncritical reuse of open-source datasets and provide a leakage-controlled, reproducible basis for evaluating compact models intended for mobile and edge deployment.

Título: Decoupling Flavor From Spoilage: A Microbial and Chemical Framework for Volatile Sulfur Compounds and Biogenic Amines in Washed-Rind and Aged Cheeses.
Resumen: Ripened washed-rind and long-ripened cheeses owe their prized sulfurous, savory character to intensive proteolysis and amino-acid catabolism; the same activity, when poorly controlled, also generates sensory off-flavors and toxic biogenic amines (BAs). Histamine and tyramine reach up to approximately 2000-2500 and 1000-2000 mg/kg in extreme samples, although most cheeses contain far less, so that a 30-g portion of a high-histamine cheese can exceed the 50-mg per-meal intake regarded as without adverse effect in healthy adults. Flavor formation and chemical safety have traditionally been studied apart. This critical review reframes them as two outcomes of one metabolism: Proteolysis liberates a shared free amino-acid pool from which volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) and BAs arise. Because the principal VSCs derive from methionine whereas the major BAs derive from histidine, tyrosine, ornithine, arginine, and lysine, we treat the branches not as direct competitors for one substrate but as metabolically coupled fates linked by shared proteolytic supply, overlapping physicochemical controls and microbial cross-feeding. Integrating evidence across cheese families, we reclassify the ripening microbiota into condition-dependent functional guilds, formalize metabolic bivalence (organisms that both generate flavor and degrade amines), and define a sensory inflection point separating the windowed VSC dose-response from the monotonic BA hazard. We critically appraise multi-omics, volatilomics, biosensors, machine learning, and digital twins, and outline a precision-fermentation roadmap. Current, largely in vitro, and single-variety evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, controllable decoupling, which we frame as a testable hypothesis that recasts cheese quality as a controllable metabolic-allocation problem.

Título: Multivariate analysis of morphometric traits for chicken breed discrimination.

ID (PMID): 42859288
Título: Calibration of Low-Cost Particulate Matter Sensors for Exposure Assessment: A Critical Review.
Resumen: Low-cost particulate matter (PM) sensors make it possible to measure air pollution in homes, workplaces, and communities that are poorly represented by regulatory networks. Their readings, however, are sensitive to humidity, aerosol composition, concentration range, unit-to-unit variation, and aging. This review examines laboratory and field calibration evidence across environmental and occupational settings, emphasizing transferability and the consequences of calibration error for exposure assessment and health inference. The review identified 66 peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to 2025, including 32 laboratory evaluations and 34 field studies. The median reported calibrated coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.92 (n = 31) for laboratory studies and 0.72 (n = 29) for field studies; the corresponding median root mean square errors (RMSEs) were 2.6 µg/m³ (n = 7) and 12.3 µg/m³ (n = 9). These values summarize a heterogeneous literature rather than a common pooled effect. Studies differed in aerosol mixture, comparison instrument, concentration range, averaging interval, and validation design. Relative humidity and temperature were considered in most studies. Machine-learning and hybrid models appeared more often in field work and sometimes lowered error, although independent validation across time, place, and sensor units was uneven. Calibration is not a universal correction that can be applied once and carried unchanged into any deployment. Laboratory testing is well suited to defining response limits, particle-size sensitivity, and unit variability. Field co-location is needed to determine how the same device behaves under the sources, weather, concentrations, and time scales relevant to a health study. Credible use in epidemiology or public-health decision-making also requires independent validation, planned checks for drift, and clear reporting of calibration uncertainty.

Título: A two-stage learning framework for piecewise affine system identification.
Resumen: This paper proposes a fully data-driven and end-to-end adaptive framework for the complete black-box identification of piecewise affine ARX (PWARX) systems, in which model structure discovery, submodel parameter estimation, recursive parameter fine-tuning, and explicit polyhedral partition identification are integrated into a unified two-stage learning architecture. In Stage 1, an unsupervised process determines the number and order of submodels, computes consistent initial submodel parameter estimates, and constructs a compact labeled training set. In Stage 2, a self-tuning semi-supervised support vector machine (STS3VM) iteratively learns the submodel classifiers, while adaptive-forgetting recursive least squares fine-tunes the submodel parameters. The learned decision rule is then converted into explicit polyhedral partitions, with stage-wise convergence guarantees. Extensive simulations demonstrate high accuracy, reproducibility, robustness under diverse noise conditions, and scalability.

Título: Pipeline for acoustic classification of ant (Formica rufa) behaviours: A suggested workflow for soil macrofauna studies.
Resumen: Acoustic monitoring has been touted as an automatable monitoring technique to study the presence, activity or acoustic communication of soil animals. Yet current acoustic approaches have been criticized for lacking understanding of what soil fauna behaviours they are detecting. We investigate whether specific insect behaviours could be identified with sound by recording Red Wood Ants (Formica rufa) behaviours (running, struggling, biting and stridulation-like behaviour) with a contact microphone. We label recordings by hand, then extract two types of acoustic features, spectral and cepstral features, and show that most of the selected ant behaviours could be separated from each other based on their acoustic profiles. Based on our results, we propose an analytical workflow including principal component analysis as well as random forest classification that generates correct behavioural classifications in 67-90% of the sound snippets. Key features to separate behaviours include cepstral skewness, duration of sound events and mean frequency of the generated sound. Even if we encountered background noise, our pipeline could select relevant features from audio files and train a machine learning classifier. Our study demonstrates that acoustic features can be used to inform about specific insect behaviours and thus broaden the application of passive acoustic monitoring to species that do not communicate acoustically.

Título: Limits of machine learning for predicting stillbirth at term: a population-based cohort of 302,192 pregnancies in northern Italy.
Resumen: Stillbirth at term is a major public-health concern. In high-income settings, the most commonly identifiable causes are unrecognised fetal growth restriction (about 14%) and placental abruption (about 12%), but 20 to 40% of term stillbirths remain unexplained. Whether modern machine learning can substantively improve prediction over established clinical risk-factor models is unresolved. To evaluate the predictive performance of 3 machine-learning models, elastic-net logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting, for stillbirth at term in a population-based cohort, and to quantify the achievable ceiling using static registry variables. Secondary analysis of 302,192 term pregnancies (322 stillbirths; rate 1.07 per 1000), recorded in the Emilia-Romagna "Certificato di Assistenza al Parto" birth registry between 2014 and 2023. Three machine-learning models were trained on a stratified 80% training set with class rebalancing by Random Over-Sampling Examples applied within each cross-validation fold. Logistic-regression predicted probabilities were rescaled to natural prevalence by intercept-only Platt-style recalibration on a held-out training slice. Performance was evaluated on the held-out 20% test set (n=60,438; 66 stillbirths) using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), sensitivity, specificity, predictive values (Wilson 95% CIs), calibration intercept and slope, observed:expected (O:E) ratio, and decision curve analysis. All 3 fell below the AUC of 0.70 threshold for clinical screening. Logistic regression significantly outperformed random forest (DeLong P=.001). Positive predictive values at Youden-optimal thresholds were within Wilson-interval distance of the population baseline (0.106%). Decision curve analysis showed no model produced net benefit superior to a treat-all strategy at clinically plausible thresholds. After intercept recalibration, the logistic regression was well calibrated in the large (observed:expected ratio 1.12, 95% CI: 0.88-1.43). Gestational age, particularly early-term delivery, was the most influential predictor across models. Temporal validation degraded all 3 AUCs to 0.57 to 0.58. The previously published Salerno (2023) logistic regression specification achieved an AUC of 0.637 on the same test set, only 0.02 below the elastic-net logistic regression. In a large, decade-spanning population cohort, 3 machine-learning models achieved similarly limited discrimination for term stillbirth (AUC: 0.53-0.66), with the simpler regularised regression significantly outperforming the random forest. Static registry variables, even those captured by a high-quality regional surveillance system, do not carry sufficient signal for clinically useful term-stillbirth prediction. The empirical ceiling defined by this study should motivate a shift toward dynamic, physiology-based surveillance for future prediction research.

Título: Uncertainty-aware auto-segmentation enables adaptive radiotherapy planning of liver metastases.
Resumen: Despite remarkable auto-segmentation performance and growing clinical adoption, models frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution. Título: Soil carbon and inundation regimes jointly regulate denitrification potential in restored riverine floodplains.
Resumen: Denitrification plays a key role in nitrogen removal in restored floodplains, yet the relative importance of inundation regimes, hydrogeomorphic setting, and soil properties remains uncertain. In this study, we evaluated the environmental controls on denitrification potential across four restored sites using a combination of machine learning, structural equation modeling (SEM), and Copula-based analysis. Among the tested models, Random Forest provided the best predictive performance and explained 71% of the variance. Variable importance and partial dependence results identified total carbon (TC), soil moisture content (MC), and bulk density (BD) as the most influential predictors of denitrification potential. Specifically, a threshold in TC between 3% and 5% was associated with a sharp increase in denitrification potential. SEM results indicated that hydrological variables primarily influence denitrification indirectly through their effects on soil moisture and carbon accumulation, accounting for up to 44.4% of the variance at the site level. Copula analysis further quantified the joint probability of elevated denitrification enzyme activity (DEA) under combinations of favorable hydrologic conditions and sufficient carbon availability. Based on these patterns, the sites were grouped into three functional regimes: hydrology-carbon coupled regulation, carbon-limited regulation, and substrate-driven regulation with hydrological enhancement. Together, these results indicate that carbon availability establishes the biogeochemical potential for denitrification, whereas hydrological and physical conditions regulate its expression, with the relative importance of these controls varying among sites. The findings highlight the need for site-specific restoration strategies, including rebuilding soil carbon in degraded agricultural areas and maintaining appropriate inundation regimes while preserving favorable soil conditions in carbon-rich systems to enhance nitrogen removal.

Reliability was evaluated by comparing limits-of-agreement between SRTs achieved by repeated runs of CHAT and ASL tests using Bland-Altman analysis. Results revealed limits-of-agreement between repeated runs of CHAT and ASL were ±3.6 dB and ±3.1 dB, respectively. The area under the ROC curve was 0.97 for CHAT, 0.95 for ASL and 0.89 for FAAF. The correlation between SRT and PTA results was 0.86 for CHAT, 0.82 for ASL and 0.79 for FAAF. These findings indicate that CHAT demonstrates reliability and validity comparable to human-recorded ASL and FAAF, supporting the use of synthetic speech for speech-in-noise testing. Overall, the results suggest that AI tools can help create and administer conversational speech-in-noise tests.

Prespecified exploratory analyses included principal component analysis, Gaussian mixture modelling, and machine-learning-based feature analysis. Primary isolated TTS hearts developed progressive systolic and diastolic dysfunction characterized by reductions in left ventricular developed pressure, rate-pressure product, and coronary flow together with prolongation of surrogate isovolumic relaxation constant (TAU) (primary endpoint: <i>P</i> = 0.001; <i>q</i> = 0.002). Temporal modelling identified three reproducible physiological phases: hyperactivation, transition, and functional nadir. Echocardiography demonstrated characteristic apical ballooning, reduced ejection fraction, impaired global longitudinal strain, and increased left ventricular akinesia index. Progressive cardiac troponin release and representative histological alterations provided supportive biochemical and structural corroboration of the functional phenotype. We describe the first primary isolated heart model reproducing the core functional phenotype of TTS entirely within an isolated heart preparation. Thus, intrinsic myocardial responses to acute catecholaminergic stress are sufficient to generate regional dysfunction of TTS in the absence of systemic neurohumoral input.

Título: Predicting Collision Cross Sections with GRACE: Geometric Residual Adduct Conditioning via Early-fusion.

Diagnostic analyses suggest that residual learning stabilizes training by removing the dominant mass-CCS trend, while early fusion improves adduct-sensitive prediction relative to late fusion. Across four independent external test sets, GRACE shows consistently lower error than the other evaluated models. On a held-out set, GRACE also attains the lowest mean percent difference when compared with four previously reported physics-based workflows. These results support residual learning and encoder-level adduct conditioning as practical inductive biases for fast, accurate CCS prediction.

Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies now reveal that both sources and sinks consist of diverse cell populations with specialized metabolic and transport functions. In this review, we synthesize emerging insights from single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and integrative multi-omics to show how cellular heterogeneity shapes photosynthetic source strength, vascular transport interfaces, and sink development. We further discuss how stress responses, signaling molecules, and plant-associated microbiomes dynamically reprogram source-sink relationships in a spatially structured manner. Finally, we highlight opportunities to integrate high-resolution molecular atlases with physiological modeling and machine learning approaches to develop predictive frameworks for carbon allocation. These advances suggest that future crop improvement strategies will increasingly rely on cell-type-specific engineering of transport processes and metabolic sinks rather than simply enhancing photosynthesis.

Histopathological subtype assignment showed high interobserver reproducibility (Fleiss' κ=0.879, 95% CI 0.810-0.938). Stimulated LNs demonstrated enhanced immune activation features, whereas depleted LNs exhibited stromal remodeling, innate inflammatory activation, and impaired adaptive immune signaling. These histopathological subtypes were strongly associated with previously defined molecular LN subtypes. Among 12 machine-learning approaches, the random survival forest model achieved the best prognostic performance, with C-indices of 0.877 in the training cohort, 0.777 in cross-validation, 0.744 in temporal validation, and 0.748 in geographic validation. The resulting risk stratification system consistently discriminated overall survival across independent cohorts and clinically relevant subgroups. Título: Digital twins in toxicology: Toward predictive, personalized and real-time risk assessment.
Resumen: Toxicology has accumulated many predictive tools - physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models, quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) frameworks organ-on-chip systems, quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models, adverse outcome pathway (AOP) networks and machine-learning approaches. Yet predictive practice remains fragmented. Each tool captures a slice of biology; few capture the whole; none captures the patient. We argue that the concept of a digital twin - a continuously updated, mechanistically grounded, data-driven digital representation of an individual biological system - offers the missing organisational layer. We first trace the origin of digital twins from aerospace engineering through biomedicine into toxicology, emphasising how the defining properties (dynamic data assimilation at the pace a decision requires, multi-scale integration, hybrid mechanistic-statistical architecture, personalisation, predictive simulation) map onto existing toxicological methods. We then position PBPK and QSP as mature proto-twin components and name the architectural gaps - continuous data flow, uncertainty quantification, feedback-driven recalibration and regulatory-grade validation - that separate today's best models from a working twin. A four-layer architecture is proposed: data, mechanistic, AI and simulation. Six published systems are tested against the five conditions; none satisfies all five. We examine applications in drug development, personalised risk assessment, mass-poisoning response, chemical-biological-radiological-nuclear (CBRN) preparedness and antidote discovery for unknown toxins. Finally, we confront the translational gap: data heterogeneity, validation standards, interpretability, regulatory acceptance and ethical custody of patient-level models. Toxicology, we conclude, has most of the ingredients needed for digital-twin implementation; what remains is the integration work, two unresolved scientific problems and the institutional willingness to address them.

Título: Integrated human and natural regulation of carbon concentrations and fluxes dynamics in the Yangtze River mainstream over the past two decades.
Resumen: Rivers play a key role in the global carbon cycle, yet the long-term spatiotemporal dynamics of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) in large rivers remain uncertain, particularly for large Asian rivers where simultaneous assessments of all three forms are scarce. We compiled a monthly database (2000-2022) of DOC, POC, and DIC concentrations at 10 sites along the Yangtze River mainstream by integrating 2022 field campaigns with a systematic literature synthesis, and applied three machine learning algorithms to reconstruct continuous monthly concentrations. From headwaters to estuaries, all three fluxes increased, driven by precipitation-controlled runoff growth, whereas concentrations diverged: DOC increased downstream through elevated COD<sub>Mn</sub> (permanganate index) from runoff flushing; POC declined via vegetation interception and reservoir retention; and DIC decreased through runoff dilution. The corresponding concentration changes-a rise in DOC and declines in POC and DIC-were primarily driven by cascade reservoir construction and climate warming. Consequently, the Yangtze River mainstream is transitioning from a system historically dominated by POC and DIC export toward one increasingly characterized by DOC export. This transition has important implications for carbon burial efficiency and greenhouse gas emissions.

Título: Smooth total variation regularization for interference detection and elimination (STRIDE) for MRI.
Resumen: <i>Objective.</i>Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly required to operate near electronic devices that emit dynamic electromagnetic interference (EMI). STRIDE also resulted in lower or equal root-mean-square error than both EDITER implementations in all 8 phantom EMI conditions tested. These results held across both phantom and<i>in-vivo</i>datasets.<i>Significance.</i>STRIDE shows that incorporating known properties of MR images into the EMI removal problem provides meaningful improvements over methods that rely on measured data alone. The approach is deterministic, training-free, sequence-independent, and compatible with existing EMI sensor hardware. STRIDE therefore extends reference-channel EMI removal to scenarios where existing methods fail, particularly point-of-care and interventional MRI outside fully shielded environments, providing a deterministic, training-free alternative to machine-learning approaches.

The accelerated implementations provided large additional speed-ups while retaining controllable errors relative to the exact solution.<i>Significance.</i>The proposed framework extends exact finite-pulse solutions of the Bloch-Torrey equation to diffusion confined to cylindrical surfaces and provides practical implementations for directional and orientationally averaged diffusion MRI signals. It therefore offers an approximation-free reference for assessing faster signal approximations and for applications requiring large numbers of model evaluations.

ID (PMID): 42854394
Título: Enhancing local robustness with Hölder regularization.
Resumen: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to small input perturbations, resulting in instability and adversarial susceptibility. While adversarial training methods such as PGD-AT and TRADES improve robustness by generating worst-case adversarial examples, they do not explicitly regulate the model's local smoothness. In this paper, we propose Hölder Regularization (HR), a novel method to enhance local robustness by constraining the model's output variations based on Hölder continuity. Unlike conventional adversarial defenses, HR directly controls the functional smoothness of the model by regulating the relationship between input distances and output variations. We provide theoretical insights showing that the proposed regularization directly tightens an upper bound on the adversarial risk, thereby improving robustness. We also demonstrate that HR can be effectively combined with adversarial training, offering a complementary approach to existing techniques. We further compare HR with representative robustness baselines, including adversarial training methods and spectral normalization, showing that HR achieves superior or competitive performance across different perturbation settings. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, BSEQ, and ISOLET show that our method consistently improves robustness under PGD attacks, Gaussian noise, ℓ<sub>∞</sub>-perturbations, and feature masking. Furthermore, the proposed approach remains computationally efficient, as the Hölder regularization term is approximated via mini-batch sampling, introducing only a modest overhead.

Single‑molecule calculations employed DMol<sup>3</sup> with the same PBE functional and DNP basis set, with Grimme's D2 dispersion correction. The SCF convergence thresholds were set to 1 × 10<sup>-5</sup> Ha for energy, 0.002 Ha/Å for force, and 0.005 Å for displacement.

Additionally, we show that even flexible machine learning models may offer lower accuracy and precision than correctly specified parametric models. Resumen: Novel technologies for the acquisition of protein expression data at the single cell level are emerging rapidly. To overcome this limitation, scProfiterole uses Arnoldi orthonormalization to implement polynomial interpolations of any given spectral graph filter. Our results on comprehensive single cell proteomic data show that (i) GCL with learnable polynomial coefficients that are carefully initialized improves the effectiveness and robustness of cell type identification, (ii) HK and BK improve clustering performance over adjacency matrices or random walks, and (iii) polynomial interpolation of spectral filters outperforms approximation or truncation. The source code for scProfiterole and Supplementary Data are available at https://github.com/mustafaCoskunAgu/scProfiterole.

Título: Identification of CDKN1A as a Candidate Therapeutic Target in Peripheral Artery Disease Progression: Integrative Multi-omics and Mendelian Randomization Study.
Resumen: Therapeutic strategies for advanced Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD), including angiogenic gene therapy trials, have yielded limited clinical benefit, partly because target selection has relied on empirical biological reasoning rather than genetic causal evidence. Since the progression from Intermittent Claudication (IC) to Critical Limb Ischemia (CLI) represents a critical stage of PAD progression, identifying genetically supported causal targets underlying this transition is essential for developing effective molecular interventions. An integrative analytical framework was applied, combining bulk transcriptomics, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, Protein- Protein Interaction (PPI) network construction, and machine-learning-based feature selection. Candidate genes were further characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and validated in an in vivo murine Hindlimb Ischemia model (HLI). Immune infiltration was assessed by CIBERSORT. Genetic causal evidence was obtained through GWAS colocalization and bidirectional Mendelian Randomization (MR). Computational gene perturbation analysis was performed to predict downstream transcriptional consequences. Phenome-Wide Association Study (PheWAS) and drug-gene interaction analyses were conducted to explore pleiotropy and therapeutic relevance. Multi-stage screening consistently identified CDKN1A as a central hub gene associated with ischemic severity. At single-cell resolution, CDKN1A was broadly upregulated across multiple cell types within the ischemic niche and positively correlated with M2 macrophage infiltration. This ischemia-dependent induction was confirmed at the protein level in vivo. Integrative genetic analyses, including GWAS colocalization (PP.H4 = 0.90) and bidirectional MR, provided evidence supporting a causal link between genetically predicted CDKN1A expression and PAD risk, with no evidence of reverse causation. Computational gene perturbation analysis identified downstream transcriptional programs associated with extracellular matrix remodeling, TGF-beta signaling, and angiogenesis. PheWAS showed no genome-wide significant associations across 19 phenotype categories, and drug-gene interaction analysis identified resveratrol as a candidate modulator. The current findings indicate that CDKN1A-mediated stress response represents a key mechanism in PAD progression, linking ischemic injury to maladaptive remodeling and supporting its relevance as a genetically supported candidate therapeutic target in PAD. Our findings provide convergent transcriptomic, cellular, and genetic evidence supporting CDKN1A as a genetically supported candidate causal target associated with PAD progression. These results suggest that CDKN1A-mediated cell-cycle arrest and associated stress-response programs are associated with ischemic tissue remodeling, providing a rationale for future gene-directed or pharmacological intervention strategies aimed at attenuating the transition to CLI.

Título: Artificial Intelligence-enabled Antibiotic Discovery and Repurposing: Precision Strategies to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance.
Resumen: The effectiveness of some existing antibiotics is being compromised by the ever-rising rate at which antimicrobial resistance develops. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the most significant technological innovations that have become possible through which chemical diversity can be explored, interactions between drugs and targets predicted, and novel compounds developed to address bacterial infections. This paper will discuss the role of artificial intelligence technology in antibiotic discovery. The capabilities of generative AI, deep learning, and machine learning to contribute to drug design, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic property optimization, molecular screening, and prediction of mode of action were analyzed. Examples such as the discovery of halicin and peptide design using AI were also considered. The advent of AI technology has made it possible to predict the activity and resistance mechanisms for antibiotics, as well as to create structurally diverse molecules. Multimodal data analysis, neural network docking, and reinforcement learning have helped in decreasing preclinical attrition. Despite the huge promise offered by these technologies, several challenges must be overcome before these can be fully adopted. Issues such as low data quality, poor interpretability of the models, and regulatory requirements might slow down the implementation of AI technologies. Ethics and data formatting will be important determinants of the successful integration of AI technologies. AI represents an efficient and promising tool for antibiotic development through the integration of advanced computational techniques with empirical evaluation.

ID (PMID): 42852722
Título: Pressure-temperature phase diagram from global structure prediction and self-consistent phonon calculations based on polynomial machine learning potentials: Application to elemental silicon.
Resumen: Polynomial machine learning potentials (MLPs) based on polynomial rotational invariants have been systematically developed for various systems and applied to efficiently predict crystal structures. In this study, we propose a methodology founded on polynomial MLPs to enumerate crystal structures under high-pressure conditions and evaluate their phase stability at finite temperatures. The proposed approach involves constructing polynomial MLPs with high predictive accuracy across a broad range of pressures, conducting reliable global structure searches for structures containing up to the specified number of atoms, and performing exhaustive self-consistent phonon calculations with reduced errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by examining elemental silicon at pressures up to 100 GPa and temperatures up to 1000 K, revealing stable phases across these conditions. The framework established in this study offers a powerful strategy for predicting crystal structures and phase stability under high-pressure and finite-temperature conditions.

Título: Associations between advanced lung cancer inflammation index score and kidney outcomes in intensive care unit patients with diabetes: A retrospective cohort study.
Resumen: ObjectiveAcute kidney injury is commonly observed in critically ill patients with diabetes and is associated with adverse outcomes. The advanced lung cancer inflammation index score, which reflects nutritional and inflammatory status, has not been well studied in relation to acute kidney injury and subsequent kidney events in this population.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Adult intensive care unit patients with diabetes were included. Associations of log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores with acute kidney injury and major adverse kidney events within 30 days were assessed using logistic regression and Cox models, respectively. Restricted cubic spline analyses, eXtreme gradient boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations interpretation, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate model-based contribution, effect modification, and robustness.ResultsIn total, 2337 critically ill patients with diabetes were included in the acute kidney injury occurrence analysis, of whom 1624 developed acute kidney injury. Each 1-SD increase in log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation scores was associated with lower odds of acute kidney injury (odds ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.81-0.99). Among the 1624 patients with acute kidney injury, 750 developed major adverse kidney events within 30 days. Higher log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores were associated with a lower hazard of major adverse kidney events within 30 days (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.82-0.96). Dose-response analyses revealed a consistent inverse association between the advanced lung cancer inflammation index score and adverse kidney outcomes, particularly major adverse kidney events within 30 days. Machine-learning interpretation supported the contribution of the advanced lung cancer inflammation index score to model output for kidney outcomes, and sensitivity analyses yielded similar results.ConclusionsAmong intensive care unit patients with diabetes, higher advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores were associated with lower odds of acute kidney injury and a lower hazard of major adverse kidney events within 30 days after acute kidney injury. The advanced lung cancer inflammation index score may serve as a simple marker for inflammation and nutritional status associated with short-term kidney outcomes; however, its clinical utility requires validation in independent cohorts.

Título: Accelerating SCF Convergence Through Equivariant Density-Matrix Learning and Analytic Refinement.
Resumen: We present dm-PhiSNet, a physically constrained PhiSNet-based equivariant model that predicts one-electron reduced density matrices (1-RDMs) directly from molecular geometries in an atomic-orbital (AO) basis to accelerate self-consistent-field (SCF) convergence. Training follows a two-stage schedule with progressively introduced physically motivated objectives, and the resulting predictions are refined by a lightweight analytic block. This block enforces electron-number conservation, drives the 1-RDM toward generalized idempotency with respect to the AO overlap matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> , and regularizes the occupation spectrum of the density matrix in an orthogonalized AO representation. Across six closed-shell systems- <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow><msub><mi>H</mi> <mn>2</mn></msub> <mi>O</mi></mrow> </math> , <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CH</mi> <mn>4</mn></msub> </math> , <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi> <mn>3</mn></msub> </math> , HF, ethanol, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msubsup><mi>NO</mi> <mn>3</mn> <mo>-</mo></msubsup> </math> -the refined 1-RDMs provide SCF initial guesses that substantially reduce iteration steps by 49%-81% relative to standard initializations. Beyond SCF acceleration, the learned 1-RDMs yield accurate one-shot total energies and Hellmann-Feynman atomic forces without force supervision, indicating that the model captures chemically meaningful electronic structure. These results demonstrate that combining equivariant learning with analytic constraint enforcement provides a simple, general route to solver-ready density-matrix initializations and accelerated SCF calculations.

ID (PMID): 42852689
Título: A two-stage framework for fast proton spot map generation in pencil beam scanning prostate SBRT planning.
Resumen: In pencil beam scanning (PBS) proton therapy, treatment plans are encoded as proton spot maps (PSMs). Although deep-learning methods can rapidly predict three-dimensional (3D) dose distributions from patient anatomy and planning intent, there is still no widely adopted direct, non-iterative approach to convert doses into physically deliverable spot patterns. This limits end-to-end automation in treatment planning and adaptive replanning for PBS. We developed and retrospectively evaluated GenSpot, a two-stage framework that reconstructs a PBS PSM from CT and dose. This study focused on the dose-to-spots reconstruction step under controlled, achievable-dose conditions, using clinical Monte Carlo (MC) dose distributions as input in a single-institution prostate stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) cohort. GenSpot uses a physics-informed projected proton spot map (PrPSM) representation that projects individual proton spots through the CT using water-equivalent thickness and percentage depth dose (PDD) information, aligning the spots with the CT and dose voxel grid while preserving a linear relationship with spot weights. Our dataset comprised 1036 fields from 259 prostate SBRT plans, split into training, validation, and test sets in an 80%/10%/10% ratio. A 3D SwinUNETR model was trained to predict PrPSMs from CT and dose inputs. Field-specific PSMs were then reconstructed from the predicted PrPSMs using column-wise nonnegative Lasso regression with precomputed PDD curves. MC dose distributions from GenSpot and clinical PSMs were compared using voxel-wise mean absolute error (MAE), 3D gamma analysis (3%/3 mm, 10% low-dose threshold), and dose-volume histogram (DVH) metrics at the composite-plan level. Within the held-out test dataset, the selected SwinUNETR model achieved a mean PrPSM MAE of 0.06 ± 0.02 (normalized units) with high structural similarity to projected clinical PrPSMs. At the dose level, MC doses from GenSpot PSMs showed low MAE (0.07 ± 0.03 Gy in the nonzero-dose region) and high mean gamma passing rates (0.92 ± 0.05 at the field level and 0.99 ± 0.02 at the plan level). Composite-plan DVH metrics differences were generally within 1 Gy for targets and organs at risk, although the high-dose tail of the clinical target volume showed a modest systematic increase. Spot map complexity, measured by the number of energy layers and spot counts, was similar to that of clinical plans, with 20% more spots for GenSpot PSMs. For a four-field case, GenSpot PSM generation required approximately 2.9 ± 0.2 min excluding final MC recalculation. GenSpot reconstructed machine-compatible PSMs from CT and clinical MC dose with close composite-plan dose agreement in a single-institution prostate SBRT cohort. These results support GenSpot as a rapid, physics-informed dose-to-spots reconstruction component under achievable-dose conditions. The present study does not establish performance for arbitrary predicted or adapted dose inputs, and final MC recalculation and standard QA remain required before clinical use. Further validation with non-idealized dose inputs, multi-institution data, higher-resolution dose representations, and dedicated optimization-based baselines is needed before broader clinical implementation.

Título: PLEKHA5-targeted photothermal-gene combination therapy via mPDA@DMEA@siRNA nanoparticles suppresses melanoma progression.
Resumen: Melanoma is an aggressive skin malignancy characterized by high metastatic potential and resistance to current systemic therapies, highlighting the need for novel molecularly targeted and minimally invasive treatment strategies. Photothermal therapy enables localized tumor ablation with reduced systemic toxicity; however, its monotherapeutic efficacy is limited by incomplete tumor elimination and adaptive cellular stress responses. To address these limitations, we employed an integrative bioinformatics approach combining bulk transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, single-cell RNA sequencing, survival analysis, and three machine learning algorithms to identify melanoma-relevant therapeutic targets. This analysis identified PLEKHA5 as a key melanoma-associated gene with significant prognostic value and preferential expression in malignant cell populations. We then engineered a mesoporous polydopamine-based nanoplatform, mPDA@DMEA@siRNA, for concurrent PLEKHA5 gene silencing and near-infrared (NIR)-driven photothermal therapy. In this system, mPDA serves as the photothermal core, and surface modification with N,N-dimethylethylenediamine (DMEA) enables efficient electrostatic siRNA loading. The nanoplatform exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, broad NIR absorption, and potent photothermal conversion. <i>In vitro</i>, mPDA@DMEA@siRNA combined with NIR irradiation induced A375 melanoma cell death, enhanced reactive oxygen species generation, and silenced PLEKHA5 at both mRNA and protein levels. In an A375 xenograft model, mPDA@DMEA@siRNA markedly suppressed tumor growth, with histological analyses showing decreased proliferation, increased apoptotic cell death, reduced angiogenesis, and effective PLEKHA5 silencing. Systemic biosafety was supported by normal hematological parameters, stable serum biochemical indices, and absence of major organ pathology. Collectively, this study identifies PLEKHA5 as a candidate therapeutic target and demonstrates that mPDA@DMEA@siRNA is a promising nanoplatform for photothermal-gene combination therapy in melanoma.

Título: Brittle Star-Inspired Composites With Excellent Tribopositivity, Tensile Properties, and Self-Healing Capability for Self-Powered Flexible Sensors.
Resumen: Self-powered sensing devices for human-machine interaction suffer from poor mechanical robustness, fragile structural stability, and fluctuating sensing signals under cyclic deformation, severely restricting their long-term operational reliability. Integrating self-healing functionality into triboelectric substrates is an effective approach to address these bottlenecks, but it remains challenging to simultaneously realize superior stretchability, steady electrical output, and efficient self-healing performance in a single material system. Inspired by the arm structure of brittle stars, a waterborne polyurethane (WPU) incorporating dynamic disulfide and hydrogen bonds was fabricated, and the hydrogen-bonding interfacial network between MXene and WPU was tailored. A composite system enabling synergistic multilevel energy dissipation through reversible dynamic bonds and disulfide exchange was therefore constructed. The resulting MXene/WPU (M-WPU) composite film exhibits a tensile strength of 14.7 MPa, an elongation at break of 970%, a triboelectric output of 14 µA, and a self-healing efficiency of 89% after thermal healing at 100°C for 12 h. The flexible sensor assembled from this M-WPU film, integrated with machine learning, enables accurate handwriting recognition and human-machine interaction. Notably, after macroscopic crack self-healing, the M-WPU can still maintain stable electrical signal output, offering novel design insights for the development of long-life, highly reliable self-powered flexible sensors.

Título: Machine Learning-Enhanced Fiber-Optic Raman Spectroscopy for In Situ Oral Cancer Classification.
Resumen: A portable Raman spectroscopy system was developed for in vivo diagnosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) in clinical settings. 46 patients with histopathologically confirmed OSCC were involved. The preprocessed dataset was used to train four supervised machine learning classifiers, support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), ensemble algorithms (EA), and linear discriminant analysis (LDA), under a stratified ten-fold cross-validation scheme. Comparative evaluation demonstrated that SVM achieved perfect classification accuracy (100%), outperforming LDA (96.6%), EA (90.7%), and KNN (83.3%). SVM performance was evaluated against retained PC count to assess robustness and generalizability. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) remained above 80% with two PCs and increased to 96% when eight PCs were retained. These findings underscore the clinical translational potential of machine learning driven Raman spectroscopy, with high discriminative power and generalizability for oral cancer.

Título: Machine-learning-accelerated discovery of a σ-channel C-O activation mechanism.
Resumen: Carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) electroreduction is a promising route for carbon recycling and energy regeneration, with the development of dual-atom catalysts (DACs) being critical to its advancement. Conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) models based on DFT-derived descriptors are plagued by prohibitive computational time and resource costs. Herein, we extract 20 fundamental chemical descriptors exclusively from structural data and deploy a lightweight ML model to a dataset of 250 880 entries, eliminating the need for 12 544 DFT computations and rapidly identifying 10 high-performance two-dimensional BN-based DACs for CO<sub>2</sub> electroreduction. The model's reliability and the catalyst's stability and performance are validated <i>via</i> DFT, <i>ab initio</i> molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations and literature evidence. Contrary to the classic π-backbonding mechanism that relies on strong CO adsorption to trigger activation, we reveal an unprecedented σ-donation-enabled pathway that achieves efficient CO activation <i>via</i> reduced C-O σ bond order within weak-adsorption regions. This defining σ-channel strategy decouples the intrinsic adsorption-activation coupling of π-backbonding theory, markedly alleviating catalyst poisoning, and further offers a cost-effective, high-efficiency paradigm for high-throughput screening of advanced catalytic materials.

Título: Predicting nonunion - a hybrid machine-learning model combining patient factors and mechanobiological simulation features exceeds clinician accuracy.
Resumen: To compare the accuracy of a mechanobiological simulation against that of clinicians in forecasting long bone nonunions, and to determine whether the simulation's results can be effectively used as input for a machine-learning algorithm. This was a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study using a cohort of 98 patients who underwent surgery for tibial shaft fractures at four tertiary care trauma institutions in Germany between January 2018 and December 2023, 20 of whom developed nonunion. Biplanar pre- and postoperative radiographs and detailed demographic and clinical information (sex, age, BMI, comorbidities, fracture characteristics, surgical protocol, and implants used) were provided to clinicians to predict the likelihood of nonunion. All data were also analyzed with the Leeds-Genoa Non-Union-Index (LEG NUI) and entered into a mechanobiological simulation model, a machine-learning model, and a hybrid model. Performance metrics were then compared across all five assessment methods. Comparing the overall predictive performance of the clinicians' heuristic, the LEG NUI score, and the three computational models, the hybrid model outperforms all contenders concerning sensitivity (80%), positive predictive value (59%), negative predictive value (94%), and Matthews correlation coefficient (59%). Specificity was high (86%), solely outperformed by the specificity of the LEG NUI score (95%) and the mechanobiological simulation (90%). The AI-based hybrid model outperforms human experts in predicting nonunions in long bone fractures, enabling the early detection of patients at risk and the modification of treatment strategies to improve patient outcomes.

Título: Force-regulated robotic diffuse reflectance spectroscopy scanning.
Resumen: Intraoperative discrimination between malignant and benign tissue is essential for achieving complete tumor resection while preserving healthy structures. Robotic diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) enables automated intraoperative tissue assessment, but unregulated probe-tissue contact forces introduce spectral artifacts and risk tissue damage, limiting clinical translation. We present and evaluate an autonomous robotic DRS scanning system incorporating real-time contact force regulation to enable safe, repeatable, and large-area <i>ex vivo</i> tissue assessment. A serial robot manipulator equipped with a fiber-optic DRS probe, load cell, and camera employed hybrid visual servoing and force feedback control, maintaining 0.08 N target force with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo><</mo> <mn>0.30</mn> <mtext>  </mtext> <mi>N</mi></mrow> </math> peak limits. The system achieved 100% and 93% scan completion rates on bovine and ovine tissues, respectively, without visible tissue damage. Autonomous operation enabled 46 continuous trials over <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∼</mo> <mn>30</mn> <mtext>  </mtext> <mi>min</mi></mrow> </math> without human intervention. Mean applied force (0.079 N) matched manual sampling (0.080 N) with reduced variance and lower peak forces. Robotic spectral acquisitions aligned with manual measurements, yielding mean inter-observer spectral angles of 1.43 deg, comparable to inter-human operator variability. Tissue classification demonstrated high discriminatory accuracy in bench-top validation. Force-regulated robotic DRS enables standardized, autonomous tissue scanning with expert-level spectral consistency, advancing spectroscopic sensing toward reliable automated surgical margin assessment.

ML models demonstrated effective performance in predicting orthodontic treatment duration and in identifying fast- and slow-finishing cases. Key demographic, dental, and skeletal features-particularly age, extraction plan, incisor AP position, and vertical/incisal characteristics-were consistently strong predictors. The integration of big data and ML provides a scalable approach to enhance orthodontic diagnosis, optimize scheduling, improve communication of expectations, and support individualized treatment planning. Título: SEFCA-Net: a semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention network for diabetic retinopathy lesion segmentation.
Resumen: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) lesion segmentation provides pixel-level lesion localization in fundus images. However, such lesions are often tiny, sparsely distributed, low-contrast, morphologically diverse, and visually similar to vessels or surrounding retinal structures, making accurate localization difficult. Many existing methods emphasize multi-scale spatial representation learning and handle boundary ambiguity and subtle texture differences mainly through encoder-decoder fusion. We therefore examine boundary and frequency representations as explicit, complementary inputs to semantic decoding. We aim to develop SEFCA-Net, a semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention network for diabetic retinopathy lesion segmentation. The main objective is to examine whether semantic, edge, and frequency-domain representations can be fused under semantic guidance to improve pixel-level lesion localization without compromising the semantic decoding stream. The evaluation focuses on four lesion categories, including hard exudates, hemorrhages, soft exudates, and microaneurysms, using public benchmarks and a DDR-to-IDRiD cross-dataset setting. SEFCA-Net uses HRNet-W48 as the semantic backbone to extract multi-scale semantic features and explicitly constructs edge and frequency-domain representations from input fundus images. The learnable multi-scale edge branch extracts boundary-sensitive features, while the all-channel multi-scale discrete cosine transform (DCT) frequency-domain branch generates texture-sensitive responses to low-contrast lesions. The semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention decoder uses the semantic representation as the primary stream and injects edge and frequency-domain features through semantic-guided window-based cross-attention. Performance is evaluated using the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR), Dice, and Intersection-over-Union (IoU). On DDR, SEFCA-Net achieves 47.85% mean AUPR (mAUPR), 46.76% mean Dice, and 31.22% mean IoU. On IDRiD, it reaches 69.74% mAUPR; when trained on DDR and tested on IDRiD, it obtains 59.83% mAUPR. Ablation studies show that either auxiliary branch improves the semantic-only baseline and that the complete configuration gives the highest mAUPR. Multi-scale Sobel modeling and DCT outperform the tested single-scale and wavelet alternatives, respectively. SEFCA-Net shows that semantic features can remain the main decoding stream while boundary-sensitive features and texture-sensitive responses are integrated in a controlled manner. Under the evaluated protocols, the model shows competitive in-domain performance and records the highest DDR-to-IDRiD mAUPR among the reproduced methods.

Título: Machine Learning Predictions of PM<sub>2.5</sub> and Their Applications to Exposure and Health Assessment in the CONUS.
Resumen: Atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM<sub>2.5</sub>) is one of the most important risk factors for various respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. We develop a two-phase data-driven framework that uses geostationary Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals to predict hourly PM<sub>2.5</sub> at 0.01° × 0.01° resolution and support exposure assessment across multiple spatial and temporal contexts. Control strategies are subsequently reviewed across charging and discharging regulation, mode switching, and system dispatch. Finally, key research gaps are identified in high-temperature material durability, long-term multiphysics reservoir modeling, integrated turbomachinery-TES dynamics, multitime scale dispatch-control coordination, and fault-tolerant operation under extreme grid disturbances. By integrating thermodynamic design, TES material selection, CAR behavior, and advanced control strategies, this review provides systematic guidance for the design, optimization, and reliable deployment of next-generation ACAES systems.
